search_strategy: the authors used ‘straw returning’ or ‘straw mulching,’ and ‘maize’ in the keyword search to collect peer-reviewed journal articles from the china national knowledge infrastructure and web of science.
selection_criteria: to avoid any bias, the authors selected publications with the following criteria: 1) field experiment; 2) cropping system includes maize; 3) included control (no straw returning; ck) and treatments (straw mulching or straw incorporation); 4) means, standard deviations (or standard error), and number of replications available or can be calculated; 5) included yield or water use efficiency measurements.
data_analysis: to derive the overall response effect of the treatments (straw mulching or straw incorporation) groups and control (no straw returning) group, the weighted response ratio (rr++) between the treatments (straw mulching or straw incorporation) groups and control (no straw returning) group was calculated. metawin2.1 was used to generate 95% confidence intervals around the logarithmic response ratios (rr) with 4999 iterations. the authors applied a t-test to determine variation in each variable between the control and treatment and the difference in rr++ between subgroups.
background: Straw mulching and straw incorporation are widely used for conservation tillage as the primary methods of returning straw to the field. However, few studies have investigated the effects of straw mulching and straw incorporation under various agronomic management and environmental and edaphic factors.
objective: in this study the authors undertook a meta-analysis to: 1) analyze the effects of n application rate, straw returning amount, annual average precipitation, temperature, and evaporation, and soil texture on maize yield, wue, and nue with straw mulching and straw incorporation; 2) identify suitable methods of straw returning for different temperatures, precipitation, and soil textures in china; 3) determine the appropriate of straw returning amount and n application rate.
result1: the meta-analysis showed that straw incorporation significantly increased maize yields (rr++: 0.0996).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: straw incorporation have a positive effect on maize yield.

search_strategy: the meta-analysis was based on published and unpublished data.the unpublished studies were conducted by the international plant nutrient institute (ipni) china program, and a comprehensive literature survey of peer-reviewed papers from chinese rice field studies published from january 2000 to december 2016 was conducted using the china knowledge resource integrated database and web of science. the following search terms and their variations were used: rice yield, controlled or slow release fertiliser, organic fertiliser, green manure, crop residue, and secondary or micronutrients.
selection_criteria: 1) the fertilisation measures were conducted under field conditions in china; no pot or greenhouse experiments were included; 2) the study reported yield and the number of field replication; 3) conventional chemical fertiliser application was included as a control treatment; 4) the experimental and control treatments had to be applied to the same agricultural system and site.
data_analysis: the meta-analysis was performed using metawin 2.1 software (rosenberg et al., 2000).
background: Applying alternative fertilisation practices instead of conventional fertilisers might improve rice yield and nutrient use efficiency in rice cropping systems. However, the results range widely among individual studies,making generalizations difficult.
objective: 1) to comprehensively evaluate the effect of different alternative fertilisation options (slowrelease n fertiliser, organic fertiliser, straw return, green manure, and secondary/micronutrient fertiliser) on rice yield and nue relative to conventional chemical fertiliser application in chinese rice cultivation; 2) to investigate how the magnitude of the yield response varies with rice type (early, middle, late, and single season rice); 3) to determine the maximum proportion of conventional chemical nitrogen input that can be substituted with alternative fertilisation options without causing a decrease in rice yield. here, only results regarding the effect of green manures on rice yields are reported.
result1: there was a significantly positive yield response of early, middle, and late rice to straw return relative to straw removal, with percentage changes of 8.4%, 5.1%, and 4.8%, respectively. the overall magnitude of the yield response to straw return was 5.4%.
result2: there was no significant yield response of single rice to straw return compared to straw removal, and this trend was also observed in response to the application of organic fertilisers.
general_conclusion: there was an overal positive effect of straw return on yield (5.4%).

search_strategy: we used several databases such as web of science, google scholar, china national knowledge infrastructure database, china wanfang data, current contents connect (isi), academic search complete (ebsco), scopus, and cab abstracts to search peer‐reviewed publi- cations (before august 2018) related to the effects of straw return on various nr losses, crop productivity, and soil c sequestration. the keywords used in the search included “crop straw or crop residue or crop stubble,”“nr losses (nh3 emissions, n2o emissions, n leaching, and runoff), soc content, crop productivities (crop yield, crop n uptake, and n use efficiency (nue)) and/or other soil properties.”
selection_criteria: 1) the control (mineral n fertilisation) and straw treatment (mineral n fertilisation plus straw return) received equal mineral n fertilisation rates, which indicated that the straw treatment provided additional straw n supply to soils; 2) publications needed to report on at least one of the target variables and sample sizes for the con- trol and treatment plots. multiple observations that were conducted at the same experimental site over several sampling years were aver- aged; 3) the observation duration of the experiment must have covered the main discharge period of various nr losses.
data_analysis: mean effect sizes and the 95% confidence intervals (cis) were generated by a bootstrapping procedure with 4,999 iterations, using metawin 2.1. effects of straw return were considered significant if the 95% cis did not overlap with zero. the means of the categorical variables were consid- ered significantly different from each other if their 95% cis did not overlap.
background: It is widely recommended that crop straw be returned to croplands to maintain or increase soil carbon (C) storage in arable soils. However, because C and nitrogen (N) biogeochemical cycles are closely coupled, straw return may also affect soil reactive N (Nr) losses, but these effects remain uncertain, especially in terms of the interac- tions between soil C sequestration and Nr losses under straw addition.
objective: this paper is aimed to: 1) evaluate the overall effects of straw return on various nr loss pathways (nh3 emissions, n2o emissions, n leaching, and runoff), crop productivity and soil c sequestration in agroecosystems under different environ- mental and management conditions (straw quality and quantity, soil properties, agricultural management, and climate conditions); 2) explore the interactions between various nr losses and soc sequestration following straw return; 3) estimate how straw return has affected nr losses from global croplands and the overall cropland nr balance for the period 2005−2015.
result1: overall, straw return significantly increased crop yield by 5.1% (n = 636) in global agroecosystems, with a similar increase in 5.3% (n = 214) for rice paddies and 4.9% (n = 422) for upland crops.
result2: the increase in crop yield was significantly and positively cor- related with mineral n fertilisation rate (p < 0.01), straw n input rate (p < 0.01), and mean annual temperature (mat; p < 0.001; table 2)
general_conclusion: overall, straw return significantly increased crop yield by 5.1% (n = 636) in global agroecosystems.

search_strategy: we used several databases, such as web of science, google scholar and scopus to search peer-reviewed publications (before april 2020). the keywords used in the search were “cropland or crop or wheat or maize or barley or rice,” “soc or soil organic matter,” and/or “ch4, n2o and yield (grain).
selection_criteria: studies related to the management practices investigated were then selected. each study selected contains measurements of ghg emissions for both control and treatment management practices. studies with the following measurements were excluded: (i) measurements made in pot, laboratories or greenhouses and (ii) measurements conducted in organic (peaty) soils where n2o are much higher than those in mineral soils and where soil carbon fluxes are different (ipcc, 2006).

background: Smart cropland management practices can mitigate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions while safeguarding food security. However, the integrated effects on net greenhouse gas budget (NGHGB) and grain yield from different management practices remain poorly defined and vary with environmental and application conditions.
objective: evaluate the integrated effects of alternative management practices on cropland net greenhouse gas budget and grain yield

search_strategy: experimental research papers were identified via a search for field-based reports on the effects ofcrop residue return on crop yields and wue that were published prior to 2018. chinese and english databases were used, including the china knowledge network, weipu, wanfang, web ofscience, springer, engineering village, and google scholar. the keywords included “straw”, “mulching”, “residue”, and “yield”.
selection_criteria: the studies were selected using the following criteria: 1) the experiment must have been conducted in the field; 2) the experimental duration must have been >= 2 years; 3) there were >= 3 replicates; 4) the test site and year were clearly identified; 5) the test treatments included both crop residue return and no return; 6) in cases where many years of production data were included, only the most recent year was used.
data_analysis: meta-analysis was performed using metawin 2.1 software. the mean effect sizes were evaluated with a random-effects model. the 95% ci for each mean effect size was estimated by applying bootstrapping with 4999 iterations. mean effect sizes were considered significantly different when the 95% cis did not overlap, and the gaussian distribution lines were made using origin 8.5 software. the images were processed using graphpad prim 6.0 software.
background: Although there has been extensive research on the effects of crop residue return, the results are inconsis- tent or contradictory because of differences in soil conditions, planting systems, and climatic conditions.
objective: the authors conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate the impacts of crop residue return on crop yields and wue relative to those of crops grown without crop residue treatment (referred to here as no-straw).
result1: the overall effect of crop residues return on crop yield was positive, but it was significantly affected by crop type (p < 0.05).
result2: the results for soybean, rape, and pea overlapped zero, suggesting no significant effect ofcrop residue return on their yields. wheat crops had the smallest increase in yield associated with crop residue return (2.7%). the effects ofcrop residue return on the yields ofrice and corn crops were 5.3% and 8.0%, respectively.
result3: the increases in yields attributed to crop residue return were affected little by mean annual temperature and soil total n content.
result4: the highest increases in yield occurred for cases with rainfall > 800 mm (9.5%), ploughing depths of > 20 cm (6.5%), corn crops (8.0%), crops with a full year ofripening (10.1%), no irrigation (11.9%), nk fertiliser (20.0%), low rates of n application (0–100 kg n ha-1; 10.8%), organic matter contents > 15 g kg-1 (9.4%), effective nitrogen contents >100 mg kg-1 (10.3%), and ph < 6.5 (11.2%).
general_conclusion: the meta-analysis showed that crop yields increased by an average of 5.0% when crop residue return was used, compared to no-straw treatment.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed journal articles were systematically searched in the web of science database, with the search term combinations [fertiliser managements or fertilisation or nitrogen] and [ch4 emission or ch4] and [rice or paddy field].

search_strategy: the authors searched for peer-reviewed publications investigating the effectiveness of measures to address compacted (sub)soils, using web of science and china knowledge resource integrated database (cnki, for chinese studies not published in english language). search terms were (“soil compaction” or “compacted soil” or “compacted subsoil” or “subsoil compaction”) and (“yield” or “biomass”) and (“density” or “penetration” or “soil cone index”) in titles, keywords, and abstracts.
selection_criteria: in web of science, conference proceedings and non-english publications were excluded. the search process was followed by a screening procedure that was based on the following criteria: 1) field studies must include side by side comparisons of soil compaction prevention, remediation and/or alleviation treatments, and control (or reference) treatments; 2) for each paired comparison, treatments and reference treatments have the same location, cropping system, cropping management, and year; 3) grain yields and/or biomass yields were reported; 4) soil bulk density and/or soil penetration index data were reported; 5) the test crops were cereals, including wheat, maize, barley, oat, and sorghum; 6) location(s), year(s), and basic soil information of the experiment(s) were stated. only studies with cereal crops as test crops were included. one
data_analysis: for the calculation of a grouped effect size, a linear mixed-effect model was used for which we used the r-package ‘nlme’. results of treatments addressing soil compaction were set as fixed effects and study numbers were set as random effects, to allow accounting for variances among studies. we used the equal weighting method (e.g., [35]) when comparing studies with different number of replicates.
background: The compaction of subsoils in agriculture is a threat to soil functioning. Measures aimed at the prevention, amelioration, and/or impact alleviation of compacted subsoils have been studied for more than a century, but less in smallholder agriculture.
objective: 1) to quantitatively examine the effects of measures aimed at avoiding and ameliorating soil compaction and at alleviating the impacts of compacted subsoils on crop yield, soil bulk density, and soil penetration resistance, using results of published studies; 2) to examine the effectiveness of measures in smallholder and mechanized agriculture.

search_strategy: the data for the present meta-analysis were collected from published peer-reviewed experimental studies that reported changes in soil quality, environmental impacts, and crop production indicators responding to rr compared with residues removed in china's croplands from the web of science (before the year of 2017, http://apps.webofknowledge.com.proxy.insermbiblio.inist.fr/) and the china knowledge resource integrated database (before the year of 2017, http://www.cnki.net/) with the key words of 'residue or straw,' 'retain or retention or return or mulch or incorporation,' and 'china.'
selection_criteria: (a) the experiment was designed as side-by-side paired-plot field studies with well-defined control composing of crop residues removal treatment as rr in china's croplands (mainland china); (b) other field managements that were clearly stated or described as 'similar field managements were conducted involving both controls and treatments' (e.g., the same cropping intensity, irrigation, and fertilisation); (c) one or more variables of soil quality, crop production, and environmental impacts parameters were obtainable with the same sampling and measuring methods under rr and residues removed treatments; and (d) location for each field experiment was provided.
data_analysis: a random-effect meta-analysis was conducted to assess crop residues removal(rr)-induced changes for microbial biomass carbon. the weighted mean effect size (lnr++) and 95% confidence interval were generated by bootstrapping through 4,999 iterations.
background: Crop residue retention (RR) is a recommended practice in China and globally. However, comprehensive assessment of changes and mechanisms affecting crop production and soil processes with RR and thus identifying systems of sustainable residues management are not widely studied.
objective: the objectives of the present study were to (a) compile a national dataset of published literatures and conduct a national meta-analysis on the positive and negative responses of soil quality, environmental impacts, and crop production under rr; (b) identify the combined effects of different farming practices with rr; (c) determine the interactive relationships among these indicators; and finally (d) hypothesize possible mechanisms on how rr affects crop production and soil processes.
result1: under residues retention (rr) compared with residue removed, significant increases in ghgs emissions were observed.
result2: among them, rr significantly increased ch4 emission by 130.9% (p < .05), which was the highest followed by n2o (12.2%, p < .05) emissions.
general_conclusion: residue retention in china's croplands increase emissions of greenhouse gases (by 130.9% and 12.2% for ch4 and n2o, respectively).

search_strategy: we used web of science, google scholar, and china national knowledge to search for publications focusing on the comprehensive analysis of residue return and its effect on soil n losses, published before 11 january 2020. the search terms were “(residue or straw or organic amendment)” and “(n2o emission or no3− leaching).”
selection_criteria: (a) the study was based on practice-relevant field, mesocosm, and lysimeter experiments, excluding lab experiments; (b) n losses (n2o emission or no3− leaching) in the experiment were measured for at least one growing season (observations made over several growing seasons were averaged); (c) experimental and control plots had been established in the same ecosystem and included at least one comparison of n losses; (d) statistical information such as mean values of n2o emission and no3− leaching, standard deviation (sd), and samples size in the experiment were directly extractable from the tables of the published articles, or were extracted from the graphs with the getdata graph digitizer software (version 2.26: http://getdata-graph-digitizer.com/download.php).
data_analysis: weighted mean effect sizes were calculated. the 95% bootstrap confidence interval (ci) of lnrr was calculated according to curtis and wang (1998) by bootstrapping 4999 iterations (rosenberg et al. 1997). the statistical tests were considered significant at the p < 0.05 level. all of the meta-analysis procedures were conducted using metawin 2.1 software (sinauer associates, inc., sunderland, ma, usa), and statistical analyses were performed using spss 21.0 (ibm deutschland gmbh, ehningen, germany) for windows. potential publication bias was analyzed with funnel plot analysis and egger’s indicator test (egger et al. 1997) with the stata statistical software (version 16, 2019, statacorp llc, college station, tx, usa), using a 95% confidence interval.
background: Incorporation of crop residues into the soil has been widely recommended as an effective method to sustain soil fertility and improve soil carbon sequestration in arable lands. However, it may lead to an increase in the emission of nitrous oxide (N2O) and leaching of nitrate (NO3−) to groundwater due to higher nitrogen (N) availability after crop residue incorporation.
objective: evaluate the effects of crop residue return on soil n2o emissions for different locations, climatic and soil conditions, and agricultural management strategies.
result1: upland soil amended with crop residues showed a significant increase of n2o emission, which was 46% higher than control. conversely, it decreased the n2o emission by 18% in paddy soil.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: crop residue return increases n2o emission in upland soils while it decreases n2o emission in paddy soils.
knowledge_gaps: the determination of the optimal tillage frequency with crop residue return requires further study.

search_strategy: data were compiled from 156 published experimental studies by extensively searching google scholar, web of science (1900–2017), china knowledge resource integrated database (avail- able online), and baidu scholar.
selection_criteria: 1) the experimental duration and land use were clearly recorded and the measurements of treatment and control groups were conducted within the same temporal and spatial scales; 2) crop residue was added di-rectly to the agroecosystem and paired data (control and treatment) for at least one of the chosen variables was reported; 3) studies with an experimental duration less than one year were excluded to avoid short-term noise; 4) the control and treatment plots started with the same soil type, n fertiliser application rate, climatic conditions, crop species, and other conditions; (5) the primary data—from which means, standard deviations (sd), or standard errors (se), and sample sizes (n) could be calculated—were directly provided or these statistics could be calculated from the results.

background: The return of crop residue to the soil has been suggested as a nutrient-conserving practice that effectively increases soil fertility and crop nutrition. However, the overall direction and magnitude of changes in the agroecosystem nitrogen (N) cycle in response to crop residue return are poorly quantified.
objective: the present a global synthesis of the agroecosystem n cycle in response to crop residue return so that the efficacy of this practice for agricultural sustainability can be rigorously evaluated.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed research articles published before 1 january 2021 were searched in google scholar and web of science with the following keywords: “residue” or “straw” or “stubble” and “nitrous oxide” or “n2o” or “greenhouse gas” or “ghg” or “emission factor”.
selection_criteria: (i) the experimental design had to be sufficiently detailed regarding the treatments and recent history; (ii) included treat- ment replicates; and (iii) were conducted under realistic field conditions. all the studies included pairwise comparisons in which all factors (e.g., fertilisation, irrigation, tillage practices) were the same for the treat- ment (with crop residue retention) and control (with crop residue removal) groups. for grassland, we compared permanent grassland (control) to grassland termination (treatment), the analogous practice to crop residue incorporation in these systems.
data_analysis: the authors used the log response ratio (lnrr) as effect size, which is a common metric in meta-analyses. they performed a weighted mixed-effects meta-analysis, using the rma.mv func- tion of the ‘metafor’ package, including “study” as a random effect because several studies contributed more than one effect size. effect sizes from individual comparisons were weighted by the inverse of their variance. missing variances were estimated using the average coficient of variation across the dataset. we used awald test to evaluate statistical differences between subgroups within categories at p-value < 0.05.
background: Crop residue incorporation is a common practice to increase or restore organicmatter stocks in agricultural soils. How- ever, this practice often increases emissions of the powerful greenhouse gas nitrous oxide (N2O). Previous meta- analyses have linked various biochemical properties of crop residues to N2O emissions, but the relationships between these properties have been overlooked, hampering our ability to predict N2Oemissions from specific residues.
objective: the objective of this meta-analysis was to synthesise the results of field studies measuring the effect of crop residue retention on soil n2o emissions. the authors aimed to identify the main drivers of soil n2o emissions associated with the application of crop residues and to rank their importance.
result1: averaged across all studies, crop residue retention increased n2o emissions by 43% (95% ci: 23–66%; p < 0.001).
result2: the differences between crop types were large. crop residues increased n2o emissions for cover crops (50%, ci: 19–88%), grasslands (216%, ci: 114–366%) and vegetables (183%, ci: 85–334%), but not for cereals, grain legumes, rice or sugar cane

search_strategy: mitigation measures for n2o emissions from crop residues were collated from the literature using isi web of science, scopus and google scholar. the search terms were: “residue” or “straw” or “stubble” and “nitrous oxide” or “n2o” or “greenhouse gas” or “ghg” or “emission factor” and “measure” or “strategy”.

(2022). crop residues are considered as any above- ground plant component of a crop returned to the soil. the database consisted of 367 selected pairwise comparisons reported in 78 studies, which met predetermined quality criteria (only studies with replication, with detailed information, and performed under realistic field conditions). pairwise comparisons only included observations where a treatment (i.e., with crop residue retention) and a control (i.e., with crop residue removal) could be compared with all other factors unchanged.
data_analysis:
after screening the literature, the measures were categorized according to: residue physical management, residue incorporation timing, interactions with fertilisation, additives and crop residue modifications, crop type, and edaphoclimatic conditions. 
we conducted a weighted mixed-effects model meta-analysis using the “rma.mv” function from r package “metafor” (viechtbauer, 2010). since several studies contributed more than one paired observation, we consid- ered “study” and “observation” as random factors in the mixed-effects models. for ease of interpretation, the overall effect size was converted into percentage change, i.e., (elnr − 1) ∗ 100%. we considered the effect size to be significant (i.e., it changes n2o emissions compared to crop resi- due removal) when the 95%ci ofexperimental classes did not include zero. to evaluate statistical differences between sub-groups within mitigation measures, we used a wald-type test.
background: Crop residues are of crucial importance to maintain or even increase soil carbon stocks and fertility, and thereby to ad- dress the global challenge of climate change mitigation. However, crop residues can also potentially stimulate emis- sions of the greenhouse gas nitrous oxide (N2O) from soils. A better understanding of how to mitigate N2O emissions due to crop residue management while promoting positive effects on soil carbon is needed to reconcile the opposing effects of crop residues on the greenhouse gas balance of agroecosystems.
objective: the authors combine a literature review and a meta-analysis to identify and assess measures for mitigating n2o emissions due to crop residue application to agricultural field.
result1: n2o emissions from surface-applied or incorporated residues are not significantly different due to the large variation within each category.
result2: although the effect was not significant, the meta-analysis indicates a trend for higher n2o emissions when crop residues were incorporated at depth (>15 cm) as compared to a shallower incorporation (p ≤ 0.10).
result3: the meta-analysis did not find an effect of the season in which crop residues are incorporated on the magnitude of n2o released.
general_conclusion: crop residues deep incorporation into the soil has no effect on n2o emissions compared to shallow incorporation. crop residues shallow incorporation has no effect on n2o emissions compared to crop residues surface applied.
knowledge_gaps:
knowledge gaps include the interactions between management, climate and residue composition that make emissions difficult to predict at regional and global scales. if future research confirms the n2o mitigation potential of residue mixtures, they can be implemented in many agroecosystems: multi-species swards in grasslands, cover crops, diversified crop rotations (effects such as changes in decomposer communities are expected to act over longer time-frames than a cropping season), and also in intercropping. 
previous meta-analyses have found lower n2o emissions after crop residue application to fields for soils with a high clay content. this implies that avoiding crop residue incorporation in coarse-textured soils whenever possible could be an n2o mitigation strategy. from a climate change perspective, this may provide a dual benefit: fine-textured soils, which have the highest potential to sequester c via crop residue incorporation, may be the ones with the lowest n2o emissions after crop residue incorporation, particularly if the initial soc content is low. this needs to be confirmed in future studies, since the positive relationship between soil clay content and the capacity of soil to store c is not always consistent, and because increases in soc may eventually lead to higher n2o emissions.

objective: the present a global synthesis of the agroecosystem n cycle in response to crop residue return so that the efficacy of this practice for agricultural sustainability can be rigorously evaluated.
result1: across all studies, crop residue returns enhanced and increased the total n pool in crop by 34.9%.
result2: crop residue return significantly increased crop n uptake by 9.0%.
result3: crop residue return had no significant effect on nitrogen use efficiency.
general_conclusion: the results have shown that crop residue return can improve crop nitrogen uptake while crop residue return has no effect on nitrogen use efficiency.

search_strategy: the authors used ‘straw returning’ or ‘straw mulching,’ and ‘maize’ in the keyword search to collect peer-reviewed journal articles from the china national knowledge infrastructure and web of science.
selection_criteria: to avoid any bias, the authors selected publications with the following criteria: 1) field experiment; 2) cropping system includes maize; 3) included control (no straw returning; ck) and treatments (straw mulching or straw incorporation); 4) means, standard deviations (or standard error), and number of replications available or can be calculated; 5) included yield or water use efficiency measurements.
data_analysis: to derive the overall response effect of the treatments (straw mulching or straw incorporation) groups and control (no straw returning) group, the weighted response ratio (rr++) between the treatments (straw mulching or straw incorporation) groups and control (no straw returning) group was calculated. metawin2.1 was used to generate 95% confidence intervals around the logarithmic response ratios (rr) with 4999 iterations. the authors applied a t-test to determine variation in each variable between the control and treatment and the difference in rr++ between subgroups.
background: Straw mulching and straw incorporation are widely used for conservation tillage as the primary methods of returning straw to the field. However, few studies have investigated the effects of straw mulching and straw incorporation under various agronomic management and environmental and edaphic factors.
objective: in this study the authors undertook a meta-analysis to: 1) analyze the effects of n application rate, straw returning amount, annual average precipitation, temperature, and evaporation, and soil texture on maize yield, wue, and nue with straw mulching and straw incorporation; 2) identify suitable methods of straw returning for different temperatures, precipitation, and soil textures in china; 3) determine the appropriate of straw returning amount and n application rate.
result1: the meta-analysis showed that straw incorporation significantly increased nue (rr++: 0.0931).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: straw incorporation has a positive effect on nutrient use efficiency of maize compared to no straw return.

search_strategy: the meta-analysis was based on published and unpublished data.the unpublished studies were conducted by the international plant nutrient institute (ipni) china program, and a comprehensive literature survey of peer-reviewed papers from chinese rice field studies published from january 2000 to december 2016 was conducted using the china knowledge resource integrated database and web of science. the following search terms and their variations were used: rice yield, controlled or slow release fertiliser, organic fertiliser, green manure, crop residue, and secondary or micronutrients.
selection_criteria: 1) the fertilisation measures were conducted under field conditions in china; no pot or greenhouse experiments were included; 2) the study reported yield and the number of field replication; 3) conventional chemical fertiliser application was included as a control treatment; 4) the experimental and control treatments had to be applied to the same agricultural system and site.
data_analysis: the meta-analysis was performed using metawin 2.1 software (rosenberg et al., 2000).
background: Applying alternative fertilisation practices instead of conventional fertilisers might improve rice yield and nutrient use efficiency in rice cropping systems. However, the results range widely among individual studies,making generalizations difficult.
objective: 1) to comprehensively evaluate the effect of different alternative fertilisation options (slowrelease n fertiliser, organic fertiliser, straw return, green manure, and secondary/micronutrient fertiliser) on rice yield and nue relative to conventional chemical fertiliser application in chinese rice cultivation; 2) to investigate how the magnitude of the yield response varies with rice type (early, middle, late, and single season rice); 3) to determine the maximum proportion of conventional chemical nitrogen input that can be substituted with alternative fertilisation options without causing a decrease in rice yield. here, only results regarding the effect of green manures on rice yields are reported.
result1: when substituting chemical fertiliser with some proportion of of, no significant effect was observed in any types of nue. the aen and pfpn increases (18.4% and 4.7%) under straw return were significant, whereas that of ren under straw return was not.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: straw return has a positive effect on recovery efficiency of nitrogen and agronomic efficiency of nitrogen in rice compared to straw removal, while it has no effect on partial factor productivity of nitrogen.

search_strategy: four paired field management practices (n input, irrigation, tillage, and straw management) of winter wheat production in the north china plain were considered in this study. according to the research topic, the authors first identified “north china plain” or “huang-huai-hai plain” “winter wheat”“crop product*” as the search keywords. then, the authors collected peer reviewed journal articles from the china national knowledge infrastructure (published from january 1979 to december 2016) and web of science (published from january 1900 to december 2016).
selection_criteria: 1) the field experiment must have been conducted in the north china plain; 2) the cropping system in field experiment must contain winter wheat; 3) one or more of the following practice comparisons (e.g., no n versus n input, rain fed versus irrigated, rotary tillage versus other tillage methods, and straw removed versus straw return, with the former as the control and the later as the treatment) must be included; 4) data including the number of replications, nar, and yield must be presented or could be directly computed.
data_analysis:
in this random-effect meta-analysis, the natural logarithm of the response ratio (lnr) is used as the effect size. due to the lack ofstandard deviations given in some studies, the number of experimental replications was used to calculate the weight (w) of each lnr. the 95% confidence interval (ci) and weighted mean effect size (lnrþþ) were generated by bootstrapping (4999 iterations), and the between-group heterogeneity was assessed by using randomization procedures with 4999 replications. this study used microsoft office 2016 to collect
and manage data. they applied arcgis 10.2 to visualize the experimental data. the meta-analysis was conducted using metawin 2.1, and sigmaplot 14.0 was utilized for the correlation analysis and graphing.
background: Increasing nitrogen use efficiency by optimizing field management practices is necessary to promote intensive and sustainable development of winter wheat production.
objective: the objectives of this study were to 1) assess the effects of different field management practices (e.g., n application, irrigation, tillage, straw management, etc.) on the nue of wheat; 2) under- stand the influence of major factors of field management practices on nue; 3) identify the suitable strategies to improve the nue of winter wheat in the north china plain.
result1: the study indicated that straw return did not significantly improve the npfp of winter wheat in the north china plain.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: straw return has no effect on nitrogen partial factor productivity.

search_strategy: based on the two databases of the web of science and china national knowledge infrastructure (cnki), we searched for peer-reviewed scientific journal articles before december 2016 that were related to the effects of n input, irrigation, tillage, and straw return, on the n use of summer maize in ncp. the keywords used in a rigorous literature search included “north china plain or huang-huai-hai plain” “maize or corn or summer maize or summer corn” and “yield or output or crop product*”.
selection_criteria: a) the research object must be summer maize in the winter wheat-summer maize cropping system; b) the experiments described in the literature must be field experiments conducted in ncp (excluding pot experiments, laboratory experiments, and model studies); c) the research must focus on one or more of the four main farming practices (e.g., no n input versus n input, rain-fed versus irrigation, no-till versus other tillage methods, and straw removed versus straw return, with the former as the control and the later as the treatment; and d) each set of study data must include the number of trial replications (minimum of three) and the yield.
data_analysis: the replication-based weighting method was applied in a random-effect meta-analysis. we used metawin 2.1 (state university of new york at stony brook, usa) to obtain mean effect sizes and the 95% confidence intervals (cis) through a bootstrapping procedure with 4,999 iterations, and assess heterogeneity between subgroups by using randomization procedures with 4,999 replications.
background: Inappropriate nitrogen (N) use in maize (Zea mays L.) production can reduce crop productivity, decrease farm profitability, and cause serious environmental pollution. However, there is no consensus among researchers on the most appropriate farming practices regarding N use.
objective: assess the impact of farming practices on the n use of summer maize
result1: relative to straw removed, the aboveground n uptake of maize increased significantly through straw return (11%, p < 0.05)
result2: NA
general_conclusion: positive effect of straw return on nitrogen uptake of maize.

search_strategy: we used several databases such as web of science, google scholar, china national knowledge infrastructure database, china wanfang data, current contents connect (isi), academic search complete (ebsco), scopus, and cab abstracts to search peer‐reviewed publi- cations (before august 2018) related to the effects of straw return on various nr losses, crop productivity, and soil c sequestration. the keywords used in the search included “crop straw or crop residue or crop stubble,”“nr losses (nh3 emissions, n2o emissions, n leaching, and runoff), soc content, crop productivities (crop yield, crop n uptake, and n use efficiency (nue)) and/or other soil properties.”
selection_criteria: 1) the control (mineral n fertilisation) and straw treatment (mineral n fertilisation plus straw return) received equal mineral n fertilisation rates, which indicated that the straw treatment provided additional straw n supply to soils; 2) publications needed to report on at least one of the target variables and sample sizes for the con- trol and treatment plots. multiple observations that were conducted at the same experimental site over several sampling years were aver- aged; 3) the observation duration of the experiment must have covered the main discharge period of various nr losses.
data_analysis: mean effect sizes and the 95% confidence intervals (cis) were generated by a bootstrapping procedure with 4,999 iterations, using metawin 2.1. effects of straw return were considered significant if the 95% cis did not overlap with zero. the means of the categorical variables were consid- ered significantly different from each other if their 95% cis did not overlap.
background: It is widely recommended that crop straw be returned to croplands to maintain or increase soil carbon (C) storage in arable soils. However, because C and nitrogen (N) biogeochemical cycles are closely coupled, straw return may also affect soil reactive N (Nr) losses, but these effects remain uncertain, especially in terms of the interac- tions between soil C sequestration and Nr losses under straw addition.
objective: this paper is aimed to: 1) evaluate the overall effects of straw return on various nr loss pathways (nh3 emissions, n2o emissions, n leaching, and runoff), crop productivity and soil c sequestration in agroecosystems under different environ- mental and management conditions (straw quality and quantity, soil properties, agricultural management, and climate conditions); 2) explore the interactions between various nr losses and soc sequestration following straw return; 3) estimate how straw return has affected nr losses from global croplands and the overall cropland nr balance for the period 2005−2015.
result1: on average, crop n uptake and fertiliser nue were significantly increased by 10.9% (n = 157) and 15.0% (n = 100) under straw return, respectively, with a similar increase for rice paddies and upland crops.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: crop nitrogen uptake and fertiliser nitrogen use efficiency were significantly increased by 10.9% and 15.0% under straw return.

search_strategy: the authors searched the peer-reviewed literature using the science direct, pubmed, and proquest databases from january 1, 1970, to january 1, 2019. the search terms were as follows: (straw or straws or stalk or stalks or residue or residues) and (soil or ground) and ((microbial biomass carbon) or mbc)) and ((mineral fertilisation) or (mineral nitrogen) or fertilisation or nitrogen)).
selection_criteria:
criteria for inclusion: 1) straw included; 2) in english; 3) control group included, straw treatments and controls had the same soil type and management; 4) microbial biomass carbon (mbc) data included (for biological community diversity, shannon index data included); 5)
original research. criteria for exclusion: 1) straw not used; biochar or biogas residue used; 2) non-english; 3) no control group; 4) no mbc data (for biological community diversity, no shannon index data included); 5) review.
data_analysis: meta-analyses and forest plot creation were conducted using the review manager software (version 5.3, copenhagen: nordic cochrane centre, cochrane collaboration) and the r version 3.2.2 software. the higgins method was used to examine the p-value and i2 statistics. for biological community diversity, shannon index data were calculated using continuous data.
background: Soil microbial biomass carbon (MBC) can reveal the total microbial count, and microbial community diversity can be investigated using the Shannon index. Straw application is an important factor affecting soil MBC. Many studies have found that straw application increases soil MBC, although some studies suggest that straw application decreases soil MBC.
objective: the aim of the paper was to understand the effect of straw application on soil microbial biomass carbon change.
result1: straw application prompts a significant improvement in mbc content both for "straw application with fertilisation" and for "straw application without fertilisation".
result2: all types of straw (wheat, maize, rice) application significantly improved the mbc content.
general_conclusion: straw retention with or without fertilisation has a positive effect on soil microbial biomass carbon.

search_strategy: the data for the present meta-analysis were collected from published peer-reviewed experimental studies that reported changes in soil quality, environmental impacts, and crop production indicators responding to rr compared with residues removed in china's croplands from the web of science (before the year of 2017, http://apps.webofknowledge.com.proxy.insermbiblio.inist.fr/) and the china knowledge resource integrated database (before the year of 2017, http://www.cnki.net/) with the key words of 'residue or straw,' 'retain or retention or return or mulch or incorporation,' and 'china.'
selection_criteria: (a) the experiment was designed as side-by-side paired-plot field studies with well-defined control composing of crop residues removal treatment as rr in china's croplands (mainland china); (b) other field managements that were clearly stated or described as 'similar field managements were conducted involving both controls and treatments' (e.g., the same cropping intensity, irrigation, and fertilisation); (c) one or more variables of soil quality, crop production, and environmental impacts parameters were obtainable with the same sampling and measuring methods under rr and residues removed treatments; and (d) location for each field experiment was provided.
data_analysis: a random-effect meta-analysis was conducted to assess crop residues removal(rr)-induced changes for microbial biomass carbon. the weighted mean effect size (lnr++) and 95% confidence interval were generated by bootstrapping through 4,999 iterations.
background: Crop residue retention (RR) is a recommended practice in China and globally. However, comprehensive assessment of changes and mechanisms affecting crop production and soil processes with RR and thus identifying systems of sustainable residues management are not widely studied.
objective: the objectives of the present study were to (a) compile a national dataset of published literatures and conduct a national meta-analysis on the positive and negative responses of soil quality, environmental impacts, and crop production under rr; (b) identify the combined effects of different farming practices with rr; (c) determine the interactive relationships among these indicators; and finally (d) hypothesize possible mechanisms on how rr affects crop production and soil processes.
result1: microbial biomass carbon responded positively to crop residues retention (rr) and was significantly increased by 36.8% (p>.05).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: residue retention significantly increased microbial biomass carbon by 36.8% compared with crop residue removal.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed articles published between january 1990 and may 2018 were extracted using one of the following search terms and their abbreviations: “β-glucosidase,” “permanganate oxidizable carbon,” “active carbon,” “readily oxidable carbon,” and “fluorescein diacetate hydrolysis.” these were combined with one or more of the following terms: “management practice,” “tillage,” “cover crop,” “residue,” “organic fertiliser,” and “manure.” this search was carried out using thomas reuters web of science database (thomas reuters) and google scholar (google).
selection_criteria: the retrieved articles were screened to retain studies containing pairwise comparisons of sqi values in soils maintained under conservation and conventional practices.
data_analysis: the sqi responsiveness to use of conservation practices, and the influence of site, sampling covariates, and analytical methods on sqi responsiveness, were estimated by determining the weighted es of each category with 95% confidence intervals (ci) using a bootstrapping procedure with 5,000 iterations in the r “boot” package (canty & ripley, 2017). weights were assigned based on the number of records extracted from each study. the relative heterogeneity of sqi responsiveness among covariate categories was evaluated using the randomization procedure (adams et al., 1997) implemented in r with 5,000 iterations.
background: Efforts to protect and improve soil health commonly seek to discourage use of conventional, tillage-based cropping systems that degrade soil services and result in negative environmental outcomes, and to promote use of conservation practices including vegetative fallow, reduced or no-tillage, and increased additions of organic residues that can enhance soil quality and associated soil health.
objective: responsiveness of biochemical soil quality indicators (sqis) (β-glucosidase activity [bg], fluorescein diacetate hydrolysis [fda], and permanganate oxidizable c [poxc]) to management and their interactions with site and experimental factors were evaluated using a meta-database to quantify effect sizes.
result1: residue return increased bg and fda, while has no effect on poxc.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: residue return compared to residue removal increased β-glucosidase (bg) and fluorescein diacetate hydrolysis (fda), while has no effect on permanganate oxidizable c (poxc).

search_strategy: we collected data from relevant peer-reviewed publications. the publications were identified using the online database isi web of science, within the period 1997–2017. publications were searched using the keywords “organic amendment” and the results were refined using additional words—“long-term”, “yield”, “manure”, “compost”, “olsen p”, and “microbial biomass”. additionally, articles cited in review papers which had analysed data from long-term agricultural studies (≥ 10 years)  were also included in the dataset.
selection_criteria: 1) studies that reported crop yield, soil organic carbon, microbial biomass (mb) and/or plant-available p data for at least two types of treatments: (a) those that did not receive any fertiliser (‘nil control’); or (b) those where only inorganic npk fertiliser (if, ‘standard control’) was applied, and (c) where organic amendments (oa) with or without supplemental if was used. we defined oa as raw or composted materials derived from animals (e.g., manure), plant (e.g., straw) and municipal waste (e.g., sludge). the standard control did not always receive equivalent nutrient rates to those in oa and oa + if treatments; 2) crop yield data were included only for wheat, barley, corn, and rice grain in order to minimise differences in nutrient needs and rooting systems.
data_analysis: the meta-analysis was performed according to hedges et al. (1999) and cayuela et al. (2014) using metawin 2.0 software. the effect sizes (responses) of soil oc, mb, and olsen p were calculated  using a categorical random effects model, where the effect size is weighted by the inverse of the variance.
background: In recent years there has been a renewed interest in using organic amendments (OA) to agricultural soils as partial or full substitutes for inorganic fertilisers (IF) in order to manage nutrients more cost effectively, decrease our dependence on non-renewable resources (for example, P from phosphate rock), reduce and recycle waste that would otherwise be disposed to landfill, and increase soil organic matter.
objective: the present work aims to investigate the effect of oa and oa + if additions on soil nutrient fertility by carrying out a meta-analysis based on results from 132 long-lasting fertility trials (≥ 10 years) worldwide. in this study, the responses of crop yield—along with those of soil organic carbon (oc), size of mb, and plant-available p (i.e., olsen p)—to oa and oa + if relative to if alone (standard control) and no fertilisation (nil control) are determined. here results of the effect of oa and oa + if additions on soil microbial biomass are presented.
result1: the long-term application of oa and oa + mf caused an overall increase in the size of the soil microbial bioass.
result2: oa type had no significant influence on the variability of the mb responses.
general_conclusion: the long-term application of oa and oa + mf caused an overall increase in the size of the soil microbial biomass.

search_strategy: published peer-reviewed journal articles from 1990 to 2016 were identified using isi web of science and the china knowledge resource integrated database, with the keywords ‘‘microbial activity’’, ‘‘enzyme’’, ‘‘fertilisation’’, ‘‘manure’’, or ‘‘straw’’.
selection_criteria: 1)  studies were carried out in the territory of mainland china. six fertilisation practices were primarily focused on, including unbalanced application of one or two types of chemical fertiliser (ucf); balanced chemical fertilisation with n, p and k (cf); straw residue retention combined with the application of chemical fertilisers (cfs); straw residue retention only (s); application of manure and chemical fertilisers (cfm); and manure application only (m). 2) the mean and standard deviation (sd) or standard error (se) of the enzyme activities were provided either as part of the experimental design or in figure captions. 3) if an individual study had more than one treatment type (e.g. inorganic fertiliser, straw residue, manure), measurements from different treatment types were considered as independent observations to evaluate the effects of fertiliser management on soil enzymes; 4) studies were based on field trials, with an experimental duration lasting 3 years as a minimum; 5) studies had clear specifications of the experimental design and a minimum of three replications (or blocks); 6) if results were from multiple soil depths, measurements from the uppermost soil layer (0–100, 0–150, 0–200 and 100–200 mm in 15, 9, 70 and 6% of studies, respectively) were used for comparison; 7) published general methodologies were used to measure enzyme activities; 8) experiments had at least one control (no fertilisation) and one fertilisation treatment.
data_analysis: the variance, weighted response ratio (rr++), standard error of rr++ and 95% confidence interval (ci), were calculated using routine statistical methods. a random-effect-model was applied. in addition, meta-regression analysis was performed using the metafor package to investigate whether the activities of urease, phosphatase, invertase and peroxidase under different fertiliser management practices, were influenced by site-specific factor variables (map, mat, initial soil ph, initial soc and experimental duration).
background: The effects of fertilisation and residue retention practices on enhancing crop yield and soil productivity, have been extensively investigated in various cropping system studies. However, various potential interactions exist among system components (soil, plant, microbial).
objective: using a meta-analysis of 85 peer-reviewed articles published in the past three decades, we synthesized the eeas of four major soil enzymes (urease, phosphatase, invertase, and peroxidase), which are affected by various fertilisation and residue management practices used in cropping systems of china.
result1: regardless of spatial distribution, experimental duration and cropping intensity, all fertilisation treatments had significantly positive effects on the activity of urease, phosphatase and invertase.
result2: straw had significant positive effects on the activity of dehydrogenase, while the other fertilisation treatment had non-significant effects on the activity of dehydrogenase.
result3: straw and convertional fertilisation + straw (cfs) had non-significant effects on the activity of peroxidase.
result4: treatment cfs had significant positive effects on the activity of b-glucosidase (no data for s).
general_conclusion: straw retention had significant positive effects on the activities of urease, phosphatase and invertase enzymes. furthermore, straw residue retention had strong positive effects on the activity of dehydrogenase. it has no effect on peroxidase.
knowledge_gaps: the author mentioned that the analysis largely ignored the interactions with other management-related factors such as irrigation and tillage; larger confidence interval was present due to insufficient data for straw treatment condition and more studies that would incorporate these practices will be needed to draw more precise conclusions.

search_strategy: data were compiled from 156 published experimental studies by extensively searching google scholar, web of science (1900–2017), china knowledge resource integrated database (avail- able online), and baidu scholar.
selection_criteria: 1) the experimental duration and land use were clearly recorded and the measurements of treatment and control groups were conducted within the same temporal and spatial scales; 2) crop residue was added di-rectly to the agroecosystem and paired data (control and treatment) for at least one of the chosen variables was reported; 3) studies with an experimental duration less than one year were excluded to avoid short-term noise; 4) the control and treatment plots started with the same soil type, n fertiliser application rate, climatic conditions, crop species, and other conditions; (5) the primary data—from which means, standard deviations (sd), or standard errors (se), and sample sizes (n) could be calculated—were directly provided or these statistics could be calculated from the results.
data_analysis: the average response ratio was calculated using the mixed model of the meta-analytical software, metawin 2.0. the variance in the mean effect size was calculated using resampling methods. if the 95% ci value of rr++ for a response variable overlapped with zero, the response ratio was not significant. to test the influence of categorical classes, the total heterogeneity among groups (qt) was partitioned into within-group heterogeneity (qw) and between-group heterogeneity (qb).
background: The return of crop residue to the soil has been suggested as a nutrient-conserving practice that effectively increases soil fertility and crop nutrition. However, the overall direction and magnitude of changes in the agroecosystem nitrogen (N) cycle in response to crop residue return are poorly quantified.
objective: the present a global synthesis of the agroecosystem n cycle in response to crop residue return so that the efficacy of this practice for agricultural sustainability can be rigorously evaluated.
result1: across all studies, crop residue returns enhanced the total n pool in microbes by 34.9%.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: crop residue return can improve agricultural soil microbial biomass nitrogen compared to no residue return

search_strategy: the authors searched the institute for scientific information (isi) web of science database for keywords related to ‘bacterial/microbial community,’ ‘bacterial/microbial alpha-diversity,’ and ‘mineral nitrogen/ straw/manure/fertiliser types’ for papers published from january 2008 to february 2020. studies
selection_criteria: studies were selected according to the following criteria: 1) included mineral nitrogen, straw, or manure addition; 2) field trial duration ≥ 1 year; 3) reported bacterial alpha-diversity (shannon or chao1) and/or sensitive bacterial phyla for mineral nitrogen, straw or manure addition and non-fertilized (i.e., control) treatments.
data_analysis: a mixed-effects model was used to determine whether mineral nitrogen, straw, or manure addition significantly affected soil physicochemical properties and soil bacterial alpha-diversity and composition using metawin 2.1. if the 95% confi- dence interval (95% ci) values for effect size did not overlap zero, then the effect of the mineral nitrogen, straw, or manure addition on soil bacterial alpha-diversity and composition was considered significant; otherwise, it was not significant. conventional heterogeneity statistics (q-statistics) were used to test between-group heterogeneity (qm). structural equation modeling (sem) was used to describe the relationship between environmental factors and bacterial alpha-diversity.
background: Different types of fertiliser can significantly change soil fertility. The response of soil bacterial communities to different fertilisation regimes has been studied widely, but the inconsistent results urged us to systematically study the effect of multiple environmental factors on bacterial diversity and composition under different fertilisation regimes.
objective: the study evaluated the 1) general trend in bacterial community diversity under different fertilisation regimes; 2) changes in sensitive bacterial phyla under different fertilisation regimes; 3) factors with the greatest effect on soil bacterial alpha-diversity and phyla under mineral nitrogen, straw, and/or manure addition.
result1: straw addition had a significant negative effect on the overall mean of the shannon index (straw: –11.83%) and the chao1 index (straw: –11.57%).
result2: the shannon and chao1 indices varied with crop type, soil texture, land use type, experimental duration, climate soc, tn, and ph.
result3: straw addition significantly increased proteobacteria (10.58%; p < 0.05), bacteroidetes (15.47%; p < 0.05), gemmatimonadetes (6.10%; p < 0.05), and firmicutes (18.52%; p < 0.05), decreased acidobacteria (–4.90%; p < 0.05), planctomycetes (–8.61%; p < 0.05), and nitrospirae (–23.21%; p < 0.05), and had no effect on actinobacteria (3.93%; p > 0.05) and verrucomicrobia (4.08%; p > 0.05).
general_conclusion: straw retention significantly decreased the shannon and chao indices, while it has no effect on soil microbial biomass carbon.

search_strategy: a search of peer-reviewed articles published from january 1980 to june 2018 was conducted using the isi web of science (http://apps.webofknowledge.com.proxy.insermbiblio.inist.fr/) and china knowledge resource integrated database (http://www.cnki.net/) using “microbial,” “bacteria,” “actinomycete,” “fungi,” or “biological property” and “conservation,” “tillage,” or “till” as search terms.
selection_criteria: (1) paired observations between ct or ct with residue retention (cts) and conservation tillage under field conditions were included in the study. specific practices chosen for comparison were reduced tillage with surface residue removed after crop harvest (rt), no-tillage with surface residue removed after crop harvest (nt), and nt with residue retention (nts). the experiments selected for inclusion in this meta-analysis were established on the same experimental site, i.e., with the same microclimate, vegetation and soil type among the treatments described above. if an individual study used different sampling times at the same site, we used the data collected from the last sampling in a study. if a study used more than one form of conservation tillage practice at the same site, the study separately paired different conservation tillage practices with the ct treatment. (2) included studies had at least three replicates. (3) at least one microbial parameter was reported, such as soil microbial count (bacteria, fungi, and actinomycetes), total microbial biomass [total soil microbial phospholipid fatty acid (plfa) concentrations], or microbial community structure (fungi to bacteria ratio and gram-positive to gram-negative bacteria ratio). the potential response of soil microorganisms varied across depths (joergensen and wichern, 2018), and thus only data from the uppermost 0-10 cm (depending on the study) soil layer were included in this analysis when studies reported data from several soil layers (jian et al., 2016). (4) the main objective of the included studies was to evaluate the effect of conservation tillage practices, with other essential agronomic practices such as crop rotation, study duration, fertiliser management, and irrigation being similar between the paired treatments (i.e., nt, rt, or nts) and control (ct). because available studies did not meet all criteria, the study results of rt with residue retention were excluded.
data_analysis: to derive the overall response effect of the treatment group relative to the control, a weighted effect size (rr++) between the treatment and control was calculated. the 95% confidence interval (ci) was calculated by rr++ ± 1.96 × s(rr++). a random-effects meta-analysis was performed using the restricted maximum likelihood estimator (rmle) estimation. for each parameter (microbial count, diversity, and plfa concentrations), the mean rr++ and its 95% ci were calculated with bias-correction generated via bootstrapping. a chi-square test was used to determine whether the heterogeneity (q) among the weighted effect sizes of changes in the microbial count, diversity, or plfa concentrations under conservation tillage practices significantly exceeded the expected sampling error. publication bias was tested using funnel plots and egger's regression test.
background: Despite the large body of literature on conservation tillage (here defined as no tillage/reduced tillage with/without residue retention), there is an inconsistent understanding of the effects of conservation tillage on the soil microbial community.
objective: the authors conducted a global-scale meta-analysis to address the following objectives: (1) to determine the direction and magnitude of changes in soil microbial count, phospholipid fatty acid (plfa, indicator of microbial biomass) concentration, microbial diversity, and community structure in response to different conservation tillage practices and (2) to evaluate the effect of environmental conditions and experimental duration on those parameters.
result1: the bacterial count was 38% higher in conventional tillage with residue retention (cts) than in conventional tillage (ct) (p < 0.05). the fungal count was 41% higher in cts than in respective treatments without residue retention (p < 0.05). cts increased the actinomycete count by 28% compared to ct (p < 0.05).
result2: no effect of cts vs ct for soil microbial biomass, with the exception of soil biomass of actinomycetes, which was lower in cts compared to ct.
result3: the shannon index for soil fungi community was 13.5% higher (p < 0.05) higher in cts than in ct.
general_conclusion: bacteria, fungi, and actinomycete counts were 38%, 41%, and 28%, respectively, higher in the conventional tillage plus residue retention treatment than in the conventional tillage treatment without residue retention.

search_strategy: we used several databases such as web of science, google scholar, china national knowledge infrastructure database, china wanfang data, current contents connect (isi), academic search complete (ebsco), scopus, and cab abstracts to search peer‐reviewed publi- cations (before august 2018) related to the effects of straw return on various nr losses, crop productivity, and soil c sequestration. the keywords used in the search included “crop straw or crop residue or crop stubble,”“nr losses (nh3 emissions, n2o emissions, n leaching, and runoff), soc content, crop productivities (crop yield, crop n uptake, and n use efficiency (nue)) and/or other soil properties.”
selection_criteria: 1) the control (mineral n fertilisation) and straw treatment (mineral n fertilisation plus straw return) received equal mineral n fertilisation rates, which indicated that the straw treatment provided additional straw n supply to soils; 2) publications needed to report on at least one of the target variables and sample sizes for the con- trol and treatment plots. multiple observations that were conducted at the same experimental site over several sampling years were aver- aged; 3) the observation duration of the experiment must have covered the main discharge period of various nr losses.
data_analysis: mean effect sizes and the 95% confidence intervals (cis) were generated by a bootstrapping procedure with 4,999 iterations, using metawin 2.1. effects of straw return were considered significant if the 95% cis did not overlap with zero. the means of the categorical variables were consid- ered significantly different from each other if their 95% cis did not overlap.
background: It is widely recommended that crop straw be returned to croplands to maintain or increase soil carbon (C) storage in arable soils. However, because C and nitrogen (N) biogeochemical cycles are closely coupled, straw return may also affect soil reactive N (Nr) losses, but these effects remain uncertain, especially in terms of the interac- tions between soil C sequestration and Nr losses under straw addition.
objective: this paper is aimed to: 1) evaluate the overall effects of straw return on various nr loss pathways (nh3 emissions, n2o emissions, n leaching, and runoff), crop productivity and soil c sequestration in agroecosystems under different environ- mental and management conditions (straw quality and quantity, soil properties, agricultural management, and climate conditions); 2) explore the interactions between various nr losses and soc sequestration following straw return; 3) estimate how straw return has affected nr losses from global croplands and the overall cropland nr balance for the period 2005−2015.
result1: the increase in nutrients availability was associated with an increase in microbial biomass c and n (mbc, 37.3%, n = 101; mbn, 38.4%).
result2: straw return significantly increased soil urease activity by 18.5% (n = 133; figure 1), which governs nr loss through nh3 emissions in agricultural soils.
general_conclusion: straw return also significantly increased soil microbial biomass c, soil microbial biomass n and soil urease activity.

search_strategy: published journal articles from 1990 to 2015 were searched using the isi web of science (http://apps.webofknowledge.com/) and china knowledge resource integrated database (http://www.cnki.net/) with search terms of “fertilisation or microbial biomass” and “microbial biomass carbon or microbial biomass nitrogen”.
selection_criteria: to avoid bias in the publication selection process, the following criteria were used: 1. studies were performed in china's farmland soils, involving production of wheat, maize, soybean, and rice. soil cmic and nmic concentrations data were based on the 30-cm top soil (tillage layer). 2. studies were based on field trials and the experimental duration was at least 3 yr (tian et al., 2015). 3. experiments had at least one control (no fertilisation) and a fertilisation treatment. data were obtained from 14 types of inorganic fertiliser, straw, and manure treatments. inorganic fertilisation treatments included inorganic n only (n); n and p (np); n and k (nk); p and k (pk); and n, p, and k (npk). straw treatments included straw return only (s); n plus straw return (ns); n and p plus straw return (nps); and n, p, and k plus straw return (npks). manure treatments included manure only (m); n plus manure (nm); n and p plus manure (npm); n and k plus manure (nkm); and n, p, and k plus manure (npkm).
data_analysis: mean difference for each study was calculated with bias-corrected 95% cis generated by a bootstrapping procedure. a chi-squared test was used to determine whether the heterogeneity among the md of changes to cmic and nmic under fertilisation (qtotal) was significantly larger than the expected sampling error. then, a randomization test was used to determine the significance of the between-group heterogeneity (qb) and to test whether the md of the categories differed between the levels of the factors. chi-squared tests were also used to determine whether the remaining within-group heterogeneity (qw) was significant.
background: Soil microbial biomass (SMB) plays an important role in enhancing soil aggregation, promoting nutrient cycling, and making a substantial contribution to soil organic matter. Little is known about the underlying mechanism and broad-scale responses of SMB to long-term fertilisation practices on a regional scale.
objective: the objective of this study is to characterize changes in smb of predominant cropping systems in china (mainly producing maize [zea mays l.], wheat [triticum aestivum l.], rice [oryza sativa l.], and soybean [glycine max l.]) under different fertilisation regimes using meta-analysis.
result1: application of s had significantly positive effect on microbial carbon concentration and microbial nitrogen concentration.
result2: NA

background: Conservation management practices e including agroforestry, cover cropping, no-till, reduced tillage, and residue return e have been applied for decades to control surface runoff and soil erosion, yet results have not been integrated and evaluated across cropping systems.

selection_criteria: the published papers considered for the current analysis reported on (i) field experiments under natural rainfall conditions at plot scale, (ii) soil and/or soil carbon losses (mass per unit area per unit time), (iii) specific land use or land uses where experimentswere carried out, and (iv) experiments that lasted at least one full rainfall season. in addition, preferred papers were those that published results of experiments carried out in the last 25 years; this choice wasmade to limit the potential impact of climate change on the results. moreover, it was assumed that these reports most likely used closely similar methods for analyses.

background: Corn (Zea mays L.) stover is a global resource used for livestock, fuel, and bioenergy feedstock, but excessive stover removal can decrease soil organic C (SOC) stocks and deteriorate soil health. objective: the objectives were to: (a) assess the overall effects (direction and magnitude) of stover removal on global final experimental soc stocks and accrual rates over time and (b) identify factors driving the observed soc changes.

search_strategy: the data for the present meta-analysis were collected from published peer-reviewed experimental studies that reported changes in soil quality, environmental impacts, and crop production indicators responding to rr compared with residues removed in china's croplands from the web of science (before the year of 2017, http://apps.webofknowledge.com.proxy.insermbiblio.inist.fr/) and the china knowledge resource integrated database (before the year of 2017, http://www.cnki.net/) with the key words of 'residue or straw,' 'retain or retention or return or mulch or incorporation,' and 'china.'

data_analysis: a random-effect meta-analysis was conducted to assess crop residues removal(rr)-induced changes for microbial biomass carbon. the weighted mean effect size (lnr++) and 95% confidence interval were generated by bootstrapping through 4,999 iterations.

search_strategy: data were compiled from 156 published experimental studies by extensively searching google scholar, web of science (1900–2017), china knowledge resource integrated database (avail- able online), and baidu scholar.
selection_criteria: 1) the experimental duration and land use were clearly recorded and the measurements of treatment and control groups were conducted within the same temporal and spatial scales; 2) crop residue was added di-rectly to the agroecosystem and paired data (control and treatment) for at least one of the chosen variables was reported; 3) studies with an experimental duration less than one year were excluded to avoid short-term noise; 4) the control and treatment plots started with the same soil type, n fertiliser application rate, climatic conditions, crop species, and other conditions; (5) the primary data—from which means, standard deviations (sd), or standard errors (se), and sample sizes (n) could be calculated—were directly provided or these statistics could be calculated from the results.
data_analysis: the average response ratio was calculated using the mixed model of the meta-analytical software, metawin 2.0. the variance in the mean effect size was calculated using resampling methods. if the 95% ci value of rr++ for a response variable overlapped with zero, the response ratio was not significant. to test the influence of categorical classes, the total heterogeneity among groups (qt) was partitioned into within-group heterogeneity (qw) and between-group heterogeneity (qb).
background: The return of crop residue to the soil has been suggested as a nutrient-conserving practice that effectively increases soil fertility and crop nutrition. objective: the present a global synthesis of the agroecosystem n cycle in response to crop residue return so that the efficacy of this practice for agricultural sustainability can be rigorously evaluated.

search_strategy: the authors searched the institute for scientific information (isi) web of science database for keywords related to ‘bacterial/microbial community,’ ‘bacterial/microbial alpha-diversity,’ and ‘mineral nitrogen/ straw/manure/fertiliser types’ for papers published from january 2008 to february 2020. studies
