search_strategy: literature was searched using the “web of science” search engine that published before 2021. specifically, we used the “web of science core collection” to search using the keywords “soil carbon” and “soil nitrogen” and “agricultur* or farmland or upland or padd*”.
selection_criteria: i) three ca practices (minimal soil disturbance, crop rotation/diversification, residue return) must be compared with con- trol using conventional tillage; ii) experimentation must have taken place in the field; iii) the experiments on fertiliser inputs need to have the types of nitrogen inputs used well defined (manure, inorganic or mixed); iv) experiments on tillage must have compared tillage operations (no-till, tillage, tillage with residue) and their association with cropping systems must be clear; v) all studies must report both soc and tn content; vi) the control and treatment must be well defined and the number of replications reported.
data_analysis: a random-effect model was used to determine each crop and soil management practice's effect on the initial soc and tn conditions. the effect of treatment on control is considered significant (p < 0.05) only when the 95 % ci value did not overlap with 0. statistical processing of the data through the random effects model was done with metawin. bootstrapping (4999 iterations) was used to obtain 95 % confidence intervals (ci) and between-group variance (qb) of categorical variance.
background: Conservation agriculture (CA) can be an important strategy for improving soil organic carbon (SOC) and total nitrogen (TN). Numerous studies have examined SOC and TN dynamics in different cropping systems. However, there is some uncertainty regarding the relative impacts of some CA practices, and it is not always clear how other agricultural man- agement, particularly nitrogen addition, interacts with these practices to influence SOC and TN sequestration.
objective: the authors hypothesized that (1) ca system and each of its components would increase soc and tn content; (2) the utilization of manure and mineral fertiliser would increase the accumulation the soc and tn compared to no-fertiliser; and (3) crop rotations with legumes and cover crops would decrease in the c/n ratio. the main objectives were to (i) identify the impact of conservation agriculture and its components on soc and tn storage in different environments; (ii) deter- mine the impact of fertilisation and fertiliser type on soc and tn content; (iii) assess the impact of crops systems on the c/n ratio.
result1: residue retention significantly increased tn content at 0–15 and 0–30 cmcompared to no residue retention. the highest increase in tn (27.29 %) was at the depth of 0–30 cm.
result2: residue retention combined with no-tillage resulted in a significant increase (p<0.05) in tn content (24.53%) compared to no residue retention.
result3: in contrast, conventional tillage combined with residue retention caused a smaller increase in tn of 8.22 %.
general_conclusion: residue retention increased soil total nitrogen compared to residue removal.
knowledge_gaps: the adoption and application of conservation agriculture (ca) are difficult in several regions of the world. the primary constraints are the lack of knowledge regarding how best to manage a ca system and the lack of resources and adequate techniques to simultaneously implement all three ca system principles.

search_strategy: to gather relevant articles, journal articles from january 1987 to april 2018 were searched using the isi web of science (http://apps.webofknowledge.com/) and china knowledge resource integrated database (http://www.cnki.net/). specific keywords included: “soil physical properties”, “hydraulic conductivity”, “aggregate”, “available water”, “porosity”, “bulk density” and “conservation practice”, “tillage”, “till”.
selection_criteria: to minimize bias, the following criteria were followed to select and include articles: (1) selected articles included paired observations comparing conventional tillage with (cts) or without residue retention (ct), and a conservation tillage practice based on field experiments. specific conservation tillage practices selected for comparison in this study were reduced tillage with (rts) or without residue retention (rt), and no tillage with (nts) or without residue retention (nt). if a study used more than one conservation tillage practice at the same site, the study separately paired different conservation tillage practices with the ct or cts. additionally, during the selection process, other agronomic practices such as cropping intensity, fertiliser management, study duration, and irrigation had to be similar between paired control (ct, or cts) and treatments (nt, rt, nts, or rts). data_analysis: the mean effect size (lnrr) and its 95% ci were calculated with bias-correction, generated using bootstrapping. a chi-square test determined whether the heterogeneity among the lnrr of changes in soil properties with conservation tillage treatments (qtotal) significantly exceeded the expected sampling error. a randomization test determined the significance of between-group heterogeneity (qb). chi-square tests were also used to determine the statistical significance of the within-group heterogeneity (qw). authors used meta-regression to investigate the linear associations between the response ratios of soil properties to the experiment’s duration. the meta-regression was conducted with the restricted maximum likelihood (rmle) using the knapp and hartung (kh) adjustment. models were compared using the akaike's information criterion (aic). the lowest aic indicated the best-fitting model.
background: There is currently no up-to-date global synthesis of the effects of conservation tillage practices on soil physical properties and soil pH based on a comprehensive dataset.
objective: a global-scale meta-analysis was designed to: 1) determine the direction and magnitude of changes in soil physical properties and soil ph in response to conservation tillage practices and, 2) evaluate the interactive effects of experimental duration and conservation tillage practices on changes in soil physical properties.
result1: soil bulk density decreased by 2.9% with nts practices compared with nt (p < 0.05), and decreased 3.9% with rts practices compared with reduced tillage without residue retention (rt, p < 0.05). similarly, nts decreased penetration resistance by 10.1% (p < 0.05) compared to nt.

search_strategy: the authors searched for peer-reviewed publications investigating the effectiveness of measures to address compacted (sub)soils, using web of science and china knowledge resource integrated database (cnki, for chinese studies not published in english language). search terms were (“soil compaction” or “compacted soil” or “compacted subsoil” or “subsoil compaction”) and (“yield” or “biomass”) and (“density” or “penetration” or “soil cone index”) in titles, keywords, and abstracts.
selection_criteria: in web of science, conference proceedings and non-english publications were excluded. the search process was followed by a screening procedure that was based on the following criteria: 1) field studies must include side by side comparisons of soil compaction prevention, remediation and/or alleviation treatments, and control (or reference) treatments; 2) for each paired comparison, treatments and reference treatments have the same location, cropping system, cropping management, and year; 3) grain yields and/or biomass yields were reported; 4) soil bulk density and/or soil penetration index data were reported; 5) the test crops were cereals, including wheat, maize, barley, oat, and sorghum; 6) location(s), year(s), and basic soil information of the experiment(s) were stated. only studies with cereal crops as test crops were included. one
data_analysis: for the calculation of a grouped effect size, a linear mixed-effect model was used for which we used the r-package ‘nlme’. results of treatments addressing soil compaction were set as fixed effects and study numbers were set as random effects, to allow accounting for variances among studies. we used the equal weighting method (e.g., [35]) when comparing studies with different number of replicates.
background: The compaction of subsoils in agriculture is a threat to soil functioning. Measures aimed at the prevention, amelioration, and/or impact alleviation of compacted subsoils have been studied for more than a century, but less in smallholder agriculture.
objective: 1) to quantitatively examine the effects of measures aimed at avoiding and ameliorating soil compaction and at alleviating the impacts of compacted subsoils on crop yield, soil bulk density, and soil penetration resistance, using results of published studies; 2) to examine the effectiveness of measures in smallholder and mechanized agriculture.

general_conclusion: residue return decreased soil bulk density and soil penetration resistance.

search_strategy: all published peer-reviewed scientific journal articles on the water use of winter wheat-summer maize cropping systems were collected from the china national knowledge infrastructure (1979–2019) and web of science (1979 – 2019). different combinations of search terms that included “north china plain” or “huang-huai-hai plain” and “winter wheat” or “summer maize” or “summer corn” and “crop product*” or “yield” or “output” were used for the selection of published studies.
selection_criteria: (i) the research object must be field experiments conducted in the ncp, excluding pot and laboratory experiments and model simulations; (ii) the cropping system must be the winter wheat-summer maize cropping sys- tem; (iii) the studies must be about one or more of the four leading management practices (e.g., no nitrogen versus nitrogen input, no irrigation versus irrigation, rotary tillage versus other tillage methods, and straw removal versus straw return, with the former as the control and the later as the treatment); and (iv) the data must include the number of trial replications, crop yield, wue, or seasonal crop evapotranspiration (etc). the studies that met the criteria and could be used for meta- analysis are shown in the meta-analysis references.

search_strategy: the authors conducted a review of peer-reviewed scientific journal articles on water productivity in maize production published from january 2000 to march 2018 using the china national knowledge infrastructure and web of science databases. the different combinations of search terms included “irrigation” and “maize” or “corn” and “yield” and “water use efficiency” or “water productivity” and “china” were used for article selection.
selection_criteria: (1) all data were from field experiments, so laboratory experiments, pot experiments, experiments under rain-proof shelter conditions, and model simulations were excluded; (2) data were required to include maize yield, seasonal water supply and wp in the maize growth period.
data_analysis: the authors used a linear mixed-effects model with yield (ln-transformed), water supply (ln-transformed), and water productivity (wp) (ln-transformed) as response variables and experimental year (continuous, transformed), study agro-ecological zones (categorical, three levels), maize cultivars (categorical), seasonal average temperature (st) (continuous, ln-transformed), seasonal average precipitation (sp) (continuous, ln-transformed), seasonal irrigation depth (continuous, ln-transformed),  vapor pressure deficit (vpd) (continuous, ln-transformed), seasonal n application amount (continuous, ln-transformed), soil organic matter (som) (continuous, ln-transformed), latitude (continuous, ln-transformed) and plant density (continuous, ln-transformed) at the study locations as independent variables. the authors included interaction terms for some factors (sp * irrigation depth) in the model. finally, they included a random intercept term for the experimental sites of studies data from previous studies (i.e., chinese provinces). to identify effective crop management practices for improving maize wp and yield, authors pooled studies that included side-by-side comparisons of different crop management practices (i.e., the treatment was the same as the control in all aspects except for the each crop management practice) and calculated effect sizes for pairwise comparisons: optimal irrigation vs. farmer’ irrigation; plastic mulch vs. no mulch; straw re-incorporation vs. no straw re-incorporation; deep tillage/deep ripping vs. rotary tillage; no tillage vs. rotary tillage; ridge planting vs. flat planting; and polymer application vs. no polymer application.

search_strategy: experimental research papers were identified via a search for field-based reports on the effects ofcrop residue return on crop yields and wue that were published prior to 2018. chinese and english databases were used, including the china knowledge network, weipu, wanfang, web ofscience, springer, engineering village, and google scholar. the keywords included “straw”, “mulching”, “residue”, and “yield”.
selection_criteria: the studies were selected using the following criteria: 1) the experiment must have been conducted in the field; 2) the experimental duration must have been >= 2 years; 3) there were >= 3 replicates; 4) the test site and year were clearly identified; 5) the test treatments included both crop residue return and no return; 6) in cases where many years of production data were included, only the most recent year was used.
data_analysis: meta-analysis was performed using metawin 2.1 software. the mean effect sizes were evaluated with a random-effects model. the 95% ci for each mean effect size was estimated by applying bootstrapping with 4999 iterations. mean effect sizes were considered significantly different when the 95% cis did not overlap, and the gaussian distribution lines were made using origin 8.5 software. the images were processed using graphpad prim 6.0 software.
background: Although there has been extensive research on the effects of crop residue return, the results are inconsis- tent or contradictory because of differences in soil conditions, planting systems, and climatic conditions.
objective: the authors conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate the impacts of crop residue return on crop yields and wue relative to those of crops grown without crop residue treatment (referred to here as no-straw).
result1: crop residue return significantly increased wue for corn (13.7%), and wheat (13.2%) com- pared to no-straw (p < 0.05). in contrast, no difference in wue was recorded between crop residue return and no-straw treatments for the different tillage types, fertiliser types, experimental durations, or depths of tillage.
result2: the effect ofcrop residue return on wue was significantly affected by the amount ofn fertiliser, soil organic matter, cropping system, mean annual temperature, and irrigation conditions.
result3: the greatest magnitudes of increase in wue associated with crop residue return were associated with corn (yield increase = 13.7%), medium nitrogen content (100–150 kg ha-1; 23.3%), high soil organic matter (> 15 g kg-1; 25.5%) and low air tempera- tures (< 10 ˚c; 19.9%).
general_conclusion: the meta-analysis showed that water use efficiency was increased when crop residue return was used, compared to no-straw treatment.

search_strategy: authors performed a search of web of science (v.5.16) on 28 october 2014 using the search terms (crop* rotation or crop* system or agroecosystem) and (soil carbon or soil organic matter) and (long-term or field) not (greenhouse or pot).
selection_criteria: criteria for inclusion were at least two levels of crop species diversity (e.g., one and two species or two and four species), or at least two levels of functional group diversity (e.g., cereals and cereals + perennial crop). all crop rotations included at least one grain crop; agroforestry and pasture systems were beyond the scope of the study.
data_analysis: authors explored the response of soc to species and functional group diversity by calculating an effect size using the log transformed response ratio of treatment to control. authors performed an unweighted metaanalysis, in which the variance assigned to all response ratios was 1. around the mean effect size for each control–treatment comparison, we created bias-corrected bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals with 5,000 iterations using metawin software version 2.0. authors used multiple linear regression to explore whether the effect of crop rotation diversity on soc was mediated by site-specific environmental factors. forward selection was used for  independent variable. site was used as a random effect. authors ran the mixed effects model using the lmer function in the r package lme4. models were compared using akaike information criterion (aic) values.
background: More diverse crop rotations have been promoted for their potential to remediate the range of ecosystem services compromised by biologically simplified grain-based agroecosystems, including increasing soil organic carbon (SOC).
objective: authors conducted a meta-analysis of crop rotation experiments to test the hypothesis that increasing diversity in grain-based cropping systems is more likely to increase soc if it includes crop functional groups that increase c input.
result1: relative to crop rotations of only grains, perennial cropped rotations increased soc concentrations by 6.2%
result2: within grain-only rotations including a legume grain in rotation with cereal grains decreased soc concentrations by 5.3% compared to rotations of only cereal grains
result3: increasing the species diversity of grain-only rotations without adding perennial crops or cover crops had no detectable effect on soc concentrations.
general_conclusion: more diverse crop rotations have the potential to provide a broad suite of ecosystem services compared to biologically simplified grain-based agroecosystems, including increasing soc. however, increasing the species diversity of grain-only rotations without adding perennial crops or cover crops had no detectable effect on soc concentrations.
knowledge_gaps: few cropping system sites testing the typologies of crop rotations- cover cropped and perennial cropped- able to provide some of the greatest environmental benefits in terms of soc storage. studies exploring the role that legume n fixation may play in mediating the effect of crop functional diversity on soc. studies using species-specific plant traits, including tissue biochemistry, in order to identify the features of crop rotation functional diversity most effective for increasing soc.

search_strategy: the method of data collection and meta-analysis followed was that of bai et al. (doi: 10. 1016/j. agee. 2018. 05. 028). briefly, we performed literature review using web-based research engines including web of science and google scholar. key search terms included soil organic matter, nmr spectroscopy, and various agricultural managements (i.e., fertilizers, manure, compost, grazing, tillage, crop rotation, and liming).
selection_criteria: authors collected a total of pairwise data from articles on the effect of agricultural management practices on the distribution of c functional groups measured by solid-state 13c nmr spectroscopy published from 1995 to 2020 worldwide
data_analysis: a meta-analysis was conducted to quantify the effect of each agricultural management practice on the distribution of the c functional groups. statistical analyses were performed using sas version 9.4. medians, first quartile (q1), third quartile (q3), and standard deviation (sd) were computed by the proc means procedure, and least square means, standard error, and coefficient were computed by the proc mixed procedure. tukey’s studentized range test was used for multiple comparisons of the effects of temporal period (i.e., long-term repeated annual applications > 10 years, vs. short-term repeated annual applications < 10 years). a type i error rate of p = 0.05 was used for all statistical tests. all data used in the study were the mean values where n > 3.
background: To improve soil health and to aid in climate change mitigation, the quantity of soil organic matter (SOM) should be maintained or increased over the long run. In doing so, not only the total quantity of SOC but also the stability of SOC must be considered.
objective: to better understand and quantify how these changes are influenced by agricultural management practices, we collected 670 pairwise data from the body of literature that has evaluated changes in the distribution of c functional groups of som measured by solid-state 13c nmr spectroscopy.
result1: crop rotation positively affected aromatic and carbonyl groups and negatively affected the alkyl groups the the a/o, and a/aroma ratios
result2: NA
general_conclusion: crop rotations, especially legume-based rotations, were found to increase soc stability (the proportion of aromatic groups in som).
knowledge_gaps: only limited research data are available on the impact of rotation on the distribution of the c functional groups of som. other influencing factors in combination with agricultural management practices should be further explored (e.g., soil types, soil ph ).

search_strategy: authors initially searched the literature in 2012 using isi web of knowledge v.5.6 (available online).2 the initial search terms were ‘‘crop’’ and ‘‘soil,’’ which were subsequently refined by ‘‘rotation’’ and ‘‘continuous’. authors expanded the search by checking the reference and citation lists of studies that met our basic criteria.
selection_criteria: authors selected only studies that included a monoculture treatment, were in place for a minimum of three years, and reported the effects of crop rotations on total soil c or n, microbial biomass c or n, or a combination of these variables. studies that included a fallow period in rotation, characterized by no crop production and frequently intensive tillage or herbicide use to control weeds, were excluded from our analysis because of the wide variation in specific fallow management practices. authors included both field and vegetable crops in our analysis.
data_analysis: log response ratio (lnr) represents the influence of adding one or more crops to a monoculture crop. authors used metawin v.2.1 to calculate r and 95% bias-corrected confidence intervals (ci) with 9999 iterations. authors used funnel plots to determine that there was no evidence of publication bias and used an unweighted metaanalysis where all studies had a variance equal to 1. moderating variables were analyzed using metawin v.2.1 in a procedure similar to anova. total group heterogeneity (qt) was partitioned into within-group (qw) and between-group (qb) heterogeneity, similar to partitioning variation in an anova.
background: Reductions in the number of crops in rotation or the replacement of rotations by monocultures are responsible for the loss of biodiversity. The belowground implications of simplifying agricultural plant communities remain unresolved; however, agroecosystem sustainability will be severely compromised if reductions in biodiversity reduce soil C and N concentrations, alter microbial communities, and degrade soil ecosystem functions as reported in natural communities.
objective: autohrs conducted a meta-analysis to examine crop rotation effects on total soil c and n concentrations, and the faster cycling microbial biomass c and n pools that play key roles in soil nutrient cycling and physical processes such as aggregate formation.
result1: rotation increased tc by 3.6%. however, rotations without cover crops did not significantly influence tc.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: crop rotations sustain soil quality and productivity by enhancing soil c and n. however, the increase in soil c under rotations found in this study seems to be driven largely by the inclusion of a cover crop

search_strategy: experiments from the published literature that recorded response of soc to changes in tillage or crop rotation, and that were greater than 5 yr in duration, were used in this study.
selection_criteria: long-term experiments in the published literature that recorded the response of soc to changes in agricultural management.
data_analysis: a paired t-test, using minitab v. 12.23 (minitab, 1999), was used on all groups of paired treatments to determine whether the new management scenario was significantly different than the baseline scenario.
background: Changes in agricultural management can potentially increase the accumulation rate of soil organic C (SOC), thereby sequestering CO2 from the atmosphere.
objective: this study was conducted to quantify potential soil c sequestration rates for different crops in response to decreasing tillage intensity or enhancing rotation complexity, and to estimate the duration of time over which sequestration may occur.
result1: changing from continuous corn to a corn–soybean rotation did not result in increased c sequestration.
result2: an analysis of all corn rotation enhancements, not including corn to corn–soybean rotations resulted in a mean c sequestration rate of 19+-11 g c m-2 yr-1
result3: rotating wheat with one or more different crops increased c sequestration (51 +- 47 g c m-2 yr-1)
general_conclusion: enhancing rotation complexity can increase mean c sequestration rate

search_strategy:
information about the effects of cropping systems and associated management practices (cropping system, intensity of tillage, fertilizer inputs, and rotation length) on soil organic matter
or soc was collected from peer-reviewed articles published between january of 1990 and january of 2011. searches were conducted using electronic databases, primarily using the thomas reuters web of science database (thomas reuters, philadelphia, pennsylvania) and by reviewing the reference sections of peer-reviewed publications of lead authors known to study soil organic matter in relationship to soil management. in a meta-analysis
selection_criteria: only articles that report results from field-based studies or on-farm research conducted in the continental united states were considered.
data_analysis: for analyses, we used meta-analytic methods outlined by gurevitch and hedges (1993). the effect sizes were calculated as the response ratio.  since the great majority of data presented in the articles selected did not provide information about variability, we performed an unweighted analysis using the statistical software metawin specifically developed for meta-analysis of ecological data (rosenberg et al. 2000). bootstrapping and permutation methods were further used to generate 95% confidence intervals and significance levels of test results.
background: Increased understanding of the influences of management practices on soil properties and associated ecosystem function is needed to improve tools used to administer conservation programs in the United States.
objective: this study used meta-analysis to assess the influence of management practices (nitrogen fertility and rotation length) on soil organic carbon (soc).
result1: across depths, the response ratios for the 2-year rotations were either close to 1 or their confidence intervals overlapped 1, indicating that this specific rotation does not contribute to soc accumulation more than the 1-year rotation.
result2: use of ≥3-year rotations contributed to increases in soc of 25%, 7%, 8%, and 14% in comparisons across the four sampling depths (0-10, 0-15, 0-20, 0-30).
general_conclusion: comparison of rotation length showed cropping systems with rotations of 3 years or longer were better able to increase soc than shorter rotations, whereas 2-year rotations  specific rotation does not contribute to soc accumulation more than the 1-year rotation.
knowledge_gaps: gaps in the peer-reviewed literature and limited detail provided about agronomic practices applied in the field greatly limit the use of a wider data set in meta-analysis. specifics on management practices being investigated must detail types of equipment used, timing of practice or amendment application, and rates of input application. note that additional detail about the statistical design and reports on measures of variability are necessary for a more effective use of meta-analytic techniques on agricultural management literature

search_strategy: results from published long-term research trials, non peer-reviewed reports and by inquiring at universities and governmental research institutions were amalga mated to review the effect of land use management on soc in ontario.
selection_criteria: criteria: the research experiments were longterm trials (10 yr) that were maintained with consistent treatments as well as recently established trials expected to have a long-term duration. long-term crop cultivar or watershed experiments were excluded.
data_analysis: a meta-analysis was conducted to accumulate knowledge across studies. each paired data point was presented as soc on an area basis, and the change in soc due to the treatment was calculated as a net change, relative change (%), and rate of change. the variations associated with the un-weighted means indicated if the treatment effect on soc was significant (i.e., if the mean9standard error overlapped with zero, then the treatment was not significant). also within each dataset, a proc mixed means comparison (lsd test) with the fixed effect of site was applied to test for site variation and significant differences set at alpha <=0.05.
background: Soil organic carbon (SOC) is crucial for maintaining a productive agro-ecosystem. Long-term research must be synthesized to understand the effects of land management on SOC storage and to develop best practices to prevent soil degradation.
objective: authors conducted a meta-analysis of long-term ontario studies to assess soc storage under common ontario land management regimes.
result1: the meta-analysis showed a positive but not significant effect of rotational cropping on soc compared with continuous corn.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: our review of long-term agricultural management effects on soc in ontario indicated trends towards, but not significant increase in, higher soc with crop rotation than continuous corn.
knowledge_gaps: carbon contribution from roots due to total root biomass and rhizodeposition is not well known for many crops and warrants future research

search_strategy: a synthesis was performed based on published data (1980–2018) collected from the web of science (http://apps.webofknowledge.com/) and the china knowledge resource integrated database (http://www.cnki.net/), using “crop rotation,” “cropping system,” and “yield” as keywords.
selection_criteria: to be included, an experiment had to meet the following criteria 1) it was performed under field conditions in china and treatments were randomized with replications; 2) the succeeding crop was a field crop; 3) means and standard deviations were provided or could be calculated; 4) a continuous monoculture control and at least one rotation treatment were included; 5) the preceding and succeeding crop species were identified; and 6) treatments differed only in rotation and monoculture crop management. we also excluded multiple publications reporting on the same trials to avoid duplication.
data_analysis: mean effect sizes and 95% cis were determined by building random-effect models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation (rmle) in openmee. moderator analyses were performed only when there were at least two levels with large enough sample sizes. the rmle method was used to estimate between-group heterogeneity (qb) and the i2 index.
background: Crop rotation has been widely used to mitigate weed, insect, and pathogen pressure, as well as to increase plant diversity. However, the magnitude of and variability in crop yield with rotation in China remain uncertain.
objective: we conducted a meta-analysis to examine the effects of crop rotation on yield and to explore the importance of environmental factors and field management in determining yield variability.
result1: rotation increased crop yield by 20.1 ± 3.5% compared to continuous monoculture yields (p < 0.001)
result2: NA
general_conclusion: rotation increased crop yields by 20.1 ± 3.5% when compared with continuous monoculture practices across china. the benefits are highly context dependent.
knowledge_gaps: a topic that needs further research is the effect of soil water availability and crop water management on subsequent crop yield. moreover, more efforts are needed to quantify the magnitude of rotation effects at a large-scale by using remote sensing technology or to illustrate the mechanism of rotation effects at a micro-scale using next-generation sequencing techniques. crop growth simulation models can be applied to local rotation systems to maximize our understanding of the agronomic and environmental benefits.

search_strategy: a scientific screening of research literature on web of science and google was performed to select research papers that reported canola crop water, nutrient, planting date, planting depth, seeding rate, tillage, residue management, and rotation effects one at a time. in addition, unpublished data available to us were included.
selection_criteria: the main criteria for inclusion of a publication were mainly availability of canola yield information and north american geographical location. availability of yield data “with” and “without” the management factor was among selection criterion.
data_analysis: the effect size of rotation over continuous cropping (rotation vs. monocrop) was analyzed via utilization of a fixed-effect analysis. a forest plot was used to summarize the effect of each component evaluated.
background: Canola (Brassica napus L. cv. ‘Canola’) production has both economic and agronomic advantages. The mechanism of how multiple factors interact to influence canola yield and the level of their significance has been rarely reported.
objective: the objective of this study was to quantify the impact of continuous wheat or canola production compared with canola–wheat rotation on the yields of the two crops.
result1: crop rotation compared to continuous cropping resulted in increased yield (mean difference = 0.36; 95% ci: 0.06 - 0.68).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: this review suggests that diversifying rotation (canola every 3 or 4 yr) is a best management practice to increase yields.
knowledge_gaps: only limited research data are available on the impact of rotation of canola with summer crops such as corn, soybean, and sorghum. for regions such as the us great plains, where a summer crop–wheat rotation is dominant, the impact of including canola in rotation remains a research gap.

search_strategy: an extensive literature search was performed using web of science with the search terms “soil n mineralization or potentially mineralizable nitrogen not forest not tree” which resulted in 6665 studies published before the cut-off date of 1 july 2014. a search was also performed using google scholar, but no additional studies were found relevant to our analysis
selection_criteria: exclusion criteria: studies that were not relevant in the context of this paper or were not found to include sufficient information regarding soil, crop management, or crops. conference abstracts and studies not providing quantitative results were also rejected.
data_analysis: the effect size was expressed as a response ratio (rr), natural log transformed for normality. authors applied weights using the reported number of replications. the homogeneity among lrr values from all the studies was analyzed. the data were analyzed for outliers by plotting each observation against the natural log of the response ratio and a box plot. weighted analysis of variance was used to compare mean response ratio for different management practices and treatments. a meta-regression analysis was performed to analyze data for the effect of continuous variables such as the duration of the management practice and the soil depth. all statistical analyses were conducted with r (version 3.4.2). significant difference between treatments was considered if p values < 0.05. bootstrapping procedures were used to generate 95% confidence intervals for weighted mean effect sizes using 500 iterations.
background: In fertile soils with high soil organic matter (SOM) content, the mineralization of SOM nitrogen (SOM-N) is a major source of N for crop uptake and has been positively associated with crop yield. As a result, researchers have suggested that knowledge about the fraction of SOM-N susceptible to mineralization may help to optimize N fertilizer management. This fraction of SOM-N, commonly referred to as potentially mineralizable nitrogen (PMN). However, the effect size and relationship with crop yield across specific management practices remain uncertain.
objective: authors conducted a quantitative review to understand how conservation agriculture management practices affect pmn
result1: crop rotation had no effect on crop yield when high diversity cropping systems were compared to less diverse systems (rr= 1.07, ci= 0.88 - 1.35)
result2: NA
general_conclusion: crop rotation had no effect on crop yield

search_strategy: authors conducted a comprehensive literature search from the internet database of the web of knowledge and scholar google search (http://scholar.google.ca/) with ―maize/corn-legume rotation‖ entered as keywords, and performed a meta-analysis.
selection_criteria: the criterion for including an article in the meta-analysis database was whether it contained detailed data on maize yield, comparing maize-grain legume rotation (mainly including maize-soybean/cowpea rotation and maize-alfalfa/green manure rotation) with cc from field experiments, which had been conducted in an acceptable scientific manner.
data_analysis: the meta-analysis was conducted using a meta-analytical software package (metawin 2.1, sinauer associates, inc., sunderland, ma, usa). to estimate the maize-legume rotation (mlr) effect compared with continious cropping cc in term of maize yield, the natural log of the response ratio (r = variable in mlr/cc) was used as the metric for analysis, and it is reported as the percentage changes from control as (r-1) * 100%. a positive percentage change indicates a yield increase from the mlr treatment compared with the yield from cc, while a negative value indicates a yield reduction due to mlr. this meta-analysis used an un-weighted approach in which the variance of the effect size was calculated using resampling techniques after 9999 iterations. confidence limits around the effect size were calculated using a bias method.
background: Legume-cereal rotation systems not only maximize cereal and legume productivity, but also optimize agricultural sustainability across a far more complex landscape of production, which has recently caused unprecedented changes in our environment. Thus, this practice has been regarded as a promising strategy for reducing GHG emissions, and thus lowering the negative environmental impact.
objective: the study focuses on the rationale and assessment methodology of a maize-legume rotation system. it highlights the main advantages of maize-legume rotation with special emphasis on the superiority of maize yield; the suppression of pests, diseases and weeds; and the potential benefits to the environment.
result1: compared with continuos cropping, maize yield in the maize-grain legume (including soybean) rotation (mglr) significantly increased by 28.7% with ci of 22.1-35.6%.
result2: overall, maize-legume rotation (mlr) significantly increased the maize yield by 9.6% compared with cc, with 95% confidence intervals (ci) of 5.9% to 12.6% . on average, maize yield in the msr rotation system was 9.6 t ha-1, compared to 8.8 t ha-1 in the cc system.
general_conclusion: maize, grown in rotation with legume crops, such as alfalfa or soybean, yields more than continuous monoculture. maize, grown in rotation with soybean, yields more than continuous monoculture.

search_strategy: an exhaustive literature search of studies investigating n2o emissions from grain cropping systems was conducted with isi-web of science for articles published before june 2014. because the first search produced a limited numbers of papers for enhanced efficiency fertilizers, cover crops and diversified rotations, we conducted a second search focusing on these practices in december 2015 to increase the size of the database and enable meta-analysis of these practices.
selection_criteria: only studies conducted in field conditions that were at least one growing season in durationwere included.
data_analysis:
the effect size for each control–treatment pair was estimated using the response ratio (r = xt/xc), where xt is the mean n2o emission from the treatment, and xc is the mean n2o emission from the control. to perform meta-analysis, the natural logarithm of response ratio (lrr) was used to normalize data distribution. authors performed an unweighted meta-analysis because
roughly more than half of the studies did not report a measure of variance. bias-corrected 95% confidence intervals (95% cis) were generated through a bootstrapping procedure in metawin 2.0 (5000 iterations). for groups with <10 observation pairs, authors used 95% cis.
background: Understanding how agricultural management practices impact nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions is prerequisite for developing mitigation protocols.
objective: authors conducted a meta-analysis to assess how management affects n2o emissions.
result1: authors found no detectable effect of diversifying rotations on n2o emissions, possibly because the ‘‘diverse’’ rotations usually consisted of only two alternating crops.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: diversifying rotations did not affect n2o emissions.
knowledge_gaps:
the complexity of n2o production processes requires that cross-scale and interdisciplinary studies are conducted in order to fully understand how to best reduce these emissions from food production systems. studies providing life cycle analysis. the role of soil microbial community composition in mitigating n2o emissions. temporal dynamics of n cycling and n2o emissions
also need more attention. studies investigating interactions between different management practices.

search_strategy: relevant studies on n2o emissions in corn cropping systems in the midwestern u.s. and south-east canada were identified through a literature search in march 2012 using the web of science (keywords ‘n2o’ and ‘corn’ or ‘maize’), and through personal communications with researchers in the field.
selection_criteria: n2o emissions had to represent at least a full growing season, covering emissions across furrows and seedbeds, and capturing anticipated n2o emissions peaks after tillage, fertilization and wetting. (22) only data from field experiments was included. in addition to growing-season or annual n2o emissions (in kg n2o–n ha–1 yr–1) for each of the field-treatment-year combinations in each study, data for a suite of ancillary variables pertaining to management practices and environmental characteristics were recorded.
data_analysis: heterogeneity and publication bias were evaluated, fixed versus random effects models were tested, effect sizes were weighted by the pooled variance or the number of observations per study, and parametric versus nonparametric confidence intervals were constructed. the final results selected for presentation in this paper are conservative and based on a random effects meta-analytic model, using the pooled variance as a weighting function, and with 95% confidence intervals that are generated nonparametrically by bootstrapping (1000 iterations)
background: One of the unintended nitrogen (N)-loss pathways from cropland is the emission of nitrous oxide (N2O), a potent greenhouse gas and ozone depleting substance.
objective: the objective of the current study is to expose data availability and quantitatively summarize effects of a suite of agronomic management practices on n2o emissions in corn cropping systems in the midwestern u.s. and south-east canada through meta-analysis. corn is selected as a focus crop, because it covers the greatest proportion of u.s. cropland and receives more n than any other u.s. crop.
result1: crop rotation (i.e rotation with soybean) had no effect on fie and n2o emissions
result2: for 4 out of 17 side-by-side comparisons included in this meta-analysis (two out of five studies), a n-credit from the soybean crop was taken into account, and n-rates were higher for the continuous corn systems compared to the corn years of the corn-soybean rotations. the n-rate was fixed for the other side-by-side comparisons.
result3: therefore, the selection of n-rates for comparing the performance of continuous corn versus corn-soybean rotations might have confounded the results and complicates the interpretation and applicability of findings from the present study.
general_conclusion: crop rotation (i.e rotation corn with soybean) had no effect on fie and n2o emissions

search_strategy: data on gwp and ghgi were pulled from the available literature from 57 experiments and 225 treatments from national and international regions and grouped by individual and combined management practices that included tillage, cropping systems, and n fertilization rates using all available resources (e.g.web of science, goggle scholar, scopus, etc.).
selection_criteria:
1. all experiments should be conducted in croplands in the field. croplands included both  uplands and lowlands under all agricultural irrigated and dryland crops. number of crops grown in a year should be two or less. data on gwp and ghgi estimated by models were excluded for analysis. 2. treatments in the experiments should be replicated, randomized, and arranged in a proper experimental design. 3. for gwp and ghgi calculated by using the soc method, soil c sequestration should have occur to a depth of 20 cm from the initiation of the experiment to the end of ghg measurement period. in the soil respiration method, experiments should have started in the previous year where the amount of crop residue returned to the soil was known. 4. measurement of ghg emissions should occur at regular events. 5. a time horizon of 100 yr should be used to calculate the co2 equivalents of n2o and ch4 emissions. 6. carbon dioxide emissions associated with use of farm equipment for irrigation, tillage, fertilization, planting, herbicide and pesticide application, and harvest as well as manufacture and application of fertilizers and other chemical inputs should be either calculated based on the number of hours the equipment were used multiplied by co2 emissions per liter of fuel
or estimated as shown by various researchers. 7. for comparing the effects of individual and combined management practices on gwp and ghgi, the soc method was used to calculate these parameters.
data_analysis: a paired t-test was used for data analysis to compare the effects of individual and combined treatments of improved vs. traditional management practices on gwp and ghgi by evaluating significant difference between practices. regression analysis was used to relate changes in gwp and ghgi due to improved vs. conventional management with duration of the experiment to examine if the changes vary with time. multiple linear regressions were conducted to include soil and climatic factors in these analyses to determine if the relationships can be improved.
background: Management practices, such as tillage, crop rotation, and N fertilization, may affect net global warming potential (GWP) and greenhouse gas intensity (GHGI), but their global impact on cropland soils under different soil and climatic conditions need further evaluation.
objective: available global data were evaluated for individual and combined effects of tillage, cropping systems, and n fertilization rates on gwp and ghgi which accounted for co2 equivalents from n2o and ch4 emissions with or without equivalents from soil c sequestration rate (δsoc), farm operations, and n fertilization.
result1: crop rotation increased gwp by 46% and ghgi by 41% compared with monocropping (full dataset). this was especially true for large grain crops, such as corn (zea mays l.) and soybean (glycine max l.), where gwp and ghgi were 215 and 325%, respectively, greater under corn-soybean than continuous corn.
result2: in contrast, for small grain crops, such as barley (hordeum vulgare l.) and pea (pisum sativum l.), gwp was 22% lower under barley-pea than continuous barley.
general_conclusion: analysis of available global data revealed that improved management practices, such as diversified cropping systems can reduce gwp and ghgi compared with traditional management practices (less diversified cropping system) for specific crop rotations.

search_strategy:
authors conducted a systematic search of relevant literature using isi web of knowledge (wos, available online). a search was conducted in january 2018, using the following boolean string:
("crop rotation*" or "crop sequence*" or "multiple cropping*" or “organic”) and (management* or control*) and ("weed biomass*" or "weed density*" or "weed seed bank*") not (orchard* or vineyard* or agroforestry*). an additional 10 records came from the authors’ collections of relevant literature.
selection_criteria: criteria: (a) articles were published in peer-reviewed journals (as opposed to book chapters or conference abstracts), (b) articles were based on studies conducted with structured experimental designs in a field setting, (c) articles reported one or both of the following response variables: weed biomass and weed density, (d) studies included a simplified rotation (control) and a diversified rotation (treatment).
data_analysis: all data manipulation, analysis and graphics were completed with the r (version 3.5.1). to identify the factors with the strongest effects on weed density, we fit a generalized boosted regression tree (brt) model with the nine modifiers as predictors using the r package gbm and caret for model tuning. to estimate effect sizes, authors took the natural log of the response ratio and fit a linear mixed model in r using the lme4 package, with study as a random effect and weighting. to evaluate the effect of moderators identified as important by the brt, mixed-effect models were fit for responses using each moderator as a single fixed effect, study as a random effect, and non-parametric weighting
background: Diversifying crop rotations through addition of crop species and their associated managements may suppress weeds and reduce selection pressure for herbicide resistance by altering stress and mortality factors affecting weed dynamics.
objective: autohrs conducted a meta-analysis from 54 studies across six continents to compare weed responses due to simple and more diverse crop rotations.
result1: diversification of crop rotations significantly reduced weed density compared to simple rotations, with a mean reduction of 49% (p < 0.001).
result2: the effect of diversification on weed biomass was weaker (-21%) and non-significant (p = 0.22)
general_conclusion: diverse rotations are more effective in suppressing weeds relative to simpler ones.
knowledge_gaps: additional studies measuring the effects of crop rotational diversity on weed biomass are needed.

search_strategy:
the literature was searched using electronic databases, including google scholar, agris, sciencedirect, elsevier and wiley by entering the following search terms used in various combinations:
crop rotation, microbial diversity, microbial richness. the boolean operators ‘and’ and ‘or’ were used to combine two separate searches and include alternative search terms. in addition, studies were also identified through a ‘snowballing’ technique where reference lists of acquired studies were searched for additional relevant studies.
selection_criteria: criteria: (1) only peer reviewed articles in journals; and (2) studies with sufficient sample size to determine both a mean and standard error. studies were excluded because they did not (1) contain the control, experimental treatment/s and diversity measures as listed above, (2) contain purely agricultural cash crops, or (3) metadata was not available upon request.
data_analysis: meta-analysis calculates the weighted average of a number of study results, and different models have been developed to assign individual study weights based on sample size, variance and other criteria related to study bias. the effect size estimate used was the weighted mean difference (wmd). within metaxl, the quality effects model was used with effect size estimates weighted by variance, at 95% confidence intervals, as well as a quality score. the distribution of studies within the funnel plots were assessed to see if there is a ‘gap’ in the area of non-significance
background: Agricultural intensification can involve the simplification of agroecosystems to crop monocultures while the practices of crop rotation, intercropping and companion planting maintain some crop diversity over time and space. It is generally postulated that reduced diversity can have an impact on ecosystem function.
objective: authors determine whether decreased aboveground crop diversity affects belowground microbial biodiversity by conducting a meta-analysis of studies comparing monocultures and crop rotations.
result1: the meta-analysis revealed that increasing crop diversity increased soil microbial shannon’s diversity index and richness on average by 3.36% and 15.11%, respectivelly (p < 0.05)
result2: NA
general_conclusion: the adoption of crop rotation as a management practice is beneficial for soil microbial diversity
knowledge_gaps:
future research on the link between above and belowground diversity would do well to measure the associated effects on components of agroecosystem function (e.g. soil n fertility) as well
as the spatial and temporal changes therein. in addition, the use of next generation sequencing techniques can aid in understanding the role of specific functional groups in the yield increase of crop rotation systems.

search_strategy: authors conducted a literature search, last updated in october 2019, using the web of science (thomson reuters) search engine. studies of interest were identified based on a search string (detailed in the paper). to complete our literature search, we allowed for discrete inclusions of relevant publications before the screening process.
selection_criteria:
authors discarded articles considering only one plant-parasitic nematode species (e.g., meloidogyne sp.), review articles, studies conducted in greenhouses, in unmanaged ecosystems and articles not on the soil system (e.g., fresh water). inclusion
criteria: (1) data should be available in the articles either in table or in graphical forms. (2) nematode data should be a measurement of the abundance of nematode trophic groups, and studies had to report at least one diversity indices. (3) studies needed to evaluate the effects of at least one of the four main agricultural practices: managing plant diversity (rotation, cover crop and association), pesticide input (herbicide, biocides and nematicide), tillage, organic and mineral fertilization. (4) the samples should be collected from the topsoil layer. (5) studies needed to report means, standard deviation or standard errors and sample size of nematode variables in control and treatment groups.
data_analysis: to calculate the combined effect size and its corresponding variance, authors used a multilevel meta-analysis model (mixed model) run with the “rma.mv” function from the metafor package. the average response ratios were tested for heterogeneity using the qe statistic. to further determine whether the collected metadata (moderators) explained the heterogeneity of effect sizes, authors used a mixed model with moderator variables as a fixed factor and ‘study id’ as a random factor.
background: Agricultural practices significantly affect soil biodiversity and functions, altering biogeochemical cycles and potentially compromising food production. Increased employment of sustainable agricultural practices is of growing policy concern and requires a better understanding and quantification of how agriculture affects soil functioning.
objective: autohrs conducted a worldwide meta-analysis to quantify the effect of agricultural practices on soil nematodes, known to be key biological indicators of soil health
result1: rotation did not affect total abundance of nematodes
result2: a significant reduction in the absolute abundance of plant feeders (pf, −47.2%) without impacting the total abundance or the abundance of other trophic groups when a rotation of more than 2 years was applied.
result3: rotation also promoted taxonomic richness (+19.3%), the maturity index (+20.3%), enrichment index (+47.0%) and abundance of omnivore-predators (+55.8%, although not significant), while slightly reducing the plant parasitic index (−5.2%).
general_conclusion: rotation did not affect total abundance of nematodes
knowledge_gaps: a large number of studies did not compute the nematode indices nor provide the full raw data of community taxonomic composition.

search_strategy: to select trials for the analyses, we searched for articles published from january 1988 to august 2003 on the isi web of science. the search combinations entered were ‘mycorrhiza* and agriculture’, ‘mycorrhiza* and tillage’, ‘mycorrhiza* and fallow’, ‘mycorrhiza* and cropping system’, ‘mycorrhiza* and cover crop’ and ‘mycorrhiza* and inoculation and field’.
selection_criteria: all glasshouse and field studies that reported colonization were included except when either (1) fumigation or other soil sterilizing methods were used, because sterilization of the soil can result in the destruction of more than mycorrhizal fungi, or (2) seedlings were inoculated prior to outplanting, because small differences between mycorrhizal and nonmycorrhizal plants established early, prior to outplanting, could be the sole cause of the mycorrhizal effect observed at the harvest.
data_analysis:
authors weighted effect size based on sample size, distinguishing between field trials and glasshouse trials, and conducted the weighting within each group separately. the few studies that did not report the number of replicates were removed from further analysis. the effect size to express a change in mycorrhizal colonization was analyzed using a three-factor analyses of variance
(anova) as a mixed model in sas. for the effect sizes expressing a change in yield, biomass, and shoot p concentration as a result of a significant increase in mycorrhizal colonization authors conducted single-factor anovas within groups. data were transformed to fulfil the requirements of normality and homogeneity of variance when necessary. the 95% confidence interval around the estimated least significant mean was calculated using standard error.
background: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) are components of the great majority of natural and agricultural ecosystems. Little is known about the symbiosis in nonsterile soil, which can harbor many other kinds of organisms that independently influence both plants and AMF.
objective: authors conducted meta-analyses to determine the effects of various agricultural practices on mycorrhizal colonization in nonsterile soils, and the consequence of those effects on yield, biomass, and phosphorus (p) concentration.
result1: mycorrhizal rotational systems did not increased mycorrhizal colonization in nonsterile soils compared to mycorrhizal continuous cropping systems.
result2: rotation with a mycorrhizal crop instead of a nonmycorrhizal crop increased mycorrhizal colonization
general_conclusion: crop rotations with mycorrhizal plants had no significant effect on mycorrhizal colonization. rotation with a mycorrhizal crop instead of a nonmycorrhizal crop increased mycorrhizal colonization

search_strategy: authors initially searched the literature in 2012 using isi web of knowledge v.5.6 (available online).2 the initial search terms were ‘‘crop’’ and ‘‘soil,’’ which were subsequently refined by ‘‘rotation’’ and ‘‘continuous’. authors expanded the search by checking the reference and citation lists of studies that met our basic criteria.
selection_criteria: authors selected only studies that included a monoculture treatment, were in place for a minimum of three years, and reported the effects of crop rotations on total soil c or n, microbial biomass c or n, or a combination of these variables. studies that included a fallow period in rotation, characterized by no crop production and frequently intensive tillage or herbicide use to control weeds, were excluded from our analysis because of the wide variation in specific fallow management practices. authors included both field and vegetable crops in our analysis.
data_analysis: log response ratio (lnr) represents the influence of adding one or more crops to a monoculture crop. authors used metawin v.2.1 to calculate r and 95% bias-corrected confidence intervals (ci) with 9999 iterations. authors used funnel plots to determine that there was no evidence of publication bias and used an unweighted metaanalysis where all studies had a variance equal to 1. moderating variables were analyzed using metawin v.2.1 in a procedure similar to anova. total group heterogeneity (qt) was partitioned into within-group (qw) and between-group (qb) heterogeneity, similar to partitioning variation in an anova.
background: Reductions in the number of crops in rotation or the replacement of rotations by monocultures are responsible for the loss of biodiversity. The belowground implications of simplifying agricultural plant communities remain unresolved; however, agroecosystem sustainability will be severely compromised if reductions in biodiversity reduce soil C and N concentrations, alter microbial communities, and degrade soil ecosystem functions as reported in natural communities.
objective: autohrs conducted a meta-analysis to examine crop rotation effects on total soil c and n concentrations, and the faster cycling microbial biomass c and n pools that play key roles in soil nutrient cycling and physical processes such as aggregate formation.
result1: rotation increased mbc by 20.9% and mbn by 26.1%.
result2: rotation increased mbc:tc and mbn:tn ratios by 10% and 24%, respectively
general_conclusion: observed increases in mbc and mbn, as well as in the proportion of total soil c and n in the mbc and n pools, point to a proportional shift of c and n into som pools with rapid cycling times, which is likely to be accompanied by a general increase in potential soil biological activity
