The belowground implications of simplifying agricultural plant communities remain unresolved; however, agroecosystem sustainability will be severely compromised if reductions in biodiversity reduce soil C and N concentrations, alter microbial communities, and degrade soil ecosystem functions as reported in natural communities.
objective: autohrs conducted a meta-analysis to examine crop rotation effects on total soil c and n concentrations, and the faster cycling microbial biomass c and n pools that play key roles in soil nutrient cycling and physical processes such as aggregate formation.
result1: rotation increased tn 5.3%. only three-crop rotations without cover crops increased tn by 7.8%.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: crop rotations sustain soil quality and productivity by enhancing soil c and n. however, the increase in soil c under rotations found in this study seems to be driven largely by the inclusion of a cover crop

search_strategy: an extensive literature search was performed using web of science with the search terms “soil n mineralization or potentially mineralizable nitrogen not forest not tree” which resulted in 6665 studies published before the cut-off date of 1 july 2014. a search was also performed using google scholar, but no additional studies were found relevant to our analysis
selection_criteria: exclusion criteria: studies that were not relevant in the context of this paper or were not found to include sufficient information regarding soil, crop management, or crops. conference abstracts and studies not providing quantitative results were also rejected.
data_analysis: the effect size was expressed as a response ratio (rr), natural log transformed for normality. authors applied weights using the reported number of replications. the homogeneity among lrr values from all the studies was analyzed. the data were analyzed for outliers by plotting each observation against the natural log of the response ratio and a box plot. weighted analysis of variance was used to compare mean response ratio for different management practices and treatments. a meta-regression analysis was performed to analyze data for the effect of continuous variables such as the duration of the management practice and the soil depth. all statistical analyses were conducted with r (version 3.4.2). significant difference between treatments was considered if p values < 0.05. bootstrapping procedures were used to generate 95% confidence intervals for weighted mean effect sizes using 500 iterations.
background: In fertile soils with high soil organic matter (SOM) content, the mineralization of SOM nitrogen (SOM-N) is a major source of N for crop uptake and has been positively associated with crop yield. As a result, researchers have suggested that knowledge about the fraction of SOM-N susceptible to mineralization may help to optimize N fertilizer management. This fraction of SOM-N, commonly referred to as potentially mineralizable nitrogen (PMN). However, the effect size and relationship with crop yield across specific management practices remain uncertain.
objective: authors conducted a quantitative review to understand how conservation agriculture management practices affect pmn
result1: an increase in crop rotation diversity from one to two or two to three or more cash crops was associated with 46% higher potentially mineralizable nitrogen (pmn)
result2: NA
general_conclusion: overall, an increase in potentially mineralizable nitrogen (pmn) occurred by increasing the number of crops in the rotation
knowledge_gaps: more studies that report both pmn and crop yield are needed to directly link laboratory measurements of pmn to crop production.

search_strategy: data were acquired by searching existing refereed literature (1971–2010) and through personal communication with individual data owners, if necessary.
selection_criteria: not specified
data_analysis: authors categorize the measures in three groups: decrease, no effect, increase of nh3 loss (the majority of the measures indicate an increase of nh3 loss). they identify factors related to nh3 loss (some soil types are associated with strong loss, and other with lower loss) using a simple meta-regression model.
background: Nitrification inhibitors (NI) can reduce production of the greenhouse gas nitrous oxide by inhibiting nitrification and subsequent denitrification processes. However, this extended retention of N in the NH4+ form in the soils treated with NI can increase ammonia (NH3) emission.
objective: the objectives of this paper is to summarize findings regarding impact of ni on nh3 emissions by categorizing reported results from peer-reviewed papers, to explore what may cause difference between results, and to discuss how to mitigate the negative impact of ni. here we report results regarding the impact of ni on nh3 emissions.
result1: in studies where a significant increase in nh3 loss was observed after application of ni treatments, increase in nh3 loss due to ni treatment (nh3 loss in n plus ni treatment − nh3 loss in n treatment) was between 1.1 and 25 % in laboratory and lysimeter experiments and between 0.3 and 19.7 % in field experiments; the overall increase in emission was 6.7 % (n = 26).
result2: decrease in nh3 loss with ni treatments ranged from −0.8 to −4.1 % in laboratory experiments and from −0.3 to −1.8 % in field experiments; the overall decrease in nh3 emission was −1.3 % (n = 6).
general_conclusion: overall the nitrification inhibitors tend to increase nh3 loss.

search_strategy: this meta-analysis was conducted based on studies of the effects of mitigation strategies (the 4r nutrient stewardship, farming practices and enhanced efficiency fertilizers) on nh3 volatilization in cropping and pasture systems published from 1971 to february 2016. extensive keyword searches of several databases (web of science (isi), scopus, cab abstracts (isi), academic search complete (ebsco) and google scholar) and of the reference list of cited references were performed.
selection_criteria: 1)the sample sizes and means of nh3 volatilization had to be reported for control and treatment plots. 2) details on experimental location; year; design and conditions must be provided to enable the cross checking of duplicate publication.
data_analysis: the meta-analysis was conducted using metawin version 2.1 (rosenberg et al., 2000). mean effect sizes and 95% confidence intervals were generated by bootstrapping (4999 iterations). a fixed-effects model or a mixed-effects model is technically not applicable for non-parametric metaanalytic procedures based on weighting by replication. however, to perform a correct bootstrapping using metawin, a fixed-effects model had to be selected.
background: Ammonia (NH3) volatilization is a major pathway of nitrogen (N) loss in agricultural systems worldwide, and is conducive to low fertilizer N use efficiency, environmental and health issues, and indirect nitrous oxide emission. While mitigating NH3 volatilization is urgently needed, a quantitative synthesis is lacking to evaluate the effectiveness of mitigation strategies for NH3 volatilization from synthetic fertilizers applied in agricultural systems.
objective: the objective of this study is to provide critical information on how to minimize n loss as nh3 in agricultural systems by conducting a quantitative synthesis of the current literature on the mitigation strategies (the 4r nutrient stewardship, farming practices and enhanced efficiency fertilizers) of nh3 volatilization. here, the results regarding the effect of urease inhibitors (ui) and controlled release fertilizers (crf) on nh3 volatilization are reported.
result1: overall, ui significantly reduced nh3 volatilization by 53.7%. cyclohexylphosphoric triamide (chpt) was the most effective ui in decreasing nh3 volatilization (by 86.6%). hydroquinone, in contrast, was the only ui that did not significantly reduce nh3 volatilization.
result2: crf effectively lowered nh3 volatilization by 68.0%.
result3: methylene urea was the most effective in decreasing nh3 volatilization (by 87.5%). coated urea fertilizers such as thermoplastic resin-coated urea, sulphur-coated urea, and polyfin-coated urea significantly reduced nh3 volatilization by 82.7%, 78.4%, and 69.4%, respectively.
result4: ni increased nh3 volatilization by an overall of 38.0% apart from 3,4-dimethylpyrazole phosphate (dmpp), which did not significantly affect nh3 volatilization, other nitrification inhibitors increased the loss by 22.6–220.1%.
general_conclusion: this synthesis shows that fertilisers amended with urease inhibitors and controlled-release fertilisers significantly decreased nh3 volatilization. the use of fertilisers amened with nitrification inhibitors increases the volatilization of nh3.

search_strategy: the authors performed a systematic literature review focusing on direct n2o emission and nh3 volatilisation in brazil. the literature search was performed using “web of science”, “science direct”, “scielo” and “google scholar” search engines.
selection_criteria: 1)studies have to be published in peer-reviewed journals; 2) performed in brazil; 3) not conducted in greenhouses or manipulated weather conditions.
data_analysis:
due to the lack of statistical information reported in some studies (standard deviation, coefficient of variation, p-value, etc.), we were not able to perform a formal meta-analysis. descriptive statistics were calculated for each variable (mean, minimum, maximum, range, standard deviation and coefficient of variation). to account for the precision
of each study, the number of samples described in each paper was used as a weighting factor (studies with more replicates were assigned greater importance).
background: The use of synthetic nitrogen fertilisers is one of the most important land management practices proposed to improve crop and pasture productivity. The use of such fertilisers in excess can lead to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, linked to climate change, as well as ammonia (NH3) emissions, linked to eutrophication and soil acidification.
objective: to assess the impact of the use of nitrogen fertilisers, the authors conducted a structured review of brazilian studies on the emission of nitrous oxide (n2o; 11 studies) and ammonia volatilisation (nh3; 13 studies) from nitrogen fertiliser application. here the reported results concern the effect of urease inhibitors (ui) and coated urea (cu) on nh3 volatilisation.
result1: lower nh3 emission factors (ef) were found when using ui or cu, reducing the average urea ef by 43 and 34%, respectively, when compared with the urea ef.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: when fertilisers amended with urease inhibitors or coated urea were used, the final nh3-ef from urea was significantly reduced. note from the reviewers: as no quantitative results are provided (not a meta-analysis), the effect of urease ihnibitors and coated urea on nh3 volatilisation is uncertain.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed publications from january 1980 to september 2017 that are related to nh3 emission mitigation measures such asfertilizer application and manure management were extracted from the isi web of knowledge database, china national knowledge infrastructure (cnki) data-base, and google scholar by basic and advanced searches.
selection_criteria: 1)data from field-, pilot-, and laboratory-scale studies; 2) control treatments must be reported to allow assessment of treatment effects, with mean values of nh3 emission for each treatment available.
data_analysis: the authors performed a meta-analysis to estimate the mean effect size and the 95% confidence intervals (cis), then they study the factors associated with higher or lower impact of inhibitors on nh3 emission (one-way anova and lsd test).
background: Ammonia (NH3) emission from agricultural sources has contributed significantly to air pollution, soil acidification, water eutrophication, biodiversity loss, and declining human health. Although there are numerous strategies for reducing NH3 emission from agricultural systems, the effectiveness of these measures is highly variable.
objective: this study aims to evaluate the effect of mitigation options such as urease inhibitors (ui) and controlled-release fertilizer (crf), on nh3 emission from agricultural systems including cropping and livestock production systems, based on individual crop/animal types, through a meta-analysis, and to offer recommendations for future research based on this meta-analysis and literature review. here only results regarding ui and crf effects on nh3 emission are reported.
result1: on average, the application of ui significantly reduced nh3 emission by 53.1%
result2: the effect of ui on reducing nh3 emission varied significantly with crop type, with the highest for rice but the lowest for maize.
result3: on average, the application of crf significantly reduced nh3 emission by 56.8%.
result4: the reduction in nh3 emission by the application of crf was greater in pasture and rice than in vegetable and maize production systems.
result5: ni application significantly increase nh3 emission by 42.6% (15.6 to 76.0%).
general_conclusion: controlled-release fertilisers, fertilisers amended with urease inhibitors significantly reduced nh3 emission from fertilisers. overall, the application of fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors increase nh3 emission.

search_strategy: data was extracted from peer-reviewed papers published in both chinese and english language journals before november 2015. papers in chinese were collected from the china national knowledge infrastructure (cnki) database and those in english from web of science.
selection_criteria: 1)side-by-side field experiments in which the effects of various fertilizer management practices on nh3 emissions, with pot and lysimeter studies excluded; 2) annual crops, with perennial crops and orchards excluded; 3) nh3 emissions over the course of the entire growing season and the number of field replications had to be reported; 4) the only differences between the control and treatments were management practices, while other conditions had to be identical; 5) a minimum of two studies per category was needed to be included in the meta-analysis.
data_analysis: the metawin 2.1 program was used to generate mean effect sizes and their bias-corrected 95% cis by a bootstrapping procedure (4999 iterations).
background: Fertilizer nitrogen (N) application is a major source of atmospheric amonia (NH3), a compound carrying severe human health and ecosystem risks. China is the world's largest emitter of gaseous NH3. Although many studies have measured NH3 emissions from croplands in China, the effect of fertilizer management on yield-scaled NH3 emissions (i.e., NH3 intensity defined as NH3 emissions per unit crop yield) is not so clear. Filling this knowledge gap is critical because China seeks to achieve not only monumental increases in production but also reduced environmental degradation.
objective: the objective of this study is to synthesize independent experimental results and quantitatively assess the effect of fertilizer management practices on nh3 emissions from croplands in china through meta-analysis. here, the results regarding the effect of urease inhibitors (ui) and slow-release fertilizers (srf) on nh3 emissions and nh3 intensity (i.e. nh3 emissions per crop yield unit) are reported.
result1: the use of sr and ui significantly reduced nh3 emissions and nh3 intensity (graphical interpretation).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: nh3 emission and intensity were reduced by the use of urease inhibitors or controlled-release fertilisers, compared to conventional fertilisers.

search_strategy: several databases were screened. words “ammonia volatilization” and “ammonia emission from soil in china” were used as keywords to collect peer-reviewed papers about ammonia volatilization in china.
selection_criteria: not specified
data_analysis: the software comprehensive meta-analysis (cma-2) was used with standardized mean difference corrected for bias (hedges’ g) to compare ammonia volatilization changes among different crop types, climatic conditions, and soil grades when using control observations only. the authors used unmatched groups and pre- and post-data pathways to assess ammonia volatilization change among different conditions where n was applied compared to a control. to study the efficiency of a strategy in reducing ammonia volatilization, another pathway was used based on correlation calculated in cma-2. heterogeneity was tested at p  0.05 using cma-2. publication bias was assessed at p > 0.05 using rosenthal’s fail-safe n test based on z-values and 2-tailed p-values (borenstein et al., 2009).
background: Numerous strategies for mitigating ammonia volatilization (AV) from agricultural land have been investigated with limited evaluation of their efficacy and response to differing field conditions across China.
objective: this meta-analysis seeks to draw conclusions about av in china, and assess the effect of crop type (wheat, maize, and rice as staple crops), climatic conditions, and soil properties on av and variations in responses that can guide selection of appropriate strategies under different conditions. here, the results regarding the impact of using improved urea (iu, i.e. slow release fertilizers) on av are reported.
result1: using iu instead of common urea reduces the av change ratio by 21.8, 14.7, and 33.2% under wheat, maize, and rice, respectively.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: urease inhibitors are an effective alternative of urea to mitigate nh3 volatilization in wheat, maize and rice.

search_strategy: data were acquired by searching existing literature published before june 2015 using the isi-web of science and google scholar. the following key words were used for searching such as meta-analysis, efficiency, nitrification inhibitor, dcd, dmpp, inorganic n, n leaching, gaseous emission and plant productivity. and the search terms were complemented with a search through the literature cited in the articles found.
selection_criteria: 1)field studies were selected and laboratory incubation studies were excluded; 2) at least one of the selected variables were measured; 3) means and sample sizes had to be reported; 4) treatment replicates were at least of three, etc.
data_analysis: the mean effect sizes were estimated using the formulas described by bai et al. (2013) and are weighed (for each study, the weighting factor was calculated as the inverse of the pooled variance, then adjusted by the total number of observations per site, when multiple observations were extracted from the same study). then a fixed-effects model option in software metawin 2.1 was employed for calculation of grouped effect sizes. confidence intervals (cis) on the weighted effect size were generated using bootstrapping (9999 iterations).
background: Nitrification inhibitors (NI) have been developed to mitigate nitrogen (N) losses through blocking the first stage of nitrification. Among the NI commercially available, dicyandiamide (DCD) and 3, 4-dimethypyrazole phosphate (DMPP) are the most widely used, but the difference of their performances across field sites is less clear.
objective: in this study, using a meta-analysis approach, authors compared the efficiency of dcd and dmpp on altering plant n uptake under various conditions including soil ph values, fertilizer n forms, fertilizer n rates and crop types.
result1: for nh3 released from soil, results showed that dcd and dmpp did not alter nh3 emissions.
result2: no significant effect on no emission (quantitative result not provided in the text, graphical interpretation form fig 1)
general_conclusion: the results showed that fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors did not alter nh3 and no emissions.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed ni studies were searched using web of science (1984–2013).
selection_criteria: 1)for soil ph and concentrations of nh4+ , no3- and din, the average value across a whole crop rotation had to be reported. 2) for leaching loss of nh4+, no3- and din, and emissions of n2o, ch4, no and nh3, the cumulative values for a whole crop rotation had to be reported, or the reported data allows to estimate the cumulative values for a whole crop rotation.
data_analysis: the mean effect sizes with bias-corrected 95% confidential intervals (ci) were estimated using bootstrap resampling procedure (adams et al., 1997), allowing studies that did not report standard errors/deviations to be included in the analysis (adams et al., 1997). total heterogeneity among the categorical group (qt) was partitioned into within-group heterogeneity (qw) and between-group heterogeneity (qb), where qt, qw and qb have chi-square distributions. publication bias was assessed with studies that reported standard errors/deviations. egger’s regression test was used to quantify publication bias, which has higher power to detect the bias than the rank correlation method (sterne et al., 2001). meta-analysis was performed by the software metawin 2.1 (sinauer associates, inc. sunderland, ma, usa).
background: Anthropogenic activities, and in particular the use of synthetic nitrogen (N) fertilizer, have doubled global annual reactive N inputs in the past 50–100 years, causing deleterious effects on the environment through increased N leaching and nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions. Yet, no study has comprehensively assessed how inhibiting nitrification affects both hydrologic and gaseous losses of N and plant nitrogen use efficiency.
objective: the objective of this study is to better understand how nitrification inhibitors (ni) application affects air pollutant emission caused by n fertilizers, by conducting a comprehensive meta-analysis, and to assess whether the responses of this variable will be altered by ni forms, ecosystem types, fertilizer types and soil texture. here the results related to the effect of nis on nitric oxide (no) and amonia (nh3) emission were reported.
result1: ni application significantly decreased no emission (-24%, ci: -38% to  -8%). this effect was estimated only under dcd application. thus dcd application significantly decreased no emission.
result2: averaged across all studies, ni increased nh3 emission (20%, ci: 7 to 33%) (publication bias detected).
result3: the responses of no emission to ni addition was similar between fertilizer type. no other factors was tested for no emission.
result4: the responses of nh3 emission to ni addition varied for different ni forms, ecosystem types, fertilizer types and soil types.
result5: dcd increased nh3 emission (34%, 20 to 50%), but dmpp and ca-carbide had no significant impact on it. nh3 emission was significantly increased in agricultural soils (21%, 4 to 44%), but not in pasture soils. ni significantly decreased nh3 emission when applied with manure (27%, 20 to 36%) but not with synthetic fertilizer. ni significantly increased nh3 emission when applied in silt (29%, 20 to 40%) and sand soils (92%, 80 to 112%) but not in clay and loam.
general_conclusion: overall, fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors reduced the emission of no but increased nh3 emission.

search_strategy: the web of science and china national knowledge infrastructure database were employed to search peer-reviewed studies published before march 2016.
selection_criteria: 1)only the field, pot, and lysimeter studies on rice, wheat, or corn growth were included. the crop grain had to be harvested and weighted at the physiological mature stage. 2) means and samples size had to be reported with a minimum of three replicates. 3) the application rates of agricultural materials had to be reported, such as fertilizers (n, p, and k) and inhibitors (ni and ui), for the consideration of the cost-benefit analysis.
data_analysis: mean effect sizes and the 95% confidence intervals (cis) were generated by a bootstrapping procedure with 4999 iterations, using metawin 2.1.
background: Knowledge-based nitrogen (N) management, which is designed for a better synchronization of crop N demand with N supply, is critical for global food security and environmental sustainability. Yet, a comprehensive assessment on how these N management practices affect food production, greenhouse gas emission (GHG), and N pollution in China is lacking.
objective: the objective of the study is to evaluate the overall effects of seven knowledge-based n management practices on crop productivity, nitrous oxide (n2o) emission, and major reactive n (nr) losses (ammonia, nh3; n leaching and runoff), for rice, wheat, and corn yields in china by conducting a comprehensive meta-analysis. here the results regarding the effect of controlled-release n fertilisers (crf) and urease inhibitors (ui) on nh3 emissions are reported.
result1: crf application overall significantly decreased nh3 emission by 60.8% (95%ci: 53.4-67.2%). nh3 volatilization was decreased by 50.0% by ui application (95%ci: 30.1-66.8%).
result2: applying crf in rice and corn showed stronger effect on reducing nh3 emission than wheat (graphical interpretation).
result3: the effect of crf on nh3 emission also varied significantly with soc and tn contents, and n application rate. crf impact on nh3 volatilization was lower in soils with organic carbon content (soc) lower than 10 g/kg (47.1%, 95%ci: 36.3-57.2%) compared to soils with intermediate (68.8%, 95%ci: 59.5-75.6%) or soc higher than 20 g/kg (76.7%, 95%ci: 57.4-87.5%). lower impact of crf was reported in soil with total n (tn) content lower than 1 g/kg (34.4%, 95%ci: 25.9-41.7%) compared to intermediate tn (i.e. tn comprised between 1 and 2 g/kg) (69.8%, 95%ci: 60.9-77.1%). lower effect of crf was detected in alkaline soils (33.12%, 95%ci: 17.2-44.3%), compared to neutral soils (62.4%, 95%ci:54.2-69.3%). crf impact was also lower in case of intermediate n application rate, i.e. comprised between 200 and 300 kg n / ha (42.6%, 95%ci:32.7-52.12%), compared to lower (70.2, 95%ci: 60.1-77.8%) or higher n application rates (66.3%, 95%ci: 52.4-77.2%).
result4: the effect of ui application was not significant in alkaline soils.
result5: ni application overall significantly increased nh3 emission by 27.5% (9.0–56.0%). ni's effect on nh3 emission was higher when soil total n (tn) content of fertilizers was lower than 2 g/kg.
general_conclusion: overall, controlled-release fertilisers and fertilisers amended with urease inhibitors application decreased nh3 volatilization. globally, an increase in nh3 emission under fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors application was observed in this study.

search_strategy: detailed review of the literature published in peer-reviewed journals through the year 2016 (cutoff date on june 30, 2016). all published data were derived from the web of science and google scholar, and papers published in the china knowledge resource integrated database (cnki) with english abstract, as well as gathering and re-evaluating the older literature cited in the prior review of stehfest & bouwman (2006). different combinations of searching keywords (‘nitric oxide’ or ‘nox’ or ‘no’ and ‘soil’) were used for data extraction.
selection_criteria: 1) publications enclosing individual field measurements with only soil no data or in the cases that both no and n2o fluxes were simultaneously measured; 2) only field measurement data were included in this analysis, without considering laboratory or pot experimental data, vertical profile monitoring data over vegetation canopy or modeling results; 3) for data from croplands, the consecutive measurement period covers at least one whole cropping season.
data_analysis: the authors calculated the balanced mean values of soil no and n2o fluxes as well as their emission factors with the residual maximum likelihood (reml) procedure using genstat release 4.2 to minimize the heterogeneity resulting from missing values and unequal number of observations among reviewed literature. the authors conducted a weighted meta-analysis using response rations (rrs), where mean effect size for each category was calculated using a categorical random effects model. the overall mean effect size and 95% confidential interval (ci) of each grouping category generated by bootstrapping (9999 iterations) were calculated with metawin version 2.0 statistical software. the authors performed sensitivity analyses to test the robustness of our meta-analysis on response of soil no emissions to fertilizer and other experimental factors.
background: Soils are among the important sources of atmospheric nitric oxide (NO) and nitrous oxide (N2O), acting as a critical role in atmospheric chemistry.
objective: 1) to examine limitations of earlier reviews by extending the findings on the factors influencing soil no emissions; 2) to highlight the global soil no emission hot spots by comparing soil no emissions from different ecosystems. here the effect of organic fertilisers on no and n2o emissions are reported.
result1: relative to synthetic n fertilizer alone, synthetic n fertilizer combined with ni substantially reduced soil no emissions by 81%.
result2: synthetic n fertilizer combined with nitrification inhibitors application greatly decreased the direct emission factors of no and of no+n2o emissions  by 82% and 39% as compared with synthetic n fertilizer being applied alone, respectively.
general_conclusion: synthetic n fertiliser combined with fertiliser amended with nitrification inhibitors decreased soil no emission as compared with common synthetic n fertiliser application alone in this meta-analysis.
knowledge_gaps: most field studies were limited within seasonal or annual timescale, and there is an urgent need for continuous long-term (multiyear) measurements to elucidate the temporal variation.

search_strategy: authors searched for peer-reviewed publications between 1980 and 2016 on efficacy of eefs via the web of science and google scholar using search terms of enhanced-efficiency fertilizer, polymer coated fertilizer, urease inhibitor, nitrification inhibitor, yield, nue, nitrous oxide, ammonia, and nitrate leaching.
selection_criteria: 1)one or more of the efficacy indicators had to be reported; 2) data must have originated from field experiments (i.e. laboratory-based studies were excluded); 3) the experiments must have been replicated; 4) information needed to be provided regarding cropping systems, inhibitor type or the coating material of controlled release fertilizer; 5) management practices such as n fertilizer type, application rate, method, and placement, crop residue management (retention or removal), tillage, irrigation, and use of other agricultural chemicals had to be the same for the eef treatment and control.
data_analysis: the efficacy of a given eef type was assessed by meta-analysis procedure. more than half of the datasets did not report standard error/deviation. to overcome this hurdle while maintaining a robust meta-analysis, we used the bootstrap resampling procedure (5000 iterations) to obtain the mean rr with a bias-corrected 95% confidence interval (ci) (adams, gurevitch, & rosenberg, 1997). in addition, we calculated the heterogeneity in lnrr between all studies (qt), within-group (qw), and between-group (qb).
background: Enhanced-efficiency fertilizers (EEFs) (polymer-coated fertilizers PCF, nitrification inhibitors NI, urease inhibitors UI, and double inhibitors DI, i.e. urease and nitrification inhibitors combined) have been developed to better synchronize fertilizer nitrogen  (N) release with crop uptake, offering the potential for enhanced N use efficiency (NUE) and reduced losses. Can EEFs play a significant role in helping address the N management challenge?
objective: the objective of the study is to obtain a global view on the productivity and n-loss reduction performance of eefs through a holistic evaluation of all four eef types in different cropping systems under wide ranging conditions. here the results regarding the effect of pcf, ui and di on amonia (nh3) volatilization are reported.
result1: overall, pcf application reduced nh3 emission by 70.2% (95% confidence interval (ci): 59.8 to 78.0%). the effect of pcf application was significantly higher in paddy (mean effect: 82.9%, ci: 76.2 to 87.5%) and in grassland (73.6%,  ci: 68.7 to 77.7%) than in dryland (27.4%, ci: 2.8 to 44.6%). the effect of pcf application was significant in coarse textured soils (78.6%, ci: 68.3 to 85.5%) but not in medium or fine textured soils.
result2: overall, ui reduced nh3 volatilization by 63.4% (ci: 57.5 to 68.9%). among ui types, a higher reduction was observed for limus (mean effect: 80.0%, ci: 76.3 to 83.9%) than for nbpt (64.3%, ci: 57.8 to 70.1%), ppd (45.0%, ci: 29.3 to 56.3%) or other forms (58.0%, ci: 34.4 to 74.7%). the higher the baseline nh3 emission, the greater the reduction by ui. dry areas (annual rainfall <800 mm) benefitted more from ui treatment, with 70% reduction in nh3 emission, compared to 50% reduction in high-rainfall areas (> 1200 mm). also, there was a greater reduction in nh3 emission by ui in soils of higher ph or coarser texture than other soils. ui effect was similar among production systems types.
result3: overall, ni increased nh3 emission by 19% (9 to 30%). dcd application significantly increased nh3- emission by 20.0% (9.3 to 33.9%), while dmpp application had not significant effect on nh3 emission. the tradeoff of ni in increasing nh3 emission was present for all cropping systems and varied from a low of 13% (3 to 22%) in grassland to a high of 28% (4 to 66%) in dryland systems.the net result, in terms of aggregated n-loss reduction, was 52, 6, and 7 kg/ha for grassland, dryland, and paddy systems.
result4: overall, di decreased nh3 volatilization by 52.7% (ci: 40.4 to 64.1%). the effect of di on nh3 volatilization was significantly higher in rice-paddy systems (mean effect: 75.5%, ci:  58.8 to 85.3%) than in grasslands (36.8%, ci: 24.2 to 48.1%). stronger di effect was found in dry (i.e. < 800 mm) areas (84.6%, ci: 54.2 to 95.5%) than in 800 - 1200 mm rainfall areas (41.1%, ci: 28.8 to 52.3%). the effect of di was higher when applied with synthetic fertilizer (69.9%, ci: 50.4 to 82.2%) than when applied with manure (38.6%, ci: 26.5 to 49.5%).
general_conclusion: polimer coated fertilisers, fertilisers amended with urease inhibitors, fertilisers amended with double inhibitors application significantly decreased nh3 volatilization. on the contrary, the application of nitrification inhibitors increased nh3 emission.

search_strategy: the authors conducted a detailed review of literature published in peer-reviewed journals through 2008 and identified field studies that compared n2o and no emissions from plots to which ni, pcf or ui were applied with those from plots to which conventional fertilizers were applied.
selection_criteria: 1)only field experiment data were included; small-scale experiments such as incubation or soil column experiments were excluded; 2) papers those emission data with the same total nitrogen application rate for treatment and control; 3) studies with no replication or no reported number of replications were excluded from the analysis.
data_analysis: to conduct a meta-analysis, the mean n2o and no emissions, sd, and number of replicates from the treatment and control are needed. when no sd was reported, the authors assigned the average sd derived from other sd reported datasets – that is, 23% of means for n2o emissions – to include as many  studies as possible in the analysis (higgins & green, 2008). if outlying data points were not obvious artifacts, outliers were included in the analysis to illustrate variability. using response ratios, a weighted meta-analysis was conducted. mean effect size for each category was calculated, with bias-corrected 95% confidential intervals (cis), using a bootstrapping procedure (9999 iterations). the meta analysis was conducted using meta-win version 2 (rosenberg et al., 2000).
background: Agricultural fields are an important anthropogenic source of atmospheric nitrous oxide (N2O) and nitric oxide (NO). Although many field studies have tested the effectiveness of possible mitigation options on N2O and NO emissions, the effectiveness of each option varies across sites due to environmental factors and field management.
objective: the aim of this study was to integrate results of field measurements to evaluate quantitatively the effect of enhanced-efficiency fertilizers (eefs) [i.e., nitrification inhibitors (ni), polymer-coated fertilizers (pcf), and urease inhibitors (ui)] on n2o and no emissions from agricultural fields, using meta analysis. here, only results regarding the effect of pcf and ui on no emissions are reported.
result1: polymer-coated fertilizers significantly reduced no emissions (-40%, 95% confidence interval, (ci): -76% to -10%.
result2: on average, ni significantly reduced no emissions ( -46%,  ci: -65% to  -35%) compared with those of conventional fertilizers.
result3: among ni, dcd ( -66%, ci: - 74% to  -37%) and dmpp (- 36%, ci: -44% to  -26%) significantly reduced no emissions.
general_conclusion: polymer-coated fertilisers and nitrification inhibitors significantly reduced no emissions compared with conventional fertilisers.

search_strategy: the reviewed literature consisted of studies published between 1990 and 2014. the literature review was further complemented by citations in the original studies.
selection_criteria: 1)nh3 losses according to time have to be reported and not only cumulative loss to compare the volatilization curves; 2) crop yield have to be reported; 3) at least three repetitions
data_analysis: the authors performed a systematic litterature review to extract nh3 losses measures. extracted data were used to fit a non linear mixed model which estimate nh3 losses in untreated urea (control) and in nbpt-treated urea (treatment). this model is used to estimate the difference in n losses between both treatements. a meta-analysis is then performed in order to caracterise nbpt effect according to several factors (soil ph, soil texture, n rate etc.).
background: Despite several studies conducted worldwide to test the efficacy of N-(n-butyl)thiophosphoric triamide (NBPT) to reduce amonia (NH3) losses from urea and potentially to increase crop yield, some questions still remain open.
objective: this study aimed to perform a meta-analysis regarding the use of nbpt to reduce nh3 volatilization loss from urea and to increase yields of major crops worldwide. here the results regarding the effect of nbpt application on nh3 volatilization are reported.
result1: the fitted model indicates that after 42 d (the longest volatilization trial in the dataset), the cumulative nh3 loss for control (untreated urea) was of 31.0% of n applied, while for nbpt-treated urea it was 14.8%, a 52% reduction in nh3 loss using the urease inhibitor.
result2: the meta-analysis' results showed that the effect of nbpt in reducing volatilization losses were reduced under high n rates. n rates >160 kg/ha showed a decrease in nh3 loss of 41.2% (32.1 to 50.4%), while n rates of 80 to 160 and <80 kg/ha showed losses of <64.3% (59.3 to 69.2%), and 60.6% (30.0 to 91.3%), respectively.
general_conclusion: treating urea with the urease inhibitor produced an average reduction in nh3 volatilization losses of 52% compared with untreated urea for major crops and different soil conditions.

search_strategy: two datasets were compiled, one for n2o emissions and one for crop yield. a literature search using google scholar and web of science was conducted with the keywords (“nitrous oxide”, “n2o”, “corn”, “maize”, “yield”, “productivity”, “corn belt”). the cut off for published articles to be included in the databases was the end of march 2015. literature cited in the articles was also reviewed to complement the keywords search. in addition to published papers; two studies from the gray literature were included (paniagua, 2006; schwager, 2015) to reduce the potential artifacts caused by publication bias (rosenthal and rosnow, 1991).
selection_criteria: 1)studies containing sufficient information about the experimental design; 2) field experiments; 3) include a minimum of three replicates; 4) report a measure of variance. for the n2o dataset an additional criteria was added: 5) have utilised a suitable sampling methodology to robustly account for temporal and spatial variations. only studies reporting side-by-side comparisons of specific practices were used.
data_analysis: all analyses were carried out in metawin 2.1 (rosenberg et al., 2000). a categorical random effects model was used where the estimated pooled variance was 0; a fixed effects model was used for the remaining cases. confidence intervals (95% cis) were generated by bootstrapping (9999 iterations). if the 95% cis did not overlap zero, mean effects were considered significantly different from zero. rosenthal’s fail-safe n technique at p = 0.05 was used to test the potential impact of publication bias (rosenthal and rosnow, 1991).
background: The potential for mitigation of nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions arising from fertilizer management practices in corn systems has been scientifically assessed in recent decades. Given the strong association between fertilizer management and crop productivity, which to a large extent determines farmers’ willingness to adopt such practices, it is essential to incorporate the impacts on yields before any mitigation practice can be recommended.
objective: a meta-analysis was conducted to concurrently characterize the response of n2o emissions and crop productivity to a set of fertilizer management options. here the impact of polymer-coated urea (pcu) use on crop yield are reported.
result1: poly-coated urea application had no significant impact on crop yield.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: poly-coated urea has a lower potential for crop yield improvements (no statistically significant response compared to urea).
knowledge_gaps: further research is needed to evaluate polymer coated urea under a wide range of environmental and soil conditions, especially its dependency on soil moisture conditions.

search_strategy: a literature survey of peer-reviewed papers published before march 2015 reporting the results of the effects of eenf on n2o emission was carried out using the isi-web of science and google scholar.
selection_criteria: 1)n2o emission had to be reported from upland cropping systems including maize, wheat and barley (horticulture crops were excluded); 2) the measurements were conducted under field conditions; 3) n2o flux rate must have been measured for an entire crop growth period; 4) the nitrogen source and application rate were same for the treatment and control; and 5) the grain yields were reported.
data_analysis: the meta-analysis was performed using the metawin 2.1. mean effect sizes were estimated with a random-effects model. the 95% confidence intervals (cis) around mean effect sizes were calculated by using bootstrapping with 4999 iterations.
background: Enhanced-efficiency nitrogen fertilizer (EENF) has gained considerable attention for improving nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) and mitigating nitrous oxide (N2O) emission in many agro-ecosystems. However, the effectiveness of EENF is highly variable under field condition.
objective: the authors performed a meta-analysis based on peer-reviewed studies to (i) evaluate the effects of eenf on n2o emissions and agronomic performance, compared with conventional nitrogen fertilizer; (ii) evaluate the impacts of climate (aridity), soil properties (soil ph and texture), fertilizer application strategies (application rate, timing and placement), and soil tillage on the efficacy of eenf. here the results regarding the impact of slow- or control-releasing fertilizer (s/crf) on crop yield are reported.
result1: on average, the effect of s/crf on crop yield was not significant.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: the effect of controlled-release fertilisers on crop yield was not significant.

search_strategy: the authors examined the studies used in recent meta-analyses (abalos et al., 2014, feng et al., 2016, qiao et al., 2015, thapa et al., 2016, yang et al., 2016) and other recent studies to investigate yield responses to nitrification or urease inhibitors when suboptimal n rates were applied.
selection_criteria: meta-analyses on the agronomic efficiency of eenfs would be greatly improved if only data sets where conventional n fertilisers and eenfs were applied using at least one sub-optimal n rate were included in the analysis.
data_analysis: data from the selected studies were extracted and yield data were converted to percentage of maximum yield and n fertiliser rates were converted to percentage of recommended rate for maximum yield. quadratic, quadratic-plateau and exponential fertiliser response curves were fitted to these data using the nls function in r. confidence intervals were estimated by propagating errors for model parameters using a monte carlo simulation with 10000 iterations via the predictnls function in the r package propagate.
background: While meta-analyses broadly suggest that nitrification and urease inhibitors can lower N2O emissions, the effect of these inhibitors on agronomic efficiency (i.e. yield and crop N-uptake) is less clear. Meta-analyses on the agronomic efficiency of nitrification and urease inhibitors would be greatly improved if only data sets where conventional N fertilisers and EENFs were applied using at least one sub-optimal N rate were included in the analysis.
objective: while the meta-analyses clearly identify that nitrification and urease inhibitors reduce n losses from volatilisation and in some cases leaching, these savings only translate into modest yield increases of 1–9%. one possible explanation for the relatively low yield increases is that the reference experiments employ control treatments with sufficient n to achieve maximum n-limited yields. any potential n-fertiliser savings arising from nitrification and urease inhibitors application would not therefore contribute to additional yield. this issue is the focus of this opinion piece.
result1: both quadratic and exponential models suggest a significant (p < 0.05) divergence in yields between conventional n fertilization vs n fertilization with nitrification and urease inhibitors, when n fertiliser rates are 25–90% of the recommended n fertiliser rate.
result2: a maximum yield difference between enhanced and conventional fertilisations was estimated to occur at 48% of the recommended n rate under an exponential model, which was similar to the yield difference estimated by the quadratic model at this n rate (p < 0.05)
result3: the magnitude of the yield benefit (∼11%) is similar to that estimated by other meta-analyses on this subject.
result4: scaling of the actual n rate against the optimum n rate, accounts for some of the variation driven by crop type/soil type/environment, thereby limiting the contribution of these confounding factors to yield variation.
general_conclusion: findings suggest that urease/nitrification inhibitors products may be able to achieve higher yields compared to conventional n fertiliser at suboptimal n fertiliser rates.
knowledge_gaps: a significant drawback to this analysis is the limited number of studies fitting the criteria of including suboptimal n rates. this prevents a thorough investigation of the role of other factors, including crop type, soil characteristics and environmental variables, in moderating the effect on yields

search_strategy: data was extracted from peer-reviewed papers published in both chinese and english language journals before november 2015. papers in chinese were collected from the china national knowledge infrastructure (cnki) database and those in english from web of science.
selection_criteria: 1)side-by-side field experiments in which the effects of various fertilizer management practices on nh3 emissions, with pot and lysimeter studies excluded; 2) annual crops, with perennial crops and orchards excluded; 3) nh3 emissions over the course of the entire growing season and the number of field replications had to be reported; 4) the only differences between the control and treatments were management practices, while other conditions had to be identical; 5) a minimum of two studies per category was needed to be included in the meta-analysis.
data_analysis: the metawin 2.1 program was used to generate mean effect sizes and their bias-corrected 95% cis by a bootstrapping procedure (4999 iterations).
background: Fertilizer nitrogen (N) application is a major source of atmospheric amonia (NH3), a compound carrying severe human health and ecosystem risks. China is the world's largest emitter of gaseous NH3. Although many studies have measured NH3 emissions from croplands in China, the effect of fertilizer management on yield-scaled NH3 emissions (i.e., NH3 intensity defined as NH3 emissions per unit crop yield) is not so clear. Filling this knowledge gap is critical because China seeks to achieve not only monumental increases in production but also reduced environmental degradation.
objective: the objective of this study is to synthesize independent experimental results and quantitatively assess the effect of fertilizer management practices on nh3 emissions from croplands in china through meta-analysis. here, the results regarding the effect of urease inhibitors (ui) and slow-release fertilizers (srf) on crop yield are reported.
result1: the use of sr and ui significantly increased crop yield (graphical interpretation).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: crop yield was significantly increased by sulfur-coated urea or urease inhibitors application, compared to conventional fertilisers.

search_strategy: data were acquired by searching existing literature published before june 2015 using the isi-web of science and google scholar. the following key words were used for searching such as meta-analysis, efficiency, nitrification inhibitor, dcd, dmpp, inorganic n, n leaching, gaseous emission and plant productivity. and the search terms were complemented with a search through the literature cited in the articles found.
selection_criteria: 1)field studies were selected and laboratory incubation studies were excluded; 2) at least one of the selected variables were measured; 3) means and sample sizes had to be reported; 4) treatment replicates were at least of three, etc.
data_analysis: the mean effect sizes were estimated using the formulas described by bai et al. (2013) and are weighed (for each study, the weighting factor was calculated as the inverse of the pooled variance, then adjusted by the total number of observations per site, when multiple observations were extracted from the same study). then a fixed-effects model option in software metawin 2.1 was employed for calculation of grouped effect sizes. confidence intervals (cis) on the weighted effect size were generated using bootstrapping (9999 iterations).
background: Nitrification inhibitors (NI) have been developed to mitigate nitrogen (N) losses through blocking the first stage of nitrification. Among the NI commercially available, dicyandiamide (DCD) and 3, 4-dimethypyrazole phosphate (DMPP) are the most widely used, but the difference of their performances across field sites is less clear.
objective: in this study, using a meta-analysis approach, authors compared the efficiency of dcd and dmpp on altering plant n uptake under various conditions including soil ph values, fertilizer n forms, fertilizer n rates and crop types.
result1: dcd significantly increased crop yield by 6.5%, while dmpp did not (increased by 1.2%; ci: − 1.6% to 5.8%).
result2: the efficiency of two ni differed in soil with different ph values. dmpp significantly increased crop yield by 9.4% (ci: 2.0% to 11.2%) only in alkaline soil, whereas dcd was both effective in acid and alkaline soil.
result3: dcd was effective along with organic fertilizer or urea, but dmpp did not significantly increase crop yield along with various n forms.
result4: dcd was effective in treatments of medium and high fertilizer n rates. dmpp did not have significant effect on crop yield under different fertilizer n rates treatments.
result5: ni application increased biomass production and biomass was more responsive to ni application than crop yield (graphical interpretation from fig1).
general_conclusion: fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors dcd significantly increased crop yield and biomass, while fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors dmpp significantly increased biomass only (no significant effect of dmpp application on crop yield).

search_strategy: peer-reviewed ni studies were searched using web of science (1984–2013).
selection_criteria: 1)for soil ph and concentrations of nh4+ , no3- and din, the average value across a whole crop rotation had to be reported. 2) for leaching loss of nh4+, no3- and din, and emissions of n2o, ch4, no and nh3, the cumulative values for a whole crop rotation had to be reported, or the reported data allows to estimate the cumulative values for a whole crop rotation.
data_analysis: the mean effect sizes with bias-corrected 95% confidential intervals (ci) were estimated using bootstrap resampling procedure (adams et al., 1997), allowing studies that did not report standard errors/deviations to be included in the analysis (adams et al., 1997). total heterogeneity among the categorical group (qt) was partitioned into within-group heterogeneity (qw) and between-group heterogeneity (qb), where qt, qw and qb have chi-square distributions. publication bias was assessed with studies that reported standard errors/deviations. egger’s regression test was used to quantify publication bias, which has higher power to detect the bias than the rank correlation method (sterne et al., 2001). meta-analysis was performed by the software metawin 2.1 (sinauer associates, inc. sunderland, ma, usa).
background: Anthropogenic activities, and in particular the use of synthetic nitrogen (N) fertilizer, have doubled global annual reactive N inputs in the past 50–100 years, causing deleterious effects on the environment through increased N leaching and nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions. Yet, no study has comprehensively assessed how inhibiting nitrification affects both hydrologic and gaseous losses of N and plant nitrogen use efficiency.
objective: the objective of this study is to better understand how nitrification inhibitors (ni) application affects air pollutant emission caused by n fertilizers, by conducting a comprehensive meta-analysis, and to assess whether the responses of this variable will be altered by ni forms, ecosystem types, fertilizer types and soil texture. here the results related to the effect of nis on nitric oxide (no) and amonia (nh3) emission were reported.
result1: across all studies, ni applications significantly increased productivity of grain (9%, ci: 6–13%), straw (15%, ci: 12–18%), and vegetables (5%, ci: 0–10%).
result2: among the four most commonly studied crops, grain productivity of barley showed the greatest increase (17%, ci: 7–29%), as compared to wheat (2%, ci: 0–5%), maize (9%, ci: 3–17%) and rice (7%, ci: 3–12%).
result3: dcd application has significantly increased grain (3%, 0 to 8%) and straw (19%, 13 to 27%) yields. dmpp application significantly increased grain (7%, 3 to 12%), straw (13%, 13-13%) and vegetable yields (7%, 1 to 14%).
general_conclusion: overall, fertilisers amened with nitrification inhibitors application significantly increased the productivity of grain, straw, and vegetable.

search_strategy: the web of science and china national knowledge infrastructure database were employed to search peer-reviewed studies published before march 2016.
selection_criteria: 1)only the field, pot, and lysimeter studies on rice, wheat, or corn growth were included. the crop grain had to be harvested and weighted at the physiological mature stage. 2) means and samples size had to be reported with a minimum of three replicates. 3) the application rates of agricultural materials had to be reported, such as fertilizers (n, p, and k) and inhibitors (ni and ui), for the consideration of the cost-benefit analysis.
data_analysis: mean effect sizes and the 95% confidence intervals (cis) were generated by a bootstrapping procedure with 4999 iterations, using metawin 2.1.
background: Knowledge-based nitrogen (N) management, which is designed for a better synchronization of crop N demand with N supply, is critical for global food security and environmental sustainability. Yet, a comprehensive assessment on how these N management practices affect food production, greenhouse gas emission (GHG), and N pollution in China is lacking.
objective: the objective of the study is to evaluate the overall effects of seven knowledge-based n management practices on crop productivity, nitrous oxide (n2o) emission, and major reactive n (nr) losses (ammonia, nh3; n leaching and runoff), for rice, wheat, and corn yields in china by conducting a comprehensive meta-analysis. here the results regarding the effect of controlled-release n fertilisers (crf) and urease inhibitors (ui) on yields are reported.
result1: overall, grain yield was significantly increased by 8.0% (95%ci: 6.8-9.1%) for crf application and 7.1% (95% ci: 5.5-8.9%) for ui application
result2: n application rates and soil properties (e.g., soil organic carbon [soc] and soil total n [tn]) also changed the yield responses to crf. crf impact was not significant in soil with high organic carbon content (soc >= 20g/kg). crf impact was higher in low tn (tn <= 1 g/kg), compared to soil with intermediate tn (1 g/kg < tn < 2 g/kg). crf impact on yield was significantly higher when n application rate was superior to 300 kg n / ha, compared to lower application rates.
result3: the impact of ui on yield varied according to n rate and ui product. ui impact was significantly higher when n application rate was higher than 300 kg n/ha (14.21%, 95%ci: 8.1-21.6%) compared to low n application rate, i.e. n rate lower than 200 kg n/ha (6.0%, 95%ci: 4.4-7.7%). the impact of hydroquinone (hq) (11.0%, 95%ci: 7.4-15.3%) was significantly higher than the impact of n-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide (nbpt) (5.7%, 95%ci: 4.1-7.5%).
result4: overall, grain yield was significantly increased by 10.0% (ci: 8.2 to 11.9%) for ni application. dcd (9.9%, 7.6 to 12.5%) and dmpp (8.5%, 5.6 to 11.6%) increased yield with similar efficiency. ni impact on yield was higher for n application higher than 300 kg/ha (18.1%, ci: 12.4 to 24.7%) than for lower n application rate (n rate >= 200 kg/ha: 8.0%, ci: 6.0 to 10.4%; 200 < n rate < 300 kg/ha: 8.2%, ci: 6.0% to 10.7%).
general_conclusion: overall, grain yield was significantly increased by controlled-release fertilisers application and fertilisers amended with urease inhibitors application. the use of fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors, especially dcd and dmpp, is effective in increasing grain yield.

search_strategy: authors searched for peer-reviewed publications between 1980 and 2016 on efficacy of eefs via the web of science and google scholar using search terms of enhanced-efficiency fertilizer, polymer coated fertilizer, urease inhibitor, nitrification inhibitor, yield, nue, nitrous oxide, ammonia, and nitrate leaching.
