Can EEFs play a significant role in helping address the N management challenge?
objective: the objective of the study is to obtain a global view on the productivity and n-loss reduction performance of eefs through a holistic evaluation of all four eef types in different cropping systems under wide ranging conditions. here the results regarding the effect of pcf, ui and di on crop yield are reported.
result1: overall, pcf application increased yield by 2.8% (95% confidence interval (ci): 1.2 to 4.2%). yield response to pcf was positive in rice-paddy systems (mean effect: 4.7%, ci: 2.2 to 7.0%) and in vegetable production systems (7.2%, ci: 3.6 to 10.6%). in grasslands pcf tended to decreased yield (-9.5%, ci: -16.5 to -0.4%), while pcf application had no significant effect on yield in maize and wheat production systems.  where temperature was favorable to plant growth (10–20°c), pcf boosted yield by 4.1% (ci: 1.0 to 7.3%), else the effect of pcf application was not significant. similarly, where rainfall was intermediate (800 - 1200 mm) and higher than 1200 mm, pcf increased yield by 7.3% (ci: 4.1 to 9.4%) and by 5.1% (ci: 2.0 to 9.4%), respectively. the positive effect of pcf on yield was shown in acidic soils (men effect: 1%, ci: 1 to 10.5%), in soils with intermediate soil organic carbon (soc) content (2.0%, ci: 0.8 to 4.1%) and when n was applied in subsurface (3.2%, ci: 1.1 to 5.2%).
result2: overall, ui application significantly increased crop yield by 6.2% (ci: 4.5 to 7.7%). the positive effect of ui was found for nbpt (mean effect: 6.7%, ci: 4.8 to 8.6%), but not for any other ui forms. yield response to ui was positive in grassland (4.6%, ci: 2.4 to 6.6%) and dryland systems (3.4%, ci: 1.4 to 5.5%), and more notable in paddy systems (8.9%, ci: 5.8 to 11.5%). the effect of ui on yield was significant in situations where mean annual temperature was comprised between 10 and 20°c (8.3%, ci: 5.1 to 11.6%) and higher than 20°c (7.3%, ci: 4.1 to 11.6%). ui significantly increased yield when rainfall were comprised between 800 and 1200 mm (6.2%, ci: 2.7 to 10.5%). the effect of ui on yield was not significant when soc was higher than 40 g/kg.
result3: overall, di increased yield by 4.9% (ci: 3.5 to 8.2%).  di effect was lower for the mixture of dcd and nbpt (mean effect: 4.6%, ci: 2.6 to 6.8%) compared to other di forms (10.5%, ci: 7.0 to 16.2%). when di was applied, greater yield increases were found in grasslands (11.1%, ci: 8.9 to 13.1%), compared to maize and wheat production systems (2.3%, ci: 0.4 to 5.3%). the di effect varied among soil textures; higher effect was found for coarse-textured soils (7.3%, ci: 5.1 to 10.5%) than for medium-textured soils (2.0%, ci: 0.3 to 5.1%) and the effect was not significant in fine-textured soils. higher yield increases were found when di was applied with manure (11.8%, ci: 10.0 to 13.7%) than with synthetic fertilizer (3.6%, ci: 0.9 to 6.8%). stronger effect of di was found in soils with intermediate (3.0%, ci: 0.5 to 5.1%) or high (12.7%, ci: 9.4 to 15.0%) soc content; the effect was not significant in soils with low soc content. di effect was significant when mean temperature was lower than 10°c (6.2%, ci: 4.1 to 9.4%), when rainfall was comprised between 10 and 20 mm (10.5%, ci: 8.3 to 12.7%), in acidic soils (10.5%, ci: 8.3 to 12.7%). in contrast, di effect on yield was not significant when mean average temperature was comprised between 10 and 20°c, in dry areas, in neutral soils.
result4: ni increased yield by 5% (ci: 4 to 7%). dcd and dmpp application significantly increased yield by 5.6 (3.8 to 7.5%) and 5.0% (0.9 to 10.0%), respectively. crops responded to ni differently. there was no significant effect of ni on vegetables, while ni effect on crop yield varied for 3% (1 to 5%) for wheat and maize to 7% (4 to 9%) for grassland. the positive effects of ni on yield depended on rainfall. it was not significant in areas of high rainfall (>1200 mm). ni increased yield by 4% (ci: 3 to 6%) and 5% (ci: 3 to 7%) in areas of moderate (800-1200 mm) and low rainfall, respectively (<800 mm).
general_conclusion: polimer coated fertilisers, fertilisers amended with urease inhibitors, fertilisers amended with double inhibitors application significantly increased crop yield. nitrification inhibitors is a viable option to increase yield across all conditions tested. among nitrification inhibitors forms, dcd and dmpp application significantly increased yield.

search_strategy: the reviewed literature consisted of studies published between 1990 and 2014. the literature review was further complemented by citations in the original studies.
selection_criteria: 1)nh3 losses according to time have to be reported and not only cumulative loss to compare the volatilization curves; 2) crop yield have to be reported; 3) at least three repetitions
data_analysis: the authors performed a systematic litterature review. extracted data were used to perform a meta-analysis to caracterise nbpt effect on yield according to several factors (soil ph, soil texture, n rate).
background: Despite several studies conducted worldwide to test the efficacy of N-(n-butyl)thiophosphoric triamide (NBPT) to reduce amonia (NH3) losses from urea and potentially to increase crop yield, some questions still remain open.
objective: this study aimed to perform a meta-analysis regarding the use of nbpt to reduce nh3 volatilization loss from urea and to increase yields of major crops worldwide. here the results regarding the effect of nbpt application on crop yield are reported.
result1: overall, the use of nbpt increased the yield of major crops by 5.3% (ci: 3.4–7.2%) compared with u.
result2: this meta-analysis shows that nbpt use in coarse-textured soils and nbpt rates >1060 mg/ha, on average, had no effect on crop yields.
general_conclusion: urease inhibitor ammendment to urea increased yield, compared to conventional urea.
knowledge_gaps: the meta-analysis procedure was adopted only when the original study showed statistical significance (p < 0.10) between treatments for yield parameters.

search_strategy: an extensive search of the scientific literature, using web of science (thompson reuters) and google scholar (google inc.) databases, was conducted in may 2015 for studies that reported n2o emissions with and without eefs in major cereal production systems. the database search was supplemented by reviewing the reference lists of the studies found in our search and those used in the prior meta-analysis by akiyama et al. (2010).
selection_criteria: 1)field studies on rice, corn, and/or wheat production (any additional components such as laboratory incubation or greenhouse experiments were excluded);  2) studies measuring n2o emissions for at least one complete growing season without missing n2o fluxes during the days following fertilization, tillage, and rainfall or irrigation events; 3) means and number of replicates for each treatment comparison reported.
data_analysis: using the response ratio and variance from individual studies, metawin version 2.1 statistical software was used to calculate weighted mean effect sizes and generate bias-corrected 95% confidence intervals (cis) using a bootstrapping procedure (4999 iterations) for each category.
background: Previous studies on the effectiveness of enhanced efficiency fertilizers (EEF), i.e. nitrification inhibitors (NI), urease inhibitors (UIs), controlled-release N fertilizers (CRFs) and combined application of both NI and UI, i.e. double inhibitors (DIs), in reducing nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions reported mixed results depending on their mode of action, soil and environmental conditions, and management factors.
objective: using meta-analysis, the study provides an overview of eef efficiency in reducing n2o emissions across eef types, crops, soils, and management practices. the main objectives of this study are to evaluate the effect of individual eef (ni, ui, di and crf) on soil n2o emission and crop yields in rice, corn and wheat systems and to identify the soil and management factors in which these eef are most effective. here the results related to ui, di and crf effect on crop yield are reported.
result1: overall, there was no significant effect of di on crop yields.
result2: crf consistently showed no effect on crop yields in this meta-analysis.
result3: ni increased overall crop yields by 7.1% (95%ci: 4.7 to 9.5%) compared with conventional n fertilizers.
general_conclusion: the use of fertilisers amended with double inhibitors or controlled-release fertilisers did not significantly increase crop yield. fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors can improve crop yields.

search_strategy: to select appropriate studies for the meta-analysis, the authors obtained data from research reports and publications from german agricultural research and extension centers in the federal states (e.g. bavaria, baden-wuerttemberg, north rhine-westphalia, saxony-anhalt, saxonia, mecklenburg-western pomerania, rhineland palatinate) and german universities such as the technische universität münchen and the bingen university of applied sciences. these reports and publications contained data from approximately 30 experimental sites on which experiments were conducted from 1997 to 2008 and on which five major agricultural crops were examined.
selection_criteria: not specified
data_analysis: the authors based the meta-analysis on the procedure described by hedges et al. (1999). briefly, each data point was summarized by a response ratio (rr), the log of the response ratio (lrr) and the sampling variance (v). each class (different class of fertilizer type, number of split n applications) was summarized by the weighted mean of lrr (lrr*) and the standard error of lrr* (se(lrr*)). lrr* was calculated by giving greater weight to data points with a lower standard deviation and higher precision. se(lrr*) to determine the standard error of the weighted mean was calculated.
background: A large number of studies have shown nitrogen (N) fertilizers with nitrification inhibitors (NI) are more environmentally friendly. In contrast, there are only a limited number of studies about effects of the N fertilizers added with NI on arable crop yields and the conclusions are also divergent.
objective: this study presents a meta-analysis of recent research in germany investigating the effects of ni on the yields of different agricultural crops (winter wheat, winter barley, winter rapeseed, potato, grain and silage maize) compared to conventional n fertilization without nis at a given n rate.
result1: yield of all agricultural crops applied with mineral n fertilizers containing ni was slightly decreased by 0.12% compared with that without ni, while their yield with slurry containing nis was increased by about 2.1%.
result2: similarly, there was no significant difference in yield and quality of winter wheat and potato between the treatments with and without ni.
result3: in contrast, a significant effect of the ni fertilizers with the reduced application number on crop's crude protein content was observed for winter wheat, even though there was no significant difference in the yield of winter wheat.
general_conclusion: the application of n fertilisers with nitrification inhibitors did not significantly influence the yields of a variety of agricultural crops (including winter wheat, winter barley, winter rapeseed, grain and silage maize and potato).

search_strategy: a literature review of english and chinese language peer-reviewed studies on n2o emissions from chinese wheat and maize fields prior to january 2017 was conducted using thomson reuters' isi-web of science research database and the china knowledge resource integrated database.
selection_criteria: 1)measurements were conducted under field conditions; 2) n2o flux rates were measured during an entire crop growth period using the static chamber method; 3) n2o emission and grain yield were determined simultaneously.
data_analysis: the mean effect sizes were calculated from lnrr of individual studies. individual studies were weighted depending on the number of experiment replicates and the number of n2o flux measurements per months. the meta-analysis was performed using metawin 2.1. mean effect sizes were estimated using the random-effects model. the 95% confidence intervals (cis) of the mean effect sizes were calculated using the bootstrapping with 4999 iterations.
background: NItrous oxide (N2O) emissions from croplands in China occur mostly during wheat and maize growing seasons in China. As a result, mitigating yield-scaled N2O emissions during these growing seasons in China plays an important role in the sustainable development of global cereal crop production.
objective: using meta-analysis, this study integrated the results of field measurements to assess the mitigation potential of major agronomic practices, including the application controlled release fertilizers (crf), on yield-scaled n2o emissions from croplands during wheat and maize growing seasons in china. here the results related to the effect of crf on crop yields were reported.
result1: compared to conventional inorganic fertilizer, crop yield significantly increased by 4.9%
result2: wheat and maize yield increased by 12.9% due to ni application compared to conventional n fertilizer.
general_conclusion: controlled-release fertilisers slightly (4.9%) increased crop yields during wheat and maize growing seasons. wheat and maize yield increased 12.9% due to nitrification inhibitors application compared to conventional n fertilisation without nitrification inhibitors.

search_strategy: an exhaustive literature survey of peer-reviewed publications was carried out using web of science v.5.16 for articles published before december 2014.
selection_criteria: 1)measurements have to be made under field conditions; laboratory incubation and soil column experiments were excluded. 2) the reported results had to include emissions for the treatment with and without ni for the inhibitor efficiency determination, or the control and treatment with ni for determination of the emission factor, or both. 3) environmental conditions and management (e.g., fertiliser application rates) were equal for the treatments with/without ni.
data_analysis: a regression analysis was carried out to determine if fertiliser application rate, the number of measurement days or the inhibitor application rate had an impact on the emission factors and the effect of the inhibitor. a meta-analysis was carried out using genstat (v.16; vsn international) to estimate ni effect according to soil, fertiliser and inhibitor type and land use. analysis of the correlations between variables was carried out using pairwise correlations and tests to estimate the correlation between the ef and the inhibitory effect with all the variables.
background: The main sources of nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions are nitrogen fertilizer and manure applications to agricultural fields. Many field studies have tested the effectiveness of nitrification inhibitors (NI) to reduce N2O emissions but results varied considerably because the studies were carried out under different climate and soil conditions.
objective: the objectives of this study are to analyse the new peer-reviewed literature to determine the variability in the efficiency of nitrification inhibitors (ni) and the effect of environmental parameters on this efficiency and to develop n2o emission factors for chemical fertilizers and animal excreta used with ni.
result1: both nis were effective in reducing n2o emissions; the inhibitory effect for dcd was 42.3%  2.2 and for dmpp was 40.2%  3.7, with emission factors (ef) for n amendment with dcd or dmpp of 0.41%  0.05 and 0.7%  0.33, respectively.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: nitrification inhibitors are effective in reducing n2o emission.

search_strategy: two datasets were compiled, one for n2o emissions and one for crop yield. a literature search using google scholar and web of science was conducted with the keywords (“nitrous oxide”, “n2o”, “corn”, “maize”, “yield”, “productivity”, “corn belt”). the cut off for published articles to be included in the databases was the end of march 2015. literature cited in the articles was also reviewed to complement the keywords search. in addition to published papers; two studies from the gray literature were included (paniagua, 2006; schwager, 2015) to reduce the potential artifacts caused by publication bias (rosenthal and rosnow, 1991).
selection_criteria: 1)studies containing sufficient information about the experimental design; 2) field experiments; 3) include a minimum of three replicates; 4) report a measure of variance. for the n2o dataset an additional criteria was added: 5) have utilised a suitable sampling methodology to robustly account for temporal and spatial variations. only studies reporting side-by-side comparisons of specific practices were used.
data_analysis: all analyses were carried out in metawin 2.1 (rosenberg et al., 2000). a categorical random effects model was used where the estimated pooled variance was 0; a fixed effects model was used for the remaining cases. confidence intervals (95% cis) were generated by bootstrapping (9999 iterations). if the 95% cis did not overlap zero, mean effects were considered significantly different from zero. rosenthal’s fail-safe n technique at p = 0.05 was used to test the potential impact of publication bias (rosenthal and rosnow, 1991).
background: The potential for mitigation of nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions arising from fertilizer management practices in corn systems has been scientifically assessed in recent decades. Given the strong association between fertilizer management and crop productivity, which to a large extent determines farmers’ willingness to adopt such practices, it is essential to incorporate the impacts on yields before any mitigation practice can be recommended.
objective: a meta-analysis was conducted to concurrently characterize the response of n2o emissions and crop productivity to a set of fertilizer management options. here the impact of polymer-coated urea use on n2o emission are reported.
result1: apart from the combined use of urease and nitrification inhibitors, no other categories of fertilizer practices showed a statistically significant effect on n2o emission although there was a general trend for treatment means to show a reduction compared to controls.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: poly-coated urea has a low potential for n2o mitigation (no statistically significant response to poly-coated urea compared to urea).
knowledge_gaps: further research is needed to evaluate polymer coated urea under a wide range of environmental and soil conditions, especially its dependency on soil moisture conditions.

search_strategy: a literature survey of peer-reviewed papers published before march 2015 reporting the results of the effects of eenf on n2o emission was carried out using the isi-web of science and google scholar.
selection_criteria: 1)n2o emission had to be reported from upland cropping systems including maize, wheat and barley (horticulture crops were excluded); 2) the measurements were conducted under field conditions; 3) n2o flux rate must have been measured for an entire crop growth period; 4) the nitrogen source and application rate were same for the treatment and control; and 5) the grain yields were reported.
data_analysis: the meta-analysis was performed using the metawin 2.1. mean effect sizes were estimated with a random-effects model. the 95% confidence intervals (cis) around mean effect sizes were calculated by using bootstrapping with 4999 iterations.
background: Enhanced-efficiency nitrogen fertilizer (EENF) has gained considerable attention for improving nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) and mitigating nitrous oxide (N2O) emission in many agro-ecosystems. However, the effectiveness of EENF is highly variable under field condition.
objective: the authors performed a meta-analysis based on peer-reviewed studies to (i) evaluate the effects of eenf on n2o emissions and agronomic performance, compared with conventional nitrogen fertilizer; (ii) evaluate the impacts of climate (aridity), soil properties (soil ph and texture), fertilizer application strategies (application rate, timing and placement), and soil tillage on the efficacy of eenf. here the results regarding the impact of slow- or control-releasing fertilizer (s/crf) on n2o emissions are reported.
result1: s/crf application significantly mitigated area- and yield-scaled n2o emissions by 17.5 and 16.3%, respectively.
result2: s/crf significantly mitigated area- and yield-scaled n2o emissions by 25.8% and 25.9% in arid regions, respectively; but did not show a significant effect on n2o emissions in humid regions. whereas, irrigation significantly enhanced the inhibition effect of s/crf on n2o emissions.
result3: s/crf significantly mitigated the area- and yield-scaled n2o emissions by 29.3% and 28.8% in alkaline soil, and by 35.0% and 34.6% in neutral soil, respectively, but the effect of s/crf application was not significant in acid soils. area-scaled n2o emission was significantly mitigated 18.2% and 43.9% by s/crf in medium and fine soils, respectively, but not reduced by s/crf in coarse soil.
result4: yield-scaled n2o emission was only mitigated 34.2% by s/crf in fine soil. s/crf only showed significant effects when n was applied after emergence as a top dressing fertilizer: area- and yield-scaled n2o emissions were reduced by 20.0% and 19.8%, respectively.
result5: s/crf significantly raised yield-scaled n2o emission when applied by surface broadcast (sbc), while it significantly reduced n2o emission under surface band (sb), but not under band incorporation (bi). the s/crf significantly mitigated the n2o emission under conventional tillage (ct), but did not under reduced-tillage (rt) and no-tillage (nt) in humid areas, while in arid regions, it was opposite.
general_conclusion: controlled-release fertilisers significantly reduced area- and yield-scaled n2o emissions compared to conventional fertilisers.

search_strategy: the authors performed a systematic literature review focusing on direct n2o emission and nh3 volatilisation in brazil. the literature search was performed using “web of science”, “science direct”, “scielo” and “google scholar” search engines.
selection_criteria: 1)studies have to be published in peer-reviewed journals; 2) performed in brazil; 3) not conducted in greenhouses or manipulated weather conditions.
data_analysis: due to the lack of statistical information reported in some studies (standard deviation, coefficient of variation, p-value, etc.), we were not able to perform a formal meta-analysis. descriptive statistics were calculated for each variable (mean, minimum, maximum, range, standard deviation and coefficient of variation). to account for the precision of each study, the number of samples described in each paper was used as a weighting factor (studies with more replicates were assigned greater importance).
background: The use of synthetic nitrogen fertilisers is one of the most important land management practices proposed to improve crop and pasture productivity. The use of such fertilisers in excess can lead to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, linked to climate change, as well as ammonia (NH3) emissions, linked to eutrophication and soil acidification.
objective: to assess the impact of the use of nitrogen fertilisers, the authors conducted a structured review of brazilian studies on the emission of nitrous oxide (n2o; 11 studies) and ammonia volatilisation (nh3; 13 studies) from nitrogen fertiliser application. here the reported results concern the effect of coated urea (cu) on n2o emissions.
result1: lower n2o emission factors (ef) were found when using cu, reducing the average urea ef by 61%, respectively.
result2: lower efs were found when using ni reducing the average urea ef by 74%. the effect of the ni was greater on oxisol (86%).
general_conclusion: when coated urea was used, the final n2o-emission factor from urea was significantly reduced. but as no quantitative results are provided (not a meta-analysis), the effect of coated urea on n2o emission is uncertain. the use of nitrification inhibitors resulted in lower efs for n2o. however, no quantitative analysis is provided.

search_strategy: the authors extracted data on soil n2o and ch4 fluxes for studies on flooded rice systems in which the effect of various fertilizer management practices were assessed in side-by-side field experiments. an exhaustive literature survey of peer-reviewed publications was carried out using isi-web of science and google scholar for articles published before august 2011.
selection_criteria:
studies needed to meet several criteria to be included in our analysis. first, n2o and/or ch4 fluxes must have been measured under field conditions for the entire growing season

(i.e. planting to harvest). second, seasonal fluxes and the number of field replications had to be reported for both control and treatment plots. third, growing conditions in the control and treatment plots had to be identical(except for the management practice being studied). 

to be included, exact fertilizer n rates needed to be reported and the grm treatment received the same total n rate as the control treatment. the n amount contributed from grm

ranged from 20 to 60 kg n ha−1 and represented 25–100% of the total n rate.
data_analysis:
studies were weighted by replication. they authors used metawin 2.1 to generate mean effect sizes and 95% bootstrapped cis (4999 iterations) (rosenberg et al., 2000). to ease interpretation, the results for the analyses on ln r were back-transformed and reported as percentage change under management treatment in question relative to the control

situation. treatment effects were considered significant if the 95% ci did not overlap with zero, and marginally significant if the 90% ci did not overlap with zero.
background: Flooded rice systems emit both methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O). Elevated CH4 emissions in rice systems can lead to a high global warming potential (GWP) relative to other crops, thus strategies to reduce greenhouse (GHG) emissions, particularly CH4, are needed. Altering water, residue (carbon) and fertilizer management practices are commonly suggested as options for mitigating GHG emissions in rice systems. While the effects of water and residue management have been reported on elsewhere, the impact of fertilizer management on GHG emissions has not been reviewed quantitatively.
objective: the objective was to analyze the peer reviewed literature to determine and quantify the effects of fertilizer management options on ghg emissions from rice systems in order to determine potential mitigation strategies for rice systems. the authors focused on the following areas: n management (rate, source, placement), the use of enhanced-efficiency n fertilizers (eenf), sulfate inputs, farmyard manure (fym) and green manure (grm). here, only results regarding the effect of green manures on ghg emissions are reported.
result1: the use of dicyandiamide, dcd, significantly reduced ch4 emissions by 18% (95% ci: −25% to −12%). dcd significantly reduced n2o emissions by 29% (95% ci: −40% to −20%).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: the use of nitrification inhibitors resulted in both lower ch4 and n2o emissions.

search_strategy: the authors collected data on cumulative n2o emission and soil physicochemical properties of treatments receiving urea, or nbpt and urea, via searching the thomson isi (r) web of science and google scholar on october 10th, 2017.
selection_criteria: not specified
data_analysis: the natural-log transformed response ratio was analyzed using both fixed and random effect model to estimate the overall effect size. a meta-regression was used to assess the relationship between effect size and soil physicochemical properties of interest (e.g. ph, tn, and om). based on these results, we arbitrarily divided the collected soils into acid and alkaline subgroups, and rerun themeta-analysis using random effect model.
background: Reducing the hydrolysis of urea via inhibition of urease activity offers a feasible and practicable approach to mitigate the nitrous oxide (N2O emissions and improve its nitrogen use efficiency. N-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide (NBPT) is the most widely used urease inhibitor for arable soils. However, its effect on reducing N2O emissions has been found to be inconsistent across studies.
objective: the objective of this study is to explore the possible mechanisms underlying the inconsistent effect of nbpt on n2o emission across soils by conducting a meta-analysis evaluating the importance of physicochemical properties including soil ph, organicmatter (om) content, and total nitrogen (tn) in regulating the efficacy of nbpt.
result1: the analysis using random effect model suggested that addition of nbpt resulted in an overall effect size of 0.76 [95% confidence interval (ci): 0.67, 0.86, p < 0.0001]
result2: the results of the meta-regression suggested that only ph was significantly and negatively correlated with the effect size (p = 0.024). subsequent analysis found that the effect sizes of alkaline soils were significantly lower than 1 [mean = 0.59; 95% ci (0.48, 0.73)], while those of acid soils were not significantly different from 1 [mean = 0.88; 95% ci (0.76, 1.00)]; moreover, the difference between these two subgroups was strongly supported (p=0.002).
general_conclusion: the addition of urease inhibitor to urea reduced n2o emission compared to conventional fertiliser.

search_strategy: relevant studies on n2o emissions in corn cropping systems in the midwestern u.s. and south-east canada were identified through a literature search in march 2012 using the web of science (keywords ‘n2o’ and ‘corn’ or ‘maize’), and through personal communications with researchers in the field.
selection_criteria: 1)n2o emissions had to represent at least a full growing season, covering emissions across furrows and seedbeds, and capturing anticipated n2o emissions peaks after tillage, fertilization and wetting; 2) only data from field experiments were included.
data_analysis: a random effects meta-analytic model was fitted using the pooled variance as a weighting function, and with 95% confidence intervals that are generated nonparametrically by bootstrapping (1000 iterations). heterogeneity and publication bias were evaluated, fixed versus random effects models were tested, effect sizes were weighted by the pooled variance or the number of observations per study, and confidence intervals were constructed using different approach (parametric vs nonparametric).
background: One of the unintended nitrogen (N)-loss pathways from cropland is the emission of nitrous oxide (N2O), a potent greenhouse gas and ozone depleting substance. Several N2O mitigation practices have been proposed and investigated, including reducing nitrogen (N) application rates, optimizing the time, place and source of applied N, reducing tillage intensity, and diversifying crop rotations. Results from such studies have been summarized in various reports and publications, but these summary analyzes have mostly remained qualitative.
objective: the objectives of this study is to expose data availability and quantitatively summarize effects of a suite of agronomic management practices on n2o emissions in corn cropping systems in the midwestern u.s. and south-east canada through meta-analysis. here, results regarding the use of urease inhibitor n-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide (nbpt) in combination with the nitrification inhibitor dicyandiamide (dcd), i.e. double inhibitors (di), and the use of polymer-coated urea (pcu) are reported.
result1: di application had a significant effect on n2o emissions (graphical interpretation) compared with fertilizer without di application.
result2: the use of pcu instead of conventional urea had no significant impact on n2o emissions.
general_conclusion: the use of fertilisers amended with double inhibitors consistently reduced n2o emission, while polymer coated urea had no significant impact on n2o emission.
knowledge_gaps: all individual studies are conducted over less than one year.

search_strategy: data were acquired by searching existing literature published before june 2015 using the isi-web of science and google scholar. the following key words were used for searching such as meta-analysis, efficiency, nitrification inhibitor, dcd, dmpp, inorganic n, n leaching, gaseous emission and plant productivity. and the search terms were complemented with a search through the literature cited in the articles found.
selection_criteria: 1)field studies were selected and laboratory incubation studies were excluded; 2) at least one of the selected variables were measured; 3) means and sample sizes had to be reported; 4) treatment replicates were at least of three, etc.
data_analysis: the mean effect sizes were estimated using the formulas described by bai et al. (2013) and are weighed (for each study, the weighting factor was calculated as the inverse of the pooled variance, then adjusted by the total number of observations per site, when multiple observations were extracted from the same study). then a fixed-effects model option in software metawin 2.1 was employed for calculation of grouped effect sizes. confidence intervals (cis) on the weighted effect size were generated using bootstrapping (9999 iterations).
background: Nitrification inhibitors (NI) have been developed to mitigate nitrogen (N) losses through blocking the first stage of nitrification. Among the NI commercially available, dicyandiamide (DCD) and 3, 4-dimethypyrazole phosphate (DMPP) are the most widely used, but the difference of their performances across field sites is less clear.
objective: in this study, using a meta-analysis approach, authors compared the efficiency of dcd and dmpp on altering plant n uptake under various conditions including soil ph values, fertilizer n forms, fertilizer n rates and crop types.
result1: dcd and dmpp both significantly decreased soil n2o emission by 44.7% (95% ci values not provided) and 47.6% (95% ci: 40.3% to 51.8%), respectively. both ni had the equal effectiveness on decreasing soil n2o emission.
result2: ch4 emission was not significantly altered by dcd and dmpp application. this result is potentially influenced by a limited number of observations (n = 6 for dcd; n = 4 for dmpp).
general_conclusion: n2o emission was significantly reduced by fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors while ch4 emission was not significantly reduced.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed ni studies were searched using web of science (1984–2013).
selection_criteria: 1)for soil ph and concentrations of nh4+ , no3- and din, the average value across a whole crop rotation had to be reported. 2) for leaching loss of nh4+, no3- and din, and emissions of n2o, ch4, no and nh3, the cumulative values for a whole crop rotation had to be reported, or the reported data allows to estimate the cumulative values for a whole crop rotation.
data_analysis: the mean effect sizes with bias-corrected 95% confidential intervals (ci) were estimated using bootstrap resampling procedure (adams et al., 1997), allowing studies that did not report standard errors/deviations to be included in the analysis (adams et al., 1997). total heterogeneity among the categorical group (qt) was partitioned into within-group heterogeneity (qw) and between-group heterogeneity (qb), where qt, qw and qb have chi-square distributions. publication bias was assessed with studies that reported standard errors/deviations. egger’s regression test was used to quantify publication bias, which has higher power to detect the bias than the rank correlation method (sterne et al., 2001). meta-analysis was performed by the software metawin 2.1 (sinauer associates, inc. sunderland, ma, usa).
background: Anthropogenic activities, and in particular the use of synthetic nitrogen (N) fertilizer, have doubled global annual reactive N inputs in the past 50–100 years, causing deleterious effects on the environment through increased N leaching and nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions. Yet, no study has comprehensively assessed how inhibiting nitrification affects both hydrologic and gaseous losses of N and plant nitrogen use efficiency.
objective: the objective of this study is to better understand how nitrification inhibitors (ni) application affects air pollutant emission caused by n fertilizers, by conducting a comprehensive meta-analysis, and to assess whether the responses of this variable will be altered by ni forms, ecosystem types, fertilizer types and soil texture. here the results related to the effect of nis on nitric oxide (no) and amonia (nh3) emission were reported.
result1: when averaged across all studies, ni application significantly decreased n2o emission ( -44%, - 48% to -39%). the reduction in n2o emission induced by ni was significant for all types of ecosystem, fertilizer and soil texture. dcd and dmpp application significantly reduced n2o emission by 57.6 and 52.5%, respectively (from 44.0 to 69.7% and from 42.8 to 60.5%)
result2: ni (data available only for dcd) had no significant impact on the emission and uptake of ch4, and the responses of ch4 emission and uptake were similar under different experimental conditions, such as ni form, ecosystem type, fertilizer type and soil texture.
general_conclusion: fertilisers amened with nitrification inhibitors application reduced n2o emission. the application of fertilisers amened with nitrification inhibitors had no significant effect on soil ch4 emission and uptake.
knowledge_gaps: small number of field studies on ch4 emission and uptake limited the statistical power of the analysis.

search_strategy: the web of science and china national knowledge infrastructure database were employed to search peer-reviewed studies published before march 2016.
selection_criteria: 1)only the field, pot, and lysimeter studies on rice, wheat, or corn growth were included. the crop grain had to be harvested and weighted at the physiological mature stage. 2) means and samples size had to be reported with a minimum of three replicates. 3) the application rates of agricultural materials had to be reported, such as fertilizers (n, p, and k) and inhibitors (ni and ui), for the consideration of the cost-benefit analysis.
data_analysis: mean effect sizes and the 95% confidence intervals (cis) were generated by a bootstrapping procedure with 4999 iterations, using metawin 2.1.
background: Knowledge-based nitrogen (N) management, which is designed for a better synchronization of crop N demand with N supply, is critical for global food security and environmental sustainability. Yet, a comprehensive assessment on how these N management practices affect food production, greenhouse gas emission (GHG), and N pollution in China is lacking.
objective: the objective of the study is to evaluate the overall effects of seven knowledge-based n management practices on crop productivity, nitrous oxide (n2o) emission, and major reactive n (nr) losses (ammonia, nh3; n leaching and runoff), for rice, wheat, and corn yields in china by conducting a comprehensive meta-analysis. here the results regarding the effect of controlled-release n fertilisers (crf) and urease inhibitors (ui) on n2o emissions are reported.
result1: averaged across all studies, n2o emission was significantly reduced by 38.3% (95%ci: 30.7-45.3%) for crf application and by 27.8% (95%ci: 17.0-40.9%) for ui application.
result2: a higher reduction in n2o emission was observed in rice (50.4%) than corn (25.3%) for crf application and in corn (37.0%) than wheat (11.9%) for ui application.
result3: the impact of crf was not significant in acidic soils.
result4: averaged across all studies, n2o emission was significantly reduced by 39.8% (34.0 to 45.6%) for ni application.
general_conclusion: controlled-release fertilisers and fertilisers amended with urease inhibitors application decreased n2o emission. fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors, especially dcd and dmpp, significantly decrease n2o emission.

search_strategy: authors searched for peer-reviewed publications between 1980 and 2016 on efficacy of eefs via the web of science and google scholar using search terms of enhanced-efficiency fertilizer, polymer coated fertilizer, urease inhibitor, nitrification inhibitor, yield, nue, nitrous oxide, ammonia, and nitrate leaching.
selection_criteria: 1)one or more of the efficacy indicators had to be reported; 2) data must have originated from field experiments (i.e. laboratory-based studies were excluded); 3) the experiments must have been replicated; 4) information needed to be provided regarding cropping systems, inhibitor type or the coating material of controlled release fertilizer; 5) management practices such as n fertilizer type, application rate, method, and placement, crop residue management (retention or removal), tillage, irrigation, and use of other agricultural chemicals had to be the same for the eef treatment and control.
data_analysis: the efficacy of a given eef type was assessed by meta-analysis procedure. more than half of the datasets did not report standard error/deviation. to overcome this hurdle while maintaining a robust meta-analysis, we used the bootstrap resampling procedure (5000 iterations) to obtain the mean rr with a bias-corrected 95% confidence interval (ci) (adams, gurevitch, & rosenberg, 1997). in addition, we calculated the heterogeneity in lnrr between all studies (qt), within-group (qw), and between-group (qb).
background: Enhanced-efficiency fertilizers (EEFs) (polymer-coated fertilizers PCF, nitrification inhibitors NI, urease inhibitors UI, and double inhibitors DI, i.e. urease and nitrification inhibitors combined) have been developed to better synchronize fertilizer nitrogen  (N) release with crop uptake, offering the potential for enhanced N use efficiency (NUE) and reduced losses. Can EEFs play a significant role in helping address the N management challenge?
objective: the objective of the study is to obtain a global view on the productivity and n-loss reduction performance of eefs through a holistic evaluation of all four eef types in different cropping systems under wide ranging conditions. here the results regarding the effect of pcf, ui and di on nitrous oxide (n2o) emissions are reported.
result1: overall, pcf application reduced n2o emission by 37.5% (95% confidence interval (ci): 27.1 to 46.6%). the effect of pcf application was significantly higher in paddy (mean effect: 74.4%, ci: 51.0 to 86.6%) than in dryland (31.0%,  ci: 20.8 to 40.2%). the effect of pcf in grassland was high, but the 95%ci was very large (73.5%,  ci: 8.6 to 86.1%), due to low number of observations (n = 3). the effect of pcf application was stronger in situations where mean annual temperature was higher than 20°c (79.2%, ci: 55.5 to 88.9%), compared to situations where temperature is comprised between 10 and 20°c (22.1%,  ci: 9.5 to 33.0%) or lower than 10°c (35.6%, ci: 20.5 to 48.3%). the effect of pcf application was significant in neutral soils (44.0%, ci: 28.8 to 56.8%), but not in acidic and alkaline soils. the effect of pcf application was stronger in soils with soil organic content (soc) lower than 10 g/kg (89.9%, ci: 86.6 to 92.2%) than in soils with intermediate soc (44.0%, ci: 28.8 to 56.8%); in contrast, applying pcf in soils with soc higher than 40 g/kg did not significantly reduced n2o emission.
result2: ui application did not significantly decreased n2o emission. however, among ui forms, hq application significantly decreased n2o emission by 4.9% (ci: 3.9 to 5.8%).
result3: overall, di decreased n2o emission by 48.8% (ci: 43.7 to 53.5%).
result4: on average, application of ni reduced n2o emission by 56% (53 to 60%). dcd and dmpp application significantly reduced n2o emission by 57.6 (53.9 to 61.3%) and 62.6% (48.5 to 74.6%), respectively. reduction in n2o emissions ranged from 33% (23 to 43%) for paddy to 58% (55 to 62%) for grassland. the higher the baseline n2o emission (i.e. emissions from the conventional fertilizer treatments), the greater the reduction in n2o loss by ni. for example, the average n2o reduction was 67% (61 to 72%) for situations where baseline emissions exceeded 20 kg n/ha, compared to a 50% (41 to 59%) reduction for baseline emissions of <1 kg n/ha. soil properties factors: ni was more effective in reducing n2o emissions in fine-textured soils (77% [56 to 88%] reduction, compared to 59% [55 to 63%], or 44% [38 to 50%] in coarse or medium-textured soils), acidic soils (64% [59 to 69%] reduction for soils of ph<6, compared to 48% [42 to 55%] or 41% [31 to 52%] for soil ph 6–8 or >8) and soils with intermediate soc (63% [58 to 67%] reduction for soc 10–40 g/kg, compared to 32% [24 to 38%] and 50% [42 to 57%] for soils with lower or higher soc).
general_conclusion: polimer coated fertilisers and fertilisers amended with double inhibitors significantly decreased n2o emission. urease ihnibitors application did not significantly decreased n2o emission. nitrification ihnibitors are a viable option to reduce n2o emission. among nitrification ihnibitors forms, dcd and dmpp application significantly reduced n2o emissions.

search_strategy: the authors conducted a detailed review of literature published in peer-reviewed journals through 2008 and identified field studies that compared n2o and no emissions from plots to which ni, pcf or ui were applied with those from plots to which conventional fertilizers were applied.
selection_criteria: 1)only field experiment data were included; small-scale experiments such as incubation or soil column experiments were excluded; 2) papers those emission data with the same total nitrogen application rate for treatment and control; 3) studies with no replication or no reported number of replications were excluded from the analysis.
data_analysis: to conduct a meta-analysis, the mean n2o and no emissions, sd, and number of replicates from the treatment and control are needed. when no sd was reported, the authors assigned the average sd derived from other sd reported datasets – that is, 23% of means for n2o emissions – to include as many  studies as possible in the analysis (higgins & green, 2008). if outlying data points were not obvious artifacts, outliers were included in the analysis to illustrate variability. using response ratios, a weighted meta-analysis was conducted. mean effect size for each category was calculated, with bias-corrected 95% confidential intervals (cis), using a bootstrapping procedure (9999 iterations). the meta analysis was conducted using meta-win version 2 (rosenberg et al., 2000).
background: Agricultural fields are an important anthropogenic source of atmospheric nitrous oxide (N2O) and nitric oxide (NO). Although many field studies have tested the effectiveness of possible mitigation options on N2O and NO emissions, the effectiveness of each option varies across sites due to environmental factors and field management.
objective: the aim of this study was to integrate results of field measurements to evaluate quantitatively the effect of enhanced-efficiency fertilizers (eefs) [i.e., nitrification inhibitors (ni), polymer-coated fertilizers (pcf), and urease inhibitors (ui)] on n2o and no emissions from agricultural fields, using meta analysis. here, only results regarding the effect of pcf and ui on n2o emissions are reported.
result1: the effect of all ui on n2o emissions was not significantly different from that of conventional fertilizers (publication bias detected by rosenthal's method but not with orwin's method).  among ui forms, nbpt application was not significantly effective in reducing n2o emissions while the results suggest that hydroquinone significantly reduced n2o emissions (-5%, 95% confidence interval (ci): -6% to -4%), but the number of observations for this ui form was low (n = 2).
result2: overall, pcf significantly reduced n2o emissions (-35%, ci: -58% to -14%) compared with those of conventional fertilizers.for upland fields, the mean effect of pcf was not significantly different from that of conventional fertilizers. in contrast to upland fields, the mean effect of pcfs for grassland showed a very significant reduction ( -77%, ci: - 88% to  -58%) compared with conventional fertilizers. in upland fields, the effect of pcf varied with soil type. the mean effect of pcfs on uplands of all soil types showed a significant reduction of n2o emissions excepted for andosol upland fields (publication bias was suggested for uplands of all soil types, upland andosols, and uplands of other soils by rosenthal’s method, but not by orwin’s method).
result3: on average, ni significantly reduced n2o emissions (mean: -38%, ci: - 44% to  -31%). all types of ni included in the analysis were significantly effective, but the size of the effect varied among nis: dicyandiamide (dcd; -30%, -36% to -26%), nitrapyrin (-50%, -55% to -30%), ca-carbide (-51%, -65% to -32%), 3,4-dimethyl pyrazole phosphate (dmpp; -50%, -55% to -42%), thiosulfate (-19%, -33% to -15%), and neem (-14%, -25% to -7%). effects of ni on n2o emissions also varied with land-use type: upland fields (-34%, -43% to -26%), grassland (-54%, -60% to -43%), and paddy fields (-30%, -39% to -18%).
general_conclusion: polymer-coated fertilisers were effective in reducing n2o emission, while urease inhibitors did not significantly reduced n2o emission. the use of nitrification inhibitors is a potent and extendable mitigation option for n2o emission.

search_strategy: an extensive search of the scientific literature, using web of science (thompson reuters) and google scholar (google inc.) databases, was conducted in may 2015 for studies that reported n2o emissions with and without eefs in major cereal production systems. the database search was supplemented by reviewing the reference lists of the studies found in our search and those used in the prior meta-analysis by akiyama et al. (2010).
selection_criteria: 1)field studies on rice, corn, and/or wheat production (any additional components such as laboratory incubation or greenhouse experiments were excluded);  2) studies measuring n2o emissions for at least one complete growing season without missing n2o fluxes during the days following fertilization, tillage, and rainfall or irrigation events; 3) means and number of replicates for each treatment comparison reported.
data_analysis: using the response ratio and variance from individual studies, metawin version 2.1 statistical software was used to calculate weighted mean effect sizes and generate bias-corrected 95% confidence intervals (cis) using a bootstrapping procedure (4999 iterations) for each category.
background: Previous studies on the effectiveness of enhanced efficiency fertilizers (EEF), i.e. nitrification inhibitors (NI), urease inhibitors (UIs), controlled-release N fertilizers (CRFs) and combined application of both NI and UI, i.e. double inhibitors (DIs), in reducing nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions reported mixed results depending on their mode of action, soil and environmental conditions, and management factors.
objective: using meta-analysis, the study provides an overview of eef efficiency in reducing n2o emissions across eef types, crops, soils, and management practices. the main objectives of this study are to evaluate the effect of individual eef (ni, ui, di and crf) on soil n2o emission and crop yields in rice, corn and wheat systems and to identify the soil and management factors in which these eef are most effective. here the results related to ui, di and crf effect on soil n2o emissions are reported.
result1: the overall effect of ui on n2o emissions in the present meta-analysis did not differ from zero.
result2: in average, di reduced n2o emissions by 30% compared with conventional n fertilizers.
result3: this analysis indicated that crf reduced n2o emissions by 19% relative to conventional n fertilizers in cereal systems.
general_conclusion: compared with conventional n fertilisation, the use of fertilisers amended with double inhibitors and controlled-release fertilisers significantly reduced n2o emission while fertilisers amended with urease inhibitors did not impact n2o emission. fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors reduced n2o emissions by 38% (95%ci: -44 to -33%).

search_strategy: a comprehensive literature search for field studies of north american corn-based systems published through july 2014 was conducted. authors also compiled numerous other observation-level details, filling in some information from publicly available soil and weather databases.
selection_criteria: 1)papers about agriculture or n losses, addressed n losses and transport after the field; 2) papers that examine n fertilizer management; 3) performed in north america;  4) performed in corn systems; 5) not conducted in laboratory or greenhouse.
data_analysis: first, standard meta-analysis with effect sizes was applied to a sub-set of the data that included direct simultaneous comparisons of two or more fertilizer management techniques. second, hierarchical multi-level models were fitted to simultaneously evaluate multiple management and environmental drivers including soil and climate. both statistical approaches use data from multiple studies to determine the overall impact of management, identifying significant factors that may not be otherwise observed in individual studies, and conversely, finding other effects that apply only under specific conditions and cannot be broadly anticipated.
background: Effective management of nitrogen (N) in agricultural landscapes must account for how nitrate (NO3) leaching and nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions respond to local field-scale management and to broader environmental drivers such as climate and soil. Recent syntheses and models provide evidence of nonlinear exponential responses of N losses to fertilization rate but the effects of other fertilization practices on nitrogen (N) losses remains unclear.
objective: this research sought to address three questions: 1) how do nitrous oxide (n2o) emissions and nitrate (no3) leaching losses respond to n fertilizer application rate, source, timing, and placement, 2) how do effects of fertilizer management compare to effects of, and potentially depend on, variation in climate and soil, and 3) how do no3 and n2o losses covary with management, climate, and soil. here results concerning the effect of double inhibitor (di) or polymer-coated urea (pcu) application on n2o emissions are reported.
result1: substantial reductions in yield-scaled n2o emissions resulted when di was applied, compared to urea (26%) or to uan (graphical interpretation).
result2: the use of pcu instead of conventional urea had no significant impact on n2o yield-scaled emissions.
general_conclusion: fertilisers amended with double inhibitors application significantly reduced n2o yield-scaled emission, while polymer coated urea application had no effect on n2o yield-scaled emission.

search_strategy: a literature review of english and chinese language peer-reviewed studies on n2o emissions from chinese wheat and maize fields prior to january 2017 was conducted using thomson reuters' isi-web of science research database and the china knowledge resource integrated database.
selection_criteria: 1)measurements were conducted under field conditions; 2) n2o flux rates were measured during an entire crop growth period using the static chamber method; 3) n2o emission and grain yield were determined simultaneously.
data_analysis: the mean effect sizes were calculated from lnrr of individual studies. individual studies were weighted depending on the number of experiment replicates and the number of n2o flux measurements per months. the meta-analysis was performed using metawin 2.1. mean effect sizes were estimated using the random-effects model. the 95% confidence intervals (cis) of the mean effect sizes were calculated using the bootstrapping with 4999 iterations.
background: NItrous oxide (N2O) emissions from croplands in China occur mostly during wheat and maize growing seasons in China. As a result, mitigating yield-scaled N2O emissions during these growing seasons in China plays an important role in the sustainable development of global cereal crop production.
objective: using meta-analysis, this study integrated the results of field measurements to assess the mitigation potential of major agronomic practices, including the application controlled release fertilizers (crf), on yield-scaled n2o emissions from croplands during wheat and maize growing seasons in china. here the results related to the effect of crf on n2o emission were reported.
result1: compared to conventional inorganic fertilizer, n2o emission was reduced 18.2% by crf
result2: yield-scaled n2o emission was significantly mitigated by 22.0% due to crf.
result3: compared to conventional n fertilizer, ni significantly reduced n2o emissions by 34.2%. wheat and maize yield increased 12.9% due to ni application compared to conventional n fertilizer, thereby resulting in a significant reduction in yield-scaled n2o emission by 41.7%
general_conclusion: controlled-release fertilisers were recommended for the mitigation of n2o emission during wheat and maize growing seasons. nitrification ihnibitors are recommended for the mitigation of both area-scaled and yield-scaled n2o emission during wheat and maize growing seasons.
knowledge_gaps: no data on other crops than wheat and maize. only n2o emissions during wheat and maize growing season.

search_strategy: data were acquired by searching existing literature published before june 2015 using the isi-web of science and google scholar. the following key words were used for searching such as meta-analysis, efficiency, nitrification inhibitor, dcd, dmpp, inorganic n, n leaching, gaseous emission and plant productivity. and the search terms were complemented with a search through the literature cited in the articles found.
selection_criteria: 1)field studies were selected and laboratory incubation studies were excluded; 2) at least one of the selected variables were measured; 3) means and sample sizes had to be reported; 4) treatment replicates were at least of three, etc.
data_analysis: the mean effect sizes were estimated using the formulas described by bai et al. (2013) and are weighed (for each study, the weighting factor was calculated as the inverse of the pooled variance, then adjusted by the total number of observations per site, when multiple observations were extracted from the same study). then a fixed-effects model option in software metawin 2.1 was employed for calculation of grouped effect sizes. confidence intervals (cis) on the weighted effect size were generated using bootstrapping (9999 iterations).
background: Nitrification inhibitors (NI) have been developed to mitigate nitrogen (N) losses through blocking the first stage of nitrification. Among the NI commercially available, dicyandiamide (DCD) and 3, 4-dimethypyrazole phosphate (DMPP) are the most widely used, but the difference of their performances across field sites is less clear.
objective: in this study, using a meta-analysis approach, authors compared the efficiency of dcd and dmpp on altering plant n uptake under various conditions including soil ph values, fertilizer n forms, fertilizer n rates and crop types.
result1: on average, dmpp and dcd application significantly decreased no3- leaching (no quantitative results provided) and din leaching (no quantitative results provided). the effect of dcd and dmpp on nh4+ are contradictory: dmpp application significantly increased nh4+ leaching (no quantitative results provided), while dcd application significantly decreased nh4+ leaching.
result2: in neutral soils or along with urea, dmpp was more effective in decreasing soil no3- leaching than dcd.
general_conclusion: application of fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitor decreased no3- leaching, din leaching. nh4+ leaching was increased by dmpp application, while it was decreased by dcd application.

objective: the objective of the study is to obtain a global view on the productivity and n-loss reduction performance of eefs through a holistic evaluation of all four eef types in different cropping systems under wide ranging conditions. here the results regarding the effect of pcf, ui and di on nitrate (no3-) leaching are reported.
result1: overall, pcf application reduced no3- leaching by 65.9% (95% confidence interval (ci): 41.8 to 81.3%). the effect of pcf application was significantly higher in paddy (mean effect: 91.9%, ci: 83.6 to 96.8%) than in dryland (42.3%, ci: 20.2 to 66.9%).
result2: ui application did not significantly decreased no3- leaching.
result3: no3- leaching was reduced by 45% (ci: 38 to 50%) by ni amendment. dcd and dmpp application significantly decreased no3- leaching by 43.8 (37.0 to 50.2%) and 54.2% (48.6 to 59.1%), respectively.
result4: ni affected n losses in a similar pattern across all cropping systems, reducing no3- leaching loss by 35% (ci: 13 to 52%) in dryland to 52% (ci: 45 to 53%) in paddy.
result5: di application did not significantly decreased no3- leaching.
general_conclusion: polimer coated fertilisers application decreased no3- leaching. the effect of fertiliser amended with urease inhibitors or with double inhibitors was not significant. nitrification inhibitors (more specifically, dcd and dmpp) significantly reduced no3- leaching.

search_strategy: published peer-review studies were identified from several databases (included google scholar, web of science, and china knowledge resource integrated) by using the key search terms “urease inhibitor”, “nitrification inhibitor”, “double inhibitor”, “nitrogen stabilizer”, “nitrogen recovery”, “15n recovery”.
selection_criteria: 1)field, pot or lysimeter studies; 2) 15n tracer method had to be used to determine fertilizer nitrogen uptake by the crop or retained in the soil ; 3) n derived from fertilizer (ndff) or fertilizer n recovery in the crop and the soil have to be reported; 4) control (fertilizer without inhibitors) and treatments (fertilizer with inhibitors) have to be subjected to the same management (such as fertilizer type and application rate, irrigation, or micro-plot size).
data_analysis: the mean effect size of each group was calculated by a categorical random-effect model and its 95 % confidence intervals (cis) were generated using a bootstrapping procedure with 4999 iterations. the heterogeneity in different categorical groups (qbetween/qtotal) for each explanatory variable is also reported in table s1. the potential impact of study methods (field or pot) and sampling procedures (premature or mature harvest) were tested. for further analysis of the importance of the explanatory variables to the effects of n-stabilizers on n recovery, boosted regression tree (brt) analysis was used to rank their contribution for different recovery n pools (crop recovery, soil retention and total recovery).
background: Nitrogen (N) fertilizer stabilizers (including urease inhibitors, i.e. UI, nitrification inhibitors, and double inhibitors, i.e. DI) are promising tools to mitigate N pollution from agricultural production. A better understanding is required on how N stabilizers impact the fate of fertilizer-N and which factors (such as soil properties and management conditions) have a major contribution to the efficacy of the N stabilizers.
objective: the aim of this study was to assess the efficacy of n stabilizers (ui and di) in improving agronomic and environmental management of nitrogenous fertilizers and enable the provision of advice on the application of n stabilizers for sustainable agricultural production. here the results of ui effect and di effect on fertilizer-n crop recovery are reported.
result1: fertilizers amended with ui significantly enhanced fertilizer n-recovery through crop uptake by 24.1%.
result2: fertilizers amended with di significantly enhanced fertilizer n-recovery through crop uptake by 47.6%.
result3: ui amendments better increased crop fertilizer-n recovery under paddy field than dry land conditions.
result4: fertilizers amended with ni significantly enhanced fertilizer-n recovery through crop uptake by 10.5%. among ni types, dcd and dmpp application have no significant effect on recovery in crop. the best crop fertilizer-n recoveries were associated with using nitrapyrin as ni. the best crop fertilizer-n recoveries were associated with organic fertilizer or urea; increase in total fertilizer-n recovery in the soil-crop system was associated ni amendment to urea.
result5: higher increase of crop fertilizer-n recovery was  associated when relatively high n rate (above 100 kg n ha−1) was applied. ni impact on crop fertilizer-n recovery was higher when added to a neutral soil with medium som content. best crop fertilizer-n recoveries were observed under paddy field than dry land conditions. recovery of applied fertilizer-n in the soil-crop system under paddy field conditions was improved by 22.5 % for ni amendment. the greatest soil n retention was associated with a higher n application rate (above 100 kg n ha−1), multiple application timings, and neutral coarse textured soils.
general_conclusion: application of fertilisers amended with urease inhibitors and fertilisers amended with double inhibitors significantly increased crop recovery. fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors application significantly enhanced fertiliser-n recovery through crop uptake.

search_strategy: data were acquired by searching existing literature published before june 2015 using the isi-web of science and google scholar. the following key words were used for searching such as meta-analysis, efficiency, nitrification inhibitor, dcd, dmpp, inorganic n, n leaching, gaseous emission and plant productivity. and the search terms were complemented with a search through the literature cited in the articles found.
selection_criteria: 1)field studies were selected and laboratory incubation studies were excluded; 2) at least one of the selected variables were measured; 3) means and sample sizes had to be reported; 4) treatment replicates were at least of three, etc.
data_analysis: the mean effect sizes were estimated using the formulas described by bai et al. (2013) and are weighed (for each study, the weighting factor was calculated as the inverse of the pooled variance, then adjusted by the total number of observations per site, when multiple observations were extracted from the same study). then a fixed-effects model option in software metawin 2.1 was employed for calculation of grouped effect sizes. confidence intervals (cis) on the weighted effect size were generated using bootstrapping (9999 iterations).
background: Nitrification inhibitors (NI) have been developed to mitigate nitrogen (N) losses through blocking the first stage of nitrification. Among the NI commercially available, dicyandiamide (DCD) and 3, 4-dimethypyrazole phosphate (DMPP) are the most widely used, but the difference of their performances across field sites is less clear.
objective: in this study, using a meta-analysis approach, authors compared the efficiency of dcd and dmpp on altering plant n uptake under various conditions including soil ph values, fertilizer n forms, fertilizer n rates and crop types.
result1: dcd application increased plant n uptake by 18.1%. dmpp application did not significantly increased plant n uptake.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitor dcd significantly increased plant n uptake. in contrast, fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitor dmpp did not significantly impacted plant n uptake.

search_strategy: references given by edmeades and mcbride (2011, 2012) were examined and additional searching for trials and reports was also undertaken with the internet (sfp, 2013; google web; google scholar; stateuniversity annual reports) and databases (cab abstracts and massey university general database search) searching for keywords of chemistry terms for the active ingredient. researchers were contacted, if required and possible, to obtain sufficiently detailed research reports.
selection_criteria: the current study analyzed all trials that metthe stated criteria of edmeades and mcbride (2012).
data_analysis: trial means were analyzed after natural log transformation to reduce the effect of a positive skew towards high response ratios and improve normality of residuals from the statistical models. since measures of trial variability were not available for all sustain green trials, confidence intervals were constructed without weighting.
background: Efficient fertilizer use is crucial for economic and environmental reasons. Fertilizer enhancers can increase nutrient use efficiency (NUE) but their efficacy needs to be assessed appropriately.
objective: the aim of this study is to estimate the effects of three fertilizer-enhancing products using meta-analysis. here, the results regarding the effect of sustainn green (urease inhibitor-coated urea) application on nue are reported.
result1: the estimated mean increased response ratio was 1.2 (95% confidence interval (ci) 1.11–1.34, n = 28, symmetrical log transformation) meaning that there were around 1.2 times the nitrogen response from urease inhibitors than from urea alone.
result2: mean response difference (kg dry matter (dm)/kg n for urease inhibitors - kg dm/kg n for urea) over all trials was calculated as 3.3 kg dm/kg n (95% ci 1.80–4.89, n = 28).
general_conclusion: the use of urease inhibitor increased nue compared to conventional n fertiliser.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed ni studies were searched using web of science (1984–2013).
selection_criteria: 1)for soil ph and concentrations of nh4+ , no3- and din, the average value across a whole crop rotation had to be reported. 2) for leaching loss of nh4+, no3- and din, and emissions of n2o, ch4, no and nh3, the cumulative values for a whole crop rotation had to be reported, or the reported data allows to estimate the cumulative values for a whole crop rotation.
data_analysis: the mean effect sizes with bias-corrected 95% confidential intervals (ci) were estimated using bootstrap resampling procedure (adams et al., 1997), allowing studies that did not report standard errors/deviations to be included in the analysis (adams et al., 1997). total heterogeneity among the categorical group (qt) was partitioned into within-group heterogeneity (qw) and between-group heterogeneity (qb), where qt, qw and qb have chi-square distributions. publication bias was assessed with studies that reported standard errors/deviations. egger’s regression test was used to quantify publication bias, which has higher power to detect the bias than the rank correlation method (sterne et al., 2001). meta-analysis was performed by the software metawin 2.1 (sinauer associates, inc. sunderland, ma, usa).
background: Anthropogenic activities, and in particular the use of synthetic nitrogen (N) fertilizer, have doubled global annual reactive N inputs in the past 50–100 years, causing deleterious effects on the environment through increased N leaching and nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions. Yet, no study has comprehensively assessed how inhibiting nitrification affects both hydrologic and gaseous losses of N and plant nitrogen use efficiency.
objective: the objective of this study is to better understand how nitrification inhibitors (ni) application affects air pollutant emission caused by n fertilizers, by conducting a comprehensive meta-analysis, and to assess whether the responses of this variable will be altered by ni forms, ecosystem types, fertilizer types and soil texture. here the results related to the effect of nis on nitric oxide (no) and amonia (nh3) emission were reported.
result1: on average, ni increased plant n concentration (7%, ci: 1–16%), n uptake (15%, ci: 11–20%) and n recovery (58%, ci: 34–93%), although publication bias was detected for n concentration (egger’s p-value < 0.01).
result2: ni impact on plant n concentration and on n recovery differed between ni types.
general_conclusion: on average, the results suggest a higher nue under fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors application, as indicated by greater plant n uptake, n recovery rate and higher plant-n concentration.

search_strategy: the web of science and china national knowledge infrastructure database were employed to search peer-reviewed studies published before march 2016.
selection_criteria: 1)only the field, pot, and lysimeter studies on rice, wheat, or corn growth were included. the crop grain had to be harvested and weighted at the physiological mature stage. 2) means and samples size had to be reported with a minimum of three replicates. 3) the application rates of agricultural materials had to be reported, such as fertilizers (n, p, and k) and inhibitors (ni and ui), for the consideration of the cost-benefit analysis.
data_analysis: mean effect sizes and the 95% confidence intervals (cis) were generated by a bootstrapping procedure with 4999 iterations, using metawin 2.1.
background: Knowledge-based nitrogen (N) management, which is designed for a better synchronization of crop N demand with N supply, is critical for global food security and environmental sustainability. Yet, a comprehensive assessment on how these N management practices affect food production, greenhouse gas emission (GHG), and N pollution in China is lacking.
objective: the objective of the study is to evaluate the overall effects of seven knowledge-based n management practices on crop productivity, nitrous oxide (n2o) emission, and major reactive n (nr) losses (ammonia, nh3; n leaching and runoff), for rice, wheat, and corn yields in china by conducting a comprehensive meta-analysis. here the results regarding the effect of controlled-release n fertilisers (crf) and urease inhibitors (ui) on aboveground n uptake are reported.
result1: on average, the aboveground n uptake was significantly increased by 10.9% (95%ci:9.0-12.8%) for crf application and by 5.9%% (95%ci: 3.4-8.5%) for ui application. crf impact on tn uptake was lower in soils with organic carbon content (soc) higher than 20 g/kg (4.9%, 95%ci: 1.3-8.2%) compared to soils with soc lower than 10 g/kg (10.6%, 95%ci: 8.4-13.0%). higher impact of crf was reported in acidic soils (3.7%, 0.6-7%), compared to neutral (10.5%, 95%ci: 7.9-13.3%). crf impact on tn uptake was also lower in case of intermediate n application rate, i.e. comprised between 200 and 300 kg n / ha (8.3%, 95%ci: 6.4-11.4%), compared to higher n application rates (23.15%, 14.3-34.0%). the impact of ui on abovegroung n uptake was not significant in intermediate soil organic carbon content (soc) and in acidic soils.
result2: the grain nue was significantly improved by employing crf or ui by 34.4 (95%ci: 29.6-39.5%) and 31.3% (95%ci: 22.0-42.0%), respectively. ui’s impact on nue was not significant when soc was higher than 20 g/kg and in acidic soils. ui impact was significantly higher for intermediate n application rates, i.e. when n application rate is comprised between 200 and 300 kg n/ha (59%, 95%ci: 24.7-108.6%)) than for lower (31.5%, 95%ci: 21.0-43.8%) or higher rates (11.8%, 95%ci: 5.2-18.7%).
result3: on average, the aboveground n uptake was significantly increased by 12.1% (ci: 8.5 to 16.0%) when ni was applied. overall, nue was also significantly improved by ni application by 26.5% (ci: 20.4 to 33.6%). the increase of nue was equivalent after dcd (26.7%, 17.9 to 37.4%) and dmpp (27.9%, 17.8 to 38.3%) application.
general_conclusion: overall, controlled-release fertilisers and fertilisers amended with urease inhibitors application significantly increased aboveground n uptake and grain nue. the use of fertilisers amended with nitrification inhibitors is effective in increasing total abovegroung n uptake and nue.

search_strategy: authors searched for peer-reviewed publications between 1980 and 2016 on efficacy of eefs via the web of science and google scholar using search terms of enhanced-efficiency fertilizer, polymer coated fertilizer, urease inhibitor, nitrification inhibitor, yield, nue, nitrous oxide, ammonia, and nitrate leaching.
selection_criteria: 1)one or more of the efficacy indicators had to be reported; 2) data must have originated from field experiments (i.e. laboratory-based studies were excluded); 3) the experiments must have been replicated; 4) information needed to be provided regarding cropping systems, inhibitor type or the coating material of controlled release fertilizer; 5) management practices such as n fertilizer type, application rate, method, and placement, crop residue management (retention or removal), tillage, irrigation, and use of other agricultural chemicals had to be the same for the eef treatment and control.
data_analysis: the efficacy of a given eef type was assessed by meta-analysis procedure. more than half of the datasets did not report standard error/deviation. to overcome this hurdle while maintaining a robust meta-analysis, we used the bootstrap resampling procedure (5000 iterations) to obtain the mean rr with a bias-corrected 95% confidence interval (ci) (adams, gurevitch, & rosenberg, 1997). in addition, we calculated the heterogeneity in lnrr between all studies (qt), within-group (qw), and between-group (qb).
background: Enhanced-efficiency fertilizers (EEFs) (polymer-coated fertilizers PCF, nitrification inhibitors NI, urease inhibitors UI, and double inhibitors DI, i.e. urease and nitrification inhibitors combined) have been developed to better synchronize fertilizer nitrogen  (N) release with crop uptake, offering the potential for enhanced N use efficiency (NUE) and reduced losses. Can EEFs play a significant role in helping address the N management challenge?
objective: the objective of the study is to obtain a global view on the productivity and n-loss reduction performance of eefs through a holistic evaluation of all four eef types in different cropping systems under wide ranging conditions. here the results regarding the effect of pcf, ui and di on n use efficiency (nue) are reported.
result1: overall, pcf application increased nue by 8.7% (95% confidence interval (ci): 3.7 to 13.9%). nue responses to pcf were significant in rice-paddy systems (mean effect: 26.4%, ci: 15.6 to 38.7%) as well as vegetable production systems (11.2%, ci: 3.7 to 18.9%). where temperature and rainfall were favorable for growth (10–20°c and 800–1200 mm), pcf boosted nue by 13.9 (ci: 6.2 to 22.1%) and by 15.0% (ci: 9.4 to 20.9%), respectively. the effect of pcf was significant in neutral soils (5.1%, ci: 0.2 to 11.6%) but not in acidic and alkaline soils. the effect of pcf was not significant in soils with soil organic carbon (soc) content lower than 10 g/kg; when soc was intermediate (10-40 g/kg) or high (> 40 g/kg), pcf application increased nue by 8.3% (ci: 2.0 to 15.0%) and by 29.7% (ci: 4.1 to 61.6%), respectively. pcf application increased nue when n was applied in surface (mean effect: 13.9%, ci: 6.0 to 22.1%), else not.
