objective: the objective of this meta-analysis is to quantify the mitigation efficiency of several mitigation strategies for manure composting and stockpiling to reduce ghg emissions (methane (ch4) and nitrous oxyde (n2o)).
result1: the results showed that additives can be effective in ch4 mitigation, with mitigation efficiency of -97.0% (p=0.102) but it may increase n2o emission by 135.0% (p=0.109). in both cases, p value are above 0.05, so the results were considered as not significant.
result2: for beef manure stockpiling, ch4 emission and n2o emissions can be increased by 29.8% (p<0.05) and 13.0% (p=0.128) with straw or sawdust covering, respectively. in the case of n2o, p value is above 0.05, so the result was considered as not significant.
result3: incorporation can decrease n2o emission by 65.0% (p<0.05) when compared with manure surface application.
result4: manure additives such as biochar and nitrification inhibitor resulted an integrated n2o mitigation efficiency of -28.0% (p=0.100). the p value was superior to 0.05 so the result was considered as not significant.
general_conclusion: this study shows that the different tested mitigation strategies were not significantly effective in reducing ghg emissions. stockpile covers had negative effect on ch4 emissions.
knowledge_gaps: there are only 2 papers that studied the impact of compost additives on gas emissions from beef cattle manure, with one study specified for ch4 and n2o and the other for nh3; no research is available for the effect of biofilter on compost ch4 and n2o emissions specifically for beef cattle manure;

search_strategy: studies related to manure management and emissions of nh3, n2o and ch4 were searched using the bibliographical database scopus, until the beginning of 2014.
selection_criteria: only data from studies with reference treatments (i.e. without mitigation/processing measures) were included in our database, so as to allow side-by-side comparisons. to maximize the number of studies, both laboratory and field experiments were taken into account. the reported experiments and measurements were predominately conducted in eu, united states and canada. mean values of replicates for each treatment were included in the database. manure characteristics (e.g. manure type, dry matter content, total n content, ammoniacal n content and ph), land use parameters (e.g. soil texture, vegetation), environmental conditions (e.g. temperature, seasons and geographical locations) were also included, and used to, if possible, quantify their relationships with emissions and the effectiveness of the measures.
data_analysis: for calculation of grouped effect sizes, a mixed-effects model was used and performed in the nlme package of r statistical software version 3.1. experimental sites were considered as a random effect factor, to allow accounting for variances among studies. the lnr of individual pairwise comparison was the dependent variable. the mean effect size and the 95% confidence intervals (cis) of each categorical group were estimated. the significance of the effects on emissions was statistically assessed at 0.05 level. in the graphs (forest plots), the ‘effect-size’ (the mean value and 95% cis) of each grouping was transformed back (i.e. exponentially transformed) and converted to a percentage change in gas emissions relative to the reference treatment.
background: Livestock manure contributes considerably to global emissions of ammonia (NH3) and greenhouse gases (GHG), especially methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O). Various measures have been developed to mitigate these emissions, but most of these focus on one specific gas and/or emission source.
objective: the overall objective of this study is to make a quantitative assessment of the effects of (sets of) mitigation options on the nh3, n2o and ch4 emissions from the whole manure chain, namely livestock housing, manure storage and land application. first, the impacts of a suite of nh3 mitigation measures on nh3 emissions at individual stages, and also the associated impacts on n2o and ch4 emissions were analysed by means of a meta-analysis of published data. second, we evaluated the overall impacts of combinations of mitigation measures (including manure processing) on nh3, ch4, and (direct and indirect) n2o emissions from the whole manure management chain through scenario analysis.
result1: slurry acidification also led to a statistically significant reduction (on average, 87%) of ch4 emissions during slurry storage
result2: methane emissions were slightly suppressed by artificial film covers, but the effect was not statistically significant (p > 0.05). similarly, for all other grouped side-by-side comparisons, the changes in ch4 emissions showed negative mean values. these effects were not statistically significant.
result3: emissions of n2o were enhanced by a factor of 8.6, when stored slurry was covered by chopped straw (p < 0.01). by contrast, slurry covered with artificial film decreased n2o emissions by 98% (p < 0.01).
general_conclusion: slurry acidification significantly decreased emissions of nh3 and ch4 from slurry storages. covering slurry storages with straw significantly increased n2o emissions, covers with plastic films significantly reduced n2o. covers had no effects on ch4 emissions.
knowledge_gaps: the results collected did not allow comparing management options across animal species (e.g. pigs vs. cattle). data from both field-and laboratory-scale studies were included in our database as data solely from field-scale studies were insufficient.

search_strategy: the authors gathered the available peer-reviewed literature published before november 2013 concerning gaseous emissions during composting and/or storage of organic solid waste. articles were searched on the isi web of knowledge and google scholar database by combining specific keywords related to treatment.
selection_criteria: first, studies describing data of ch4, n2o, or nh3 fluxes (at least one of them) over a reported measurement period were collected. we decided to analyze gaseous losses in terms of cumulative emissions, as a proportion of initial carbon (c) or n content in the waste material (%ch4-c, %nh3-n, %n2o-n). thus, to harmonize the data included in our dataset, in some cases, it was necessary to transform the reported data into values referred to an element mass basis. those studies not describing results as cumulative emissions or not reporting enough details to perform this conversion were excluded from the analysis. additionally, we decided to include articles which expressed results just in terms of total n losses, based on a n mass balance, because this approach can add valuable information with regard to the general influence of different treatments and conditions in the overall n conservation through solid waste management. this parameter involves the already mentioned n gaseous emissions (nh3, n2o) but also any other kind of n losses via gas or liquid, such as dinitrogen (n2) or nitrate.
data_analysis: the only criterion used for weighting was the number of aggregated independent treatments contained in our composite datasets. weighted mean effect sizes of each category were calculated, with bias-corrected 95% confidence intervals (cis) generated by a bootstrapping procedure (10 000 iterations), using metawin software. mean effects of treatments were considered different from the control at the 0.05 significance level when the 95% confidence interval did not overlap zero.
background: The establishment of sustainable soil waste management practices implies minimizing their environmental losses associated with climate change (greenhouse gases: GHGs) and ecosystems acidification (ammonia: NH3). Although a number of management strategies for solid waste management have been investigated to quantify nitrogen (N) and carbon (C) losses in relation to varied environmental and operational conditions, their overall effect is still uncertain.
objective: the authors have analyzed the current scientific information through a systematic review. the authors quantified the response of ghg emissions, nh3 emissions, and total n losses to different solid waste management strategies (conventional solid storage, turned composting, forced aerated composting, covering, compaction, addition/substitution of bulking agents and the use of additives).
result1: unlike composting methods, covering and compaction are management strategies which involve a restriction in the o2 supply within the waste material, thus limiting biological activity and preventing temperature increase. no significant effect on ch4 or n2o emissions was observed by covering or compacting practices.
result2: when aiming at reducing n2o emissions, the application of specific additives has not resulted in consistent effects.
general_conclusion: covering or compaction did not show significant effects on reducing either ch4 or n2o emissions. the use of specific additives has no effect on n2o, while few data where available for ch4. nevertheless, their effectiveness varies depending on the substance, dosage, and operational conditions.
knowledge_gaps: the number of studies reporting ch4 losses from solid waste management applying additives is limited. our results are based on 9 experiments from only two studies examining the effect of phosphogypsum addition on gaseous emissions. average values suggest that this strategy tends to reduce ch4 emissions (mean: -59%). however, more data are still required to confirm this trend. although the number of experiments investigating the influence of management practices on ghg emissions has grown during the last decade, an important restriction of our dataset is that there is still a limited knowledge basis with respect to gaseous losses from solid waste management, particularly for ch4 and n2o emissions at commercial scale. in addition to this, the collected results showed large variability, which emphasizes the need to produce additional data through precise and accurate research methods to obtain robust ef estimates that can help reduce current uncertainties.

background: There is a need for a comprehensive review of recent Canadian relevant research evaluating options for mitigating GHG emissions from enteric fermentation and manure management.
objective: the objectives of this paper were to (1) review recent canadian research on enteric methane (ch4) emissions, and ch4 and nitrous oxide (n2o) emissions from stored manure related to dairy cattle, and (2) identify strategies for ghg mitigation that can currently be used in canadian dairy farms and promising technologies that have potential to be used as mitigation strategies in the future.
result1: one study observed about 50% lower total ghg emissions (ch4 and n2o) from the completely emptied manure storage compared with emissions from the partially emptied storage. in another pilot level study, the presence of a small quantity of inoculum (∼8%) could support the immediate production of appreciable amounts of ch4 from manure within 10 d after refilling the storage with new manure, indicating that the storage should be emptied nearly completely to prevent old manure becoming an effective inoculum.
result2: several recent experiments evaluating the effect of various cover types on ch4 and n2o emissions from dairy manure have indicated appreciable reductions of these two gases combined (up to 26% reduction) compared with emissions from uncovered slurry.
general_conclusion: this review identify several promising strategies for mitigating ghg emissions from dairy manure, including ad, solid–liquid separation, composting, manure storage covers, and complete emptying of liquid manure storage at spring application. these results are uncertain due to the methodology used in this study (only systematic review, no quantitative analysis).
knowledge_gaps: no quantitative statistical analysis is reported in this synthesis study.

search_strategy: emission reduction potentials for the identified abatement options were estimated using effective observations from published literature according to the methods described in recent studies that focus on emission abatement in manure management systems.
selection_criteria: the selection criteria were as follows: (i) the animal category was either cattle or pigs; (ii) the study was subject to at least one of the eight chosen abatement options; (iii) the study measured and reported either nh3 and/or ghg emissions for at least one of the manure management stages of housing, treatment, storage, or application; (iv) the study included data on reference treatments and base emissions; and (v) the article was peer reviewed and available in english. this resulted in a selection of 89 peer-reviewed papers and reports measuring nh3 and/or ghg emissions from on-farm and experimental farm settings.
data_analysis: descriptive statistics were used to quantify and describe the emission reductions. means and sds were calculated and reported for all existing datasets. high variability occurred in several instances, with sds exceeding the mean value such that reported trends may be merely indicative. the use of complex statistical models was not possible due to a small sample size.
background: Farm livestock manure is an important source of ammonia and greenhouse gases. Concerns over the environmental impact of emissions from manure management have resulted in research efforts focusing on emission abatement. However, questions regarding the successful abatement of manure-related emissions remain. The deficiencies in single-pollutant, single-stage approaches when devising abatement strategies are also highlighted, along with potential solutions and the way forward in tackling these deficiencies.
objective: the present study identifies potential abatement options to reduce greenhouse gases (ghgs) and ammonia (nh3) emissions collectively. it also sheds light on the potential cobenefits and the issue of pollution swapping by determining the trends in interactions of methane (ch4), nitrous oxide (n2o), and nh3 among the various abatement options identified. here the results regarding the impact of different abatement options at different stages of pig and cattle manure management (feeding strategies, animal housing, manure treatment and manure storage) on ghgs (ch4 and n2o) emissions are presented.
result1: in the case of ch4 emissions, estimates from the present study show a reduction in emissions by 29 ± 116%, primarily during the storage of digestate. n2o emissions increased by 20 ± 41% during the storage of anaerobic digestate. n2o emissions decreased by 29 ± 43% during the application of anaerobic digestate.
result2: this study indicates that acidification of manure can reduce ch4 emissions by 74 ± 22% during the storage of manure. overall estimates indicate a n2o reduction of 56 ± 51% during storage of acidified manure. overall estimates indicate a n2o reduction of 52% when acidified manure was applied to the soils.
result3: results from the analysis indicate a reduction in ch4 emissions by 12 ± 33%  with the use of covers. the use of covers led to large  increases in n2o emissions (>500%). this estimate was accompanied by high variability, due to contrasting emission trends among all the covering materials analyzed.
general_conclusion: this study shows that several abattement options can reduce ghg emissions from from pig and cattle manure management. however, several options are associated with tradeoffs between the different ghg considered. these results are based on descriptive statistics, but not on a model taking into account between-studies variability.

search_strategy: a systematic literature search was conducted on the databases of scopus, google scholar, and gray literature, and from the websites of governmental/non-governmental agencies by combining the following keywords: ammonia emission, ammonia abatement, europe, abatement strategies, integrated assessment, systematic review, meta-analysis, air quality, long-range transboundary air pollution (lrtap), livestock, livestock management, animal housing, manure treatment, animal diet, europe, france, belgium, germany, netherlands, spain, uk, sweden, finland.
selection_criteria: not specified
data_analysis: to analyze the combined effect of different measures, taking sample sizes into account, testing for moderators, and obtaining corresponding forest plots, the meta-analytical software openmee was used (http://www.cebm.brown.edu/openmee). a random effect model was used to aggregate the collected data into a meta-analysis, to satisfy the assumption of variance heterogeneity.
background: Research efforts are in place for the abatement of NH3 emissions at the various stages of the manure management chain, namely; the feeding, housing, treatment, storage, and application stages to ensure a whole-farm management model. However, the impact of these mitigation strategies on the emission of other GHGs has not received equal attention.
objective: investigate the consequences of the most effective measures to decrease nh3 emissions from slurries, for the emission of other ghg (swapping effect)
result1: slurry acidification was effective for the reduction of ammonia emissions (-69%) and had no pollution swapping effect with other greenhouse gases, like nitrous oxide (-21%) and methane (-86%).
result2: all other management strategies, like different storage covers, the concealing of the liquid slurry with different materials were effective to varying degrees for the abatement of ammonia emission, but also resulted in the increased emission of at least one other greenhouse gas.
result3: the strategies focusing on the decrease of ammonia emissions neglected the consequences of the emissions of other greenhouse gases.
general_conclusion: slurry acidification was effective for the reduction of ammonia emissions, and had no pollution swapping effect with other greenhouse gases, like nitrous oxide and methane. all other management strategies, like different storage covers and the concealing of the liquid slurry with different materials were effective to varying degrees for the abatement of ammonia emission, but also resulted in the increased emission of at least one other greenhouse gas.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed literature, theses and conference papers from 1994 to 11th february 2018 were collected, using the electronic databases: web of science, google scholar and the china national knowledge infrastructure. in this literature search, the following specific keywords were combined: composting, additives (amendments), nitrogen loss, ammonia, nitrous oxide, methane or greenhouse gas emissions.
selection_criteria: to be included in this meta-analysis, studies needed to meet the following criteria: (i) the study should include control treatments; (ii) the study described the mitigation efficiency of at least one of tn, nh3, n2o and ch4 for each treatment; (iii) aerobic composting process was ensured by forced aeration and/or turning; and (iv), the composting process was complete, as indicated by the compost temperature remaining stable at the ambient temperature.
data_analysis: mean effect sizes and bias-corrected 95% confidence intervals were generated by running a bootstrapping procedure with 5000 iterations using metawin 2.1.4 software. the effects of 3 variables on mean effect were explored: additive type, application dosage and feedstock properties.
background: Composting of solid waste can be associated with a loss of the agronomic value (nutrient loss), as well as a source of environmental impact through the emission of the greenhouse gases (GHG) nitrous oxide (N2O) and methane (CH4) and volatilization of ammonia (NH3). Additives have been considered as a useful option to mitigate these environmental emissions, but the wider effects of using different additives on multiple gas emissions is still uncertain.
objective: the objectives of this study were: (i) to quantify and compare the mitigation effect of different additives on multiple gases; (ii) to assess the importance of feedstock properties (moisture content, c/n ratio and ph) on mitigation effect; (iii) to investigate the relationship between additive application dosage and mitigation effect; (iv) to explore optimal options to reduce tn loss and nh3, n2o and ch4 emissions. here the results concerning the impact of additives during composting on tn losses are reported.
result1: according to this meta-analysis, the use of additives can significantly reduce tn loss (46.4%, on average), compared with the control.
result2: there was a range in mitigation efficiencies depending on the additive type. application of chemical additives was more efficient at reducing tn loss (52.0%), compared with other additives. the effectiveness of chemical additives on tn loss can vary according to additive properties. specifically, phosphate and magnesium salts had the greatest mitigation potential, reducing tn loss by 68.0%, followed by superphosphate. acids were very effective in reducing tn loss during composting (37.1%).
result3: the application of physical additives was also an effective option to reduce tn loss, with respective average reductions of 43.5%, with biochar and zeolite giving significant reductions.
result4: the present meta-analysis showed that the application of microbial additives were less effective than chemical or physical additives in reducing tn loss, with average reduction of 10.2%.
result5: there was significant linear correlation between application dosage of phosphate and magnesium salt and the mitigation efficiency for tn loss between 0 and 20%, with tn loss decreasing by 4.7% for every 1% increase in the application of phosphate and magnesium salt. the magnitude of the mitigation of tn loss increased as the dosage rate of superphosphate increased over the range of 0–20%, with decreases in tn losses of 3.2% for every 1% increase in superphosphate application. chemical additives at low moisture content were more effective in mitigating tn loss (57.8%) than these at high moisture content (40.9%). at low c/n ratios (≤20), chemical additives resulted in a greater mitigation of tn loss compared to physical additives, although at high c/n ratios (>20 to ≤ 30) there was a tendency for the opposite effect.
general_conclusion: this first global meta-analysis establishes that the use of additives can significantly reduce the tn loss during composting.

search_strategy: the authors searched for relevant peer-reviewed publications between 2000 and 2018 in international and chinese journals using google scholar and web of science. studies related to composting and n loss were searched with keywords “compost, co-compost (i.e. compost consisting of two or more types of feedstock), nitrogen loss, ammonia volatilization, nitrous oxide loss, nitrogen emission reduction, pig manure, chicken manure, cow manure, organic household waste, kitchen waste, sewage sludge, food waste”.
selection_criteria: 1) the focus had to be on active composting (traditional static stockpiling studies were excluded), 2) studies reported on raw feedstock characteristics (type of feedstock, total c and tn, c/n ratio, ph, moisture), composting procedure (composting type, duration, aeration rate, turning frequency), n loss mitigation technology (c/n ratio modulation, microbial inoculation, physical or chemical additives, covering, aeration rate and turning frequency), 3) studies reported on at least one of the focus n losses (tn, nh3, n2o), on gas emissions as cumulative emissions and as proportion of the initial n content of the feedstock, 4) studies provided sample size for treatments and, lastly, 5) data that had been used in multiple publications were analyzed only once.
data_analysis: the authors used the bootstrap resampling procedure (4999 iterations) to obtain the weighted mean effect size and the 95% confidence intervals (cis) of each technology category
background: Composting is an important technology to treat biowastes and recycle nutrients, but incurs nitrogen (N) losses that lower the value of the final products and cause pollution. Technologies aimed at reducing N losses during composting have inconsistent outcomes.
objective: advance quantitative knowledge of n losses during composting and the mitigation potential of in situ technologies.  1) quantify n losses (tn, nh3 and n2o) from composting, 2) analyze the factors driving n losses; and 3) determine the n mitigation potential of in situ technologies. here, we report only data regarding the mitigation potential of in-situ technologies. here we report only results regarding mitigation technologies.
result1: taken together, the in situ technologies reduced losses of total nitrogen by 31.4.
result2: the reduction of total nitrogen losses across all technologies was statistically, and averaged ca 38.1%, pa 28.6%, co 27.8% and mi 20.1%.
result3: physical additives clay and biochar significantly reduced tn by 38.8% (clay); and 30.2% (biochar). zeolite did not affect tn losses. chemical additives (with the exception of dcd that had no measurable effect) significantly reduced tn loss, ranking mg-p salts 60.9% > acid substances 44.8% > metal salts 41.5% > ca-superphosphate 19.7% > gypsum 15.0%.
general_conclusion: the reduction of total nitrogen losses across all technologies was statistically, and averaged chemical additives 38.1%, physical additives 28.6%, c/n regulation 27.9%, covering 27.8%, optimized aeration 26.9%, and microbial inocula 20.1%. biochar and magnesium-phosphate salts emerged as the most effective n-conserving strategies.

search_strategy: peer-review scientific literature published between january 1, 1980 and march 31, 2021 were searched using a combination of keywords (such as “nh3 volatilization” or “nh3 emission”) from the web of science and china knowledge resource integrated databases.
selection_criteria: 1) only experiments conducted in china were included; 2) studies must have reported a mean value of cumulative soil nh3 volatilization after fertilization; 3) field, in-situ pot or lysimeter studies were included.
data_analysis: a random-effect model was employed to calculate the mean effect size of each improved farming practice, and it's 95 % confidence interval (ci) was obtained using a bootstrapping procedure with 4999 iterations (rosenberg et al., 2000). a categorical random-effect model was used to determine the mean effect size of different groups among the improved farming practices and to derive impact factors of specific improved farming practices. calculations were performed using metawin 2.1. the improved farming practice was deemed to have a significant impact on av or ysav when the 95 % ci did not overlap with the zero line. categorical groups were deemed significantly different where the 95 % cis did not overlap with each other.
background: High ammonia (NH3) emissions from fertilized soil in China have led to various concerns regarding environmental safety and public health.
objective: select effective measures based on absolute (av) and yield-scaled (ysav) nh3 volatilization reduction potential, with the aim of establishing a comprehensive nh3 mitigation framework covering various crop production sectors, and offering a range of potential solutions.
result1: in dryland cropping regions, plastic film mulching reduced ammonnia volatilization (av) and yield scale ammonia volatilisation (ysav) by 52.2 and 52.4 %, respectively compared to un-mulched soil.
result2: for paddy fields, applying ground rice bran, a molecular film or a vegetative film to the flood water reduced av by 14.6, 22.3 and 26.3 %, respectively, and ysav by 20.5, 31.7 and 33.3 %, respectively.
result3: significant av and ysav reductions were associated with applying straw to neutral or alkaline soils with low soil organic matter content, adopting maize or cash crops as crop type, or by applying added n fertilizer to the soil subsurface.
general_conclusion: reduction of ammonia volatilisation with soil muching compared to no mulching.

search_strategy: several databases, including scopus, google scholar, research gate, web of science (isi), china national knowledge infrastructure (cnki), and agricultural and environmental journals (e.g., environment international, field crops research, frontiers in ecology and the environment, soil & tillage research etc.) were screened. words “ammonia volatilization” and “ammonia emission from soil in china” were used as keywords to collect peer-reviewed papers about ammonia volatilisation in china. more than 2000 papers were searched online and papers suspected to match our criteria were downloaded.
selection_criteria: 1) experimental details including paper citation, province, location, trial type, year, number of replicates, climatic conditions, crop type, and soil properties; 2) treatment details including irrigation and tillage systems, fertilizer type, rate and methods of application, and amendments like mulching, biochar, and inhibitors; 3) av rate (kg ha-1) and standard deviation (std)-missing stds were imputed using standard error, variance, p-values, and t- values applied by the meta-analysis.
data_analysis: the software comprehensive meta-analysis (cma-2) was used with standardized mean difference corrected for bias (hedges’ g) (continuous means for unmatched groups, post-data only pathway) to compare av changes among different crop types, climatic conditions, and soil grades when using control observations only. publication bias was assessed at p > 0.05 using rosenthal’s fail-safe n test based on z-values and 2-tailed p-values.
background: Numerous strategies for mitigating ammonia volatilization (AV) from agricultural land have been investigated with limited evaluation of their efficacy and response to differing field conditions across China.
objective: this study aimed to answer the following questions: 1) what is the general comment on ammonia volatilisation from three staple crops in china? 2) how might ammonia volatilisation respond to variations in crop type, soil properties, and climatic conditions? 3) what are the optimal strategies for control of ammonia volatilisation under various conditions?
result1: mulch has a greater effect on reducing ammonia for maize (28.6%) than wheat (26.3%) and rice (20.4%).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: mulching reduced ammonia volatisation in wheat, maize and rice compared to no mulching.

search_strategy: we searched peer-reviewed papers published before oct 2018 using the google scholar and china national knowledge resource infrastructure database (including scientific jour- nal articles and dissertations) using the search terms: “maize and wheat”, “plastic film mulch or mulching or soil management”, “water content”, “china”.
selection_criteria: 1) field studies involved mulching treatments and non-mulching controls; 2) studies reported soil water index, soil water content (%) and/or soil water storage (mm); 3) crops applied plastic film mulching without irrigation throughout the growing season; 4) studies with multifactorial analyses showed no significant interactions among treatments; 5) studies reported mean data, standard deviations (sd) and the number of replications (n); 6) studies included deep soil sampling (≥100 cm); 7) the location and year of the experiments (at least two years) were provided.
data_analysis: where xe and xc are means of the relevant variable in treatment (plastic mulching treatments) and control (ck, non-mulching) groups, respec- tively. if the estimated pooled variance was greater than 0, the categorical random-effects model was used; otherwise, the fixed-effects model was used. the mean effect sizes and 95% confidence intervals (cis) were calculated with a bootstrapping pro- cedure using the statistical software metawin with resampling of 999 iterations. if the 95% cis did not overlap zero, the effect size was considered to be statistically significant. the results of the lnr were reported as the percentage changes [(r-1)×100] under treatment effects. negative or positive values indicate a decrease and increase in the response variable to plastic mulching treatment. for each category, total heterogeneity (qt) was divided into within-group (qw) and between-groups (qb). the dif- ference of qb was significant if the 95% cis of their effect sizes did not overlap each other (p < 0.05). in the meta-analysis, we evaluated the relationships between the response size of the sws and the two other factors (duration of study and et). moreover, linear regression analysis was carried out between the response size of the et and the growing- season precipitation.
background: In rain-fed semiarid areas, low soil water availability is a major challenge constraining crop productivity and agricultural sustainability. Soil surface mulching with plastic film has been widely used to improve soil water availability in the Loess Plateau of China. However, a systematic assessment on soil water balance dynamics under plastic mulching is still lacking.
objective: the objectives of meta-analysis were to (1) investigate the ef- fects of plastic mulching on the spatiotemporal dynamics of sws under different climate regions and different management practices, (2) analyze the characteristics of et and soil water balance under plastic mulching in dryland farming systems, and (3) assess the field produc- tivity, soil water and quality sustainability under plastic mulching in loess plateau.
result1: overall, plastic mulching has little effect on soil organic carbon content. however, plastic mulching significantly decreased soil organic carbon content (soc) by 7.1% when annual mean precipitation was over 600 mm, and the effects were not significant in the other annual precipitation zones.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: overall, plastic mulching has little effect on soil organic carbon content.

search_strategy: the web of science and china national knowledge internet were used to find peer-reviewed studies published before january 2017. search terms included ‘plastic film mulch’ or ‘mulching’, ‘nitrogen’, ‘nitrate’, ‘water content’ or ‘soil organic carbon’ in the article title, abstract, and keywords.

search_strategy: published journal articles related to the effect of film mulching on soc and soil ghg fluxes were searched for on web of science using the following research keywords: ts = (mulch) and (soil) and (carbon or “nitrous oxide” or n2o or methane or ch4 or “greenhouse gas”). additionally, the china national knowledge infrastructure was used to search for published articles related to our topics. in addition, we also searched for other articles via literature citations that were not covered by these keywords.
selection_criteria: first, the selected studies must contain at least one of our targets (soc in the 0–20 cm layer, ch4 emissions/uptake and n2o emissions) in both non-mulched and film-mulched soils. second, management practices, such as the amount/type of fertilization, must be consistent in both treatments. third, we selected observations of soc and soil ghg fluxes from only field experiments rather than from pot or greenhouse experiments. fourth, because upland fields are generally atmospheric ch4 sinks and paddy fields are generally atmospheric ch4 sources, we considered the effects of plastic film mulching on ch4 uptake only in uplands and on ch4 emissions only in paddy fields. in addition, we did not consider a few studies that reported opposite results for ch4 fluxes.

background: The use of plastic film in agriculture strongly affects the decomposition of soil organic carbon (SOC) and the release of methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O) by influencing soil biogeochemical processes. However, no systematic conclusions have been reached regarding the effect of plastic film mulching on SOC stocks and greenhouse gas (GHG) budgets.
objective: a meta-analysis was performed to analyze the effect of film mulching on soc and soil ghg fluxes across different agricultural systems and to identify the major factors affecting their responses to film mulching to address the following questions: (1) how does plastic film mulching influence soc and soil ghg fluxes across different agricultural ecosystems (rainfed uplands, irrigated uplands and paddy fields) and (2) how do mulching variables (e.g., the coverage ratio, film type, mulching method and film thickness) and environmental variables affect soc and soil ghg fluxes under film mulching?
result1: film mulching did not significantly influence soc in average over all studies.
result2: different agricultural systems significantly (p < 0.05) affected the response of soc to film mulching.
result3: differences in mulching practices (including the coverage ratio, film type and mulching method) significantly affected the response of soc to mulching.
general_conclusion: film mulching did not significantly influence soil organic carbon in average, but some specific types of film had a significant positive or negative impacts.

search_strategy: to investigate the effect of fm on soil microbial abundance, diversity, and functional parameters, the authors conducted an extensive search of peer-viewed articles of databases including web of science, google scholar, and china knowledge resource integrated database in june 2020. the following keyword combinations were used as the first step to screen articles: “plastic film” or “film mulch” and “microbial commu- nity” or “microbiome”.
selection_criteria: 1) field-based study with an experimental design allowing pairwise comparison between film mulch treatments and bare soil controls; 2) at least one soil microbial community parameter (abundance, diversity, or function) was reported; 3) treatment pairs established with same ecosystem types, crop types, and soil types; 4) for articles with experimental data for more than one growing season/year, only the last data were extracted for meta- analysis; the approach can greatly eliminate the non-independence of the data.
data_analysis: all statistics were conducted using r v 3.6.0. to correct for the nested structure and non-independence of observations, we used the mixed-effect models to evaluate the effects of pm on soil microbial parameters and other related properties, the models were constructed via rma.mv() function in the “metafor”package and the overall effect and the 95% confidence interval (ci) were calculated. the sensitivity of the few variables with potential publication bias was then examined using the trim-and-fill model. we conducted “leave-one-out” tests to check the robustness of variables’ effect sizes by function leave1out() in package “metafor”, this is a kind of sensitivity analysis; the funnel plots were used to display the comparison of data from all cases to the aggregated weighted mean within-study suggests.

objective: the study aimed to: 1) explore whether fm shapes distinct soil microbial abundance, diversity, and functionality patterns; 2) clarify the underlying drivers of these responses; 3) determine whether microbial parameters are related to changes in crop yield and whether these parameters belong to specific microbial parameters, such as abundance, diversity or functionality.

search_strategy: a comprehensive search for peer-reviewed publications related to the effect of pm on crop yields and environmental impacts from jan 1980 to dec 2015 was conducted using two databases: web of science and the china academic journal network publishing database. the article titles, abstracts, and keywords were searched using the terms ‘wheat or maize’, ‘plastic mulch or soil manage- ment’, and ‘china’.
selection_criteria: (1) comparisons between pm and nm practices were made; (2) at least one parameter of interest (yield, evapotranspiration (et), water use efficiency (wue), harvest index, soil carbon, soil nitrogen, or amount of plastic film residue) was re- ported, and (3) the experimental location was stated. studies that described only the relationship between pm and crop yield without a nm treatment or that did not provide a clear description of the experimental methods were rejected.
data_analysis: the mean value of all observations on a countrywide scale was calculated by weighting, and the weight was calculated by replications. statistical analyses were con- ducted using the regression procedure of sas v9.2. the relationship between yield increase and increase in ghg emission was analyzed using regression analysis. fisher's test was used to determine the significance of the differences between means with a significance level of p < 0.05.
background: Numerous individual reports have emphasized the importance of soil surface plastic mulch (PM) as an auxiliary means of increasing crop yields, but a comprehensive assessment of yields and environmental benefits on a national scale has not been performed.

result1: pm application reduced soil organic carbon by 5% although the difference was not significant.

search_strategy: the selected publications were collected by searching isi web of science database and china knowledge resource integrated database using the following search criteria: ts = (plastic mulching∗) and (soil organic carbon∗ or microbial biomass carbon∗ or enzyme activities∗ or co2∗ or ch4∗) and ts = (film mulching∗ or plastic mulching∗) and (maize∗ or wheat∗ or potato∗ or yield∗ or root∗ or biomass∗).
selection_criteria: (i) the selected study included at least one parameter of interest (i.e. response variables) as economic yield (ey), aboveground biomass (ab), root biomass (rb), soil organic carbon (soc), co2 emission, ch4 flux, microbial biomass carbon (mbc), c‒related soil enzyme activities (i.e. glucosidase, sucrase, catalase, urease and alkaline phosphatase); (ii) only field study with replicated experimental design was included, greenhouse and laboratory incubation experiments excluded. pairwise comparisons on mulching and non‒mulching farming management were performed under the same pedo‒climatic conditions (e.g., temperature, precipitation, soil texture, and soil type) for at least 2 consecutive years; (iii) provided treatment means, sample sizes, and variances, or these could be extracted from tables or the figures using software; (v) duration of plastic mulching should be at least one full crop season for each year. when there were more than one articles on the same experiment, the article with longest mulching duration was included; (iv) to avoid pre‒mulching heterogeneity of soc stock between treatment and control, the values of soc contents at the beginning and end of each trial should be provided for the calculation of actual changes due to mulching. however, only few studies provided the baseline values of soc stocks for both experimental and control plots. given the fact that all data considered originated from pairwise system comparisons including controlled field trials, baseline differences in soc stocks among the different plots of one comparison were expected to be negligible. the authors therefore decided to also included the studies that the baseline values were not known into the data pool.
data_analysis: a mixed effect model that included a random effect for multiple studies from the same site was performed to calculate the mean effect sizes and variances for the concerned response variables. the authors used heterogeneity tests to confirm if models could explain significant variation. the majority of results show significant inter‒study heterogeneity, so the authors rejected the null hypothesis that all studies share a common effect size in favor of the interpretation that true effect sizes vary between studies. the sensitivity of the results was examined using the trim‒and‒fill model (i.e. the authors repeated the model for each of concerned responsory variable to account for the number of missing studies). the authors tested for potential publication bias using egger’s regression. the analysis results did not suggest that there was bias in most cases.
background: Plastic mulching provides many advantages for crop production, especially in dry croplands, such as reducing evaporation, improving water temperature conditions, and minimizing soil erosion. After three decades of practical application, however, a comprehensive nationwide assessment of its potential environmental consequences, in terms of SOC stock, was not available.
objective: the objective was to quantify the nationwide effects of plastic mulching application on crop net primary productivity, soil c fluxes, and total soc pool, and further identify the dominant environmental, edaphic, and anthropogenic drivers on these effects.
result1: plastic mulching did produce a significant and positive effect on soc stocks (effect size: 6.2%, 95% ci: 3.9–8.5%) compared with non‒mulching. the effect sizes were strongly dependent on crop type (p < 0.001), planting density (p < 0.001), and n application level (p = 0.002).
result2: across the entire dataset, the application of plastic mulching significantly increased soc stocks by 0.303 mg c ha−1, compared to non‒mulching. c sequestration rates under plastic mulching farming was 0.012 mg c ha−1 higher than in non‒mulching farming, however, this value was statistically insignificant.
result3: the mean effect size for root c input was 48% (95% ci: 40–56%), equivalent to 0.24 mg c ha−1 y−1 (95% ci: 0.20–0.28 mg c ha−1 y−1). crop type, growing precipitation and temperatures produced significant differences in the magnitude of root c input.
general_conclusion: overall, plastic mulching increased soil organic carbon storage compared with traditional non‒mulching farming; the magnitude was strongly affected by agronomic, environmental, and edaphic factors.
knowledge_gaps: 1) although the authors computed a significant and positive effect size, one needs to be cautious when applying these results to practical applications because of possible uncertainty stemming from the limited sample number; 2) the calculated root c input was probably underestimated for two major reasons. firstly, the majority of studies merely provided post‒harvest root biomass, which thus excluding a certain amount of c from the fine roots which had decomposed before crop maturity, and secondly, rhizodeposited‒c released from living plant roots, a significant contributor to soil organic carbon stocks, was not included in the estimation due to the limited data available.

search_strategy: the authors collected articles published up to december 2018 from the web of science and the china national knowledge infrastructure using keywords including ‘loess plateau’, ‘plastic film mulch’, ‘wheat’, ‘maize’, ‘yield’, ‘water use efficiency’ and ‘evapotranspiration’.
selection_criteria: 1) the field experiments have been conducted in rainfed crops in the loess plateau of china; 2) crop yield was measured at maturity; 3) the treatments must contain a control (without plastic film mulch), and at least one plastic film mulch treatment, pm or fm; 4) the experimental treatment had at least three replications; 5) the evapotranspiration (et) was estimated by soil depth greater than 150 cm; 6) crops were not limited by nutrients. in addition, the mean, standard deviation (or standard error), and sample size of the relevant variables must be directly available or can be calculated from the data.
data_analysis: to evaluate the effect of plastic film mulch on yield and wue, the natural logarithm of response ratio (lnr) was calculated with meta win 2.1,22 as the effect size. the normality-test (kolmogorov–smirnov test) showed yield and wue depart from normal distribution (p < 0.001), so the authors used the bootstrapping process (9999 iterations) to generate the average effect size and bias corrected 95% confidence intervals (cis). a significant effect (p < 0.05) corresponded to zero effect outside the 95% ci. all the statistical analyses were done with spss 18.0 software.
background: Plastic film mulch is widely used to improve crop yield and water use efficiency (WUE, yield per unit evapotranspiration) in semi-arid regions. It is commonly applied as partial-film mulch (PM: at least 50% soil cover) or full-film mulch (FM: complete soil cover). The PM has lower economic and environmental cost; hence it would be a superior technology provided it delivers similar gains in yield and WUE in relation to FM.
objective: this article presents a meta-analysis comparing yield, water use, and wue of wheat and maize under partial mulching (pm) and full mulching (fm) in the loess plateau. the authors hypothesized that: 1) the improvement in crop yield and wue are similar for pm and fm; 2) the benefits of these practices vary with environmental conditions, such as precipitation, elevation, and soil type.
result1: both fm and pm increased the grain yield by 26–20% in wheat and by 52–37% for maize.
result2: the yield increase was statistically undistinguishable between fm and pm.
result3: both fm and pm increased shoot biomass of wheat (35–29%) and maize (31–20%).
result4: plastic film mulch increased hi in maize (fm: 21%; pm: 15%) but not in wheat.
general_conclusion: plastic film mulching, both when done on full area (100%) or partial area (50%), has a positive effect on crop yield and on biomass both for wheat and maize. the effect on the harvest index is positive for maize but no effect is reported for wheat.

search_strategy: literature searches were conducted in the isi web of knowledge core database targeting peer- reviewed articles published online until april 30, 2015 in two steps. in a first query, we tested it by including a spe- cific management option such as “irrigation” because water shortage is conceived as a potential threat to the mediterranean agricultural system. the search terms for the first query was thus (“agro*” or “agri*” or “farm*”) and (mediterranean*) and (ecosystem*) and (management*) and (irrigat*) in the topic field. then, the authors strove to capture the diversity of farming practices studied in case studies by not including any `a priori restrictive search terms. this additional query was made with com- binations of keywords including (“agro*” or “agri*” or “farm*”) and (mediterranean*) and (management*) in the topic field.
selection_criteria: the authors selected empirical case studies which measured ecosystem services-related properties both for conservation (treatment) and conventional (control) management options. this step excluded pure simulation modeling studies and reviews. the authors focused on papers reporting results from the mediterranean basin but included six well-designed papers reporting from mediterranean climate regions outside the basin (i.e., south and south west australia, the cape of south africa, central chile, and california).
data_analysis:
to secure statistical significance by keeping a sufficient sample size, we decided to weight observations using the sample sizes: studies with larger sample sizes were weighted higher during aggregation. for the uncertainty analysis, we report the means and
95% confidence intervals (cis) of the wlrr. the cis were constructed by non-parametric bootstrapping (nboot =10, 000) using the percentile method. all calculations were done in r version 3.3.1 using the packages boot and vioplot.
background: In the Mediterranean region, the long-term provision of agro-ecosystem services is threatened by accelerating climate change, unsustainable farming practices, and other pressures. Alternative management practices such as conservation agriculture could be expected to ensure sustainability of ecosystem services from Mediterranean agro-ecosystems. Conservation agriculture is characterized by minimal soil disturbance, permanent soil cover, and diversification of crop species.
objective: the objective of this study is to fill this knowledge gap by conducting a meta-analysis on the impact of conservative management practices on ecosystem services in the mediterranean basin based on published literature. our goal is to identify the positive and negative impacts of conservation farming practices on ecosystem services in the mediterranean basin, providing evidence-based recommendations for sustainable land management in the mediterranean basin in the future.

search_strategy: different online databases (google scholar, science direct, scopus (elsevier), pubmed, jstor, and web of science) were explored for peer-reviewed articles published in eng- lish from 2000 to 2021 that investigated effects of rfrh and mulching on crops. the keywords used in the literature search for the meta-anal- ysis (ma) were: “mulching”, and/or “rainwater harvesting”, and/or “yield” and/or “ridge and furrow”.
selection_criteria: 1) the experiment was conducted in a semi-arid region; 2) field trials with at least ridge and furrow, plastic film mulched ridge, biochar or straw mulched furrow, compared with flat planting treatments; 3) mulched ridge and furrow; and flat planting plots were established within the same ecosystem and had similar environmental characteristics at the start of the study; 4) data on maize, wheat or potato yield was reported; 5) the experimental duration was clearly specified and the experiment was repeated, at least, two growing seasons.
data_analysis: ma based on the response-ratio approach was conducted with a construction confidence interval analysis using the random-effect model of nordic cochrane centre's review manager software. in this ma, effect size was calculated as natural log (ln) of the response ratio (r), which is the ratio of mean crop yield in mulched ridges and furrows plots to mean crop yield in flat planting plots. the nordic cochrane centre's review manager software package (revman; ver- sion. 5.3, denmark) was used to implement random-effects models to derive effect sizes of ridge and furrow treatment and flat planting with or without mulching for crop yields. chi-square (χ2) and i2 tests were performed to determine heterogeneity between studies.
background: Low crop productivity due to prolonged droughts, inappropriate water saving practices, low soil fertility and soil erosion is a major threat to food security in semi-arid areas. In these areas, ridge and furrow rainwater harvesting (RFRH) technique is widely adopted to minimize water deficiency problems. Incorporating mulching in ridge and furrow rainwater harvesting (RFRH + M) is also being promoted to increase water storage and conservation for crop usage. Till date, evidence estab- lishing the efficacy of incorporating mulching and biochar in ridge and furrow system, and modalities for improving crop yield has not been synthesized quantitatively to promote widespread adoption.
objective: the objective of this ma was to assess the whether the integration of ridge and furrow rainwater harvesting systems (rfrhs) with soil amendments, namely biochar or mulches affect crop yield and soil properties rela- tive to traditional no-till flat planting.
result1: in areas with sun- shine hours longer than 1300 h, straw mulched ridge and furrow rainwater harvesting system had an over- all significant effect (p = 0.04) on maize as compared with the flat planting without mulching.
result2: in maize cultivation, air temperature and pre- cipitation had no significant moderating effect (p > 0.05) on maize with straw applied as mulch compared with flat planting without mulching
general_conclusion: plastic film mulched ridge-furrow has a positive effect on yield of maize and potato while it shows no effect on wheat yield. straw mulched ridge-furrow has a positive effect on maize yield. plastic film with straw mulched ridge-furrow has a positive effect on maize yield while has no effect on wheat yield.

search_strategy: we searched peer-reviewed papers published before oct 2018 using the google scholar and china national knowledge resource infrastructure database (including scientific jour- nal articles and dissertations) using the search terms: “maize and wheat”, “plastic film mulch or mulching or soil management”, “water content”, “china”.
selection_criteria: 1) field studies involved mulching treatments and non-mulching controls; 2) studies reported soil water index, soil water content (%) and/or soil water storage (mm); 3) crops applied plastic film mulching without irrigation throughout the growing season; 4) studies with multifactorial analyses showed no significant interactions among treatments; 5) studies reported mean data, standard deviations (sd) and the number of replications (n); 6) studies included deep soil sampling (≥100 cm); 7) the location and year of the experiments (at least two years) were provided.
data_analysis: where xe and xc are means of the relevant variable in treatment (plastic mulching treatments) and control (ck, non-mulching) groups, respec- tively. if the estimated pooled variance was greater than 0, the categorical random-effects model was used; otherwise, the fixed-effects model was used. the mean effect sizes and 95% confidence intervals (cis) were calculated with a bootstrapping pro- cedure using the statistical software metawin with resampling of 999 iterations. if the 95% cis did not overlap zero, the effect size was considered to be statistically significant. the results of the lnr were reported as the percentage changes [(r-1)×100] under treatment effects. negative or positive values indicate a decrease and increase in the response variable to plastic mulching treatment. for each category, total heterogeneity (qt) was divided into within-group (qw) and between-groups (qb). the dif- ference of qb was significant if the 95% cis of their effect sizes did not overlap each other (p < 0.05). in the meta-analysis, we evaluated the relationships between the response size of the sws and the two other factors (duration of study and et). moreover, linear regression analysis was carried out between the response size of the et and the growing- season precipitation.
background: In rain-fed semiarid areas, low soil water availability is a major challenge constraining crop productivity and agricultural sustainability. Soil surface mulching with plastic film has been widely used to improve soil water availability in the Loess Plateau of China. However, a systematic assessment on soil water balance dynamics under plastic mulching is still lacking.
objective: the objectives of meta-analysis were to (1) investigate the ef- fects of plastic mulching on the spatiotemporal dynamics of sws under different climate regions and different management practices, (2) analyze the characteristics of et and soil water balance under plastic mulching in dryland farming systems, and (3) assess the field produc- tivity, soil water and quality sustainability under plastic mulching in loess plateau.

general_conclusion: plastic mulching resulted in a significant positive effect on crop aboveground biomass when compared with no mulching, both considering mulching done on full area (100%) or partial area (50%).

search_strategy: peer-reviewed journal articles published in english from 1985 to 2016 were collected to build the database based on web of science search using the following sets of keywords: (i) wheat or maize; (ii) film mulch or plastic mulch or plastic cover; and (iii) water stress or water deficit or drought or irrigation deficit. the authors replaced the phrases ‘film mulch’; ‘plastic mulch’ and ‘plastic cover’ with ‘irrigation’ and ‘china’ to search for articles discussing supplementary irrigation specific to the region.
selection_criteria: only articles from china that met the following criteria were included in the database: (i) the experiments were conducted under field conditions where the effect of irrigation or plastic mulching was compared with flat (even or level topography); rainfed conditions; (ii) the reported plants were monoculture cereals of maize (zea mays) and wheat (i.e.; bread wheat; triticum aestivum); and (iii) the articles reported crop response as grain yield.

background: Plastic mulching technology for wheat and maize has been commonly used in China, but their effect on yield, soil water content, evapotranspiration (ET), and WUE has not been compared with traditional irrigation.
