search_strategy: a literature review of published papers was carried out to gather crop yield and water consumption data under different soil tillage practices in northern china up to december 2017. papers written in english were collected from google scholar and the web of science, and papers written in chinese were collected from the china national knowledge infrastructure.
selection_criteria: data collections were restricted to field ex- perimental studies conducted in northern china, including crop yield, water consumption or wue under a particular type of soil tillage practice.
data_analysis: in order to avoid assigning extreme high weights to individual experiments, a random-effects model was utilized to assign the weight to each experiment and implemented using the openmee software.
background: Water deficiency seriously restricts the agricultural production in Northern China. Soil tillage practices can conserve water and increase yield effectively, but the regional applicability of soil tillage practices has not been systematically studied so far. It is significant to study the regional characteristics of tillage practices on water- conserving and yield-increasing so that the optimal practices for improving the crop water production and maintaining the agricultural sustainable development can be determined.
objective: this study aims to: 1) quantify the effects of different tillage practices on crop yield, water consumption and wue of wheat and maize in dif- ferent sub-regions of northern china; 2) build the crop water pro- duction functions of wheat and maize under different soil tillage practices to quantify the characteristics of each tillage practice; 3) analyze the suitability of the different tillage practices in the three sub- regions of northern china.
result1: mulching and ridge and furrow planting with mulching significantly improved the yield of wheat (p < 0.05) in northern china compared with conventional tillage and bare soil.
result2: compared to ct as the benchmark, mulching and ridge and furrow planting with mulching improved the yield of maize in northern china by 17.7 ± 6.2 % and 36.6 ± 11.8 %.
general_conclusion: mulching and ridge coupled with furrow planting with mulching had a positive effect on crop yield of wheat and maize.

search_strategy: the authors conducted a review of peer-reviewed scientific journal articles on water productivity in maize production published from january 2000 to march 2018 using the china national knowledge infrastructure and web of science databases. the different combinations of search terms included “irrigation” and “maize” or “corn” and “yield” and “water use efficiency” or “water productivity” and “china” were used for article selection.
selection_criteria: (1) all data were from field experiments, so laboratory experiments, pot experiments, experiments under rain-proof shelter conditions, and model simulations were excluded; (2) data were required to include maize yield, seasonal water supply and wp in the maize growth period.
data_analysis: the authors used a linear mixed-effects model with yield (ln-transformed), water supply (ln-transformed), and water productivity (wp) (ln-transformed) as response variables and experimental year (continuous, transformed), study agro-ecological zones (categorical, three levels), maize cultivars (categorical), seasonal average temperature (st) (continuous, ln-transformed), seasonal average precipitation (sp) (continuous, ln-transformed), seasonal irrigation depth (continuous, ln-transformed),  vapor pressure deficit (vpd) (continuous, ln-transformed), seasonal n application amount (continuous, ln-transformed), soil organic matter (som) (continuous, ln-transformed), latitude (continuous, ln-transformed) and plant density (continuous, ln-transformed) at the study locations as independent variables. the authors included interaction terms for some factors (sp * irrigation depth) in the model. finally, they included a random intercept term for the experimental sites of studies data from previous studies (i.e., chinese provinces). to identify effective crop management practices for improving maize wp and yield, authors pooled studies that included side-by-side comparisons of different crop management practices (i.e., the treatment was the same as the control in all aspects except for the each crop management practice) and calculated effect sizes for pairwise comparisons: optimal irrigation vs. farmer’ irrigation; plastic mulch vs. no mulch; straw re-incorporation vs. no straw re-incorporation; deep tillage/deep ripping vs. rotary tillage; no tillage vs. rotary tillage; ridge planting vs. flat planting; and polymer application vs. no polymer application.
background: Understanding water productivity (WP) on a regional scale is useful for identifying and managing inefficiencies in irrigated crop production systems. However, relevant WP analyses are not available for maize production systems in China.
objective: the authors conducted a meta-analysis of maize yield and water use data presented in peer-reviewed studies in northern china (2354 observations from 282 studies) to: 1) investigate the current state of irrigated maize wp and influencing factors, 2) evaluate management practices to improve wp, and 3) estimate the boundary function for wp within different maize-production regions.
result1: plastic mulch significantly improved yield compared to no mulching.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: plastic mulch significantly improved yield compared to no mulching.

search_strategy: using google scholar, web of science and china national knowledge infrastructure, we collected pub- lished peer-reviewed papers that reported crop yield and crop water productivity as affected by various farming practices under a range of conditions in china from 1980 to 2019, using the following key words: ridge-furrow, cultivation, film mulching, rainfall harvest system, crop yield and crop water productivity.
selection_criteria: (1) field experiment was conducted in china; (2) the study contained the control treatment: conventional flat planting without film mulching (f), and at least one of those three treatments: ridge-furrow planting with film mulching (rffm), ridge-furrow planting without film mulching (rf) and flat planting with film mulching (fm); (3)the crop water pro- ductivity (wp, kg ha−1 mm−1) of mulched or ridged crop was calcu- lated as the ratio of crop yield (kg ha−1) to the water consumed by the crop or crop evapotranspiration (et, mm) in the growing season (fernándeza et al., 2020; meng et al., 2020); (4) crop yield and wp for one study had mean and variance, or at least two replicates, or more than two years of data; (5) location, year, planting on the ridge or in the furrow were stated; (6) papers with the same test data to those in the other papers were removed, and the combined effects of various treatments in one study such as fertilization, irrigation and planting density, were ignored; (7) the order of ridges or planting, the color difference of plastic film, and the difference in shape and size of the ridge in the same study were ignored, regardless of whether the ridge was continuously ridged or whether the film was covered both on the ridge and in the furrow or just on the ridge.
data_analysis: since most studies collected in this study did not provide variance, an unweighted approach proposed by chen et al. (2013) was considered by using meta win 2.1. a random-effect model was used to assess the impact of rffm, rf and fm on crop yield and wp compared with f. when the number of observations was less than 20, bootstrapping with 9999 iterations was used to generate bias corrected 95 % confidence interval(ci) of mean effect sizes because confidence limits based on bootstrapping tests were wider than standard confidence limits. differences in the mean effect size among groups were calculated using random effect models. the difference was considered significant if the bootstrap confidence interval did not overlap each other. the effect of farming practices was considered significantly different from con- ventional flat planting (p<0.05) if the 95 % ci did not reach zero.
background: Crop yields are significantly restricted by the shortage of water resources in semi-arid and semi-humid regions around the world. Farming practices like ridge-furrow planting with plastic film mulching (RFFM) can effec- tively improve crop yield and crop water productivity (WP) by enhancing soil moisture and temperature availability.
objective: the main objective of this study was thus to comprehensively evaluate the performances of three major farming practices, ridge-furrow planting with plastic film mulching (rffm), ridge-furrow planting without film mulching (rf) and flat planting with film mulching (fm) in comparison with conventional flat planting without film mulching (f) on yield and wp of wheat, maize and potato in china under a range of conditions (i.e., planting region, climatic condition, altitude, soil type and seeding method) based on meta-analysis.
result1: different farming practices significantly increased mean crop yields (rffm: 33.8 %; ffm: 27.0 %).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: both ridge-furrow planting with plastic film mulching and flat planting with film mulching significantly increased yield of wheat, maize and potato, when compared with the conventional flat planting without film mulching.

search_strategy: the authors used ‘straw returning’ or ‘straw mulching,’ and ‘maize’ in the keyword search to collect peer-reviewed journal articles from the china national knowledge infrastructure and web of science.
selection_criteria: to avoid any bias, the authors selected publications with the following criteria: 1) field experiment; 2) cropping system includes maize; 3) included control (no straw returning; ck) and treatments (straw mulching or straw incorporation); 4) means, standard deviations (or standard error), and number of replications available or can be calculated; 5) included yield or water use efficiency measurements.
data_analysis: to derive the overall response effect of the treatments (straw mulching or straw incorporation) groups and control (no straw returning) group, the weighted response ratio (rr++) between the treatments (straw mulching or straw incorporation) groups and control (no straw returning) group was calculated. metawin2.1 was used to generate 95% confidence intervals around the logarithmic response ratios (rr) with 4999 iterations. the authors applied a t-test to determine variation in each variable between the control and treatment and the difference in rr++ between subgroups.
background: Straw mulching and straw incorporation are widely used for conservation tillage as the primary methods of returning straw to the field. However, few studies have investigated the effects of straw mulching and straw incorporation under various agronomic management and environmental and edaphic factors.
objective: in this study the authors undertook a meta-analysis to: 1) analyze the effects of n application rate, straw returning amount, annual average precipitation, temperature, and evaporation, and soil texture on maize yield, wue, and nue with straw mulching and straw incorporation; 2) identify suitable methods of straw returning for different temperatures, precipitation, and soil textures in china; 3) determine the appropriate of straw returning amount and n application rate.
result1: the meta-analysis showed that straw mulching significantly increased maize yields (rr++: 0.0862).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: straw mulching has a positive effect on maize yield.

search_strategy: a literature search was conducted to retrieve articles published from 1997 to 2021 on mulching and the yield and water use efficiency (wue) of winter wheat in the dryland area of the loess plateau. the web of science and china national knowledge infrastructure databases were searched with the following keywords: “winter wheat” and “plastic film mulching /straw mulching /mulching” and “yield /water use efficiency”.
selection_criteria: 1) the experimental locations were in the loess plateau; 2) the experimental method was a field trial with no irrigation throughout the crop growth stage; 3) the experimental treatments included plastic film mulching or straw mulching, with no mulching as the control for each treatment; 4) the yield, wue, and other indicators of winter wheat were reported in the form of digits, figures, or tables; 5) articles with repeat data (the same experimental locations, years, and results) were excluded.
data_analysis: because most of the studies did not provide variance, an unweighted method was adopted and meta win 2.1 was used to bias-correct the 95% confidence intervals (cis). differences in mean effect size among groups were calculated using random effect models. a bootstrapping pro- cedure (9999 iterations) was used to improve the probability that the confidence interval was calculated around the cumulative mean effect size for each categorical variable. if the 95% confidence interval did not overlap with zero, there are significant positive or negative differences between mulching and no-mulching treatments (p＜0.05); otherwise, the treatment effect was not considered significant between methods.
background: Mulching practice reduces evaporation, modifies soil temperature and thereby affects crop yields. But the effects of mulching practices on moisture preservation and yield increase are not consistent under different precipitation and temperature conditions. The Loess Plateau spans a wide range, with distinct spatiotemporal variation in its hydrothermal conditions, so the reported effects of mulching are sometimes contradictory. A
objective: hence in this study, we focused on the situation in the loess plateau to study the effects of mulching on yield, water consumption and water use efficiency under different temperatures and precipitation situation.
result1: the analysis of the yield gap under different mulching practices indicated a decreasing trend under pfm conditions, whereas little difference was observed under sm compared with no mulching treatment.
result2: when the yield gap change rates under pfm and sm conditions were analysed with no mulching treatment as the control, both pfm and sm reduced the yield gap significantly.
result3: pfm increased wheat yield by 24%, while straw mulching resulted in a yield increase of 12%.
general_conclusion: plastic film mulching and straw mulching significantly increased wheat yield compared with no mulching.

search_strategy: the authors searched the china national knowledge infrastructure and the web of science for peer-reviewed papers reporting the effects of fm on alfalfa yield and wue in china with a cut-off date of 31 may 2021. the search terms included mulch, film, straw, rainwater har- vesting, and alfalfa, and the search was limited to the titles, abstracts, and keywords of the papers.
selection_criteria: non-english-language publications and conference proceedings were excluded. a paper had to meet the following criteria to be included in the analysis: (1) the experiment was conducted under field conditions in china including both fm and non- mulching (nm) treatments; (2) average yield or wue, its standard de- viation, and sample sizes of fm and nm treatments were provided or could be calculated; (3) key basic information was clear, including the location, experimental year, average annual temperature (aat), average annual precipitation (aap), altitude, mulching scope, planting pattern, mulching material, growth year, sowing rate (sr), and nitrogen application rate (nar); and (4) if the same experimental data were published in different journals, then the paper with the most information was selected.
data_analysis: the mean percentage change was considered significantly different from zero if its 95% ci did not overlap zero. a positive percentage change indicated an increase under fm compared with nm. otherwise, a decrease occurred. to analyze whether there were statistically significant differences between the results of different studies, heterogeneity analysis was tested using the q statistic in our study. both rank correlation tests and funnel plots were used in our study to test for publication bias.
background: Alfalfa (Medicago sativa L.), a globally vital forage crop with abundant nutrition and high yield, is commonly planted in arid and semi-arid regions where water resources are scare, such as China. In order to adapt water limitation conditions, farmland mulching (FM) is gradually being applied in alfalfa production. However, the effects of FM on alfalfa in different climatic conditions and management practices should be investigated before concluding that it is universally effective.
objective: the authors conducted a meta-analysis and regression analysis to systematically analyze available information on the effects of fm on alfalfa yield and wue in china. specifically, the objectives were to: 1) quantify the effects of fm on alfalfa yield and wue in china; 2) investigate how these effects varied with environmental conditions and management practices; 3) provide the direction for further improving the alfalfa production under fm conditions.
result1: overall, the alfalfa yield significantly increased with fm compared with nm, resulting in a mean increase rate (ir) of 38.5% (95% ci = 30.8–46.7%).
result2: however, the increase rate (ir) of yield varied with mulching type, region, management, and length of growth year.
general_conclusion: plastic film mulching significantly increased alfalfa yield on average by 38.5% compared to no mulching.

search_strategy: published journal articles related to the effect of film mulching on soc and soil ghg fluxes were searched for on web of science using the following research keywords: ts = (mulch) and (soil) and (carbon or “nitrous oxide” or n2o or methane or ch4 or “greenhouse gas”). additionally, the china national knowledge infrastructure was used to search for published articles related to our topics. in addition, we also searched for other articles via literature citations that were not covered by these keywords.
selection_criteria: first, the selected studies must contain at least one of our targets (soc in the 0–20 cm layer, ch4 emissions/uptake and n2o emissions) in both non-mulched and film-mulched soils. second, management practices, such as the amount/type of fertilization, must be consistent in both treatments. third, we selected observations of soc and soil ghg fluxes from only field experiments rather than from pot or greenhouse experiments. fourth, because upland fields are generally atmospheric ch4 sinks and paddy fields are generally atmospheric ch4 sources, we considered the effects of plastic film mulching on ch4 uptake only in uplands and on ch4 emissions only in paddy fields. in addition, we did not consider a few studies that reported opposite results for ch4 fluxes.
data_analysis: NA
background: The use of plastic film in agriculture strongly affects the decomposition of soil organic carbon (SOC) and the release of methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O) by influencing soil biogeochemical processes. However, no systematic conclusions have been reached regarding the effect of plastic film mulching on SOC stocks and greenhouse gas (GHG) budgets.
objective: a meta-analysis was performed to analyze the effect of film mulching on soc and soil ghg fluxes across different agricultural systems and to identify the major factors affecting their responses to film mulching to address the following questions: (1) how does plastic film mulching influence soc and soil ghg fluxes across different agricultural ecosystems (rainfed uplands, irrigated uplands and paddy fields) and (2) how do mulching variables (e.g., the coverage ratio, film type, mulching method and film thickness) and environmental variables affect soc and soil ghg fluxes under film mulching?
result1: plastic film mulching also significantly (p < 0.05) increased crop yield and shoot and root biomass by 48.6%, 51.4% and 57.8%, respectively.
result2: specifically, the agricultural system, coverage ratio, film type and film thickness significantly (p < 0.05) affected the response of crop yield to mulching.
result3: film mulching significantly (p < 0.05) increased yields by 60.2%, 32.5% and 6.2% in rainfed uplands, irrigated uplands and paddy fields, respectively.
result4: low and high coverage ratios significantly increased yields by 38.8% and 56.8%, respectively.
result5: transparent, black and biodegradable film mulching significantly enhanced crop yields by 71.8%, 35.1% and 25.7%, respectively. in addition, thin and thick film mulching significantly increased crop yields by 55.0% and 34.9%, respectively.
general_conclusion: plastic film mulching, including mulching covering 50% and 100% of the area, biodegradable film, black and transparent film, different thickness, all have a positive effect on crop yield.

search_strategy: relevant literature of the grain yield of maize with different mulching and tillage practices was searched using the online databases of the chinese academy of sciences (http://www.isiknowledge.com.proxy.insermbiblio.inist.fr/ and http://www.cnki.net/) and google scholar (http://scholar.google.com.proxy.insermbiblio.inist.fr/). the search terms were ‘mulch’ or ‘mulching’, ‘maize’ and ‘yield’ in the article title, abstract, and keywords.
selection_criteria: (1) the studies had to be conducted in the field and include both control (no mulch and flat plots, ck) and treatments (either flat or ridge-and-furrow tillage and/or straw or plastic-film mulch) (table 1); (2) the maize was not be irrigated at any time within the growing season; (3) the location and year of the experiment were provided; (4) for factorial experiments, only data from non-mulched and mulched treatments were used and data from interactions among treatments, such as fertilization × straw mulch or plastic-film mulch, were excluded; (5) data without a control treatment, that is sown on flat plots without mulch, were only used for regression analysis, not in the meta-analysis.
data_analysis: authors used a fixed effect model because the estimate of the mean pooled variances for maize yield, wue, et and soil types (clay loam, silt loam and clay) were less than or equal to zero. the metawin2.1 was applied to generate 95% confidence intervals around the logarithmic response ratios with 4999 iterations. regression analysis was used to analyze the relationships between observed maize yield and growing-season (late april to early october) precipitation and temperature under the five management practices.
background: Ridge-furrow mulching can reduce soil evaporation and conserve rainfall, thereby increasing crop yield and water use efficiency (WUE) in dryland cropping systems.
objective: this meta-analysis aimed to quantify the effects of different mulch and tillage practices on maize yields, wue and evapotranspiration across a series of hydrothermal gradients.
result1: the meta-analysis showed that all four mulch and tillage treatments significantly increased maize yields (mean effect sizes were greater than 0) relative to the respective control; straw mulched flat plots (smf) by 9%, straw mulched ridge-furrow plots (smr) by 12%, plastic mulched flat plots (pmf) by 33% and plastic mulched ridge-furrow plots (pmr) by 58% relative to their respective control. the mean effect sizes of the mulch/tillage practices were ranked in the order of pmr > smr = smf. the mean effect of pmr was 0.282 (95% ci: 0.278–0.286), pmf it was 0.258 (0.097–0.420), smr it was 0.121 (0.100–0.143), and smf it was 0.106 (0.093–0.118), thus the maize yield in the pmr treatment was significantly greater than in the smr and smf treatments, but not the pmf treatment.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: the meta-analysis has shown that both straw and plastic mulch significantly increased maize yield.

search_strategy: a search of the peer-reviewed published papers was performed to collect data on the effects of mulching on potato yield and wue in china up to december 2017. data published in english were collected from the isi-web of science (http://apps.webofknowledge.com/) and google scholar (google inc., mountain view, ca, usa), and data published in chinese were collected from the china national knowledge infrastructure (http://www.cnki.net/).
selection_criteria: data collections were restricted to field experimental studies containing at least one of the two major mulching practices (i.e. plastic and/or straw mulching) and no-mulching control. a study was included if it contained available data on potato yield and/or wue.
data_analysis: mean effect sizes and bias-corrected 95% confidence intervals (cis) were generated using a bootstrapping procedure (4999 iterations).
background: As one of the main food crops in China, potato is widely planted under various mulching practices. However, the effects of mulching practices often differ and are in some cases contradictory in the literature, since the effects may be influenced by different climatic conditions, soil characteristics, crop species, and field managements
objective: the objectives of our study were (1) to quantify the effects of two major mulching practices (plastic and straw mulching) on the yield and wue of potato in china, and (2) to investigate how the effects of mulching vary with respect to location, temperature, water input and fertilizer applications.
result1: the yield of potato was significantly increased by both plastic mulching and straw mulching compared to the no-mulching control. on average, the increase in potato yield with plastic mulching was 24.3%, significantly higher than that of straw mulching (16.0%).
result2: geographic regions, mean growth air temperature and water input had significant effects on potato yield, respectively. potato yield significantly responded to n and k inputs. there were significant interactions between temperature and water input in potato yield during growing season. the interactions between water and input, water and p input, n and k input, water, n, p and k input were also significant.
general_conclusion: mulching significantly increased the yield of potato compared with no-mulching practice.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed literature related to the impacts of tfm and bfm on crop growth and economic benefits was systematically searched for using the web of science, springerlink, and the cnki database before december 2018.
selection_criteria: the studies on potato, maize, or wheat production had to be conducted in the field, and the crops were harvested at maturity. second, the trials had to include three treatments: non-mulching, tfm, and bfm. for instance, studies that described only the relationship between bfm and yield, or between tfm and yield were rejected. in each study, except for the comparison of the mulching systems (non-mulching, tfm, and bfm), the other soil properties and management conditions (including seeds, chemical fertilizers, machinery, and pesticides) had to be the same. no herbicide is used in bfm system because of the low light permeability of the black plastic film.
data_analysis: r (version 3.6.1) was used to perform the data analysis. because sampling variances were not available for individual observations, bootstrapping procedures in the ‘boot’ package were used to obtain 95 % confidence intervals (cis) for weighted mean effect sizes using 4999 iterations. one-way analysis of variance (anova) with statistical analysis system program was conducted to determine the significance of differences in soil temperature, soil water storage, and weeds biomass (fig. 4) and net economic benefits. when the anova results were significant, the least significant difference (lsd) test was employed to determine the significance of the differences between treatments with a significance level of p < 0.05.
background: Plastic film mulching systems are widely used in crop production because of great benefits in increasing crop yields, but transparent film mulching (TFM) has negative impacts on crop production due to the high soil temperature under certain conditions. Because of its lower impacts on soil temperature, black film mulching (BFM) is being considered as an alternative to TFM.
objective: the aims of the present research were to 1) quantify the effects of tfm and bfm on crop growth and yield; 2) estimate the economic benefits of applying tfm and bfm; 3) provide solutions for the future development of film mulching systems.
result1: the overall effects of film mulching on yield were positive, with increases of 22 % and 23 % for potato, 17 % and 24 % for maize, and 33 % and 35 % for wheat under tfm and bfm, respectively.
result2: compared with tfm, bfm significantly increased maize yield by 6%, while there was no difference between tfm and bfm in potato and wheat yield.
result3: compared with tfm, bfm significantly increased the marketable tuber rate by 9%. for maize production, film mulching increased aboveground biomass by 27–32 %, compared with non-mulching. in wheat production, film mulching increased aboveground biomass by 58–59 %, while there was no significant difference in these factors between tfm and bfm.
general_conclusion: the overall effects of film mulching on yield were positive, with increases of 22 % and 23 % for potato, 17 % and 24 % for maize, and 33 % and 35 % for wheat under transparent film mulching and black film mulching, respectively.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed journal articles reporting maize and wheat yields and greenhouse gas emissions as affected by soil mulching up to may 2021 were collected to build the database based on web of science (http://apps.webofknowledge.com/), the google scholar (http://www.scholar.google.com), china national knowledge infrastructure (https://www.cnki.net/) and the wanfang data of china (http://www.wanfangdata.com.cn/) using the following search formulation: yield* and (greenhouse gas* or ch4 or n2o or co2 or methane or nitrous oxide or carbon oxide) and mulch* and (maize or corn or wheat).
selection_criteria: (1) the field experimental design was clear; (2) the study included the conventional flat planting with no mulching (nm) and at least one mulching practice, i.e. plastic film mulching (pm) and straw mulching (sm); (3) at least one kind of ghg emissions (n2o, co2 and ch4) over an entire season was reported; (4) the means and standard deviations (sds) could be obtained from the tables or figures by getdata graph digitizer.
data_analysis:
the effect size was measured by the natural log of the response ratio (ln r), which was calculated by the ratio of the mean values of the experimental group under soil mulching (xt) and the mean values of corresponding control treatment (xc). weighting approach tends to be well replicated in field experiments, assigning greater weight to estimate effect size more precise. mean effect
sizes were estimated as a weighted average. meta win 2.1 was used to pro- duce mean effect sizes and 95 % bootstrapped cis (rosenberg et al., 2000). for ease of interpretation, all analysis results were reported as the percentage change with soil mulching (pm and sm) relative to the control treatment (non-mulching).
background: Understanding the effects of soil mulching on crop yields and greenhouse gas (N2O, CO2 and CH4) emissions is important for developing sustainable agriculture. However, no systematic conclusions have been drawn yet because the environmental factors vary among various studies.
objective: evaluate the impact of plastic film mulching (pm) and straw mulching (sm) on crop yield from two major cereal crops (maize and wheat)
result1: maize yields were significantly enhanced by straw mulching (7.3 %) and plastic film mulching (13.3 %) compared to that of no-mulching.
result2: compared with the effect of straw mulching on wheat yields (3.5 %), the increase in wheat yield under plastic film mulching was significantly enhanced (12.5 %).
general_conclusion: plastic mulching, straw mulching and plastic-covered ridge coupled with furrow planting zone with bare soil significantly increased maize yield and wheat yield compared with no mulching, when averaged across all studies. only straw mulching showed no effect on wheat yield.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed journal articles were explored in the web of science, china national knowledge infrastructure (cnki), and google scholar using the keywords ‘soil mulching or straw mulching or film mulching’ and ‘yield or greenhouse gas or ghg or carbon dioxide or nitrous oxide or ch4 or co2 or n2o’ for the years 2000 –2020.
selection_criteria: (a) the experimental site must be in china, and experimental crops are wheat, maize, or rice; (b) the research must be field experiments, every treatment must be in triplicate at minimum, and the number of replicates should be indicated in the paper; (c) there must be a corresponding no-mulching (nm) control treatment; (d) the sm treatment must involve natural decay, and no articles with added decomposition agents or microbial strains to speed up straw decay are included, and (e) yield observations must be the current season, and ghg observations must be cumulative emissions, or provide average emissions and the days of growing season.
data_analysis: to assess for potential bias, the authors used forest plots of individual studies, which enabled us to visualize the relationship between sample size and effect size. furthermore, the authors tested publication bias with egger regression, and the trim-and-fill method was used to evaluate the impact of publication bias to the results. the “metafor” package (version 2.4–0) and “forestplot” package (1.10.1) in r (version 4.0.3)were applied in the above data analysis process. the authors performed a model selection analysis to calculate the relative importance of all predictive variables affecting the effect size of response variables under soil mulching, using the “glmulti” package (1.0.8) in r 4.0.3.
background: Soil mulching either with plastic film or straw is a common agricultural practice, which can improve crop growth by reducing evaporation and regulating soil temperature, and is widely applied globally. Although soil mulching can significantly affect crop yield and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, there is controversy regarding its effect on crop yield and GHG emissions in the long run.
objective: this study had three main objectives: (a) evaluate the overall impact of two dominant soil mulching methods (fm and sm) on yield and ghg emissions in maize, wheat, and rice, according to published research in china; (b) determine the most important factors affecting the response variables under soil mulching through the model selection analysis of relevant agronomic measures, soil factors, and meteorological climate factors, and (c) quantify the impact of n input, annual mean temperature (amt), and annual total precipitation (atp) on mulching performance.
result1: soil mulching had a positive effect on yield increase, and the effect size was moderated by agronomic practices, soil texture, and mulching method. the average effect size of soil mulching was 19% (95% ci: 16 – 22%); i.e., crop yield increased by 19% under soil mulching compared with nm.
result2: mulching with plastic film and straw increased yield by 39% (95% ci: 26 – 52%), which was higher than for mulching with plastic film (28%) and mulching with straw (9%). also, different mulching ratios significantly affected yield, full film (34%) resulted in a higher yield than for half film (21%).
result3: crop type and planting method were the main agronomic practices affecting crop yield. the yield increase was greater in double-furrow planting (66%) compared to flat planting (29%) and ridge-furrow planting (24%).
general_conclusion: overall, soil mulching improved crop yield (16 – 22%). plastic film mulching and straw mulching increased yield by 28% and 9% compared with no-mulching, respectively.

search_strategy: to investigate the effect of fm on soil microbial abundance, diversity, and functional parameters, the authors conducted an extensive search of peer-viewed articles of databases including web of science, google scholar, and china knowledge resource integrated database in june 2020. the following keyword combinations were used as the first step to screen articles: “plastic film” or “film mulch” and “microbial commu- nity” or “microbiome”.
selection_criteria: 1) field-based study with an experimental design allowing pairwise comparison between film mulch treatments and bare soil controls; 2) at least one soil microbial community parameter (abundance, diversity, or function) was reported; 3) treatment pairs established with same ecosystem types, crop types, and soil types; 4) for articles with experimental data for more than one growing season/year, only the last data were extracted for meta- analysis; the approach can greatly eliminate the non-independence of the data.
data_analysis: all statistics were conducted using r v 3.6.0. to correct for the nested structure and non-independence of observations, we used the mixed-effect models to evaluate the effects of pm on soil microbial parameters and other related properties, the models were constructed via rma.mv() function in the “metafor”package and the overall effect and the 95% confidence interval (ci) were calculated. the sensitivity of the few variables with potential publication bias was then examined using the trim-and-fill model. we conducted “leave-one-out” tests to check the robustness of variables’ effect sizes by function leave1out() in package “metafor”, this is a kind of sensitivity analysis; the funnel plots were used to display the comparison of data from all cases to the aggregated weighted mean within-study suggests.
background: Plastic film mulch alters the soil environment and improves crop production. Although the response of above- ground parts of agroecosystems to plastic film mulch has been extensively studied, no studies have investigated the response of the soil microbiome to plastic film mulch and its effect on crop yield.
objective: the study aimed to: 1) explore whether fm shapes distinct soil microbial abundance, diversity, and functionality patterns; 2) clarify the underlying drivers of these responses; 3) determine whether microbial parameters are related to changes in crop yield and whether these parameters belong to specific microbial parameters, such as abundance, diversity or functionality.
result1: the mean effect size for crop yield increased significantly (+0.389, 95% ci: +0.333 to + 0.444).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: plastic film mulching has a positive effect on crop yield.

search_strategy: a comprehensive search for peer-reviewed publications related to the effect of pm on crop yields and environmental impacts from jan 1980 to dec 2015 was conducted using two databases: web of science and the china academic journal network publishing database. the article titles, abstracts, and keywords were searched using the terms ‘wheat or maize’, ‘plastic mulch or soil manage- ment’, and ‘china’.
selection_criteria: (1) comparisons between pm and nm practices were made; (2) at least one parameter of interest (yield, evapotranspiration (et), water use efficiency (wue), harvest index, soil carbon, soil nitrogen, or amount of plastic film residue) was re- ported, and (3) the experimental location was stated. studies that described only the relationship between pm and crop yield without a nm treatment or that did not provide a clear description of the experimental methods were rejected.
data_analysis: the mean value of all observations on a countrywide scale was calculated by weighting, and the weight was calculated by replications. statistical analyses were con- ducted using the regression procedure of sas v9.2. the relationship between yield increase and increase in ghg emission was analyzed using regression analysis. fisher's test was used to determine the significance of the differences between means with a significance level of p < 0.05.
background: Numerous individual reports have emphasized the importance of soil surface plastic mulch (PM) as an auxiliary means of increasing crop yields, but a comprehensive assessment of yields and environmental benefits on a national scale has not been performed.
objective: the authors collected and synthesized data pertaining to crop production and ghg emissions under no-mulch (nm) and plastic mulch (pm) in china to: 1) explore the reasons for variation in yield increase caused by pm application; 2) quantify the ghg emissions associated with pm application; 3) determine the appropriate conditions for pm application based on managing the tradeoffs between yield increase and ghg emissions.
result1: the authors quantified yield increases due to pm applications on a countrywide scale, and found that adoption of pm overall increased the mean yield by 18% for wheat and 27% for maize.
result2: crop yield varies profoundly with precipitation and n inputs. wheat and maize yields under nm and pm were increased as the annual precipitation and n inputs increase. in comparison with nm, yield increases under pm increased gradually with n inputs increase, whereas it gradually reduced with increasing annual precipitation.
general_conclusion: the adoption of plastic mulch overall increased the mean yield by 18% for wheat and 27% for maize.

search_strategy: the selected publications were collected by searching isi web of science database and china knowledge resource integrated database using the following search criteria: ts = (plastic mulching∗) and (soil organic carbon∗ or microbial biomass carbon∗ or enzyme activities∗ or co2∗ or ch4∗) and ts = (film mulching∗ or plastic mulching∗) and (maize∗ or wheat∗ or potato∗ or yield∗ or root∗ or biomass∗).
selection_criteria: (i) the selected study included at least one parameter of interest (i.e. response variables) as economic yield (ey), aboveground biomass (ab), root biomass (rb), soil organic carbon (soc), co2 emission, ch4 flux, microbial biomass carbon (mbc), c‒related soil enzyme activities (i.e. glucosidase, sucrase, catalase, urease and alkaline phosphatase); (ii) only field study with replicated experimental design was included, greenhouse and laboratory incubation experiments excluded. pairwise comparisons on mulching and non‒mulching farming management were performed under the same pedo‒climatic conditions (e.g., temperature, precipitation, soil texture, and soil type) for at least 2 consecutive years; (iii) provided treatment means, sample sizes, and variances, or these could be extracted from tables or the figures using software; (v) duration of plastic mulching should be at least one full crop season for each year. when there were more than one articles on the same experiment, the article with longest mulching duration was included; (iv) to avoid pre‒mulching heterogeneity of soc stock between treatment and control, the values of soc contents at the beginning and end of each trial should be provided for the calculation of actual changes due to mulching. however, only few studies provided the baseline values of soc stocks for both experimental and control plots. given the fact that all data considered originated from pairwise system comparisons including controlled field trials, baseline differences in soc stocks among the different plots of one comparison were expected to be negligible. the authors therefore decided to also included the studies that the baseline values were not known into the data pool.
data_analysis: a mixed effect model that included a random effect for multiple studies from the same site was performed to calculate the mean effect sizes and variances for the concerned response variables. the authors used heterogeneity tests to confirm if models could explain significant variation. the majority of results show significant inter‒study heterogeneity, so the authors rejected the null hypothesis that all studies share a common effect size in favor of the interpretation that true effect sizes vary between studies. the sensitivity of the results was examined using the trim‒and‒fill model (i.e. the authors repeated the model for each of concerned responsory variable to account for the number of missing studies). the authors tested for potential publication bias using egger’s regression. the analysis results did not suggest that there was bias in most cases.
background: Plastic mulching provides many advantages for crop production, especially in dry croplands, such as reducing evaporation, improving water temperature conditions, and minimizing soil erosion. After three decades of practical application, however, a comprehensive nationwide assessment of its potential environmental consequences, in terms of SOC stock, was not available.
objective: the objective was to quantify the nationwide effects of plastic mulching application on crop net primary productivity, soil c fluxes, and total soc pool, and further identify the dominant environmental, edaphic, and anthropogenic drivers on these effects.
result1: the mean effect sizes were 38% (95% ci: 33–45%) for aboveground biomass and 55% (95% ci: 45–55%) for economic yield. crop type and planting density were the most influential agronomic factors on crop productivity.  soil texture significantly affected mulching‒induced enhancement of crop productivity, especially for grain yield. the magnitude of effect sizes significantly increased with elevation, but decreased with mean growing season precipitation and temperature for both biomass and grain yield (p < 0.001).
result2: averaged across the three crop types, plastic mulching increased the national aboveground net primary productivity by 1.41 mg c ha−1 y−1 compared with non‒mulching.
general_conclusion: overall, plastic mulching brought cop productivity benefits compared with traditional non‒mulching farming; the magnitude was strongly affected by agronomic, environmental, and edaphic factors.

search_strategy: we comprehensively collected peer-reviewed journal articles of publications investigating the effects of applying plastic film mulching technology on crop fields domestically and abroad from 1980 to december 2017. data were collected from the web of science and the china national knowledge infrastructure. search terms included ‘plastic film’ and ‘residual plastic film’ in the article title, abstract, and keywords.
selection_criteria: conference proceedings publications were excluded. due to the lack ofrelevant field trials covering plastic film use in peanut, rice, soybean, and sunflower, we removed those crops from the analysis. the database only contained articles and papers based on the following criteria: (1) the research area was located within china; (2) studies had to contain plastic mulching and no-mulching treatments or plastic residue and no residual control; (3) a study was only included if it contained available data on crop yield or wue; (4) crop yield or wue included mean and standard deviation or more than two repeats or test duration at least two years; (5) location, year, and color of plastic mulching film of the experiments were stated; and (6) we eliminated duplicates ofthe same data appearing in different articles, and ignored the confounding effects between treatments (differences in planting density, fertilization, etc.).
data_analysis: because most of the studies did not provide variance, an unweighted method was adopted and meta win 2.1 was used to bias-correct the 95% confidence intervals (cis). differences in mean effect size among groups were calculated using random effect models. a bootstrapping procedure (9999 iterations) was used to improve the probability that the confidence interval was calculated around the cumulative mean effect size for each categorical variable. if the 95% confidence interval did not overlap with zero, there are significant positive or negative differences between mulching and no-mulching treatments (p < 0.05); otherwise the treatment effect was not considered significant between methods.
background: China is a large agricultural country, and food security is significantly limited by the shortage of water resources. Plastic mulching technology can effectively modify the crop growth environment and crop production due to differences in climatic conditions, spatial distribution characteristics, and cropping systems and methods.
objective: the objectives of this study, therefore, were: (1) to examine the effect ofmulching on yield and wue of different crops in china; (2) to analyze how the effects of mulching vary with respect to location, film color, and mulching methods; and (3) to quantify the effects of plastic residue on yield of crops in china.
result1: the yield of all four crops were significantly increased by plastic mulching compared to the no-mulching control.
result2: average mean effects of plastic mulching on crop yield for the four crops was 24.32%.
general_conclusion: plastic mulching significantly increased crop yield (24%). residual plastic has a negative effect on yield.

search_strategy: a search of peer-reviewed publications was performed to collect data on the effects of pm on yield, economic benefit, nr, and nitrogen footprint of potato, maize, and wheat grown in china. data published in english were collected from google scholar and isi-web of science, and data published in chinese were collected from baidu scholar and the china national knowledge infrastructure. the keywords were searched using the terms “potato, maize, or wheat”, “mulch, plastic mulch, or soil management”, and “china”.
selection_criteria: (1) the field studies must include treatmentswith pmand non-pmcontrol (nm); (2) the amount of fertilizers application, plant density, and yield were reported or amena- ble to being calculated from the data; (3) the means, standard devia- tions (or standard errors), and sample sizes of the variables concerned must be directly available or amenable to being calculated from the data; and (4) the experimental locationwas stated. data were recorded by experimental year for publications reporting results frommulti-year experiments. the year of publication was restricted from 1970 to july 2019, the publications after july 2019were not included.
data_analysis: the weighted mean log ratio (ln−r) was calculated for all independent studies. the kolmogorov-smirnov test indicated that the distributions of yield, economic benefit, nr, nfg, and nfe were not a typical normal distribution (p < 0.05). therefore, confidence interval (ci) values were generated using the bootstrapping test for yield, economic benefit, nr, nfg, and nfe. a mixed-effects model was employed to estimate whether pm significantly affected each dependent variable using the statistical software metawin 2.1 with a resampling of 9999 iterations. if the 95% bootstrapping ci values for a variable did not overlap zero, the effect of the pm treatment on thevariablewas significant; otherwise, it was not significant. means of the different categorical variables were considered significantly different from one another if their 95% bootstrapping cis did not overlap.
background: Sustainably feeding the growing population amid rising global temperatures and dwindling resources is a grand challenge facing mankind. Plastic mulching (PM) is widely used in China aiming to the increase of crop produc- tivity. However, the impact ofPM on reactive nitrogen (Nr) emissions and nitrogen (N) footprint has not been explicitly described.
objective: the present study is a meta-analysis of field experiments on food crop production with pm in china that seeks answers to determine: 1) how yield, economic benefit, nr, and n footprint of major food crops respond to pm; 2) whether this is influenced by crop species, growing region, n fertilizer rate, or precipitation.
result1: overall, pm significantly increased yield and energy output. the effects of pm on yield were parallel to the energy output from economic yield.
result2: yield under pm was significantly increased by an average of 24% compared to nm.
general_conclusion: plastic mulching has a positive effect on yield for potato, maize and wheat.

search_strategy: the authors conducted an exhaustive literature search in the databases of the web of science and china national knowledge infrastructure by searching for ‘mulching’, ‘film mulching’ and ‘degradable film mulching’ in the titles, abstracts and keywords of articles published before 31 july 2019.
selection_criteria: publications were selected based on the criteria: 1) the research area was within china; 2) field studies had to contain df mulching and nf treatments or pf mulching; 3) maize, wheat, potato and cotton were studied because mulching areas are much larger for these four crops than for other crops in china; 4) a study was included if it contained data for crop yield or wue.
data_analysis: the analysis of confidence intervals (cis) was used to compare the magnitude of the response ratio between df and pf mulching or nf mulching. the authors used an unweighted method and meta win 2.1 to bias-correct the 95% cis. differences in mean effect size among groups were calculated using random-effect models.
background: Degradable film (DF) has recently been demonstrated to be a good alternative to plastic film (PF) for mulching crops such as maize, wheat, potato and cotton. Whether or not the yield-increasing and water-saving effects of DF mulching vary with DF properties (type, color and thickness), field management (planting pattern) and environmental conditions (altitude, air temperature, rainfall and evaporation), however, are largely unknown.
objective: the objectives were to: 1) determine whether df could replace pf for agricultural production; 2) identify the optimal type, color, thickness and mulching pattern of df for maize, wheat, potato and cotton; 3) identify the best environmental conditions for df mulching to increase yield and wue for growing maize, wheat, potato and cotton.
result1: crop yield for df mulching were 2.8% (ci: 1.7–3.9%) lower (p<0.05) than pf mulching, and were 18.0% (ci: 16.1–20.0%) higher (p<0.05) than nf mulching.
result2: potato yield was 5.0% higher, and maize, wheat and cotton yields were 3.8% (p<0.05), 2.3% and 3.1% (p<0.05) lower, respectively, for df than pf mulching.
result3: maize, wheat, potato and cotton yields were 17.5%, 15.6%, 20.4% and 20.4% higher (p<0.05), respectively, for df than nf mulching.
general_conclusion: crop yield for degradable film mulching was 2.8% lower (ci: 1.7–3.9%) (p<0.05) compared with plastic film mulching, and 18.0% higher (ci: 16.1–20.0%) (p<0.05) compared with no mulching.

search_strategy: by the access of web of science (thomson reuters, new york, ny, usa), google scholar, and baidu scholar, search terms “plastic film” and “root” or “film mulch” and “root” were used to match peer‐reviewed articles in line with our research intentions.
selection_criteria: (1) only studies performed plastic film mulch practice in field were selected as treatment, and the no film mulch practice in field were selected as control, any studies include other treatments are controlled to keep the difference only was no film mulch and pm; (2) the control and treatment plots were established to have the same abiotic and biotic conditions in same site. if the same article reports more than one field experiment but in different environment (such as conducted in multiple locations), then each experiment is considered an independent study; (3) to avoid bias, only data of the latest season were included if the study containing data from multiple growing seasons; (4) the means, observation numbers or replicates, standard deviations of the selected variables could be directly extracted or calculated from the articles, and for the data reported in form of figures, webplotdiditizer was used for data extraction.
data_analysis: the weighted response ratio between the treatment (plastic film mulch) group and the control (no plastic film mulch) group was calculated. if the 95 % ci for rr++ involving the indicator does not cross the zero point of the abscissa, then plastic film mulch had a significant effect (increased or decreased) relative to no plastic film mulch. we used the fail-safe n analysis to judge whether publication bias existed in the present meta-analysis. all the described statistical steps and calculation methods, including the meta-analyses, were performed using openmee software .
background: Plastic film mulch (PM), a major rainwater harvesting measure, is now widely used to cope with drought in context of global climate change. However, the effects of PM on root traits are not clearly understood.
objective: the present study comprised of a meta-analysis of 9 root traits, water use efficiency and crop yield to evaluate the effect of plastic film mulch.
result1: pm could promote root growth and increase yield in clay soil better than in other soil textures.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: plastic mulching has a positive effect on crop yield.

search_strategy: this study analyzed differences in cy and wue under fmdi and nmdi by systematically searching the literature databases, including elsevier, web of science, springer link, google scholar, baidu search, and china knowledge network (as of may 2021). the main keywords searched were ‘drip irrigation system’ and ‘film mulch’. no other restrictions were included in the search process.
selection_criteria: the two main exclusion criteria were: (1) literature unrelated to drip irrigation systems and mulch cultivation and (2) literature that did not obtain or calculate cy and wue. if a study met the following two conditions, it fell within the scope of the current work: (1) based on experimental data obtained from field studies rather than a simulation; (2) the values of factors were taken into account in the course of the experiment and provided in the text.
data_analysis: we used a 95% bootstrap confidence interval (ci) (4999 iterations) to generate an average effect value and a 95% ci for each classification variable. if p > 0.05 (chi-square distribution test), the data were not heterogeneous, and if p < 0.05 (chi distribution test), the data were heterogeneous. the heterogeneity test results showed low heterogeneity between the inspection groups, so we used the fixed-effect model for analysis. any possible publishing biases related to cy and wue were evaluated separately using egger linear regression. the results showed that the p values corresponding to the regression intercepts of both variables were greater than 0.05, indicating no publishing deviation.
scale: spain, turkey, china, ethiopia, the united states, india
background: Improving water use efficiency is an effective way to conserve water in agriculture. Drip irrigation is a water-saving irrigation technology that has been adopted worldwide. Film mulching can prevent undesired water vaporization losses and enhance soil surface temperature.
objective: this study used a meta-analysis to assess the effects of mulching on crop yield (cy) and water use efficiency (wue) under drip irrigation to determine whether a superposition effect occurs when combining film mulching and drip irrigation and whether the limiting factors of film mulching play a positive role in agricultural production.
result1: compared with nonmulching drip irrigation, film-mulching drip irrigation (fdmi) crop yield increased (cy) by 20.2% (ci: 17.2–23.0%).
result2: the effect of fmdi on cy varied in different regions of the world (p < 0.05), in different regions of china (p < 0.05). differences in in the response of rf lead to differences in the response of cy to fmdi  (p < 0.05). soil type significantly affected the response of cy to fmdi (p < 0.05). crop type had different cy and wue responses to fmdi (p < 0.05). water consumption also influenced cy response to fdmi.
general_conclusion: compared with no mulching, plastic film mulching increased yield by 20%.
knowledge_gaps: the authors analyzed the factors affecting plastic film mulching in groups according to planting area, climate, soil conditions, crop type, and mulching material but did not divide the coverage methods into full and semicoated measures because there was insufficient data to support such a division. likewise, they did not divide the irrigation regimes into different types. future studies are needed to explore the effects of different film mulching measures and irrigation regimes.

search_strategy: the authors searched in peer-reviewed literature for publications investigating the effects of mulching on yield of maize and wheat using scopus (elsevier). search terms included ‘mulch’ and/or ‘mulching’, ‘maize’ and/or ‘wheat’, ‘yield’, ‘water’ or ‘nitrogen’ in the article title, abstract and keywords. conference proceedings and non-english language publications were excluded.
selection_criteria: (1) studies must contain both no-mulching and mulching treatments (either straw or plastic mulching); (2) crop yields, water input and n input were all reported so that the interactions between water and n can be quantified; (3) location, year and soil information of the experiment was stated.
data_analysis: the effect size (ln r) was statistically analyzed with a mixed-effect model. in this mixed-effect model, mulching treatments (i.e., no-mulching, straw mulching and plastic mulching) were set as fixed effects and studies were set as random effects. to investigate how the effects of mulching varied due to the levels of water input, n input and temperature, the whole dataset was separated into two sub-datasets according to the 50th percentile value of the water input, n input, temperature and soil organic matter (som) content, respectively. the analysis was conducted for wheat and maize separately. also, the overall mean effects of multiple variables and possible interactions between variables, including mulching, soil organic matter, temperature, water and n input on yield (and on wue and nue) were analysed, using the sub-datasets for wheat and maize.
background: Global crop yields are limited by water and nutrient availability. Soil mulching (with plastic or straw) reduces evaporation, modifies soil temperature and thereby affects crop yields. Reported effects of mulching are sometimes contradictory, likely due to differences in climatic conditions, soil characteristics, crop species and also water and nitrogen (N) input levels.
objective: the objectives of this study were (1) to examine the effects of mulching on wheat and maize yield, wue and nue on the basis of results of published studies; (2) to relate variations in the effects of mulching to variations in inputs of water and n, temperature and to soil organic matter; and (3) to quantify possible interactions between water and n use in yield, wue and nue.
result1: on average, straw mulching and plastic mulching increased wue of wheat by 20%. the mean effect of straw mulching on maize were similar to that of wheat, but plastic mulching increased wue of maize by ~60%.
result2: the effects of mulching were affected by water input, n input level, mean air temperature during the growing season, and soil organic matter.
general_conclusion: the results indicate that mulching significantly increased yield by up to 60%, compared with no-mulching.

search_strategy: the authors used the web of science and china knowledge resource integrated database with the keywords “film or mulch or film residue” and “crop yield or soil nutrition or soil temperature or soil moisture or soil water” for the years 2000–2017. this
selection_criteria: (a) the study must be a replicated field trial, with exception for studies on residue film ef-fects on soil water transportation, where the difficulty of measuring soil water transport limits it to pot and lab incubation experiments; (b) the agricultural management must have at least two treatments for mulching (i.e., mulching vs. non-mulching) and/or residue (residue vs. zero-residue); (c) the amount of residual film had to be reported in the publications; (d) the publications have reported on at least one of the target variables; and (e) the publications have reported sample sizes for the control and treatment plots.
data_analysis:
overall, 36.7% of the studies did not report the sd. the missing sds were approximated using the average coefficient of variation of the dataset where the sd was reported, and multiplied by the reported mean. we performed our analysis on the film residue effects in three stages, each stage informed by the results of the previous stage. first, a mu- tilevel random effect meta-analysis on three categories: low residual film lrf (<225 kg/ha), medium residual film mrf (225 to <600 kg/ha), and high residual film hrf (>600 kg/ha). second, a random effect meta-regression analysis was carried out. to assess the relationship between film residue loading and the crop or soil response variable. third, a meta-regression analysis, as per stage two, was performed on the yield dataset exclusively with the dataset split by crop type. this multilevel random effect meta-analysis approach was also applied on the effects of plastic film mulch on crop yield, soil temperature, and soil moisture content. t2 (equation 7), q – df (equation 8), and i2 statistics were used
to evaluate heterogeneity, in addition to p-value of q statistic. to further assess for potential bias, we used the approach of forest plot of individual studies, which allows us visualize the relation- ship between sample size and effect size.
background: Plastic pollution is a global concern given its prevalence in aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. Studies have been conducted on the distribution and impact of plastic pollution in marine ecosystems, but little is known on terrestrial ecosystems. Plastic mulch has been widely used to increase crop yields worldwide, yet the impact of plastic residues in cropland soils to soil health and crop production in the long term remained unclear.
objective: understanding the drivers of the use of plastic film mulch and consequences of the accumulation of film residue is crucial for policy makers to mitigate plastic pollution. in this paper, the authors conducted a meta-analysis on both the agricultural benefits and impact from the use of plastic film mulch using data from 110 peer-reviewed experimental studies globally (figure s3). the authors also present the first nationwide soil sampling (>3,600 soil quadrats) of plastic film residue in china's croplands. the authors examined the quantity, spatial distribution, and factors influencing the amount of plastic film residue in soils, and considered how these residues would affect crop production in the long run.
result1: the use of plastic film mulch benefits yields of both cash and cereal crops by increasing immediate season yield on average between 25% and 42% compared to control (95% ci).
result2: these benefits were observed, in general, regardless of film type, mulching cycle, mulching method, mulching ratio, and film thickness.
general_conclusion: mulching has a positive effect on crop yield. plastic film residues has a negative effect on crop yield of cotton.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed studies exploring the impact ofsm on ghg emissions in china and published between 2009 and 2021 were collected. several online databases, including elsevier (science direct), web ofscience, and china national knowledge infrastructure, were used as search engines in this study. during the search, keywords were focused on: 1) soil mulching or 2) mulching and greenhouse gas or 3) ghg or 4) greenhouse gas emission or 5) methane or 6) nitrous oxide or 7) carbon dioxide.
selection_criteria: 1) only publications describing experiments conducted in the field with side-by-side comparisons of soil mulching (sm) and no soil mulching (nsm) were included and pot studies were excluded; 2) crop yield and ghg emissions data in sm and nsm were reported. it should be noted that, in this meta-analysis, gwp, ch4, n2o and co2 emissions could be represented by ghg emissions; 3) the primary data of ghg emissions under sm and nsm must be comparable; 4) the mean, sample size and a measure of dispersion (se or sd) as numerical or graphical data were available, or sd of ghg emissions data could be calculated from the reported data for sm and nsm.
data_analysis: a random-effect model was adopted in this meta-analysis to examine the performance of crop yield and ghg emissions data under sm and nsm, respectively. the funnel plot were used to intuitively assess whether there is a publication bias.
background: Although soil mulching (SM) is an effective method to increase crop yield because it could conserve soil moisture and temperature, it is also an important factor affecting GHG productions and emissions. At present, research results in terms of the impact of SM on agricultural GHG emissions are still inconsistent.
objective: the main objective of this study was to quantitatively analyze the impact of sm on crop yield and ghg emissions in china, explore the response of ghg emissions to several critical influencing factors, such as mulching methods, climate conditions, soil properties, irrigation methods, and finally find a mulching method that is most conducive to ghg emission reductions.
result1: overall, compared to nsm, sm significantly improved crop yield by 21.84%.
result2: compared with nsm, grave mulching remarkably increased crop yield by 39.18%, straw mulching only slightly increased crop yield by 10.93%, under plastic mulching, crop yield was increased by 24.23%.
general_conclusion: in general, compared with no mulching, soil mulching significantly increased crop yield by 21.8%.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed journal articles published between 1968 and 2021 were searched in google scholar and web of science to evaluate the effects of fallow tillage and mulching methods on soil water and crop yield and water use in mono-culture winter wheat system. we used soil water, precipitation storage efficiency, wheat yield, and wue along with conventional tillage, conservation tillage, bare fallow, and mulching as keywords.
selection_criteria: (1)  mulching studies should be carried out in the mono-culture winter wheat cropping system experiments in a field. (2) each study should have a control treatment, e.g., conventional tillage (for tillage comparison) and bare fallow (for mulching comparison) with similar edaphic and climatic conditions. (3) storage at wheat planting (swsp), precipitation storage efficiency (pse), yield, evapotranspiration (et), and water use efficiency (wue) should be compared between straw mulching, plastic film mulching, cover cropping (as a biological mulching), stubble mulching, and a bare fallow without mulching. all crop residues should be removed immediately at harvest of the main crop, and the land kept bare during the whole fallow period as a control treatment for mulching. (4) experiments should be conducted in a rain-fed system with no irrigation applied during the entire experimental period. the simulation model and multi-cropping studies were excluded.
data_analysis: in order to analyze the impact of mulching methods on soil and crop parameters (swsp, pse, yield, et, and wue), random model was used to calculate the mean effect size of bias-based bootstrap at 95% confidence interval. the impact of the mulching methods was measured significant if the 95% confidence interval did not overlap with the zero line. correlations of the rrs of wheat yield, et, and wue to that of swsp were conducted.
background: Winter wheat monoculture is a predominant cropping system for agricultural production in dry areas. However, fallow management effects on soil water conservation and crop yield and water use have been inconsistent among studies. [Note from the reviewer: winter wheat grown following the fallow period]
objective: in this study, the authors collected the data available in the literature and conducted a meta-analysis to check the overall and individual effect of mulching methods on soil and plant parameters compared to bare fallow cropping patterns under different edaphic and climate conditions. they hypothesized that mulching would improve precipitation storage efficiency (pse), soil water storage at wheat planting (swsp), winter wheat yield, and water use efficiency (wue) compared to bare fallow. relative effects on soil water parameters may differ within mulching methods, and edaphic and climatic conditions.
result1: the mulching practices showed negative to positive rr on wheat yield, exhibiting an overall non-significant effect. compared to no mulching during fallow, straw mulching, film mulching, and stubble mulching increased winter wheat yield by 4.2, 6.2, and 5.5% (p < 0.05), respectively, while cover cropping decreased wheat yield by 7.0% (p < 0.05).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: wheat crop yield was significantly enhanced by fallow straw, plastic, and stubble mulching.

search_strategy: a literature search was conducted using google scholar with search terms including “biodegradable,” “mulch,” “crop,” “polyethylene,” and “yield” or “weed” or “soil moisture” or “soil temperature” in all fields. the search was limited to papers published between 1970 and 7 november 2019, which resulted in approximately 5380 papers.
selection_criteria: 1) include agronomic study of at least one bdm; 2) include a black pem control; 3) include data for yield (of any cultivated crop), weeds, soil moisture, and/or soil temperature for at least one bdm in comparison to pem; (4) be published in english or portuguese; 5) have full text available on-line or through the university of nebraska-lincoln library.
data_analysis:
non-parametric bootstrap confidence intervals (95%) were calculated for mean agronomic response ratios of interest using a first-order normal approximation and 4999 iterations (”boot” package; r v. 3.6.2). mean response ratios were considered significant if its bootstrap confidence intervals did not overlap with zero. differences between treatment groups were considered significant when confidence intervals between the two groups did not overlap. possible publication bias was investigated by fitting data to a random effects model using the
”metafor” package in r [27] and assessing how individual observations influenced effect sizes. because sampling variance was not available for all observations, we assigned a random standard deviation of between 10% and 20% of the mean response value. the random effects model was first used to confirm significance of individual factors (e.g., yield) and tested effects (e.g., mulch type), and then to assess potential effects of non-independence.
background: Growers are interested in biodegradable alternatives to petroleum-based polyethylene mulch film (PEM). However, many growers cite limited knowledge about biodegradable mulch films (BDMs) as a significant barrier to adoption. Agronomic field tests of BDMs are often limited temporally or spatially, and the variability of performance results relative to PEM may be contributing to this perceived knowledge gap.
objective: the objective was to use data available in the scientific literature to estimate the effects of biodegradable mulch film (bdm) type and properties on soil temperature, weed suppression, and crop yield relative to polyethylene mulch film (pem) and bare soil.
result1: results of this meta-analysis of crop yield (292 observations across 66 studies) suggest yields in bdms are greater than those in bare soil and are not different from pem yields.
result2: yield of crops grown in paper-based bdm were trending lower (−7.3% ± 12.6%), but were not different from pem or the other bdm types.
result3: the relative yield performance of bdms was somewhat unexpected given the reduced soil warming and weed suppression benefits compared to pem. paper-based bdm provided better weed suppression than pem (particularly for cyperus weed species), but soil temperatures were similar to bare soil due to the color and thermophysical properties of paper-based bdm.
result4: the lack of a clear relationship between soil warming, weed suppression, and crop yield in agricultural mulches suggests that some agronomic benefits of pem are either redundant or counterproductive.
general_conclusion: yield of crops grown in biodegradale mulching film products of any type are not different from those grown in plastic film.

It is therefore urgent to develop and adopt optimal soil-improving cropping systems (SICS) that can allow us to decouple these system parameters. Soil salinization is a major environmental hazard that limits agricultural potential and is closely linked to agricultural mismanagement and water resources overexploitation, especially in arid climates.
objective: the authors review literature pertaining soil-improving cropping systems (sics) that aim to prevent, mitigate, or remediate the negative impacts of soil salinization and ameliorate the associated soil functions and ecosystem services relevant to agricultural production, aiming not to describe the problem, but looking for solutions.
