search_strategy: a search of peer-reviewed publications was performed to collect data on the effects of mulching on yield and nue (kilogram tuber yield per kilogram n fertilizer applied) of potato grown in china. data published in english were collected from the isi-web of science and google scholar, and data published in chinese were collected from the china national knowledge infrastructure and baidu scholar. the keywords used for the search were mulching, yield, nue, and potato. the year of publication was not restricted, but publications after july 2019 were not included.
selection_criteria: 1) field experimental studies must involve a mulching treatment and a no mulching control; 2) yield, nue, and the number of replicates of the treatments were directly acquired from the publication or calculated.
data_analysis: (1) pfm, plastic film mulching; (2) sm,strawmulching; and (3) pfsm,combination of plastic filmandstraw mulching. plastic mulching materials included black plastic film and transparent plastic film. the weighted means of the logarithmic response ratios was calculated for all independent studies as individual experiments often differ in their statistical precision. the homogeneity statistic q was used to test whether variances were significantly different. a mixed or random effects model was employed to determine whether mulching significantly affected each dependent variable using the statistical software metawin 2.1 with a resampling of 9999 iterations. a random effect model was adopted in cases of high heterogeneity (a chi-square p-value < 0.05).
background: In dry environments, potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) is grown under mulching for water conservation and improving tuber yield and nitrogen use efficiency (NUE).
objective: therefore, this meta-analysis study of field trials on potato production in china aimed to determine how tuber yield and nue respond to mulching and whether the response is influenced by growing region, synthetic fertilization rate, tillage practice, and planting density.
result1: yield of potato was significantly increased by mulching compared to no mulching by 24%.
result2: tillage practices (ridge-furrow and flat plots) and mulching practices (pfm and sm) significantly affected potato yield.
result3: the positive effect of mulching on yield was highest under pfm, followed by pfsm and sm. on average, pfm, pfsm, and sm increased potato yield by 25%, 23%, and 21%, respectively, compared to no mulching.
general_conclusion: plastic film mulching, straw mulching and the combination of plastic film and straw mulching, all increase potato yield in china, but the benefits varies with the growing region, tillage, and fertilization practices.

selection_criteria: not reported

scale: asia, australia, europe and north and south america
background: A clear understanding of N2O emission from fruit cropping systems is urgently needed to improve the global budget and establish mitigation options.
objective: the primary aims of this study were to (i) quantify the variations in n2o emissions from orchards, (ii) evaluate the major controls of n2o emissions, and (iii) discuss potential mitigation strategies across climates, soil types and field managements.

search_strategy: published journal articles related to the effect of film mulching on soc and soil ghg fluxes were searched for on web of science using the following research keywords: ts = (mulch) and (soil) and (carbon or “nitrous oxide” or n2o or methane or ch4 or “greenhouse gas”). additionally, the china national knowledge infrastructure was used to search for published articles related to our topics. in addition, we also searched for other articles via literature citations that were not covered by these keywords.
selection_criteria: first, the selected studies must contain at least one of our targets (soc in the 0–20 cm layer, ch4 emissions/uptake and n2o emissions) in both non-mulched and film-mulched soils. second, management practices, such as the amount/type of fertilization, must be consistent in both treatments. third, we selected observations of soc and soil ghg fluxes from only field experiments rather than from pot or greenhouse experiments. fourth, because upland fields are generally atmospheric ch4 sinks and paddy fields are generally atmospheric ch4 sources, we considered the effects of plastic film mulching on ch4 uptake only in uplands and on ch4 emissions only in paddy fields. in addition, we did not consider a few studies that reported opposite results for ch4 fluxes.
data_analysis: NA
background: The use of plastic film in agriculture strongly affects the decomposition of soil organic carbon (SOC) and the release of methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O) by influencing soil biogeochemical processes. However, no systematic conclusions have been reached regarding the effect of plastic film mulching on SOC stocks and greenhouse gas (GHG) budgets.
objective: a meta-analysis was performed to analyze the effect of film mulching on soc and soil ghg fluxes across different agricultural systems and to identify the major factors affecting their responses to film mulching to address the following questions: (1) how does plastic film mulching influence soc and soil ghg fluxes across different agricultural ecosystems (rainfed uplands, irrigated uplands and paddy fields) and (2) how do mulching variables (e.g., the coverage ratio, film type, mulching method and film thickness) and environmental variables affect soc and soil ghg fluxes under film mulching?
result1: in paddy fields, plastic film mulching significantly reduced ch4 emissions by 103.9 kg ha− 1 year− 1. this result was mainly due to film mulching greatly increasing the activity of methane-oxidizing bacteria by maintaining aerobic conditions under non-flooded water conditionsit is worth noting that film thickness significantly affected the response of ch4 emissions to mulching, and thick film (>0.01 mm) helped to reduce ch4 emissions from paddy fields.
result2: in rainfed uplands, the soil ch4 uptake was significantly lower in mulched uplands than in non-mulched uplands. however, the negative effect of film mulching on ch4 uptake in irrigated uplands was not significant.
result3: the application of plastic film significantly (p < 0.05) increased n2o emissions by 23.9% compared to those from non-mulched fields. the agricultural system, coverage ratio, film type and mulching method significantly (p < 0.05) influenced the response of n2o emissions to mulching. film mulching significantly (p < 0.05) increased n2o emissions by 89.3% in paddy fields but had no significant effects on rainfed or irrigated uplands. the increase in n2o emissions was consistent in fields with high coverage ratios (50–100%), transparent and black pe films, and flat mulching. in addition, compared with non-mulching, mulching with thin film (≤0.01 mm) significantly increased n2o emissions by 29.7%.
general_conclusion: film mulching significantly reduced ch4 emissions in paddy fields. in rainfed uplands, the soil ch4 uptake was significantly lower in mulched uplands than in non-mulched uplands. film muching significantly increased n2o emissions

search_strategy: peer-reviewed journal articles reporting maize and wheat yields and greenhouse gas emissions as affected by soil mulching up to may 2021 were collected to build the database based on web of science (http://apps.webofknowledge.com/), the google scholar (http://www.scholar.google.com), china national knowledge infrastructure (https://www.cnki.net/) and the wanfang data of china (http://www.wanfangdata.com.cn/) using the following search formulation: yield* and (greenhouse gas* or ch4 or n2o or co2 or methane or nitrous oxide or carbon oxide) and mulch* and (maize or corn or wheat).
selection_criteria: (1) the field experimental design was clear; (2) the study included the conventional flat planting with no mulching (nm) and at least one mulching practice, i.e. plastic film mulching (pm) and straw mulching (sm); (3) at least one kind of ghg emissions (n2o, co2 and ch4) over an entire season was reported; (4) the means and standard deviations (sds) could be obtained from the tables or figures by getdata graph digitizer.
data_analysis:
the effect size was measured by the natural log of the response ratio (ln r), which was calculated by the ratio of the mean values of the experimental group under soil mulching (xt) and the mean values of corresponding control treatment (xc). weighting approach tends to be well replicated in field experiments, assigning greater weight to estimate effect size more precise. mean effect
sizes were estimated as a weighted average. meta win 2.1 was used to pro- duce mean effect sizes and 95 % bootstrapped cis (rosenberg et al., 2000). for ease of interpretation, all analysis results were reported as the percentage change with soil mulching (pm and sm) relative to the control treatment (non-mulching).
background: Understanding the effects of soil mulching on crop yields and greenhouse gas (N2O, CO2 and CH4) emissions is important for developing sustainable agriculture. However, no systematic conclusions have been drawn yet because the environmental factors vary among various studies.
objective: evaluate the impact of plastic film mulching (pm) and straw mulching (sm) on greenhouse gas emissions from two major cereal crops (maize and wheat)
result1: on average, n2o emission was significantly increased by 24.7 % under straw mulching (sm) and 18.6 % under plastic mulching (pm) in comparison to non-mulching, respectively. however, sm did not exhibit significant effects on n2o emission from the maize field and the effect of pm on n2o emission from the wheat field was not significant.
result2: on average, sm and pm significantly increased co2 emission by 4.7 % and 17.1 % relative to no-mulching. both pm and sm had significantly promoting effects on co2 emission from the wheat field, but there was no significant difference in co2 emission between sm and nm in the maize field.
result3: straw mulching tended to significantly promote ch4 uptake, 22.6 % and 27.9 % higher than that of nm in maize and wheat field, respectively. ch4 uptake was significantly inhibited by 26.4 % under pm in maize field compared with that of no-mulching. no significant difference of ch4 uptake between sm and nm was found in the wheat field.
general_conclusion: plastic mulching and straw mulching significantly increased n2o emission compared with no mulching, respectively. co2 emission was significantly increased  and ch4 uptake was significantly inhibited by plastic mulching. straw mulching had non significant effect on co2 emission but significantly promoted ch4 uptake.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed journal articles were explored in the web of science, china national knowledge infrastructure (cnki), and google scholar using the keywords ‘soil mulching or straw mulching or film mulching’ and ‘yield or greenhouse gas or ghg or carbon dioxide or nitrous oxide or ch4 or co2 or n2o’ for the years 2000 –2020.
selection_criteria: (a) the experimental site must be in china, and experimental crops are wheat, maize, or rice; (b) the research must be field experiments, every treatment must be in triplicate at minimum, and the number of replicates should be indicated in the paper; (c) there must be a corresponding no-mulching (nm) control treatment; (d) the sm treatment must involve natural decay, and no articles with added decomposition agents or microbial strains to speed up straw decay are included, and (e) yield observations must be the current season, and ghg observations must be cumulative emissions, or provide average emissions and the days of growing season.
data_analysis: to assess for potential bias, the authors used forest plots of individual studies, which enabled us to visualize the relationship between sample size and effect size. furthermore, the authors tested publication bias with egger regression, and the trim-and-fill method was used to evaluate the impact of publication bias to the results. the “metafor” package (version 2.4–0) and “forestplot” package (1.10.1) in r (version 4.0.3)were applied in the above data analysis process. the authors performed a model selection analysis to calculate the relative importance of all predictive variables affecting the effect size of response variables under soil mulching, using the “glmulti” package (1.0.8) in r 4.0.3.
background: Soil mulching either with plastic film or straw is a common agricultural practice, which can improve crop growth by reducing evaporation and regulating soil temperature, and is widely applied globally. Although soil mulching can significantly affect crop yield and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, there is controversy regarding its effect on crop yield and GHG emissions in the long run.
objective: this study had three main objectives: (a) evaluate the overall impact of two dominant soil mulching methods (fm and sm) on yield and ghg emissions in maize, wheat, and rice, according to published research in china; (b) determine the most important factors affecting the response variables under soil mulching through the model selection analysis of relevant agronomic measures, soil factors, and meteorological climate factors, and (c) quantify the impact of n input, annual mean temperature (amt), and annual total precipitation (atp) on mulching performance.
result1: in general, soil mulching reduced ch4 uptakes (−16%, 95% ci:−23% to −8%) in upland. this reduction in ch4 uptakes was highly dependent on the mulching method, soil texture, planting method, and film ratio.
result2: straw mulching and film mulching significantly influenced ch4 emissions in paddy, but there are a different effect. sm promoted ch4 emissions by 140% (n = 47) and fm reduced ch4 emissions in paddy by 51% (n = 48).
result3: soil mulching had no significant effect on n2o emissions for all crop types.
general_conclusion: the impact of soil mulching on ghg emissions varied with crop, region, and mulching method. plastic film mulching decreased ch4 emissions in paddy by 51%, and ch4 uptakes in upland by 23%, while straw mulching increased ch4 emissions in paddy by 140%. soil mulching showed no effect on n2o emissions.

search_strategy: the selected publications were collected by searching isi web of science database and china knowledge resource integrated database using the following search criteria: ts = (plastic mulching∗) and (soil organic carbon∗ or microbial biomass carbon∗ or enzyme activities∗ or co2∗ or ch4∗) and ts = (film mulching∗ or plastic mulching∗) and (maize∗ or wheat∗ or potato∗ or yield∗ or root∗ or biomass∗).
selection_criteria: (i) the selected study included at least one parameter of interest (i.e. response variables) as economic yield (ey), aboveground biomass (ab), root biomass (rb), soil organic carbon (soc), co2 emission, ch4 flux, microbial biomass carbon (mbc), c‒related soil enzyme activities (i.e. glucosidase, sucrase, catalase, urease and alkaline phosphatase); (ii) only field study with replicated experimental design was included, greenhouse and laboratory incubation experiments excluded. pairwise comparisons on mulching and non‒mulching farming management were performed under the same pedo‒climatic conditions (e.g., temperature, precipitation, soil texture, and soil type) for at least 2 consecutive years; (iii) provided treatment means, sample sizes, and variances, or these could be extracted from tables or the figures using software; (v) duration of plastic mulching should be at least one full crop season for each year. when there were more than one articles on the same experiment, the article with longest mulching duration was included; (iv) to avoid pre‒mulching heterogeneity of soc stock between treatment and control, the values of soc contents at the beginning and end of each trial should be provided for the calculation of actual changes due to mulching. however, only few studies provided the baseline values of soc stocks for both experimental and control plots. given the fact that all data considered originated from pairwise system comparisons including controlled field trials, baseline differences in soc stocks among the different plots of one comparison were expected to be negligible. the authors therefore decided to also included the studies that the baseline values were not known into the data pool.
data_analysis: a mixed effect model that included a random effect for multiple studies from the same site was performed to calculate the mean effect sizes and variances for the concerned response variables. the authors used heterogeneity tests to confirm if models could explain significant variation. the majority of results show significant inter‒study heterogeneity, so the authors rejected the null hypothesis that all studies share a common effect size in favor of the interpretation that true effect sizes vary between studies. the sensitivity of the results was examined using the trim‒and‒fill model (i.e. the authors repeated the model for each of concerned responsory variable to account for the number of missing studies). the authors tested for potential publication bias using egger’s regression. the analysis results did not suggest that there was bias in most cases.
background: Plastic mulching provides many advantages for crop production, especially in dry croplands, such as reducing evaporation, improving water temperature conditions, and minimizing soil erosion. After three decades of practical application, however, a comprehensive nationwide assessment of its potential environmental consequences, in terms of SOC stock, was not available.
objective: the objective was to quantify the nationwide effects of plastic mulching application on crop net primary productivity, soil c fluxes, and total soc pool, and further identify the dominant environmental, edaphic, and anthropogenic drivers on these effects.
result1: plastic mulching produced a significant and negative effect size on ch4 emission (effect size: ‒27%, 95% ci: ‒19 ∼ ‒35%), indicating a positive contribution to ch4 absorption by soils.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: the results suggest that plastic mulching in dry agroecosystems can have a distinct potential to curtail the anthropogenic emissions of carbon through significant increases in both soil organic carbon sequestration and crop carbon fixation.
knowledge_gaps: the authors did not conduct grouping analysis for ch4 emissions because of the paucity of related case studies.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed studies exploring the impact ofsm on ghg emissions in china and published between 2009 and 2021 were collected. several online databases, including elsevier (science direct), web ofscience, and china national knowledge infrastructure, were used as search engines in this study. during the search, keywords were focused on: 1) soil mulching or 2) mulching and greenhouse gas or 3) ghg or 4) greenhouse gas emission or 5) methane or 6) nitrous oxide or 7) carbon dioxide.
selection_criteria: 1) only publications describing experiments conducted in the field with side-by-side comparisons of soil mulching (sm) and no soil mulching (nsm) were included and pot studies were excluded; 2) crop yield and ghg emissions data in sm and nsm were reported. it should be noted that, in this meta-analysis, gwp, ch4, n2o and co2 emissions could be represented by ghg emissions; 3) the primary data of ghg emissions under sm and nsm must be comparable; 4) the mean, sample size and a measure of dispersion (se or sd) as numerical or graphical data were available, or sd of ghg emissions data could be calculated from the reported data for sm and nsm.
data_analysis: a random-effect model was adopted in this meta-analysis to examine the performance of crop yield and ghg emissions data under sm and nsm, respectively. the funnel plot were used to intuitively assess whether there is a publication bias.
background: Although soil mulching (SM) is an effective method to increase crop yield because it could conserve soil moisture and temperature, it is also an important factor affecting GHG productions and emissions. At present, research results in terms of the impact of SM on agricultural GHG emissions are still inconsistent.
objective: the main objective of this study was to quantitatively analyze the impact of sm on crop yield and ghg emissions in china, explore the response of ghg emissions to several critical influencing factors, such as mulching methods, climate conditions, soil properties, irrigation methods, and finally find a mulching method that is most conducive to ghg emission reductions.
result1: soil mulching increased gwp by 11.38%. specifically, sm increased co2 and n2o by 21.62% and 1.73%, respectively, but significantly decreased ch4 by 43.08%.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: plastic film mulching has no effect on n2o emission and a positive effect on ch4 emission, but an overall no effect on aggregated ghg emission. straw mulching has no effect on aggregated ghg, ch4 and n2o emission. gravel mulching has no effect on aggregated ghg and n2o emission.

search_strategy: a detailed evaluation was performed of peer-reviewed journal articles from the web of science (1900–2017). “straw”, “residue”, “tillage”, “n2o”, “nitrous oxide”, and “greenhouse gas” were selected as search keywords.
selection_criteria: 1) only field scale studies were selected for this meta-analysis; 2) field scale studies on n2o emission were performed using the closed chamber-gas chromatography method in agroecosystem; 3) tillage and residue returning were clearly stated; 4) cumulative n2o emission could be obtained from each study.
data_analysis: a random-effects meta-analysis was carried out to explore the impact of experimental conditions, initial soil properties, and agricultural management practices on n2o emissions (kg n2o-n ha−1) associated with crop residues. for each attribute, total heterogeneity (qt) was divided into within-group (qw) and between-group (qb) variations. the significance of qb represents mean effect sizes that are significantly different between various levels of the categorical group. the q statistic obeyed a chi-square distribution with k−1 degrees of freedom, where k was the number of paired observations for a categorical variable between residue returning treatments.
background: Much attention has been focused on the influences of residue returning on N2O emissions. However, comprehensive quantification of the effect size on N2O emission following crop residue returning in subtropical, tropical and warm temperate conditions remains untested.
objective: the objective of this study was to conduct a meta-analysis to comprehensively quantify the effect size of crop residue returning on n2o emission, varying soil conditions, and residue returning attributes based on field experiments.
result1: mc significantly increased n2o emission by 16%, compared to the controls.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: residue returning increased n2o emissions, and the effects were positively related to residue amount and nitrogen input, but negatively associated with residue c/n ratio. in warm temperate and tropical climate zones, residue returning treatments have significant stimulatory effects on n2o emissions. for land use types, soil n2o release significantly increased in upland fields, but significantly decreased in paddy fields following residue returning.

search_strategy: a comprehensive search for peer-reviewed publications related to the effect of pm on crop yields and environmental impacts from jan 1980 to dec 2015 was conducted using two databases: web of science and the china academic journal network publishing database. the article titles, abstracts, and keywords were searched using the terms ‘wheat or maize’, ‘plastic mulch or soil manage- ment’, and ‘china’.
selection_criteria: (1) comparisons between pm and nm practices were made; (2) at least one parameter of interest (yield, evapotranspiration (et), water use efficiency (wue), harvest index, soil carbon, soil nitrogen, or amount of plastic film residue) was re- ported, and (3) the experimental location was stated. studies that described only the relationship between pm and crop yield without a nm treatment or that did not provide a clear description of the experimental methods were rejected.
data_analysis: the mean value of all observations on a countrywide scale was calculated by weighting, and the weight was calculated by replications. statistical analyses were con- ducted using the regression procedure of sas v9.2. the relationship between yield increase and increase in ghg emission was analyzed using regression analysis. fisher's test was used to determine the significance of the differences between means with a significance level of p < 0.05.
background: Numerous individual reports have emphasized the importance of soil surface plastic mulch (PM) as an auxiliary means of increasing crop yields, but a comprehensive assessment of yields and environmental benefits on a national scale has not been performed.
objective: the authors collected and synthesized data pertaining to crop production and ghg emissions under no-mulch (nm) and plastic mulch (pm) in china to: 1) explore the reasons for variation in yield increase caused by pm application; 2) quantify the ghg emissions associated with pm application; 3) determine the appropriate conditions for pm application based on managing the tradeoffs between yield increase and ghg emissions.
result1: pm increased the mean yield-scaled ghg emissions by 32% for wheat and 10% for maize on a national scale.
result2: the increase in yield- scaled ghg emissions decreased gradually with n inputs increase, while it was increased with increasing annual precipitation
general_conclusion: plastic film mulching increased the mean yield-scaled ghg emissions by 32% for wheat and 10% for maize on a national scale.

search_strategy: a search of peer-reviewed publications was performed to collect data on the effects of pm on yield, economic benefit, nr, and nitrogen footprint of potato, maize, and wheat grown in china. data published in english were collected from google scholar and isi-web of science, and data published in chinese were collected from baidu scholar and the china national knowledge infrastructure. the keywords were searched using the terms “potato, maize, or wheat”, “mulch, plastic mulch, or soil management”, and “china”.
selection_criteria: (1) the field studies must include treatmentswith pmand non-pmcontrol (nm); (2) the amount of fertilizers application, plant density, and yield were reported or amena- ble to being calculated from the data; (3) the means, standard devia- tions (or standard errors), and sample sizes of the variables concerned must be directly available or amenable to being calculated from the data; and (4) the experimental locationwas stated. data were recorded by experimental year for publications reporting results frommulti-year experiments. the year of publication was restricted from 1970 to july 2019, the publications after july 2019were not included.
data_analysis: the weighted mean log ratio (ln−r) was calculated for all independent studies. the kolmogorov-smirnov test indicated that the distributions of yield, economic benefit, nr, nfg, and nfe were not a typical normal distribution (p < 0.05). therefore, confidence interval (ci) values were generated using the bootstrapping test for yield, economic benefit, nr, nfg, and nfe. a mixed-effects model was employed to estimate whether pm significantly affected each dependent variable using the statistical software metawin 2.1 with a resampling of 9999 iterations. if the 95% bootstrapping ci values for a variable did not overlap zero, the effect of the pm treatment on thevariablewas significant; otherwise, it was not significant. means of the different categorical variables were considered significantly different from one another if their 95% bootstrapping cis did not overlap.
background: Sustainably feeding the growing population amid rising global temperatures and dwindling resources is a grand challenge facing mankind. Plastic mulching (PM) is widely used in China aiming to the increase of crop produc- tivity. However, the impact ofPM on reactive nitrogen (Nr) emissions and nitrogen (N) footprint has not been explicitly described.
objective: the present study is a meta-analysis of field experiments on food crop production with pm in china that seeks answers to determine: 1) how yield, economic benefit, nr, and n footprint of major food crops respond to pm; 2) whether this is influenced by crop species, growing region, n fertilizer rate, or precipitation.
result1: overall, pm significantly reduced nitrogen footprint per unit of yield and nitrogen footprint per unit of net economic return.
result2: reactive nitrogen losses, nitrogen footprint per unit of yield and nitrogen footprint per unit of net economic return under pm were significantly reduced by an average of 11, 19, and 21%, respectively, compared to nm.
general_conclusion: plastic mulching reduces reactive nitrogen losses and nitrogen footprint per unit of net economic return compared to no mulching for maize and wheat. plastic mulching in potato reduces nitrogen footprint per unit of net economic return compared to no mulching but it has no effect on reactive nitrogen losses.

search_strategy:
peer-reviewed articles from january 1990 to july 2020 were selected using web of science and china national knowledge infra- structure (cnki) databases. three fields were used for the search in the title, abstract or keywords of the articles. the first field was tree crop
type, with the following search terms: “orchard” or “apple” or “citrus” or “vineyard” or “almond” or “olive”. the second field was cover crop type, and the search terms were “cover crop” or “ground cover” or “catch crop” or “green manure”. the third field was soil variable, with the search terms “runoff” or “soil loss” or “erosion” or “nutrient loss” or “soil and water conservation”.
selection_criteria: the case studies were chosen following the strict quality criteria: 1) the experiments or observations were conducted under field conditions (i.e., no laboratory, rainfall simulation or runoff simulation experiments, etc.); 2) both the ground cover and control (clean tillage or bare ground management) treatments were included in each case study, and the two treatments were exposed to the same environmental conditions; 3) the targeted article contained at least one response variable (runoff or soil loss or nutrients loss observations); 4) when the variable was measured at multiple time points, the average value was calculated to meet the accurate observation results; 5) multiple ground cover species in one study were considered as independent observations.
data_analysis: the mean percentage change and 95% confidential intervals were computed and compared with sigmaplot v12.0. positive reduction percentages indicated significant reductions of runoff or soil loss or nutrient losses as a result of ground cover relative to clean tillage management. when the ci crossed the invalid line (including 0), the ground cover effectiveness was deemed not significant.
background: Tree crops are mainly planted on sloped farmland, which can lead to soil erosion caused by runoff. As an important tree crop management strategy, ground cover management has been effective in controlling runoff generation and soil loss. However, a global overview is needed to comprehensively quantify the effectiveness of ground cover on water and soil conservation.
objective: the aim of this study is to provide evidence-based rationale for implementing more sustainable tree crop management practices. the objectives were to 1) quantify the effectiveness of ground cover management in reducing runoff, soil loss and nutrient loss from tree crop systems; 2) quantify the effectiveness of ground cover management according to the slope and climatic conditions of the tree crop system.
result1: including mulching reduced tn, no3 –- n and nh4 +-n losses from runoff. although a cover crop reduced tn from runoff more than mulch management, inorganic n forms (no3–-n and nh4 +-n) were more effectively intercepted with mulch management.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: compared to the clean tillage, mulching reduced all nutrient losses.

search_strategy: a literature search was conducted using google scholar with search terms including “biodegradable,” “mulch,” “crop,” “polyethylene,” and “yield” or “weed” or “soil moisture” or “soil temperature” in all fields. the search was limited to papers published between 1970 and 7 november 2019, which resulted in approximately 5380 papers.
selection_criteria: 1) include agronomic study of at least one bdm; 2) include a black pem control; 3) include data for yield (of any cultivated crop), weeds, soil moisture, and/or soil temperature for at least one bdm in comparison to pem; (4) be published in english or portuguese; 5) have full text available on-line or through the university of nebraska-lincoln library.
data_analysis:
non-parametric bootstrap confidence intervals (95%) were calculated for mean agronomic response ratios of interest using a first-order normal approximation and 4999 iterations (”boot” package; r v. 3.6.2). mean response ratios were considered significant if its bootstrap confidence intervals did not overlap with zero. differences between treatment groups were considered significant when confidence intervals between the two groups did not overlap. possible publication bias was investigated by fitting data to a random effects model using the
”metafor” package in r [27] and assessing how individual observations influenced effect sizes. because sampling variance was not available for all observations, we assigned a random standard deviation of between 10% and 20% of the mean response value. the random effects model was first used to confirm significance of individual factors (e.g., yield) and tested effects (e.g., mulch type), and then to assess potential effects of non-independence.
background: Growers are interested in biodegradable alternatives to petroleum-based polyethylene mulch film (PEM). However, many growers cite limited knowledge about biodegradable mulch films (BDMs) as a significant barrier to adoption. Agronomic field tests of BDMs are often limited temporally or spatially, and the variability of performance results relative to PEM may be contributing to this perceived knowledge gap.
objective: the objective was to use data available in the scientific literature to estimate the effects of biodegradable mulch film (bdm) type and properties on soil temperature, weed suppression, and crop yield relative to polyethylene mulch film (pem) and bare soil.
result1: variability of the weed suppression data (particularly in bare soil) also reflects differences in weed management (e.g., herbicides versus hand-weeding) and ambient weed populations among studies. nonetheless, there were significant differences in weed suppression among bdm, pem, and bare soil.
result2: paper-based bdm reduced weed pressure by 88.0% ± 7.7% compared to pem, whereas starch-polyester and other bio-based polymer bdm films were less effective than pems.
general_conclusion: paper mulch film has a positivite effect on weed suppression, while starch-polyester much film has a negetaive effect and other mulch films have no effect (include several types).
knowledge_gaps: the sample size for biodegradable mulch film (bdm) weed suppression was relatively small and quite variable, which suggests future bdm research should prioritize collecting data on weed response.

search_strategy: the authors used ‘straw returning’ or ‘straw mulching,’ and ‘maize’ in the keyword search to collect peer-reviewed journal articles from the china national knowledge infrastructure and web of science.
selection_criteria: to avoid any bias, the authors selected publications with the following criteria: 1) field experiment; 2) cropping system includes maize; 3) included control (no straw returning; ck) and treatments (straw mulching or straw incorporation); 4) means, standard deviations (or standard error), and number of replications available or can be calculated; 5) included yield or water use efficiency measurements.
data_analysis: to derive the overall response effect of the treatments (straw mulching or straw incorporation) groups and control (no straw returning) group, the weighted response ratio (rr++) between the treatments (straw mulching or straw incorporation) groups and control (no straw returning) group was calculated. metawin2.1 was used to generate 95% confidence intervals around the logarithmic response ratios (rr) with 4999 iterations. the authors applied a t-test to determine variation in each variable between the control and treatment and the difference in rr++ between subgroups.
background: Straw mulching and straw incorporation are widely used for conservation tillage as the primary methods of returning straw to the field. However, few studies have investigated the effects of straw mulching and straw incorporation under various agronomic management and environmental and edaphic factors.
objective: in this study the authors undertook a meta-analysis to: 1) analyze the effects of n application rate, straw returning amount, annual average precipitation, temperature, and evaporation, and soil texture on maize yield, wue, and nue with straw mulching and straw incorporation; 2) identify suitable methods of straw returning for different temperatures, precipitation, and soil textures in china; 3) determine the appropriate of straw returning amount and n application rate.
result1: the meta-analysis showed that straw mulching significantly increased nue (rr++: 0.0722).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: straw mulching has a positive effect on nutrient use efficiency of maize.

search_strategy: the authors searched in peer-reviewed literature for publications investigating the effects of mulching on yield of maize and wheat using scopus (elsevier). search terms included ‘mulch’ and/or ‘mulching’, ‘maize’ and/or ‘wheat’, ‘yield’, ‘water’ or ‘nitrogen’ in the article title, abstract and keywords. conference proceedings and non-english language publications were excluded.
selection_criteria: (1) studies must contain both no-mulching and mulching treatments (either straw or plastic mulching); (2) crop yields, water input and n input were all reported so that the interactions between water and n can be quantified; (3) location, year and soil information of the experiment was stated.
data_analysis: the effect size (ln r) was statistically analyzed with a mixed-effect model. in this mixed-effect model, mulching treatments (i.e., no-mulching, straw mulching and plastic mulching) were set as fixed effects and studies were set as random effects. to investigate how the effects of mulching varied due to the levels of water input, n input and temperature, the whole dataset was separated into two sub-datasets according to the 50th percentile value of the water input, n input, temperature and soil organic matter (som) content, respectively. the analysis was conducted for wheat and maize separately. also, the overall mean effects of multiple variables and possible interactions between variables, including mulching, soil organic matter, temperature, water and n input on yield (and on wue and nue) were analysed, using the sub-datasets for wheat and maize.
background: Global crop yields are limited by water and nutrient availability. Soil mulching (with plastic or straw) reduces evaporation, modifies soil temperature and thereby affects crop yields. Reported effects of mulching are sometimes contradictory, likely due to differences in climatic conditions, soil characteristics, crop species and also water and nitrogen (N) input levels.
objective: the objectives of this study were (1) to examine the effects of mulching on wheat and maize yield, wue and nue on the basis of results of published studies; (2) to relate variations in the effects of mulching to variations in inputs of water and n, temperature and to soil organic matter; and (3) to quantify possible interactions between water and n use in yield, wue and nue.
result1: on average, straw mulching and plastic mulching increased nue of wheat by 20%. the mean effect of straw mulching on maize were similar to that of wheat, but plastic mulching increased nue of maize by ~60%.
result2: the effects of mulching were affected by water input. the mulching effects were also affected by n input level.
general_conclusion: the results indicate that mulching significantly increased nitrogen use efficiency by up to 60%, compared with no-mulching.

search_strategy: a search of peer-reviewed publications was performed to collect data on the effects of mulching on yield and nue (kilogram tuber yield per kilogram n fertilizer applied) of potato grown in china. data published in english were collected from the isi-web of science and google scholar, and data published in chinese were collected from the china national knowledge infrastructure and baidu scholar. the keywords used for the search were mulching, yield, nue, and potato. the year of publication was not restricted, but publications after july 2019 were not included.
selection_criteria: 1) field experimental studies must involve a mulching treatment and a no mulching control; 2) yield, nue, and the number of replicates of the treatments were directly acquired from the publication or calculated.
data_analysis: (1) pfm, plastic film mulching; (2) sm,strawmulching; and (3) pfsm,combination of plastic filmandstraw mulching. plastic mulching materials included black plastic film and transparent plastic film. the weighted means of the logarithmic response ratios was calculated for all independent studies as individual experiments often differ in their statistical precision. the homogeneity statistic q was used to test whether variances were significantly different. a mixed or random effects model was employed to determine whether mulching significantly affected each dependent variable using the statistical software metawin 2.1 with a resampling of 9999 iterations. a random effect model was adopted in cases of high heterogeneity (a chi-square p-value < 0.05).
background: In dry environments, potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) is grown under mulching for water conservation and improving tuber yield and nitrogen use efficiency (NUE).
objective: therefore, this meta-analysis study of field trials on potato production in china aimed to determine how tuber yield and nue respond to mulching and whether the response is influenced by growing region, synthetic fertilization rate, tillage practice, and planting density.
result1: nue of potato was significantly increased by mulching compared to no mulching by 24%.
result2: tillage practices (ridge-furrow and flat plots) and mulching practices (pfm and sm) significantly affected potato nue.
result3: the positive effect of mulching on nue was highest under pfm, followed by pfsm and sm. pfm, pfsm, and sm increased nue by 25%, 23%, and 22% compared to no mulching, respectively.
general_conclusion: mulching significantly increased tuber nitrogen use efficiency by an average of 24% compared to no mulching. plastic film mulching was more effective in improving nitrogen use efficiency than straw mulching.

search_strategy: a comprehensive search for peer-reviewed publications related to the effect of pm on crop yields and environmental impacts from jan 1980 to dec 2015 was conducted using two databases: web of science and the china academic journal network publishing database. the article titles, abstracts, and keywords were searched using the terms ‘wheat or maize’, ‘plastic mulch or soil manage- ment’, and ‘china’.
selection_criteria: (1) comparisons between pm and nm practices were made; (2) at least one parameter of interest (yield, evapotranspiration (et), water use efficiency (wue), harvest index, soil carbon, soil nitrogen, or amount of plastic film residue) was re- ported, and (3) the experimental location was stated. studies that described only the relationship between pm and crop yield without a nm treatment or that did not provide a clear description of the experimental methods were rejected.
data_analysis: the mean value of all observations on a countrywide scale was calculated by weighting, and the weight was calculated by replications. statistical analyses were con- ducted using the regression procedure of sas v9.2. the relationship between yield increase and increase in ghg emission was analyzed using regression analysis. fisher's test was used to determine the significance of the differences between means with a significance level of p < 0.05.
background: Numerous individual reports have emphasized the importance of soil surface plastic mulch (PM) as an auxiliary means of increasing crop yields, but a comprehensive assessment of yields and environmental benefits on a national scale has not been performed.
objective: the authors collected and synthesized data pertaining to crop production and ghg emissions under no-mulch (nm) and plastic mulch (pm) in china to: 1) explore the reasons for variation in yield increase caused by pm application; 2) quantify the ghg emissions associated with pm application; 3) determine the appropriate conditions for pm application based on managing the tradeoffs between yield increase and ghg emissions.
result1: at the end ofthe useful lifespan of plastic film, part of it can remain as residue in soil. the annual amount of plastic film residue was approximately 8.4 kg ha-1 , which represented 11% of the total rates of plastic film
result2: NA
general_conclusion: at the end ofthe useful lifespan of plastic film, part of it can remain as residue in soil. the annual amount of plastic film residue was approximately 8.4 kg ha-1 , which represented 11% of the total rates of plastic film.

search_strategy: to investigate the effect of fm on soil microbial abundance, diversity, and functional parameters, the authors conducted an extensive search of peer-viewed articles of databases including web of science, google scholar, and china knowledge resource integrated database in june 2020. the following keyword combinations were used as the first step to screen articles: “plastic film” or “film mulch” and “microbial commu- nity” or “microbiome”.
selection_criteria: 1) field-based study with an experimental design allowing pairwise comparison between film mulch treatments and bare soil controls; 2) at least one soil microbial community parameter (abundance, diversity, or function) was reported; 3) treatment pairs established with same ecosystem types, crop types, and soil types; 4) for articles with experimental data for more than one growing season/year, only the last data were extracted for meta- analysis; the approach can greatly eliminate the non-independence of the data.
data_analysis: all statistics were conducted using r v 3.6.0. to correct for the nested structure and non-independence of observations, we used the mixed-effect models to evaluate the effects of pm on soil microbial parameters and other related properties, the models were constructed via rma.mv() function in the “metafor”package and the overall effect and the 95% confidence interval (ci) were calculated. the sensitivity of the few variables with potential publication bias was then examined using the trim-and-fill model. we conducted “leave-one-out” tests to check the robustness of variables’ effect sizes by function leave1out() in package “metafor”, this is a kind of sensitivity analysis; the funnel plots were used to display the comparison of data from all cases to the aggregated weighted mean within-study suggests.
background: Plastic film mulch alters the soil environment and improves crop production. Although the response of above- ground parts of agroecosystems to plastic film mulch has been extensively studied, no studies have investigated the response of the soil microbiome to plastic film mulch and its effect on crop yield.
objective: the study aimed to: 1) explore whether fm shapes distinct soil microbial abundance, diversity, and functionality patterns; 2) clarify the underlying drivers of these responses; 3) determine whether microbial parameters are related to changes in crop yield and whether these parameters belong to specific microbial parameters, such as abundance, diversity or functionality.
result1: the mean effect sizes of most soil microbial parameters were significantly (p < 0.05) greater than zero, but microbial beta-diversity had a significant negative value (−0.137, 95% ci: −0.264 to −0.010). fm significantly increased microbial abundance (+0.104, 95% ci: +0.070 to + 0.139). all functionality parameters increased significantly (p < 0.05), with an effect size of + 0.129 for overall functionality (95% ci: +0.087 to + 0.170).
result2: both shannon (+0.043, 95% ci: +0.022 to + 0.064) and richness index (+0.037, 95% ci: +0.007 to + 0.067) increased significantly (p < 0.05). when compared to no fm, the significant (p < 0.05) change in community structure suggested that fm alters the entire soil microbial community. fm significantly (p < 0.05) increased the abundance and diversity of soil fungal and actinobacterial communities when compared to no fm. the bacterial shannon index increased significantly (+0.021, 95% ci: +0.005 to + 0.036), whereas the bacterial richness index changed insignificantly (+0.010, 95% ci: −0.028 to + 0.047).
general_conclusion: the results highlight the beneficial effects of plastic film mulching on the soil microbial community with the only exceptions for microbial nitrogen biomass that showed no effect and for soil microbial betha diversity that showed a negative effect.

search_strategy: the selected publications were collected by searching isi web of science database and china knowledge resource integrated database using the following search criteria: ts = (plastic mulching∗) and (soil organic carbon∗ or microbial biomass carbon∗ or enzyme activities∗ or co2∗ or ch4∗) and ts = (film mulching∗ or plastic mulching∗) and (maize∗ or wheat∗ or potato∗ or yield∗ or root∗ or biomass∗).
selection_criteria: (i) the selected study included at least one parameter of interest (i.e. response variables) as economic yield (ey), aboveground biomass (ab), root biomass (rb), soil organic carbon (soc), co2 emission, ch4 flux, microbial biomass carbon (mbc), c‒related soil enzyme activities (i.e. glucosidase, sucrase, catalase, urease and alkaline phosphatase); (ii) only field study with replicated experimental design was included, greenhouse and laboratory incubation experiments excluded. pairwise comparisons on mulching and non‒mulching farming management were performed under the same pedo‒climatic conditions (e.g., temperature, precipitation, soil texture, and soil type) for at least 2 consecutive years; (iii) provided treatment means, sample sizes, and variances, or these could be extracted from tables or the figures using software; (v) duration of plastic mulching should be at least one full crop season for each year. when there were more than one articles on the same experiment, the article with longest mulching duration was included; (iv) to avoid pre‒mulching heterogeneity of soc stock between treatment and control, the values of soc contents at the beginning and end of each trial should be provided for the calculation of actual changes due to mulching. however, only few studies provided the baseline values of soc stocks for both experimental and control plots. given the fact that all data considered originated from pairwise system comparisons including controlled field trials, baseline differences in soc stocks among the different plots of one comparison were expected to be negligible. the authors therefore decided to also included the studies that the baseline values were not known into the data pool.
data_analysis: a mixed effect model that included a random effect for multiple studies from the same site was performed to calculate the mean effect sizes and variances for the concerned response variables. the authors used heterogeneity tests to confirm if models could explain significant variation. the majority of results show significant inter‒study heterogeneity, so the authors rejected the null hypothesis that all studies share a common effect size in favor of the interpretation that true effect sizes vary between studies. the sensitivity of the results was examined using the trim‒and‒fill model (i.e. the authors repeated the model for each of concerned responsory variable to account for the number of missing studies). the authors tested for potential publication bias using egger’s regression. the analysis results did not suggest that there was bias in most cases.
background: Plastic mulching provides many advantages for crop production, especially in dry croplands, such as reducing evaporation, improving water temperature conditions, and minimizing soil erosion. After three decades of practical application, however, a comprehensive nationwide assessment of its potential environmental consequences, in terms of SOC stock, was not available.
objective: the objective was to quantify the nationwide effects of plastic mulching application on crop net primary productivity, soil c fluxes, and total soc pool, and further identify the dominant environmental, edaphic, and anthropogenic drivers on these effects.
result1: plastic mulching generated a significant and positive mean effect size (5%, 95% ci: 0–10%) on mbc. agronomic management including crop type, planting densities, and n application rate, and environmental factors such as growing temperature significantly influenced the mulching effect on mbc.
result2: moreover, mulching significantly increased soil enzyme activity by 13% (95% ci: 9–17%) compared to non‒mulching . influencing factors were crop types, planting density, n inputs, soil texture, growing temperature.
general_conclusion: this study indicated that plastic mulching significantly increased eea and mbc compared to non‒mulching. the mulching‒induced changes in eea and mbc varied based upon agronomic management, environmental and edaphic conditions.
knowledge_gaps: although microbial activity is closely associated with soil ph, the study did not detect a significant eea change with soil ph across the entire dataset. this was because the majority of eligible samples was only distributed on china’s alkaline soil.

search_strategy:
peer-reviewed articles from january 1990 to july 2020 were selected using web of science and china national knowledge infra- structure (cnki) databases. three fields were used for the search in the title, abstract or keywords of the articles. the first field was tree crop
type, with the following search terms: “orchard” or “apple” or “citrus” or “vineyard” or “almond” or “olive”. the second field was cover crop type, and the search terms were “cover crop” or “ground cover” or “catch crop” or “green manure”. the third field was soil variable, with the search terms “runoff” or “soil loss” or “erosion” or “nutrient loss” or “soil and water conservation”.
selection_criteria: the case studies were chosen following the strict quality criteria: 1) the experiments or observations were conducted under field conditions (i.e., no laboratory, rainfall simulation or runoff simulation experiments, etc.); 2) both the ground cover and control (clean tillage or bare ground management) treatments were included in each case study, and the two treatments were exposed to the same environmental conditions; 3) the targeted article contained at least one response variable (runoff or soil loss or nutrients loss observations); 4) when the variable was measured at multiple time points, the average value was calculated to meet the accurate observation results; 5) multiple ground cover species in one study were considered as independent observations.
data_analysis: the mean percentage change and 95% confidential intervals were computed and compared with sigmaplot v12.0. positive reduction percentages indicated significant reductions of runoff or soil loss or nutrient losses as a result of ground cover relative to clean tillage management. when the ci crossed the invalid line (including 0), the ground cover effectiveness was deemed not significant.
background: Tree crops are mainly planted on sloped farmland, which can lead to soil erosion caused by runoff. As an important tree crop management strategy, ground cover management has been effective in controlling runoff generation and soil loss. However, a global overview is needed to comprehensively quantify the effectiveness of ground cover on water and soil conservation.
objective: the aim of this study is to provide evidence-based rationale for implementing more sustainable tree crop management practices. the objectives were to 1) quantify the effectiveness of ground cover management in reducing runoff, soil loss and nutrient loss from tree crop systems; 2) quantify the effectiveness of ground cover management according to the slope and climatic conditions of the tree crop system.
result1: compared to no mulching, mulching reduced runoff by 39.1% and soil loss by 51.2%.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: mulching reduced runoff by 39.1% and soil loss by 51.2% compared to no mulching.

search_strategy: a database of runoff, soil loss and runoff plot measurements acquired from areas where soil conservation techniques were applied was mainly compiled from scientiﬁc journal articles, books and ph.d. dissertations. the authors reviewed the isi web of science, china national knowledge infrastructure, and google scholar databases to identify articles matching the keywords, soil loss and sediment yield.
selection_criteria: 1) the article contained at least one runoff or soil loss response variable; 2) each data point was collected during at least a full year, or the reported data could be extrapolated to represent a full year with a sufﬁcient degree of reliability; 3) the same response variables were compared between lands treated with soil conservation techniques (scts), hereafter called treated, and those not treated with scts (hereafter called control); 4) the treated lands and control lands were exposed to the same environmental conditions; 5) the number of replications was reported; 6) the groups of categories contained more than two data pairs; 7) only runoff and soil loss measurements from bound runoff plots equipped with tanks for collecting runoff and soil loss were used to reduce the inﬂuence of measurement uncertainties, and only plots with a minimum length of 5 m were retained because they were considered to be representative.
data_analysis: to further analyze the efﬁciencies of soil conservation techniques among different subgroup categories, the heterogeneity of effect sizes was assessed with p-values that describe the variations in effect sizes that can be attributed to differences among the categories of each predictor variable. the overall effect sizes and 95% conﬁdential intervals (cis) were computed and compared using the program metafor 2.0.
background: The beneﬁts of soil conservation techniques (SCTs) vary according to correlations between the natural environment and anthropogenic activities, and their effects on water erosion control at the plot scale have been extensively tested in ﬁeld runoff plots. However, only a few previous studies have focused on quantifying the effects of various SCTs at the regional scale, and only one type of SCT has been studied at the national, regional and global scales. Therefore, a comprehensive overview and quantiﬁcation of various SCTs at the global scale is lacking.
objective: the objectives of this paper are: 1) to develop a documented global database of ﬁeld plot data on the use of scts; 2) to quantify the effects of different sct types on water erosion control at the global scale; and 3) to compare the effects of scts on water erosion control for different slopes, land uses, continents and climate zones (czs).
result1: mulching decreased soil loss and run-off.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: mulching reduced soil loss and run-off.
knowledge_gaps: due to a lack of detailed information about some of the influential factors and the types of soil conservation techniques in this study, as well as the substantial variation in study conditions, the environmental and experimental factors controlling the variability in the efﬁciency of each soil conservation techniques could not be clearly identiﬁed in this study.

search_strategy: the authors conducted a review of studies, including journal articles and academic dissertations, obtained through web of science (wos) and the chinese national knowledge infrastructure (cnki) conducted at plot scales in the rshr of china for all years, up to december 2018. the search terms were as follows: “soil and water conservation” or “soil retention” or “soil and water loss” or “runoff” or “erosion” or “sediment” and “china”. they refined the search results using the keywords “red soil” or “subtropical” or “granite”. additionally, references cited in searched studies were considered as well.
selection_criteria: 1) plots were observed under natural rainfall conditions and located in the rshr of china; 2) the same response variables, including at least one soil loss or erosion rate or runoff depth or runoff coefficient, were compared between plots with swcms and plots without swcms; 3) one of the factors was recorded associated with plots, such as location, precipitation, field area, slope length, slope gradient, land use, soil properties and monitoring period; 4) the number of replications, mean values, standard deviations or standard errors ofplots with swcms and plots with- out swcms were reported; 5) at least two data pairs were contained in each group (a plot with swcms and a plot without swcms); 6) identical plot data reported in different articles were included only once.
data_analysis: the mean effect sizes were calculated using a random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood method. the 95% confidential intervals (ci) were calculated with a bootstrapping approach (a method for esti- mating population by re-sampling samples) and presented for forest plots. the meta-analysis was performed by using the software openmee. a one-way anovawas used to evaluatewhether the rrs was significantly different with swcm types or land use types or slope gradients.
background: Anthropogenic pressure coupled with high rainfall and diverse heterogeneous landscapes (e.g., land use and to- pography) has resulted in severe water erosion in the red soil hilly region (RSHR) of China. Soil and water con- servation measures (SWCMs) have been extensively implemented, and their effects on runoff and sediment control have been widely tested at plot scales. However, it is difficult to gain an overview of the efficiency of SWCMs due to the difficulty of directly upscaling field observations to regional scales.
objective: the specificob- jectives of the present study are as follows: 1) to quantify the effects of different types ofswcms and the combined effects ofthesemeasures in reducing runoffand sediment; 2) to identify themost effective swcms in the rshr; 3) to explore the benefit tradeoffs relationship between.
result1: mulching reduced soil loss.
result2: considering the combination of several conservation measures, tree crop + mulching + terrace had a sediment reduction efficiency up to 99%. in addition, hedgerows +mulching was more effective in conserving soil resources than other techniques, with an efficiency value from 92% to 98%.
result4: among all thirty swcms, the values of rreir for runoff were >1.0 for only eight measures, including mulching (1.2 ± 0.08).
result5: the rreis values for sediment included eight practices with values >1.0, including mulching (1.07 ± 0.04).
general_conclusion: mulching reduced soil loss and runoff.

background: Amajor challenge of the Sustainable DevelopmentGoals linked to Agriculture, Food Security, and Nutrition, under the current global crop production paradigm, is that increasing crop yields often have negative environmental impacts. It is therefore urgent to develop and adopt optimal soil-improving cropping systems (SICS) that can allow us to decouple these system parameters. Soil salinization is a major environmental hazard that limits agricultural potential and is closely linked to agricultural mismanagement and water resources overexploitation, especially in arid climates.
objective: the authors review literature pertaining soil-improving cropping systems (sics) that aim to prevent, mitigate, or remediate the negative impacts of soil salinization and ameliorate the associated soil functions and ecosystem services relevant to agricultural production, aiming not to describe the problem, but looking for solutions.
result1: mulching  on average decreases soil salinity by 7% but it was not statistically  significant.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: plastic mulching has no effect on soil salinity.
knowledge_gaps: biosaline agriculture seems, so far, the last resort when the soil accumulates large amounts of salts in the root zone. in the near future, we may expect some help from biotechnology for reclaiming salinized lands. screening germplasm of halophytes plants could be of interest for recovering lands heavily affected by the problem of salinization. the use of tolerant rootstocks and varieties is foreseen to increase in the years to come. transgenic crops have also been proposed as a solution to deal with salinized soils. nonetheless, whatever the approach planned for halting salinization of agricultural lands, the measures proposed should also unavoidably consider stakeholders’ willingness to adopt them.

search_strategy: literature searches were conducted in the isi web of knowledge core database targeting peer- reviewed articles published online until april 30, 2015 in two steps. in a first query, we tested it by including a spe- cific management option such as “irrigation” because water shortage is conceived as a potential threat to the mediterranean agricultural system. the search terms for the first query was thus (“agro*” or “agri*” or “farm*”) and (mediterranean*) and (ecosystem*) and (management*) and (irrigat*) in the topic field. then, the authors strove to capture the diversity of farming practices studied in case studies by not including any `a priori restrictive search terms. this additional query was made with com- binations of keywords including (“agro*” or “agri*” or “farm*”) and (mediterranean*) and (management*) in the topic field.
selection_criteria: the authors selected empirical case studies which measured ecosystem services-related properties both for conservation (treatment) and conventional (control) management options. this step excluded pure simulation modeling studies and reviews. the authors focused on papers reporting results from the mediterranean basin but included six well-designed papers reporting from mediterranean climate regions outside the basin (i.e., south and south west australia, the cape of south africa, central chile, and california).
data_analysis:
to secure statistical significance by keeping a sufficient sample size, we decided to weight observations using the sample sizes: studies with larger sample sizes were weighted higher during aggregation. for the uncertainty analysis, we report the means and
95% confidence intervals (cis) of the wlrr. the cis were constructed by non-parametric bootstrapping (nboot =10, 000) using the percentile method. all calculations were done in r version 3.3.1 using the packages boot and vioplot.
background: In the Mediterranean region, the long-term provision of agro-ecosystem services is threatened by accelerating climate change, unsustainable farming practices, and other pressures. Alternative management practices such as conservation agriculture could be expected to ensure sustainability of ecosystem services from Mediterranean agro-ecosystems. Conservation agriculture is characterized by minimal soil disturbance, permanent soil cover, and diversification of crop species.
objective: the objective of this study is to fill this knowledge gap by conducting a meta-analysis on the impact of conservative management practices on ecosystem services in the mediterranean basin based on published literature. our goal is to identify the positive and negative impacts of conservation farming practices on ecosystem services in the mediterranean basin, providing evidence-based recommendations for sustainable land management in the mediterranean basin in the future.
result1: for mulching, water content was higher than in conventional farming systems, which might explain the increased yield when mulching is applied.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: mulching has a positive effect on soil water content in mediterranean areas.
knowledge_gaps: 1) the authors only included case studies based on in situ experimental results, implying that offsite effects of the farming practices are not accounted for. offsite effects such as maintenance of drinking water quality, reduction of pollution from agriculture, reduction of salinization, and eutrophication in soils and water are crucial for many surrounding areas (pascual et al. 2017). these topics could be addressed in the future research. 2) the largest number of studies concerned tillage, whereas weed management had the fewest data points. to develop more general and comprehensive recommendations, more studies dealing with rarely studied management options would be needed. 3) for the further research, longer term studies will be required to test the conservative management practices.

selection_criteria: 1) field studies involved mulching treatments and non-mulching controls; 2) studies reported soil water index, soil water content (%) and/or soil water storage (mm); 3) crops applied plastic film mulching without irrigation throughout the growing season; 4) studies with multifactorial analyses showed no significant interactions among treatments; 5) studies reported mean data, standard deviations (sd) and the number of replications (n); 6) studies included deep soil sampling (≥100 cm); 7) the location and year of the experiments (at least two years) were provided.
