search_strategy: all published peer-reviewed scientific journal articles on the water use of winter wheat-summer maize cropping systems were collected from the china national knowledge infrastructure (1979–2019, http://www.cnki.net/) and web of science (1979–2019 , h t t p : //apps.webofknowledge.com/). different combinations of search terms that included “north china plain” or “huang-huai-hai plain” and “winter wheat” or “summer maize” or “summer corn” and “crop product*” or “yield” or “output” were used for the selection of published studies.
selection_criteria: (i) the research object must be field experiments conducted in the ncp, excluding pot and laboratory experiments and model simulations; (ii) the cropping system must be the winter wheat-summer maize cropping system; (iii) the studies must be about one or more of the four leading management practices (e.g., no nitrogen versus nitrogen input, no irrigation versus irrigation, rotary tillage versus other tillage methods, and straw removal versus straw return, with the former as the control and the later as the treatment); and (iv) the data must include the number of trial replications, crop yield, wue, or seasonal crop evapotranspiration (etc).
data_analysis: the random-effect meta-analysis was used to analyze the data set of wheat water use. the metawin 2.1 software  was selected for this metaanalysis. authors obtained the 95% confidence interval (ci) and weighted mean effect size (ln r++) by bootstrapping. based on the data of winter wheat irrigation experiments, linear regression analysis in sigmaplot 14.0 was used to study the relationships between effect sizes ofwue under irrigation and other indicators.
background: Water shortage is a serious threat to agriculture production in the North China Plain. Sustainable management practices can improve the water use efficiency of winter wheat, but currently no academic consensus has been reached
objective: authors conducted a meta-analysis on the yield and water use of a winter wheat-summer maize cropping system based on peer-reviewed studies in the north china plain (ncp) to (i) investigate the current situation of water use in a winter wheat-summer maize cropping system, (ii) identify the factors that affect the wue of winter wheat, and (iii) propose sustainable management strategies to optimize the winter wheat production in the ncp.
result1: compared with rainfed, irrigation significantly increased the wheat yield by 30% (p < 0.05)
result2: NA
general_conclusion: compared with rainfed, irrigation significantly increased the wheat yield by 30%.
knowledge_gaps: 1) it is of great importance to explore the internal physiological relationship between crops and water for efficient utilization of water resources. future attention should also be focused on the interaction of field management practices (fertilization, film mulching, agronomic practices, irrigation techniques, etc.) with deficit irrigation. 2) the effects of long-term climate change should be considered in the future research on deficit irrigation schedules.

search_strategy: the authors conducted a comprehensive search of peer-reviewed reports on water use in maize production published between 1970 and 2018 using the web of science, china national knowledge infrastructure and google scholar. different combinations of searching terms included “maize” or “corn”, and “yield”, and “irrigated”, and “water productivity” or “water use efficiency” in the abstract or key words.
selection_criteria: the authors screened publications based on the following criteria: maize yield and wp were documented; data were measured in field experiments (pot experiments, experiments under rainproof shelters, and model simulations were excluded); locations of experimental sites were explicitly provided; experimental treatments (irrigated/non-irrigated) were paired; and soil water supply before sowing and at harvest was reported for a soil layer of at least 1 m.
data_analysis: the authors applied random-effects meta-analysis to assess the impact on yield, et, wp, biomass, hi, yield components under irrigated compared with non-irrigated systems. there were significant heterogeneity in the random-effects meta-analysis for the yield dataset (qt = 3776846, p< 0.0001), for et dataset (qt = 65655191, p < 0.0001) and for wp database (qt = 5560054, p < 0.0001). the authors ran mixed-effects meta-analysis models to assess the relationship between effect sizes and explanatory variables. the explanatory variables considered in this meta-analysis included seasonal precipitation levels, irrigation amounts, annual average temperature, soil organic matter (som), soil bulk density, and n fertilizer rate, the dataset (yield and wp databases) were separated into different sub-datasets. publication bias was assessed using funnel plots and egger tests. rosenberg’s fail safe-numbers (nfs) were calculated to assess the robustness of our results to publication bias. the results were considered robust despite the possibility for publication bias if nfs > 5*k +10, where, k indicated number of sizes.
background: Detailed knowledge of how irrigation affects maize yield, WP, Nr losses, and GHG emissions is critical to evaluated the potential of irrigation for sustainably feeding the growing population in tandem with climate change mitigation on a global scale. However, a quantitative synthesis of the overall responses of food security, water resource, and environments to irrigation in maize production is still lacking.
objective: in current study, the authors carried out a meta-analysis to quantitatively estimate irrigation management effects on yield, wp, nr losses, and ghg emissions by integrating available worldwide measurements.
result1: considering all 1490 paired data points, maize yield increased by 30.35% (cis: 28.53 to 32.17, qt = 3776846, p < 0.0001), from 7357 kg ha−1 under non-irrigated systems to 9512 kg ha−1 with supplemental irrigation of 146 mm. corresponding spike numbers, grain numbers, grain weight, spike diameter, and spike length in irrigated systems were significantly higher, by 9.81%, 14.9%, 5.51%, 8.34%, and 8.04%, respectively, than in non-irrigated systems. high yield in irrigated systems contributed to 31.29% higher aboveground biomass, and an 8.43% higher harvest index.
result2: irrigation amounts, seasonal precipitation, annual average temperature, and fertilizer application of n significantly affected maize yield.
general_conclusion: yield components were significantly higher under irrigated systems than non-irrigated systems.
knowledge_gaps: 1)  invest should focus on agronomic research that incorporates an ecosystem perspective, modifying and adapting intensive agricultural systems according to knowledge from diverse research disciplines; 2) the extent of yield increase through supplementary irrigation has not been widely explored globally because they are affected by lots of environmental and management factors.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed journal articles published in english from 1985 to 2016 were collected to build the database based on web of science search using the following sets of keywords: (i) wheat or maize; (ii) film mulch or plastic mulch or plastic cover; and (iii) water stress or water deficit or drought or irrigation deficit. the authors replaced the phrases ‘film mulch’; ‘plastic mulch’ and ‘plastic cover’ with ‘irrigation’ and ‘china’ to search for articles discussing supplementary irrigation specific to the region.
selection_criteria: only articles from china that met the following criteria were included in the database: (i) the experiments were conducted under field conditions where the effect of irrigation or plastic mulching was compared with flat (even or level topography); rainfed conditions; (ii) the reported plants were monoculture cereals of maize (zea mays) and wheat (i.e.; bread wheat; triticum aestivum); and (iii) the articles reported crop response as grain yield.
data_analysis: the magnitude of yield, total et, wue, and average soil water content (0–20 cm) responses throughout the crop growing season were examined based on three different types of mulch that covered the furrow: (i) plastic, (ii) straw, (iii) no cover or bare. to compare the differences in crop or soil response ratio between each treatment, meta-analysis was used to construct the confidence intervals. the authors performed a simple diagnostic test using the formula following lajeunesse to improve the reliability of lnr in estimating the effect size. bootstrapping was also iterated 9999 times to improve the probability that the confidence interval was calculated around the cumulative mean effect size for each categorical variable.
background: Plastic mulching technology for wheat and maize has been commonly used in China, but their effect on yield, soil water content, evapotranspiration (ET), and WUE has not been compared with traditional irrigation.
objective: using a meta-analysis approach, the authors quantitatively examined the efficacy of plastic mulching in comparison with traditional irrigation in china.
result1: the results show that irrigation increased crop yield when compared to flat, rainfed cropping systems (+50%).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: irrigation increased crop yield when compared to rainfed cropping systems.

search_strategy: a comprehensive search for peer-reviewed literature published from january 1990 to january 2016 related to the effects of irrigation on wheat yields was performed. literature were searched in three databases: web of science, springerlink, and the china academic journal network publishing database using the terms including ‘irrigation,’ ‘wheat,’ and ‘china’.
selection_criteria: (1) comparisons between non-irrigation and irrigation practices; (2) at least one parameter of interest (grain yield, yield components, water productivity, and et) was reported; and (3) the experimental location was stated. studies that described only the relationship between irrigation and wheat yield without a non-irrigation practice, and those that did not provide clear descriptions of the experimental methods were rejected.
data_analysis: the natural log of the response ratio (irrigation/non-irrigation) was applied to represent the effect size in our meta-analysis. the weight of individual observations was calculated by replications, with weights = (n irrigation × n non-irrigation)/(n irrigation + n non-irrigation), where n irrigation and n non-irrigation are the number of replicates for irrigation and non-irrigation practices, respectively. bootstrapping procedures were conducted with a 95% confidence interval for weighted mean effect sizes using 4999 iterations.
background: Irrigation is a crucial measure for ensuring food security; however, the complex linkages among yield increases, water productivity, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are unclear for irrigated wheat production in China.
objective: here a meta-analysis was conducted to determine the trade-offs among yield increase, water productivity, and ghg emissions in irrigated chinese wheat production systems.
result1: the grain yield increase due to irrigation nationwide in china was quantified using meta-analysis, and found that the overall average yield was increased by 23% through the use of a 172 mm of supplemental irrigation water. under irrigated systems, the mean aboveground biomass increased by 24%, whereas the mean harvest index showed no significant change compared to non-irrigated systems. with yield components, the spike number and grain number increased by 13% and 8%, respectively, whereas grain weight was not significantly affected.
result2: given various annual precipitation amounts, soil textures, and n fertilizer application rates, grain yield under irrigated systems always increased, while the yield increase (defined as the yield gap between irrigated and non-irrigated system) varied greatly.
result3: in comparison with non-irrigated systems, mean grain yield increased by 23% under both conventional irrigation amounts and optimized irrigation amounts, and by 16% and 24% given conventional irrigation periods and improved irrigation periods, respectively. similar results were observed for aboveground biomass, harvest index, spike number, grain number, and grain weight in the irrigation system compared with non-irrigated systems.
general_conclusion: in this study, irrigation increased wheat grain yield components at a national scale in china. grain weight was not impacted by any irrigation strategy, compared to rainfed systems.

search_strategy: a comprehensive literature search provided cases of impacts of awm technologies, obtained from peer-reviewed journals and non-peer reviewed conference proceedings, theses and project reports in the limpopo river basin from 1980 to 2013. the sources searched for cases through the end of april 2013 were: agris, cabdirect, proquest, econlit, text webpublisher from inmagic, science direct, database of abstracts of reviews of effects (dare) and other databases (e.g. scopus, isi web of knowledge and google scholar). the literature search used the following keywords and their combinations: maize, sorghum, millet, rainfed, reduced tillage, no-tillage, ripper, ridges, tied ridges, conservation agriculture, minimum tillage, zero tillage, infiltration pits, fanya juu, planting basins, bunds, terraces, contours, inter-cropping, agroforestry, rotation, grain yield, runoff, nutrient and water harvesting. other words used were storage, retention, water storage, supplemental irrigation, irrigation, crop residues, mulch, residue, organic, inorganic, manure, fertilizer, africa, sub-sahara africa, botswana, mozambique, south africa, zimbabwe, limpopo, olifants, mzingwane, gwanda, notwane, chokwe and xai xai.
selection_criteria: 1) located in the limpopo river basin; 2) cereals crops ; 3) reported yield, water productivity, and field runoff from treatment and control;
data_analysis: meta-analysis was used to determine the overall effect size of standardized mean difference (smd) and to impose a 95% confidence limits on the means. the random-effects model was used.  a funnel plot, which is a scatter plot of the effect estimate (smd) in relation to the size or precision of each study, standard error (se), was used for the assessment of risk of bias that may affect the cumulative evidence, such as publication bias and selective reporting within studies. factors used as covariates for the response of crop grain yield to awm technologies included: long-term rainfall, altitude, soil texture and field slope. the subgroup analyses examined whether the subgroups reduce any heterogeneity in each awm main group. the p-value used in this study relates to the summary effect in a meta-analysis. consistence of results was measured by i2 statistic.
scale: limpopo river basin (botswana, mozambique, south africa and zimbabwe)
background: Multiple agricultural water management (AWM) technologies are being promoted worldwide in rainfed agro-ecological production systems, such as the Limpopo River Basin, to close the yield gap, enhance food security and reduce poverty, but evidences on yield gains and environmental impacts are varied.
objective: this paper conducts a review of the performance of awm technologies, including water harvesting with storage (full or supplemental irrigation), against conventional farmer practices to produce adequate evidence on cereal yield and field runoff changes.
result1: the efficacy of awm technologies was highest for water harvesting with storage (smd = 0.53). water harvesting with storage that resulted in median yield increases of 34–95% provides the least risks to farmers in terms of coping with the inherent rainfall variability of the limpopo river basin. the widest variation in yield observed for this group of technology is indicative of the huge potential of yield gains that can be realized from this technology. water harvesting with storage produced the highest absolute median yields of 2.20 t ha−1 (control 1.00 t ha−1).
result2: yield stability analysis showed that under prolonged drought or very high rainfall conditions, no awm technology, except water harvesting with storage can offset the effects of these extreme conditions.
general_conclusion: yield was reduced in absence of irrigation.
knowledge_gaps: 1) no data in european union; 2) some limitations of not having actual seasonal rainfall data nor rainfall distribution to correlate to yield and water productivity, and quite low number of cases that measured erosion (67 cases) and runoff (51 cases) were considered to increase uncertainty of the results. this lack of data suggests the need for improved field monitoring to capture these aspects. 3) understanding the bio-physical and socio-economic contexts of smallholder farmers is crucial in identifying the most appropriate suite of agriculture water management (awm) technologies, as the results indicate that every technology has relative chances of success and failure depending on soils, rainfall regime, nutrient, water and farmer management practices. hence, the onus is on researchers to make additional effort in understanding when and where awm technologies work. 4) the added benefit of awm technologies in climatic adaptation through the carbon sequestration requires further investigation.

search_strategy: various english (web of science, google scholar, science direct, wiley online library, springer) and chinese (cnki) databases were searched by using keywords: wheat, yield, water stress, water deficiency, china and their combinations.
selection_criteria: the articles related with water stress on winter wheat in china from 2000-2017 were collected and screened on the basis of the following criteria: 1) area was located in northern china and year and latitude and longitude of the test site was clearly mentioned; 2) the test plot was a field whereas pot experiments were not included; 3) the experimental study had a water stress treatment and also a well-watered control; 4) only the water stress as treatment along with control, and yield data were collected in the multi-factor study, whereas, other treatments were routinely processed in the local field.
data_analysis: variables under different total water were calculated by the fixed- or random-effects model using software revman (version 5.3). in this study, the standardized mean difference were used as the effect size of the meta-analysis. random-effect model was used for moderate to high heterogeneity (x2 > 50% and a chi-square p-value < 0.05). the heterogeneity test of the data in this paper reached a significant level (pq<0.05), so a random effects model was used. the difference between total water and the control was measured by the number of samples and the standard deviation. confidence interval was finally generated by the effect size. if the 95% confidence interval size for a variable didn’t cover 0, it indicated that irrigation treatment had a significant effect on yield compared to control. engauge digitizer was used to extract data such as histograms in paper.
background: Water deficit is one of the main environmental constraints affecting the yield of winter wheat.
objective: to study the effect of water stress and latitude on the yield and yield components of winter wheat in northern china based on the meta-analysis method.
result1: grain yield (gy) was affected by different total water. the 95% confidence interval of gy effect size did not overlap with 0 indicating that the total water had a significant positive effect on gy. gy increased gradually with increasing the total water from w2 (1001-2000 m3/ha) to w4 (3001-4000 m3/ha). the gy reached the maximum at w4 and was decreased at w5 (>4000 m3/ha). the gy at w1 (1-1000 m3/ha) was slightly higher than w2. the average increase of gy at w4 was 148% relative to control.
result2: the results indicated the spike number (sn) and thousand grain weight (tgw) were significantly affected by total water. the sn and tgw at w1 were higher than w2, and sn was increased by increasing total water from w2 to w4. the sn at w4 was 39.7% higher than control. the tgw was highest at w3, which was 79.7% higher than control. the 95% confidence interval of gn effect size contains 0, which indicate that different total water have no significant effect on gn.
result3: all p-value of heterogeneity i2 test were greater than 0.05 and was less than 50%, indicating that there was no significant heterogeneity in each group of data.
general_conclusion: the results showed that all grain yield components but the grains number were significantly reduced in absence of irrigation. no significant impact on grains number.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed publications were identified from isi web of science and china knowledge resource integrated database between 1990 and 2020. nine keywords and different combinations of these words, “maize, wheat, rice, nitrogen, fertilization, water input, irrigation, yield, and water use efficiency”, were used to search the databases mentioned above.
selection_criteria: the following criteria were used to select appropriate papers: (1) field studies of fertilization or irrigation experiments performed in china (pot experiments or model simulations were excluded); (2) the field studies consisted of a control treatment, without irrigation or fertilization; (3) wue (kg ha-1 mm-1) was calculated as a ratio of crop yield (kg ha-1) to water consumed, including the amount of water lost as evapotranspiration (mm) in the growing season; (4) the field experiment had at least two sample sizes and the experiment was carried out for more than two years; and (5) the mean value and sample size of crop yield or wue were available in the paper or can be calculated.
data_analysis: a categorical random-effect model was used to calculate the mean effect size (d++) for each group and 95% confidence intervals (cis) of effect size were generated by a bootstrapping procedure with 4999 iterations. all the relevant calculations were performed in metawin 2.1.
background: The increases in crop yield in China are linked to massive increases in fertilizer and water input, which have also accelerated the degradation of soil and environmental pollution. objective: a meta-analysis was used to assess the effects of field management (n input (kg ha􀍥1), irrigation (mm), fertilizer type, fertilization frequency, and irrigation method) on crop yield and wue for maize, wheat and rice in china.
result1: irrigation increased maize and wheat yield on average by 26%, and 50%. irrigation increased rice yield.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: irrigation increased maize, wheat and rice yield compared to no irrigation.

search_strategy: a comprehensive search for peer-reviewed literature published from january 1990 to january 2016 related to the effects of irrigation on wheat yields was performed. literature were searched in three databases: web of science, springerlink, and the china academic journal network publishing database using the terms including ‘irrigation,’ ‘wheat,’ and ‘china’.
selection_criteria: (1) comparisons between non-irrigation and irrigation practices; (2) at least one parameter of interest (grain yield, yield components, water productivity, and et) was reported; and (3) the experimental location was stated. studies that described only the relationship between irrigation and wheat yield without a non-irrigation practice, and those that did not provide clear descriptions of the experimental methods were rejected.
data_analysis: the natural log of the response ratio (irrigation/non-irrigation) was applied to represent the effect size in our meta-analysis. the weight of individual observations was calculated by replications, with weights = (n irrigation × n non-irrigation)/(n irrigation + n non-irrigation), where n irrigation and n non-irrigation are the number of replicates for irrigation and non-irrigation practices, respectively. bootstrapping procedures were conducted with a 95% confidence interval for weighted mean effect sizes using 4999 iterations.
background: Irrigation is a crucial measure for ensuring food security; however, the complex linkages among yield increases, water productivity, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are unclear for irrigated wheat production in China.
objective: here a meta-analysis was conducted to determine the trade-offs among yield increase, water productivity, and ghg emissions in irrigated chinese wheat production systems.
result1: compared with non-irrigation, the results showed that yield-scaled ghg emissions decreased by 5% and 8%, respectively, with a conventional and optimized irrigation amounts when surface water was used. it respectively increased by 33% and 15% when shallow aquifer water was used, and by 68% and 36% when deep aquifer water was used, given a conventional and optimized irrigation amount.
result2: compared with non-irrigated systems, the results showed that yield-scaled ghg emissions decreased by 2% and 8%, respectively, with a conventional and an improved irrigation period when surface water was used. it increased by 27% and 19%, respectively, with conventional and improved irrigation periods when shallow aquifer water was used, and it increased by 55% and 44%, respectively, with a conventional and an improved irrigation period when deep aquifer water was used.
general_conclusion:
when surface water was used for irrigation, yield-scaled ghg emissions were lower under conventional irrigation compared with no irrigation. same results were obtained  comparing non-irrigated systems to systems with optimized irrigation. 
however, results were different when shallow or deep aquifer water was used for irrigation. in this case, yield-scaled emissions were higher under conventional irrigation   compared with non-irrigated systems. same results were obtained when comparing non-irrigated systems to systems with optimized irrigation.
knowledge_gaps: 1) no data in european union; 2) precise estimate of nitrogen losses under different nitrogen and irrigation levels is almost impossible at a national scale. this imparts considerable uncertainty to estimating greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions. 3) simultaneously optimized irrigation amounts and irrigation periods should be most beneficial to increasing yield and decreasing yield-scaled ghg emissions, but this conclusion cannot be confirmed based on our current database.

search_strategy:
peer reviewed journal articles which reported nitrate loss from corn, miscanthus and switchgrass were compiled. search criteria developed to systematically capture peer reviewed journal articles using various search engines included: scirus, web of knowledge, science direct, agricultural database (agris), ebscohost, bioone, agricultural online access (agricola), electronic archive of international organizations (who, fao) and worldwide science.
search terms included: “nitrate and loss”, “nitrate and runoff”, “kg/ha”, “ton/ha”, “t/h”, “t/ha”, “mg/lm” and “gm/m” using the keywords: nitrate-nitrogen, corn, miscanthus, and switchgrass; one at a time. also, past publications were followed through the references section of the recent peer-reviewed articles selected for this study. the abstract and result section of all pertinent sprigerlink, google scholar, journal storage (jstor) and purdue university library website research was carefully reviewed. the journal articles which furnished the experimental results in terms of annual loads or concentrations were used in the subsequent analysis.
selection_criteria: the chosen articles were thoroughly investigated using the following criteria: 1) articles must have been published in a peer-reviewed scientific journal. 2) articles should discuss nitrate loss for at least one bioenergy crop such as corn, miscanthus and switchgrass. 3) articles should discuss nitrate loss through experimental field studies. 4) articles should report annual scale study of nitrate loss with their full length of measurement covering the entire year. 5) in all cases, articles should have reported nitrate loss with a sufficient description of experimental and environmental conditions.
data_analysis: not reported
background: Due to differences in climate, biophysical dissimilarities and land management characteristics in different parts of the world the factors affecting nitrate loss are often inconsistent and hence difficult to generalize.
objective: the primary objective of this study was to reanalyze the field scale experimental studies through various bioenergy crops such as corn, switchgrass, and miscanthus fields, and compare their nitrate loss. a secondary objective of this study was to compare nitrate loss in energy crops to understand nitrate loss in various conditions based on well-studied crops such as corn.
result1: the mean nitrate loss through the irrigated corn was significantly higher in the continuous corn field compared to no-irrigation.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: the mean nitrate loss through the irrigated corn was significantly higher in the continuous maize field compared to no-irrigation.
knowledge_gaps: 1) since these experiments were not conducted over the same location, factors such as prior year precipitation, water surplus and prior year fertilization rate could also be the controlling factors. also, soils may have a different degree of variability of soil nitrate content in different sites even though the comparisons were made over the same categories of soil. 2) also, more field scale and watershed scale studies are needed in the future, especially for miscanthus and swithgrass fields, to evaluate the degree and range of nitrate loss at various spatial extents.

search_strategy: authors collected peer reviewed journal articles from the china national knowledge infrastructure (http://www.cnki.net/, published from january 1979 to december 2016) and web of science (http://apps. webofknowledge.com/, published from january 1900 to december 2016). authors first identified “north china plain” or “huang-huai-hai plain” “winter wheat”“crop product*” as the search keywords.
selection_criteria: 1) the field experiment must have been conducted in the north china plain; 2) the cropping system in field experiment must contain winter wheat; 3) one or more of the following practice comparisons (e.g., no n versus n input, rain fed versus irrigated, rotary tillage versus other tillage methods, and straw removed versus straw return, with the former as the control and the later as the treatment) must be included; 4) data including the number of replications, nar, and yield must be presented or could be directly computed.
data_analysis: in a random-effect meta-analysis, the natural logarithm of the response ratio (lnr) was used as the effect size. due to the lack ofstandard deviations given in some studies, the number of experimental replications was used to calculate the weight (w) of each lnr. the 95% confidence interval (ci) and weighted mean effect size (lnrþþ) were generated by bootstrapping (4999 iterations), and the between-group heterogeneity was assessed by using randomization procedures with 4999 replications. to better explain the results, the effect size lnrþþ was converted to the percentage change. the meta-analysis was conducted using metawin 2.1. a correlation analysis was used to study the relationship between irrigation-induced nitrogen partial factor productivity (npfp), and evapotranspiration (et).
background: Increasing nitrogen use efficiency by optimizing field management practices is necessary to promote intensive and sustainable development of winter wheat production.
objective: to 1) assess the effects of different field management practices (e.g., n application, irrigation, tillage, straw management, etc.) on the nue of wheat; 2) understand the influence of major factors of field management practices on nue; and 3) identify the suitable strategies to improve the nue of winter wheat in the north china plain. here, results on the effect of irrigation are reported.
result1: an increase in npfp by 24.01% was observed with irrigation compared to no irrigation (p < 0.05).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: irrigation significantly increased npfp. attention should be paid not only to irrigation amount applied, but also to the selection of irrigation times, as well as management factors (nitrogen applied) and environmental factors (precipitations).

search_strategy: based on the two databases of the web of science and china national knowledge infrastructure (cnki), we searched for peer-reviewed scientific journal articles before december 2016 that were related to the effects of n input, irrigation, tillage, and straw return, on the n use of summer maize in ncp. the keywords used in a rigorous literature search included “north china plain or huang-huai-hai plain” “maize or corn or summer maize or summer corn” and “yield or output or crop product*”.
selection_criteria: a) the research object must be summer maize in the winter wheat-summer maize cropping system; b) the experiments described in the literature must be field experiments conducted in ncp (excluding pot experiments, laboratory experiments, and model studies); c) the research must focus on one or more of the four main farming practices (e.g., no n input versus n input, rain-fed versus irrigation, no-till versus other tillage methods, and straw removed versus straw return, with the former as the control and the later as the treatment;  and d) each set of study data must include the number of trial replications (minimum of three) and the yield.
data_analysis: the replication-based weighting method was then applied in the random-effect meta-analysis. we used metawin 2.1 (state university of new york at stony brook, usa) to obtain mean effect sizes and the 95% confidence intervals (cis) through a bootstrapping procedure with 4,999 iterations, and assess heterogeneity between subgroups by using randomization procedures with 4,999 replications.
background: Inappropriate nitrogen (N) use in maize (Zea mays L.) production can reduce crop productivity, decrease farm profitability, and cause serious environmental pollution. However, there is no consensus among researchers on the most appropriate farming practices regarding N use.
objective: a) estimate the n use efficiency of summer maize in north china plain; b) the impact of farming practices on the n use of summer maize; c) factors affecting the partial factor productivity of n of summer maize; and d) appropriate farming practices of summer maize in ncp.
result1: partial factor productivity of applied n was increased by irrigation  (25% increase, p < 0.05).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: partial factor productivity of applied nitrogen was increased by irrigation.

search_strategy: literature searches were conducted in the isi web of knowledge core database targeting peerreviewed articles published online until april 30, 2015 in two steps. the search terms for the first query was (“agro*” or “agri*” or “farm*”) and (mediterranean*) and (ecosystem*) and (management*) and (irrigat*) in the topic field. the second query was made with combinations of keywords including (“agro*” or “agri*” or “farm*”) and (mediterranean*) and (management*) in the topic field. after removing duplicate articles (n = 17) and adding one relevant article manually as suggested by a contacted author (roper et al. 2013), a total of 1,910 articles was used as the initial data base.
selection_criteria: 1) empirical case studies which measured ecosystem services-related properties both for conservation (treatment) and conventional (control) management options. 2) papers reporting results from the mediterranean basin but included six well-designed papers reporting from mediterranean climate regions outside the basin (i.e., south and south west australia, the cape of south africa, central chile, and california). 3) if a study had not provided the sample size, the authors excluded the study from the analysis (n = 1).
data_analysis: the authors analyzed the impact of different management options on ecosystem services from publications through a meta analysis. to secure statistical significance by keeping a sufficient sample size, they decided to weight observations using the sample sizes. the 95% confidence intervals (cis) were constructed by non-parametric bootstrapping (nboot = 10, 000) using the percentile method. the bootstrapping was only conducted for management options with more than seven case studies (n ≥ 8) as the bootstrap is unreliable when the sample size is too small.
background: In the Mediterranean region, the long-term provision of agro-ecosystem services is threatened by accelerating climate change, unsustainable farming practices, and other pressures. Alternative management practices such as conservation agriculture could be expected to ensure sustainability of ecosystem services from Mediterranean agro-ecosystems.
objective: the goal of this study is to identify the positive and negative impacts of conservation farming practices on ecosystem services in the mediterranean basin, providing evidence-based recommendations for sustainable land management in the mediterranean basin in the future.
result1: under the rainfed system, total organic carbon had a negative impact on water provisionning service (note from the reviewer: few data, no statistical analysis of the effect).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: there was a negative impact of the rainfed system on water provisionning service. note from the reviewers: due to the lack of data, no statistical analysis of the effect was performed.
knowledge_gaps: 1) longer term studies will be required to test the conservative management practices. 2) offsite effects such as maintenance of drinking water quality, reduction of pollution from agriculture, reduction of salinization, and eutrophication in soils and water are crucial for many surrounding areas. these topics could be addressed in the future research. 3) developing more suitable indicators is ongoing work in the ecosystem service community, one might therefore expect a potentially clearer connection between tested indicators and the quantification of ecosystem services.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed journal articles published in english from 1985 to 2016 were collected to build the database based on web of science search using the following sets of keywords: (i) wheat or maize; (ii) film mulch or plastic mulch or plastic cover; and (iii) water stress or water deficit or drought or irrigation deficit. the authors replaced the phrases ‘film mulch’; ‘plastic mulch’ and ‘plastic cover’ with ‘irrigation’ and ‘china’ to search for articles discussing supplementary irrigation specific to the region.
selection_criteria: only articles from china that met the following criteria were included in the database: (i) the experiments were conducted under field conditions where the effect of irrigation or plastic mulching was compared with flat (even or level topography); rainfed conditions; (ii) the reported plants were monoculture cereals of maize (zea mays) and wheat (i.e.; bread wheat; triticum aestivum); and (iii) the articles reported crop response as grain yield.
data_analysis: the magnitude of yield, total et, wue, and average soil water content (0–20 cm) responses throughout the crop growing season were examined based on three different types of mulch that covered the furrow: (i) plastic, (ii) straw, (iii) no cover or bare. to compare the differences in crop or soil response ratio between each treatment, meta-analysis was used to construct the confidence intervals. the authors performed a simple diagnostic test using the formula following lajeunesse to improve the reliability of lnr in estimating the effect size. bootstrapping was also iterated 9999 times to improve the probability that the confidence interval was calculated around the cumulative mean effect size for each categorical variable.
background: Plastic mulching technology for wheat and maize has been commonly used in China, but their effect on yield, soil water content, evapotranspiration (ET), and WUE has not been compared with traditional irrigation.
objective: using a meta-analysis approach, the authors quantitatively examined the efficacy of plastic mulching in comparison with traditional irrigation in china.
result1: the results show that irrigation increased soil water content when compared to flat, rainfed cropping systems (+22%).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: the results show that irrigation increased soil water content when compared to flat, rainfed cropping systems.

search_strategy: a systematic and exhaustive literature search was conducted in february and march 2016 using google scholar and the web of science search engines with the following keywords: water use efficiency, wue, yield, ogallala, dryland, rainfed, deficit irrigation, texas.
selection_criteria: 1) the experiment characteristics had to include a dryland observation; 2) the articles had to report yield and wue for each irrigation treatment.
data_analysis:
the meta-analysis was conducted using the comprehensive meta-analysis software version 3 developed by borenstein et al. (2013). a random effects model was used to assess water use efficiency (wue) under deficit irrigation as we assumed the true effect varied across
studies. each observation was weighted using a non-parametric variance. heterogeneity was assessed using cochran’s q statistic to test the null hypothesis that all studies share a common effect size. graphical and statistical methods were used for assessing publication bias: funnel plots; duval and tweedie (2000) developed a non-parametric trim and fill procedure to estimate the number of missing studies and the impact those studies would have had on the summary point estimates; and rosenberg’s fail-safe number.
background: Since pre-development in the 1950s, intensive irrigation for crop production has depleted over half of the saturated thickness of the Ogallala Aquifer (Texas). Adoption of irrigationtechnology began with low-pressure systems such as furrow and gravity flow, but more efficient technology such as center pivot systems using Low-Elevation Spray Application (LESA), Mid-Elevation Spray Application (MESA), and Low-Energy Precision Application (LEPA) nozzles and as well as Subsurface Drip Irrigation (SDI) are more widely used. Deficit irrigation strategies are being explored to reduce water inputs, but the impact on crop yield and water use efficiency (WUE) is uncertain.
objective: to determine how a water use efficiency (wue) treatment is affected by irrigation systems and management practices on clay and clay loam soils in a semi-arid environment relative to a rainfed control.
result1: furrow irrigation only had a 14% (n = 76; ci 0.77–1.68; p value: 0.517) increase in wue compared to a 99% (n = 235; ci 1.52–2.59; p value: < 0.001) increase in center pivot  irrigation and 147% (n = 40; ci 1.30–4.72; p value: 0.006) increase with drip irrigation.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: subsurface drip and center pivot irrigation systems had the largest impacts on wue. furrow irrigation did not impact wue.

search_strategy: all published peer-reviewed scientific journal articles on the water use of winter wheat-summer maize cropping systems were collected from the china national knowledge infrastructure (1979–2019, http://www.cnki.net/) and web of science (1979–2019 , h t t p : //apps.webofknowledge.com/). different combinations of search terms that included “north china plain” or “huang-huai-hai plain” and “winter wheat” or “summer maize” or “summer corn” and “crop product*” or “yield” or “output” were used for the selection of published studies.
selection_criteria: (i) the research object must be field experiments conducted in the ncp, excluding pot and laboratory experiments and model simulations; (ii) the cropping system must be the winter wheat-summer maize cropping system; (iii) the studies must be about one or more of the four leading management practices (e.g., no nitrogen versus nitrogen input, no irrigation versus irrigation, rotary tillage versus other tillage methods, and straw removal versus straw return, with the former as the control and the later as the treatment); and (iv) the data must include the number of trial replications, crop yield, wue, or seasonal crop evapotranspiration (etc).
data_analysis: the random-effect meta-analysis was used to analyze the data set of wheat water use. the metawin 2.1 software  was selected for this metaanalysis. authors obtained the 95% confidence interval (ci) and weighted mean effect size (ln r++) by bootstrapping. based on the data of winter wheat irrigation experiments, linear regression analysis in sigmaplot 14.0 was used to study the relationships between effect sizes ofwue under irrigation and other indicators.
background: Water shortage is a serious threat to agriculture production in the North China Plain. Sustainable management practices can improve the water use efficiency of winter wheat, but currently no academic consensus has been reached
objective: authors conducted a meta-analysis on the yield and water use of a winter wheat-summer maize cropping system based on peer-reviewed studies in the north china plain (ncp) to (i) investigate the current situation of water use in a winter wheat-summer maize cropping system, (ii) identify the factors that affect the wue of winter wheat, and (iii) propose sustainable management strategies to optimize the winter wheat production in the ncp.
result1: compared with rain-fed, irrigation did not significantly influenced wue (p > 0.05)
result2: NA
general_conclusion: compared with rainfed, irrigation did not significantly influenced wue.
knowledge_gaps: in the future, studies on sustainable agricultural management practices should adopt innovative models to comprehensively consider the use of natural resources and other factors to propose an ideal model for sustainable agricultural management practices.

search_strategy: the authors conducted a comprehensive search of peer-reviewed reports on water use in maize production published between 1970 and 2018 using the web of science, china national knowledge infrastructure and google scholar. different combinations of searching terms included “maize” or “corn”, and “yield”, and “irrigated”, and “water productivity” or “water use efficiency” in the abstract or key words.
selection_criteria: the authors screened publications based on the following criteria: maize yield and wp were documented; data were measured in field experiments (pot experiments, experiments under rainproof shelters, and model simulations were excluded); locations of experimental sites were explicitly provided; experimental treatments (irrigated/non-irrigated) were paired; and soil water supply before sowing and at harvest was reported for a soil layer of at least 1 m.
data_analysis: the authors applied random-effects meta-analysis to assess the impact on yield, et, wp, biomass, hi, yield components under irrigated compared with non-irrigated systems. there were significant heterogeneity in the random-effects meta-analysis for the yield dataset (qt = 3776846, p< 0.0001), for et dataset (qt = 65655191, p < 0.0001) and for wp database (qt = 5560054, p < 0.0001). the authors ran mixed-effects meta-analysis models to assess the relationship between effect sizes and explanatory variables. the explanatory variables considered in this meta-analysis included seasonal precipitation levels, irrigation amounts, annual average temperature, soil organic matter (som), soil bulk density, and n fertilizer rate, the dataset (yield and wp databases) were separated into different sub-datasets. publication bias was assessed using funnel plots and egger tests. rosenberg’s fail safe-numbers (nfs) were calculated to assess the robustness of our results to publication bias. the results were considered robust despite the possibility for publication bias if nfs > 5*k +10, where, k indicated number of sizes.
background: Detailed knowledge of how irrigation affects maize yield, WP, Nr losses, and GHG emissions is critical to evaluated the potential of irrigation for sustainably feeding the growing population in tandem with climate change mitigation on a global scale. However, a quantitative synthesis of the overall responses of food security, water resource, and environments to irrigation in maize production is still lacking.
objective: in current study, the authors carried out a meta-analysis to quantitatively estimate irrigation management effects on yield, wp, nr losses, and ghg emissions by integrating available worldwide measurements.
result1: compared to non-irrigated systems, wp was 9.91% (cis: 8.11 to 11.72, qt = 5560054, p < 0.0001) higher in irrigated systems (20.5 kg ha−1 mm−1 vs. 19.1 kg ha−1 mm−1).
result2: irrigation amounts, seasonal precipitation, annual average temperature, and fertilizer application of n significantly affected maize wp.
general_conclusion: compared to non-irrigated systems, water productivity was higher in irrigated systems. in practice, maize water productivity response to irrigation varied among environmental conditions (e.g., irrigation amounts, annual average temperature and precipitation levels), experience condition (e.g., soil organic matter, bulk density, nitrogen inputs).
knowledge_gaps: 1) some trade-offs must be considered in terms of, for example, freshwater resource management and nitrates leaching; 2) invest should focus on agronomic research that incorporates an ecosystem perspective, modifying and adapting intensive agricultural systems according to knowledge from diverse research disciplines

objective: using a meta-analysis approach, the authors quantitatively examined the efficacy of plastic mulching in comparison with traditional irrigation in china.
result1: the results show that irrigation increased wue when compared to flat, rainfed cropping systems (+3%).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: the results show that irrigation increased water use efficiency when compared to flat, rainfed cropping systems.

search_strategy: in this meta-analysis, authors considered five commonly used management practices in agricultural production in the loess plateau region: mulching, tillage, water-saving irrigation, nitrogen fertilizer management, and straw return practices. authors used “loess plateau,”“nitrogenous fertilizer,” “mulching,” “conservation tillage,” “water-saving irrigation,” and “straw return” as keywords and searched peer-reviewed literature up to the end of 2021 using the china knowledge resource integrated database (http://www.cnki.net/), google scholar (https://xueshu.soogle.top/), and web of science (http://apps.webofknowledge.com/).
selection_criteria: 1) field experiments must have been conducted in the loess plateau region; 2) comparisons of one or more practices, e.g., no mulching versus mulching, plowing tillage versus conservation tillage, no irrigation versus water-saving irrigation, no n and n input, and straw removal versus straw return, with the former as the control and the later as the treatment; 3) the treatment group and control group must have been tested at the same time and on the same spatial scale; 4) the experiment must have been a field experiment with three or more replicates, and thus indoor and pot experiments were excluded; and 5) the crop wue was calculated as the ratio of the crop economic yield relative to water consumption, and it could be extracted or calculated directly from the collected data.
data_analysis: the weighted effect size and 95% confidence interval (ci) were calculated using the random effects model based on the restricted maximum likelihood estimation with openmee software.  to assess the relative importance of the explanatory variables, authors conducted multiple linear regression with mixed models, followed by model averaging using the r package “dmetar” (). the “dmetar” package creates a set of models with all possible combinations of the explanatory variables. the “multimodel.inference” function was used to rank the resulting set of models according to the akaike information criterion (aic) and to calculate the overall average predictions based on the aic weights.
background: The lack of water resources limits sustainable agricultural production in the Loess Plateau region of China, and optimizing field management practices to improve crop water use efficiency (WUE) is a key strategy to solve this problem. However, there is no consensus among researchers on the most appropriate field management practices regarding WUE, which requires further integrated quantitative analysis.
objective: authors conducted a meta-analysis by computing 1338 effect sizes from 171 publications to quantify the effect of agricultural practices (nitrogen (n) fertilizer management, mulching management, water-saving irrigation, straw return and conservation tillage) on crop water use efficiency (wue).
result1: water-saving irrigation improved crop wue by 15.97%  (p < 0.05)
result2: NA
general_conclusion: sprinkler irrigation, drip irrigation, and infiltration irrigation significantly increased the crop wue compared to rainfed (effects not distinguished by the authors).
knowledge_gaps: future studies should focus on more interactive analyses of the various factors that might affect the water use efficiencies of crops under drought conditions.

search_strategy: a comprehensive search for peer-reviewed literature published from january 1990 to january 2016 related to the effects of irrigation on wheat yields was performed. literature were searched in three databases: web of science, springerlink, and the china academic journal network publishing database using the terms including ‘irrigation,’ ‘wheat,’ and ‘china’.
selection_criteria: (1) comparisons between non-irrigation and irrigation practices; (2) at least one parameter of interest (grain yield, yield components, water productivity, and et) was reported; and (3) the experimental location was stated. studies that described only the relationship between irrigation and wheat yield without a non-irrigation practice, and those that did not provide clear descriptions of the experimental methods were rejected.
data_analysis: the natural log of the response ratio (irrigation/non-irrigation) was applied to represent the effect size in our meta-analysis. the weight of individual observations was calculated by replications, with weights = (n irrigation × n non-irrigation)/(n irrigation + n non-irrigation), where n irrigation and n non-irrigation are the number of replicates for irrigation and non-irrigation practices, respectively. bootstrapping procedures were conducted with a 95% confidence interval for weighted mean effect sizes using 4999 iterations.
background: Irrigation is a crucial measure for ensuring food security; however, the complex linkages among yield increases, water productivity, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are unclear for irrigated wheat production in China.
objective: here a meta-analysis was conducted to determine the trade-offs among yield increase, water productivity, and ghg emissions in irrigated chinese wheat production systems.
result1: under irrigated systems (conventional amount or timings, table 1 and 2, respectively), water productivity using irrigation did not increase, but rather decreased by 6%.
result2: the high water productivity under optimized irrigation amount systems is similar to the 17.8 kg ha−1 mm−1 found with non-irrigated systems (table 1). water productivity was not different between systems with improved irrigation timing and non-irrigated systems (table 2).
general_conclusion: in this meta-analysis, water productivity in irrigated systems was reduced compared with non-irrigated systems. optimized amounts or period had similar water productivity than in non-irrigated systems.

search_strategy: a comprehensive literature search provided cases of impacts of awm technologies, obtained from peer-reviewed journals and non-peer reviewed conference proceedings, theses and project reports in the limpopo river basin from 1980 to 2013. the sources searched for cases through the end of april 2013 were: agris, cabdirect, proquest, econlit, text webpublisher from inmagic, science direct, database of abstracts of reviews of effects (dare) and other databases (e.g. scopus, isi web of knowledge and google scholar). the literature search used the following keywords and their combinations: maize, sorghum, millet, rainfed, reduced tillage, no-tillage, ripper, ridges, tied ridges, conservation agriculture, minimum tillage, zero tillage, infiltration pits, fanya juu, planting basins, bunds, terraces, contours, inter-cropping, agroforestry, rotation, grain yield, runoff, nutrient and water harvesting. other words used were storage, retention, water storage, supplemental irrigation, irrigation, crop residues, mulch, residue, organic, inorganic, manure, fertilizer, africa, sub-sahara africa, botswana, mozambique, south africa, zimbabwe, limpopo, olifants, mzingwane, gwanda, notwane, chokwe and xai xai.
selection_criteria: 1) located in the limpopo river basin; 2) cereals crops ; 3) reported yield, water productivity, and field runoff from treatment and control;
data_analysis: meta-analysis was used to determine the overall effect size of standardized mean difference (smd) and to impose a 95% confidence limits on the means. the random-effects model was used.  a funnel plot, which is a scatter plot of the effect estimate (smd) in relation to the size or precision of each study, standard error (se), was used for the assessment of risk of bias that may affect the cumulative evidence, such as publication bias and selective reporting within studies. factors used as covariates for the response of crop grain yield to awm technologies included: long-term rainfall, altitude, soil texture and field slope. the subgroup analyses examined whether the subgroups reduce any heterogeneity in each awm main group. the p-value used in this study relates to the summary effect in a meta-analysis. consistence of results was measured by i2 statistic.
scale: limpopo river basin (botswana, mozambique, south africa and zimbabwe)
background: Multiple agricultural water management (AWM) technologies are being promoted worldwide in rainfed agro-ecological production systems, such as the Limpopo River Basin, to close the yield gap, enhance food security and reduce poverty, but evidences on yield gains and environmental impacts are varied.
objective: this paper conducts a review of the performance of awm technologies, including water harvesting with storage (full or supplemental irrigation), against conventional farmer practices to produce adequate evidence on cereal yield and field runoff changes.
result1: water harvesting with storage resulted in marginal enhancement of water productivity.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: water harvesting with storage did not significantly enhanced water productivity.
knowledge_gaps: 1) no data in european union; 2) to strengthen the evidence of the influence of rainfall in agriculture water management technologies, intra-season or crop season rainfall distribution should be collected in future studies.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed publications were identified from isi web of science and china knowledge resource integrated database between 1990 and 2020. nine keywords and different combinations of these words, “maize, wheat, rice, nitrogen, fertilization, water input, irrigation, yield, and water use efficiency”, were used to search the databases mentioned above.
selection_criteria: the following criteria were used to select appropriate papers: (1) field studies of fertilization or irrigation experiments performed in china (pot experiments or model simulations were excluded); (2) the field studies consisted of a control treatment, without irrigation or fertilization; (3) wue (kg ha-1 mm-1) was calculated as a ratio of crop yield (kg ha-1) to water consumed, including the amount of water lost as evapotranspiration (mm) in the growing season; (4) the field experiment had at least two sample sizes and the experiment was carried out for more than two years; and (5) the mean value and sample size of crop yield or wue were available in the paper or can be calculated.
data_analysis: a categorical random-effect model was used to calculate the mean effect size (d++) for each group and 95% confidence intervals (cis) of effect size were generated by a bootstrapping procedure with 4999 iterations. all the relevant calculations were performed in metawin 2.1.
background: The increases in crop yield in China are linked to massive increases in fertilizer and water input, which have also accelerated the degradation of soil and environmental pollution. Nevertheless, the long-term changes in crop yield and water use efficiency (WUE) of three major cereals (maize, wheat and rice) in response to field management practices are rarely reported.
objective: a meta-analysis was used to assess the effects of field management (n input (kg ha􀍥1), irrigation (mm), fertilizer type, fertilization frequency, and irrigation method) on crop yield and wue for maize, wheat and rice in china.
result1: irrigation increased maize and wheat wue by 10% and 31%. irrigation increased rice wue.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: irrigation increased maize, wheat and rice wue.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed publications were collected by searching web of science (http://apps.webofknowledge.com) and china national knowledge infrastructure database (https://www.cnki.net) with various combinations of keywords “nitrous oxide” or “n2o,” “nitric oxide” or “no,” and “agricultural soils.”
selection_criteria: (i) the n2o and no emissions were simultaneously measured during at least a whole growing season; (ii) only the field measurements were included, without considering incubation, pot and lysimeter experiments or modelling results; (iii) the experiments on upland soils and paddy soils during the non-waterlogging period were included, without considering those on the flooded paddy soils; and (iv) the spatial replicates and standard deviation of each treatment were clearly recorded.
data_analysis: mean effect size and the 95 % confidence intervals were generated by a bootstrapping procedure with 999 iterations using metawin 2.1. individual effect sizes were weighted. the management effects were back-transformed and reported as percentage changes ([rr-1] × 100). the effects were considered significant if the 95 % confidence intervals did not overlap with zero.
background: Evidence from individual field measurements indicates that N2O and NO emissions respond to a certain management practice in a similar or divergent manner, mostly depending on the prevailing processes, such as denitrification or nitrification, contributing to each gas.
objective: the objective of this study is to quantify the effects of various management practices on n2o and no emissions by performing a pairwise meta-analysis. results on no are reported here.
result1: no-tillage decreased no emissions (by −21.2 %).
result2: NA
general_conclusion: no-tillage increased decreased no emissions.

search_strategy: peer-reviewed publications (2000-2015) investigating the effects of no-tillage in relation to the conventional tillage practice on soil physical properties, using web of science (elsevier) indexing service, with keywords ‘tillage’ and ‘soil’ in the article abstract.
selection_criteria: conference proceedings and non-english language publications were excluded. studies were selected exclusively based on the following criteria: (1) only field experiments containing side-by-side comparisons of nt and ct practices; (2) absence of confounding effects between nt and ct; (3) with more than one form of tillage in a study, ct was taken as the tillage producing the greatest soil disturbance; (4) with residue applied, ct was conventional tillage without residue and nt was no-tillage with residue; (5) at least three years of experimental duration; (6) studies were discarded if factors other than tillage was different between ct and nt, with an exception of herbicidal treatment.
data_analysis: since the within-study variance of means of parameters was not available for most of the studies, individual observations were weighted by the experimental replications. effect sizes from individual studies were combined using a random-effects model and was considered significant if the 95% confidence intervals (cis) [mean ± 1.96 * sd/sqrt (number of observations); 1.96 is the ‘z’-value at 95%] did not overlap with zero. meta- analysis was also performed for the groups (climate, duration, texture, and cs). the between- study variability (heterogeneity) was evaluated through a standard chi-squared test (cochran’s q-statistic; cochran, 1954) and the i2 statistic (higgins et al., 2003). a statistically significant (p<0.05) cochran q-test proved heterogeneity. the i2 statistic described the percentage of variation in effect size estimates, which were due to heterogeneity rather than by chance (deeks et al., 2008). publication bias was assessed through histograms (rosenberg et al., 2000) and in none of the cases, effect sizes showed preference towards positive or negative bias. meta-regression analysis and cumulative meta- analysis were also performed to reveal the change in soil physical parameters over the period of adoption to the nt practice. the meta-regression was performed for bd, mwd, and soc, and not for fc and rld due to less number of data points. meta-regression was also not performed for 30-60 cm layer again due to very few data points. cumulative meta-analysis produced results similar to the summary meta-analysis and therefore it was not presented.
background: No-tillage (NT) practice is a proponent of better resource utilization, to improve soil physical condition, and a potential sink to atmospheric carbon. However, the impact varies across climates, over the NT history, cropping systems and soil depths.
objective: evaluate the effect of nt in comparison to conventional tillage (ct), on soil physical condition (bulk density, bd; mean weight diameter of aggregates, mwd; field capacity water content, fc; and steady-state infiltration rate, ir), soil organic carbon (soc) content, and the root response (root length density, rld).
result1: surface 0-5 and 5-10 cm layers had significantly higher soc content under nt, while in other layers, the soc content either reduced or did not change, resulting in a small and insignificant variation in the soc stock (1.1%) in favour of nt.
result2: climate, duration, soil texture, and cropping system had highly significant impacts on the soc content in all the layers
result3: a reduction in soc content in cereals and an increase in legume system were recorded under nt till 30 cm depth of the soil.
general_conclusion: no significant effect on soil organic carbon stock

search_strategy: the seach was conducted in google scholar, web of science, and scopus databases for peer-reviewed articles, theses, and dissertations assessing soc and/or tn storage in tilled and nt soils.
selection_criteria: the studies were screened for those (a) comparing paired tilled and nt plots at the same sampling time, or (b) assessing temporal changes on tilled or nt soils in comparison with a pretreatment baseline from the same plot. we only selected those studies that had similar soil type and management practices in both treatments (that is, residue management, mineral or organic n fertilization, crop number [diversity] and frequency [number of crops per year], and legume use frequency in the cropping system). discarded studies: tillage treatments were applied for <5yr, crop residue removed, burned, or grazed (5% of the database).
data_analysis: the overall cumulative effect size was calculated using a random-effects model meta-analysis. bootstrap resampling with 999 interactions was used to correct the calculated 95% ci for bias caused by small sample sizes or differences in data distribution among treatments, thus generating a 95% bootstrap ci.
background: The “4 per 1,000” initiative was launched at the 21st Conference of the Parties (COP21) stimulating a long-standing debate on the potential of no-till (NT) to promote soil C sequestration. Previous reviews found little or no soil organic C (SOC) accrual in NT soils as compared with full inversion tillage when soils are sampled deeper than 30 cm.
objective: present the results of a global meta-analysis of studies assessing soc and total n (tn) storage and dynamics in nt and tilled soils from the most important agricultural regions of the world.
result1: nt soils stored 6.7 +- 1.9 mg c ha -1 and 1.1 +- 0.4 mg n ha-1 more than tilled soils (0-to-100-cm depth) with an average of 16 yr of nt, in contrast with previous findings.
result2: soc stocks were greater in nt than in tilled soils, notably in the upper 0-to-5- and 5-to-15-cm soil layers.
result3: moldboard plow represented the greatest soil disturbance by fully inverting soil layers and reallocating fresh crop residues to the bottom of the plow layer (23 +- 5 cm), thus increasing soc storage and stabilization in relation to nt in the 15-to-30-cm soil layer.
result4: no differences on soc stocks were noticed in deeper soil layers (30-60 and 60-100 cm) on the comparison of tilled and nt soils, regardless of the tillage practice used in tilled soils.
result5: mean annual temperature was positively correlated with the mean difference of soc for the 0-to-30- and 0-to-60-cm layers of nt and tilled soils.
general_conclusion: compared to moldboard plow, soc stocks were greater in nt, notably in the upper 0-to-5- and 5-to-15-cm soil layers.

search_strategy: the authors conducted a literature search to find articles from temperate and tropical regions assessing management impacts using several criteria.
selection_criteria: selection criteria were: i) studies that either provided soc stocks or the information necessary to calculate soc stocks; ii) studies needed to report the depth of measurement and time frame over which the management change had occurred; iii) studies had to provide the location or climate data for the study sites so that we could classify them into climate regimes according to ipcc 1997 method.
data_analysis: this research was conducted to provide empirical estimates for the ipcc method, which was developed to compute the change in soc storage from a baseline condition using management factors, which are numerical values representing the relative change in soc storage due to land use and management activities. fixed effects were assumed for climate, depth and time after the management change, and all first-order interaction terms that were significant among the fixed effects at an alpha level of 0.05 were included. regressors were formed from the upper (u) and lower (l) positions values of each depth increment by assuming that the soc stock ratio declined as a quadratic function of depth, so that average soc stock ratio for a single increment was the integral from u to l depth positions of the quadratic function divided by thickness of the increment. random effects were included in the model for study and a study-by-time interaction in order to account for dependence among measurements within the same study. management factor values from the statistical models based on the integrated impact in top 30 cm of the soil profile for the first 20 years following a management change, and then computed standard errors for the factor value estimates.
background: Land use and management of agricultural systems is known to change the storage of soil organic carbon (SOC) through variation in land use, tillage, cropping practices (intensity and types of crops), irrigation, fertilization, and other activities.
objective: the effect of land use and management practices largely determine the net carbon (c) balance of agricultural soils, and here we provide statistically based estimates of those impacts for several activities, including (1) long-term cultivation, (2) changing tillage management, (3) modifying c input to the soil by varying cropping practices, and (4) setting-aside land from crop production. here the results related to tillage management are reported.
result1: more than half of the response ratios were positive for both reduced and no-till systems, demonstrating that these practices most often increase soc storage, but there were studies that found no increase in storage relative to conventional tillage.
result2: integrated over the top 30 cm of the soil profile, reduced tillage (e.g., ridge, mulch or chisel plowing) had very little if any impact on soc in the temperate dry climates, with storage increasing by a factor of 1.03 +/- 0.03 during the first 20 years after a management change, which is only an average increase of 3%. moreover, even the uncertainty in a modest 80% confidence interval (0.99-1.07) will include a factor value of 1, which would represent no change in carbon storage. there were more substantial impacts in the other climate regions, however, estimated at factors of 1.09 +/- 0.03 in temperate moist climates, 1.10 +/- 0.05 in tropical dry climates, and 1.16 +/- 0.02 in tropical moist climates.
result3: compared to reduced tillage practices, changing from conventional tillage to no-till increased soc by even larger amounts across each of the climatic regions, ranging from a factor of 1.10 +/- 0.03 in temperate dry climates to 1.16 +/- 0.02 in temperate moist climates, 1.17 +/- 0.05 in tropical dry climates, and 1.23 +/- 0.05 in tropical moist climates.
general_conclusion: overall, reducing tillage intensity increased soc, but the effect varied between climatic regions.

search_strategy: a survey of the literature comparing c stocks under nt and ct was conducted using isi web of knowledge. for the establishment of the database studies published until december 2009 were considered.
selection_criteria: selection criteria were: situations (i) displaying more than 5 years since the conversion to nt, (ii) where nt meant direct seeding (situations of minimum or reduced tillage were excluded) with crop residues left on the soil surface and ct meant mouldboard ploughing or full inversion tillage (it) that incorporates crop residues into the soil and leaves less than 30% of residue cover after tillage, (iii) with similar agricultural history until the implementation of nt, and (iv) with equal cropping systems (rotation, fertilization, etc.) in the plots under nt and it.
data_analysis: the effect of tillage on soc stocks in the 0-30 cm was tested using a pairwise t-test. the effects of the factors were investigated using multiple linear regressions, with a random effect for the study. the following mixed models were tested to try to explain relative and absolute c stock differences: (i) texture, aridity and their interaction; (ii) texture, mean temperature, annual precipitation and their interactions on the large database. (iii) yearly difference of c inputs (di, relative and absolute), texture, aridity and their interactions; (iv) di (absolute and relative), texture, mean annual temperature, annual precipitation and interactions on the reduced database. similarly, two mixed models were tested to try to explain the input differences between nt and it systems: (v) texture, aridity and their interaction; (vi) texture, mean temperature, annual precipitation and their interactions.
background: Conversion to no-till (NT) is usually associated to increased soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks in comparison to inversion tillage (IT). However, an important and unexplained variability in the changes in SOC with NT adoption exists, which impedes accurate prediction of its potential for C sequestration.
objective: the objective of this study is gaining knowledge on the effect of the conversion of regularly tilled soils to nt on soil c storage by analyzing the large and unexplained variability reported for this storage in the literature. the authors critically reviewed the existing literature on the effect on soc stocks of nt conversion of previously tilled soils in relation to continuous ct, in order to create a database from which a meta-analysis would be run to evaluate the factors affecting the storage of soc under nt compared to the tilled systems with crop residue incorporation through inversion tillage (it).
result1: nt treatment significantly increased c stocks in the 0-30 cm (n = 92; t = 2.822; p = 0.006). this increase was equal to about 6.7% of the stock under it on average and was very variable (standard deviation = 17%). in absolute value, nt conversion induced an extra storage of 3.4 mg c/ha on average.
result2: there was a very significant effect of the relative yearly difference of inputs between nt and it on relative and absolute soc stocks differences (p = 0.01 and p = 0.04, respectively) under nt and it.
general_conclusion: greater soc stocks were observed with nt in this study.
knowledge_gaps: central and south america are less represented in the database, and information from the other continents is scarce (asia) or lacking (africa).

search_strategy: a literature survey of peer-reviewed published literature in the isi-web of science and cab abstracts (ovid) between 1910 and 2013 was conducted to identify papers reporting results from studies using reduced tillage in organic farming. the following search terms and their variations were used in various combinations: reduced/minimum/shallow/chisel, tillage/ploughing/plowing, intensity, no-till/direct seeding, organic/ecological, farming/systems/agriculture/management.
selection_criteria: (i) experiment under organic management for at least 3 years prior to the date of response measurement; (ii) at least two levels of tillage intensity included as a treatment; (iii) no “mixing” of treatments, i.e., only tillage varied between experimental treatments; and (iv) included climatic zones found in europe
data_analysis: data were analyzed using unweighted meta-analysis techniques. the significance of effect sizes was tested using linear mixed effects models in the “lme4” package in r with random effects specified as experiment/year. the fixed effects of tillage class or climate were tested using this model. the effect of tillage class within a given soil type or crop class was tested after first subsetting the data by soil type or crop class and then using a mixed effects model as described above. for all analyses, least-square means and confidence intervals were generated using the “lsmeans” package in r. means were considered significantly different from zero if the 95 % ci did not overlap zero, and different from one another if their 95 % cis were non-overlapping (hedges et al. 1999). the results of each mean ratio (r) were expressed as % effect size (e), where e = (r − 1) × 100.
background: NA
objective: NA
result1: there were a total of 184 observation pairs in the first dataset where reduced tillage intensity was compared to deep inversion tillage. for this set of data, all reductions in tillage intensity increased soil c stocks by 143 g m−2
result2: there was little difference in the relative increase in c stocks depending on the tillage class, although shallow non-inversion (less than 10 cm) did not result in a significant increase in c stocks relative to the deep inversion control.
result3: for the second subset of data where reduced tillage intensity was compared to shallow inversion tillage, there was no clear increase in soil c stocks when tillage intensity was reduced.
