search_strategy: search strategy: the literature search was conducted in the web of science, covering databases like medline and biosis, with updates from january 2016 to february 2020. the search terms included biodiversity, agroforestry, and europe, using various synonyms. full texts were accessed through open access and university subscriptions.
selection_criteria:
the selection criteria for studies included in the meta-analysis were:

studies must quantify biodiversity in agroforestry.

references from reviewed studies were verified for inclusion.

extractable measures of species richness or other biodiversity metrics were required.

full texts were sought online; authors were contacted if necessary.
data_analysis: the authors used sensitivity analysis, modifying traditional inverse variance weighting based on study evidence. they assessed publication bias with a funnel plot and egger’s regression test. a random-effects model estimated the summary effect of agroforestry on biodiversity, with heterogeneity tested using a q-test and i² statistic.
background: The meta-analysis examines the impact of agroforestry on biodiversity, utilizing data from various studies. It assesses evidence quality, addresses publication bias, and employs advanced statistical methods to ensure robust conclusions. Acknowledgments highlight contributions from researchers and funding sources supporting the project.
objective: the main objective of the meta-analysis is to evaluate the impact of agroforestry on biodiversity by comparing effect sizes between agroforestry sites and control sites. key research questions include identifying environmental variables influencing this relationship and determining under what circumstances agroforestry benefits biodiversity. the main variables considered in the meta-analysis as moderators include:  sampling methods: various methods including transects and traps; diversity measure: species richness, family richness, shannon diversity; sampling year: 1984 to 2019; country of study location: european countries; climate zone: mediterranean, temperate central european, boreal.

search_strategy:
for this meta-analysis, only peer-reviewed articles on agroforestry and oc sequestration in the temperate zone from scopus, isi web of science and google scholar were considered. the search in april 2021 in the title, abstract and keywords was based on the following combination of search terms:
(agroforestry or agropastoral or agrosilvopastoral or alley cropping or bufferstrips or forest gardening or forest farming or hedgerows or or living fences or meadow orchard or riparian bufferzone or scattered fruit trees or short rotation coppice or silvopastoral or silvorarable or tree-based intercropping or windbreaks or wind buffer) and (carbon or carbon sequestration or c sequestration or soil c sequestration or soc or soc storage).
selection_criteria: several identified studies and observations had to be excluded from the meta-analysis due to e.g., duplicated sites, changes in land use or stock of trees or lack of comparable control sites. the control types diachronic, where the control is sampled on the same plot before establishment of the afs, and synchronic, where the control is a treeless neighbouring plot with similar land use and management as in the agroforestry alleys, were both included in the data set. the meta-analysis was restricted to temperate climate zones according to the köppen-geiger climate classification. as typical afs systems in temperate zones, silvopastoral systems, alley cropping, hedgerows and shelterbelts were identified. silvopasture integrates trees in animal production systems, such as cattle grazing on pasture under widely spaced or scattered trees. alley cropping uses both slow- and fast-growing woody species grown in crop fields with close in-row spacing and wider between-row spacing to allow mechanization. here, trees may be pruned to reduce shading of the crops. single rows of trees or shrubs planted at the edges of the fields are defined as shelterbelts or hedgerows.
data_analysis: data was tested for normal distribution using shapiro-wilk test followed by levene’s test for homoscedasticity. in order to test for statistically significant differences between paired groups (afs and its corresponding control sites), we applied a paired t-test as parametric or a wilcoxon signed rank test as non-parametric test. for independent groups and nominal scaling, we computed an unpaired t-test and unpaired wilcoxon signed rank test (two groups) or one-way anova and kruskal-wallis test (more than two groups). with respect to the parameters köppen climate and soil type, no further statistical testing was possible, as the number of observations per group was too small in some cases. we calculated spearman’s rank correlation coefficient for ratio scaled data. a multi-factor analysis of variance could not be applied as not all concerning data was normally distributed. the significance level was set at α = 0.05 for all test statistics. for executing these calculations and for visualisation including the map, we used the software r.
background: Soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration by improved agricultural practices is an acclaimed strategy to combat climate change. Nevertheless, the aim of increasing of SOC encounters limitations, e.g. with regards to permanence of carbon storage or leakage effects in food production. Agroforestry systems (AFS) are a promising land use option that is able to sequester substantial amounts of SOC while addressing these challenges. With a focus on temperate climate zones worldwide, available information on SOC in AFS was reviewed to determine their SOC sequestration potential and respective controlling factors.
objective: most findings on the soc sequestration potential of afs are from tropical and subtropical regions, with far fewer studies available for temperate regions. to our knowledge, there is no specific meta-study on soc sequestration by temperate afs. the aim of this work was to derive reliable estimates of the soc sequestration potential in topsoil and subsoils of afs in the temperate zone by a systematic meta-analysis. as the soc sequestration potential may depend on various factors such as the afs type, tree species and site conditions, this meta-analysis further aimed to identify the factors controlling soc sequestration in afs. all observations used in this meta-analysis were located in the northern hemisphere, most of them in europe (n = 41) followed by north america (n = 17). most of the observations were located in fully humid warm temperate climate (cfb, n = 29) with an average temperature of the four warmest moths of the year > 10 °c, with the warmest and coldest month of the year on average below 22 °c and above 0 °c. fifteen observations were located in fully humid continental climate with warm summers and at least four months of the year ≥ 10 °c and the coldest month on average below − 3 °c (dfb). with respect to absolute climatic data, map and mat ranged between 356 and 1171 mm (mean 761 ± 232 mm) and 3–16 °c (mean 9 ± 3 °c) at an average altitude of 225 ± 212 m asl
result1: afs showed higher soc stocks than its paired control sites at 0–20 cm depth. at a soil depth of 20–40 cm, in 21 of 26 observations (corresponding to 81% of the observations), afs showed higher soc stocks than its paired control sites. this result is statistically highly significant with a p-value of 0.0008 (0–20 cm, n = 61) and 0.0026 (20–40 cm, n = 26). (figure 2)
result2: regarding mean values, soc stocks under afs were significantly higher (47.1 ± 29.2 t ha-1) than those of the control sites at 0–20 cm depth (40.1 ± 24.2 t ha-1) (table 3). with respect to the 20–40 cm soil increment, soc stocks under afs were also significantly higher (31.7 ± 11.8 t ha-1) than the control plots (28.6 ± 11.4 t ha-1, respectively).
result3: the soc sequestration rate was on average slightly higher at 0–20 cm compared with 20–40 cm soil depth (0.21 ± 0.79 and 0.15 ± 0.26 t ha-1 yr-1, respectively).
result4: this data contains two positive outliers (max. 3.80 t oc ha-1 yr-1, both from wang et al., 2015) (fig. 3). a total number of 17 observations (28% of total observations) showed negative soc sequestration rates in 0–20 cm as well as 5 plots (19%) in 20–40 cm depth (fig. 3). these negative rates were in all cases more pronounced in the 0–20 cm increment than in 20–40 cm depth
result5: we found significantly higher soc stocks under hedgerow (41.4 ± 9.0 t ha-1) compared to alley cropping at 20–40 cm depth (25.8 ± 8.9 t ha-1). at 0–20 cm depth, on average highest soc stocks were found under silvopasture, but this difference was not statistically significant. hedgerows revealed statistically significant higher mean soc sequestration rates than silvopasture at 0–20 cm depth (0.32 ± 0.26 t ha-1 yr-1 and −0.17 ± 0.50 t ha-1 yr-1) and 20–40 cm depth (0.28 ± 0.15 t ha-1 yr-1 and −0.03 ± 0.26 t ha-1 yr-1, respectively).
general_conclusion: NA

selection_criteria:

grass performance data collected in the same calendar year or continuous year.

studies conducted in the field with natural tree shade.

assessment of grass responses under two contrasting seasons and multiple levels of tree cover.

exclusion of studies reporting data for only one season or one level of tree cover.

reports on soil organic carbon comparing agroforestry (af) systems to non-agroforestry land.

information on land use prior to af system adoption.

detailed experimental data (location, age, soil depth, climate).

if soil carbon data was not directly reported, it was estimated using bulk density and soil depth.

meta-analysis: this combined findings from various studies, assessing heterogeneity with random effect models and evaluating publication bias using funnel plots and egger’s test.

background: The meta-analysis examines the impact of agroforestry (AF) systems on soil carbon stocks, highlighting their role in enhancing ecosystem services for food security. objective: the main objectives of the meta-analysis are to: (i) quantify soil carbon sequestration potential in four agroforestry systems, (ii) evaluate impacts of land use change, soil depth, age, and climate on these systems, (iii) understand drivers of carbon sequestration, and (iv) assess economic feasibility for carbon sequestration.
result1: agroforestry (af) systems generally enhance soil carbon (c) sequestration, with agrisilviculture showing the highest potential. transitioning from grassland or pasture to af increases c stocks, while converting forestland negatively impacts them. all af systems are economically viable and can support carbon trading, aiding climate goals.

search_strategy: search strategy involved querying the isi web of science on april 9, 2022, using keywords related to agroforestry and maize. a total of 945 articles were identified, with 930 assessed and 835 excluded based on relevance criteria. the analysis aimed to inform maize cultivation in agroforestry settings.
selection_criteria:
the selection criteria for studies included in the meta-analysis were:

growth experiments under field conditions.

reported maize yields in weight per unit area from both agroforestry and valid control settings.

agroforestry component must consist of living trees or woody plants.

valid control settings had no trees or intercrops and received the same agronomic treatment.

exclusions included studies lacking a tree-free control, using different agricultural procedures, or involving livestock.
data_analysis: the authors used the shapiro-wilk normality test to assess data distribution, finding it non-normal (p < 2.2 × 10−16). consequently, they applied the kruskal-wallis test (α = 0.05) to identify significant group differences, visualized with boxplots indicating significance levels.
background: The meta-analysis reviewed studies from 1990 to 2021 to assess how agroforestry affects maize yields, focusing on environmental factors and trial design. It aimed to provide evidence-based recommendations for maize cultivation in agroforestry, particularly to support food security and sustainable development goals.
objective: the main objective of the meta-analysis was to assess the effects of agroforestry on maize yields and how these effects vary with environmental and management factors. it aimed to provide scientifically substantiated recommendations for maize cultivation in agroforestry settings. the main variables considered in the meta-analysis as moderators of the effect include: climate factors (aridity index values); hyper arid: <0.03; arid: 0.03–0.2; semi-arid: 0.2–0.5; dry sub-humid: 0.5–0.65; humid: >0.65; soil characteristics: soil texture (sand, clay, loam); soil ph; soil organic carbon (soc) content; total nitrogen (n) content; extractable phosphorus (p) content; trial design factors (e.g., control settings).
result1: agroforestry systems improved maize yields, with a median yield of 2.6 mg ha−1 compared to 1.9 mg ha−1 in control plots.
result2: the absolute yield difference was 0.24 mg ha−1.
result3: the response ratio for maize yields was 7%.
result4: the analysis included 95 studies with 1,215 treatment-control data pairs.
general_conclusion: agroforestry practices significantly enhance maize yields, with a median increase of 0.24 mg ha−1 (7%). the most substantial benefits occur in n-deficient soils and with n-fixing tree species, achieving up to 0.56 mg ha−1 (60%). positive effects are also linked to tree age and planting density.
knowledge_gaps:
need for studies on agroforestry systems with diverse planting patterns, such as parklands and home-gardens.

exploration of the impacts of spatial heterogeneity on yield outcomes in agroforestry settings.

search_strategy:
literature search: utilized database search engines and bibliographies to gather relevant studies on riparian buffers.

data analysis: summarized peer-reviewed research on nitrogen attenuation related to buffer width, excluding non-peer-reviewed sources.

effectiveness calculation: assessed nitrogen removal effectiveness using percentage differences and mass removal per unit distance, applying regression models for analysis.
selection_criteria: the selection criteria for studies included in the meta-analysis were based on buffer width categories (0–25 m, 26–50 m, and >50 m), vegetation cover type (forest, wetland, etc.), and hydrologic flow conditions (surface vs. subsurface).
data_analysis: the authors used linear and nonlinear regression models to analyze nitrogen removal effectiveness based on buffer width. they also employed non-parametric tests due to non-normal distribution of dependent variables, as confirmed by the shapiro–wilk test (p < 0.001).
background: The meta-analysis published in the Journal of Environmental Quality examines the effectiveness of riparian buffers in reducing nitrogen levels. It highlights that wider buffers (over 50 m) are more effective than narrower ones (0-25 m) in nitrogen removal, particularly from subsurface flow.
objective: the main objective of the meta-analysis is to evaluate the effectiveness of riparian buffers in reducing nitrogen, particularly in subsurface flow. key research questions include how buffer width and vegetation type influence nitrogen removal efficiency. the main variables considered in the meta-analysis as moderators of nitrogen removal effectiveness include:; buffer width categories: 0–25 m, 26–50 m, >50 m.; flow path: surface vs. subsurface.; vegetation type: forest, forested wetland, herbaceous, herbaceous/forest mix, wetland.
result1: riparian buffers effectively reduce nitrogen, particularly from subsurface flow. wider buffers (>50 m) consistently remove more nitrogen than narrower ones (0–25 m). vegetation type does not significantly affect nitrogen removal effectiveness. other factors, like root depth and hydrological conditions, also influence outcomes.
result2: NA
general_conclusion: riparian buffers effectively reduce nitrogen, particularly from subsurface flow. wider buffers (>50 m) consistently remove more nitrogen than narrower ones (0–25 m). vegetation type does not significantly affect nitrogen removal effectiveness. other factors, like root depth and hydrological conditions, also influence outcomes.
knowledge_gaps:
the specific mechanisms of nitrogen removal in riparian buffers are not well understood.

existing information on buffer effectiveness is not synthesized or widely distributed to resource managers.

resource managers often lack the resources to assess the effectiveness of site-specific buffers.

search_strategy: studies were identiﬁed through a comprehensive search on web ofscience last updated in april 2011, using the search string: "landscape and [agr* or crop] and [enem* or predat* or parasit* or pest or biological control]".
selection_criteria: 1) a sample size consisting of at least ﬁve unique "landscapes", in which a landscape comprises a ﬁeld and the area surrounding it, separated by a minimum distance of 1 km from anyother ﬁeld in the study; 2) quantitative measurements of landscape complexity using gis or other spatial techniques at ≥ 500 m around the farm; 3) statistics reported as the univariate relationship between landscape complexity and arthropod response or the partial contribution of landscape complexity among other factors.
data_analysis: effect size was used as the response variable in generalised linear mixed models. each study question was tested with a different model. the aic (akaike information criteria) score was used as a guide for comparing different models, but p-values for each factor were also considered. likelihood-ratio testing was used as a more robust measure for nested models to determine whether the addition of a variable improved the model. models were nested hierarchically within the model for question 1 (trophic level). publication bias was investigated using three different methods: (1) funnel plots, (2) a spearman-rank correlation test and (3) rosenthal's fail-safe number.
background: Many studies in recent years have investigated the relationship between landscape complexity and pests, natural enemies and ⁄ or pest control. However, no quantitative synthesis of this literature beyond simple vote-count methods yet exists.
objective: to examine the effects of landscape-scale complexity on crop pests and their natural enemies. speciﬁcally, we investigate ﬁve quantitative questions: 1) how are natural enemies and pests each affected by landscape complexity? 2) how does the measurement of arthropod response (i.e. abundance, diversity, predation, pest control, plant damage) inﬂuence conclusions about the impact of landscape complexity? 3) how does the measurement of landscape complexity affect conclusions about its impact? 4) do specialist and generalist enemies and pests respond differently to landscape complexity? 5) do enemies and pests or specialists and generalists respond to different spatial scales of landscape complexity? here, results for objective 3 are reported. in particular, results on the effect of % natural habitat and "other" category (comprised of one study measuring distance to natural habitat and three studies measuring linear features such as length of woody edges at the landscape scale).
result1: landscape complexity metrics produced a positive response in natural enemies.
result2: none of the landscape metrics produced a significant response in pests.
general_conclusion: the positive response of natural enemies does not necessarily translate into pest control, since pest abundances show no signiﬁcant response to landscape complexity.

search_strategy: a database of runoff, soil loss and runoff plot measurements acquired from areas where soil conservation techniques were applied was mainly compiled from scientiﬁc journal articles, books and ph.d. dissertations. the authors reviewed the isi web of science, china national knowledge infrastructure, and google scholar databases to identify articles matching the keywords, soil loss and sediment yield.
selection_criteria: 1) the article contained at least one runoff or soil loss response variable; 2) each data point was collected during at least a full year, or the reported data could be extrapolated to represent a full year with a sufﬁcient degree of reliability; 3) the same response variables were compared between lands treated with soil conservation techniques (scts), hereafter called treated, and those not treated with scts (hereafter called control); 4) the treated lands and control lands were exposed to the same environmental conditions; 5) the number of replications was reported; 6) the groups of categories contained more than two data pairs; 7) only runoff and soil loss measurements from bound runoff plots equipped with tanks for collecting runoff and soil loss were used to reduce the inﬂuence of measurement uncertainties, and only plots with a minimum length of 5 m were retained because they were considered to be representative.
data_analysis: to further analyze the efﬁciencies of soil conservation techniques among different subgroup categories, the heterogeneity of effect sizes was assessed with p-values that describe the variations in effect sizes that can be attributed to differences among the categories of each predictor variable. the overall effect sizes and 95% conﬁdential intervals (cis) were computed and compared using the program metafor 2.0.
background: The beneﬁts of soil conservation techniques (SCTs) vary according to correlations between the natural environment and anthropogenic activities, and their effects on water erosion control at the plot scale have been extensively tested in ﬁeld runoff plots. However, only a few previous studies have focused on quantifying the effects of various SCTs at the regional scale, and only one type of SCT has been studied at the national, regional and global scales. Therefore, a comprehensive overview and quantiﬁcation of various SCTs at the global scale is lacking.
objective: the objectives of this paper are: 1) to develop a documented global database of ﬁeld plot data on the use of scts; 2) to quantify the effects of different sct types on water erosion control at the global scale; and 3) to compare the effects of scts on water erosion control for different slopes, land uses, continents and climate zones (czs).
result1: soil loss reduction was greater with than without buffer strips or hedgerows.
result2: run-off reduction was great for buffer strips. however, hedgerows were not recognized as powerful tools for reducing runoff.
result3: for orchards, the beneﬁts of scts in term of soil loss reduction increased as the slope increased, and for buffer strips was 38% and 26% for terraces.
general_conclusion: buffer strips, terraces and contour bunds were effective in reducing soil erosion and run-off. however, hedgerows were effective in reducing soil erosion but were not effective in reducing run-off.
knowledge_gaps: due to a lack of detailed information about some of the influential factors and the types of scts in this study, as well as the substantial variation in study conditions, the environmental and experimental factors controlling the variability in the efﬁciency of each sct could not be clearly identiﬁed in this study.

search_strategy: data sets of runoff and sediment yield by different minimum soil disturbance practices were collected from scientific articles published in all years ending december 2017. papers published in chinese journals were collected from the china national knowledge infrastructure and wanfang databases, and  international publications were obtained from the web of science and science direct.
selection_criteria:
1) the experiments or observations were conducted under field conditions (i.e., no laboratory or greenhouse experiments); 2) the article contained at least one minimum soil disturbance practices as response variables and conventional tillage as a control; 3) the article
contained at least one response variable of runoff or sediment generation; 4) the minimum soil disturbance lands and control lands for each independently published research were under the same topography and environmental conditions; 5) the article reported the
number of replications.
data_analysis: an unweighted analysis was performed using the log response ratio (lnrr) to calculate bootstrapped confidence limits in order to include the studies that did not adequately report standard deviations using metawin 2.1. a one‐way anova was used to analyze the significance of the differences in reducing runoff and sediment yield under different minimum soil disturbance practices, slope gradient, and length. linear regressions were used to examine the relationships of runoff and sediment yield reductions to slope gradient and length.to check the heterogeneity of the data set, the robustness of the meta‐analysis results was tested using a jackknife procedure. the results showed no publication bias.
background: Slope farmlands are commonly found in China, and soil loss from slope farmland is the main source of river sediment. Minimum soil disturbance practices were considered effectively in controlling water erosion, especially on slope farmlands.
objective: the objectives of this study were to 1) quantify the overall effectiveness of minimum soil disturbance practices in reducing runoff and sediment yield; and 2) determine the effect of slope gradient and length on the efficiency of minimum soil disturbance practices in reducing runoff and sediment yield. here, the results on sediment yield are reported.
result1: minimum soil disturbance practices in china reduced runoff and sedimentyield by 36.09% and 51.69%, respectively.
result2: contour tillage with hedgerow reduced sediment yield more effectively (p < 0.05) than the other practices.
general_conclusion: overall, minimum soil disturbance practices (contour tillage with hedgerow) reduced sediment yield and run-off significantly compared with conventional tillage.

search_strategy: the authors conducted a detailed screening of research papers published in peer-reviewed journals from 1980 until march 2020 by searching the keywords “ hedgerow ” or “ barrier strip ” or “ living hedge ” or “ buffer strip ” or “ filter strip ” and “ soil, ” on the web of science, china national knowledge internet and wanfang data.
selection_criteria: 1) at least one plant hedgerow was used to control agricultural agricultural non-point source pollution (npsp); 2) the same response variables were compared between the treatments with or without plant hedgerows (control); 3) the treatment with plant hedgerows and the control were performed under the same environmental conditions; 4) the number of replicates was reported; 5) if the data were repeatedly stated, only one of the values was selected; 6) data on soil organic matter (som), total n (tn), total p (tp), total k (tk), alkali n (an), available p (ap), and readily available k (ak) were available for the treatments with or without plant hedgerows.
data_analysis: analyses were conducted in the stata 15.1 statistical software, with the mean, sd and sample size as inputs. the confidence interval (ci) was set to 95%, and the standardized mean difference (smd) was used as the statistical indicator of the effect. before combining the analysis of smd, the chi-square q-test and statistic i2 are usually used for the heterogeneity test.

objective: to explore the influence of plant hedgerows on soil nutrients.
result1: the combined effect size is 1.46 (95% ci 1.12 – 1.80 > 0). thus, plant hedgerows can effectively increase som content.

search_strategy: the authors performed a search in the isi web of science and scopus (records published until 31.12.2017 were considered). to minimise potential publication bias and to maximise the number of relevant data sets they also searched for unpublished data by contacting potential data holders through researcher networks.
selection_criteria: 1) pollination and/or pest control services in crops were measured in both crop fields adjacent to floral plantings and control fields without planting; 2) the replication at the field level was ≥ six fields per study (three fields with plantings and three without; i.e. disqualifying small-scaled plot treatment comparisons within fields).
data_analysis: the authors used a mixed effect-modelling approach to address the research questions. in all models, study was included as a random intercept to account for the hierarchical structure of the data with field measures nested within study. effect sizes provided in the text and figures are model estimates of z-transformed response variables. for statistical inference of fixed effects log-likelihood ratio tests (lrt) were used. all statistical analyses were performed in r version 3.5.2 using the r-package lme4.
background: The lack of clarity about effects of flower plantings on ecosystem service provisioning and crop yield scattered in numerous case studies is a barrier to farmer adoption of such measures.
objective: the aim was to quantitatively assess the effectiveness of two of the most commonly implemented ecological intensification measures, flower strips and hedgerows, in promoting crop pollination, pest control services and crop production. moreover, the authors aim to better understand the key factors driving failure or success of these measures to suggest improvement of their design and implementation.
result1: the provisioning of pest control services in crop fields adjacent to flower strips was enhanced by 16% on average compared to fields without flower strips.
result2: on average, pest control services were also increased in crops adjacent to hedgerows, but effects were more variable and overall not statistically significant.
general_conclusion: this synthesis demonstrates enhanced natural pest control services to crops adjacent flower strips plantings but not adjacent to hedgerows, across a broad suite of regions, cropping systems and types of flower strips studied.

search_strategy: a literature survey based on the isi web of science database was carried out, applying the following search string: (hedge* or bocage or “field margin$” or shelter$belt or wind$break) and (carbon or “*organic* *matter*” or humus) and soil. the reference lists of the obtained articles were also searched for eligible studies. the literature search was updated until may 2020 without date restrictions.
selection_criteria: 1) report soc contents or stocks in hedgerow soils 2) studies with a paired-plot design, in which adjacent agricultural fields were sampled as a control 3) original studies with measured data; model studies were not considered 4) the control plot had to have a comparable soil type, especially a comparable texture, with that of the hedgerow plot 5) studies analysing other types of field margins, e.g. windbreaks. consisting of one tree line and no shrubs or field margins with mainly herbaceous vegetation, were excluded 6) the analysis was restricted to the temperate climate zone with a mean annual temperature of between 0 and 18 °c, according to the ipcc definition of temperate climate.
data_analysis:
the difference in soc between the hedgerow soils and the soils of adjacent agricultural fields was studied through meta-analysis. unique effect sizes with corresponding 95 % wald-type confidence intervals were calculated for all studies. heterogeneity between the studies was tested with cochran’s q-test and i2
statistics. correspondingly, a random effects model was applied to calculate the overall effect sizes. the individual effect sizes were therefore weighted by the inverse of their variance. lastly, all response ratios were back-transformed into percentages to aid interpretation. analyses were performed with the metafor package in r version 3.5.3.
background: The establishment of hedgerows may be a promising strategy to promote carbon (C) sinks for climate change mitigation. However, comprehensive and quantitative overviews comprising both soil and biomass C in traditional hedgerow ecosystems in the temperate climate region are scarce.
objective: the aim of this meta-analysis and review was to derive comprehensive estimates of c stocks in both soils and biomass of hedgerows. here, results on soil organic carbon (soc) stocks are reported.
result1: the establishment of hedgerows on cropland leads to a significant increase in soc stocks. the soc stock under hedgerows was on average 32 % higher than in the adjacent cropland, with a 95 % confidence interval ranging from 15 to 51 %. using the case of average temperate cropland, this translates into an soc stock increase of 17 ± 12 mg c ha−1 with the establishment of hedgerows on cropland.
result2: in contrast, the difference between soc under hedgerows and adjacent grasslands was close to zero (average of 9 %). the 95 % confidence intervals for the grassland overall estimate ranged from −30 to 19 % and thus overlapped zero, indicating that the establishment of hedgerows compared with grassland has no statistically significant effect on soc.
result3: test for heterogeneity was significant for both subgroups (cropland control: q = 34.15, df= 9, p value <0.001; i2 = 78.82 %; grassland control: q = 21.45, df = 5, p value <0.001; i2 = 83.23 %). however, except for one site in the “grassland control” subgroup, the confidence intervals of all studies overlapped with the overall estimate. therefore, the direction and average magnitude of the treatment effect were robust for both subgroups.
general_conclusion: the establishment of hedgerows, especially on cropland, can be an effective option for c sequestration in agricultural landscapes.
knowledge_gaps: with the current dataset, it was not possible to identify an influence of hedgerow age, soil texture or climate on the effect of hedgerow establishment on soc storage due to the small dataset.
